name: Philippines
why: Zomato left in 2020; Google Maps, TikTok and Facebook food groups carry local word of mouth.

spots.name: Mayon
spots.desc: Mayon is an active stratovolcano with a nearly perfect cone in the province of Albay in the Philippines. It is the centerpiece of the Mayon Volcano Natural Park, one of the first national parks of the country.

spots.name: Trekking Mount Pinatubo
spots.desc: A once-in-a-lifetime experience, highly recommended for hiking enthusiasts. Board a Filipino 4x4 jeep and experience a thrilling drive across Crow Valley, a moon-like terrain, with vast ash fields and rocky rivers. You will hike up towards the summit passing through sandy cliffs and up a mountain path. The views of the Crater Lake are absolutely breathtaking. On the way back you have the…

spots.name: Mt. Apo
spots.desc: The highest mountain in the Philippines, a dormant volcano.

spots.name: Taal Volcano
spots.desc: Taal Volcano is an active complex stratovolcano in the province of Batangas, Philippines, on an island in Taal Lake. It is one of the provincial symbols of Batangas, appearing on the new provincial seal and flag.

spots.name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
spots.local: Pambansang Liwasang Ilog sa Ilalim ng Lupa ng Puerto Princesa
spots.desc: At over 8 km in length, it is claimed to be the longest underground river in the world. With its crystalline waters and spectacular cave formations, the Underground River is possibly Puerto Princesa's most popular attraction. The site was also declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1999. The winding path of the river is navigable via small pumpboats that depart from Sabang Beach. Travel time…

spots.name: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
spots.desc: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a Philippines national park, administratively in Palawan province, but geographically out in the middle of the Sulu Sea. It is regarded as one of the world's finest diving destinations, either snorkelling or SCUBA.

spots.name: Chocolate Hills Complex
spots.desc: This is the most popular place to see the Chocolate Hills. You can ride ATV after the viewpoints.

spots.name: Lake Lanao
spots.desc: See the commanding majestic view of the Lake Lanao. The largest lake in Mindanao and one of the deepest in the Philippines. It is one of the 15 ancient lakes of the world.

spots.name: San Agustín Church
spots.desc: A true Spanish Baroque treasure, with magnificent trompe-l'œil ceilings and a splendid high altar. Consecrated in 1607, this ancient building managed to survive the Second World War (although it, too, sustained heavy damage) and is said to be the oldest stone church still standing in the Philippines. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1993 as part of the group "Baroque Churches of…
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Real

spots.name: Banaue Rice Terraces
spots.desc: Sometimes called the "Eighth Wonder of the World", the 2000-year-old Banaue rice terraces are a designated National Cultural Treasure, and while many are still in use, the outer rims are showing signs of deterioration. They were created by the Ifugao (local native people), in a massive engineering project to cover the sides of the valleys (probably 200 m from floor to rim) for several miles…

spots.name: Hungduan Rice Terraces
spots.local: Mga Hagdan-Hagdang Palayan ng Kordilyera ng Pilipinas
spots.desc: A rice terrace complex lining the Hapao River valley in the barangays of Hapao, Nungulunan and Ba-ang. It is one of five rice terrace complexes in Ifugao included in the UNESCO World Heritage List, but is overlooked by tourists in favor of the more accessible ones in Banaue. There is a panoramic viewdeck along the Tinoc-Hungduan-Banaue Road in Hapao.

spots.name: Mount Pulag
spots.desc: At , it is the second highest mountain in the Philippines, and the highest in Luzon. It also forms the triboundary between Nueva Vizcaya, Benguet and Ifugao.

spots.name: Pila Historic Town Center
spots.desc: One of the few surviving colonial-era town centers in the Philippines, clustered around the town plaza and Saint Anthony parish church and declared a National Historical Landmark in 2001. Contrary to popular belief, only the church was built in the Spanish era, while the houses and municipal hall were built during the early years of the American occupation. Unlike other heritage towns in the…

spots.name: Mount Banahaw
spots.desc: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At , it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people.

spots.name: International Rice Research Institute
spots.local: Pandaigdigang Sanayan sa Pananaliksik sa Bigas
spots.desc: On a large (252 hectares, 620 acres) experimental farm. In the 1960s and 1970s, the facility pioneered the development of fast-growing and large-yielding "miracle rice" varieties, along with controversial genetically-modified produced.

spots.name: Philippine Stock Exchange
spots.desc: One of the two stock exchanges in the Philippines, it is known to have Asia's shortest trading times which lasts only for two hours. Nearby the PSE is the Ninoy Aquino Monument.
spots.addr: Tower One & Exchange Plaza, Ayala Triangle Gardens, Ayala Avenue

spots.name: Philippine Arena
spots.desc: With a 55,000 seating capacity, the arena is the biggest domed indoor arena not only in the Philippines but in the world. Built by local Christian sect, Iglesia ni Cristo for their centennial, the Philippine Arena hosts several events including sporting events, church events and concerts.

spots.name: Paoay Church
spots.desc: A monumental church built in a mix of Baroque and Javanese architecture that took three centuries to complete. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1993

spots.name: Malacañang Palace
spots.desc: Make way for the most important person in the Philippines....the President. The official residence of the President, the etymology of the name Malacañan is from the Tagalog phrase "may lakan diyan" meaning "there's a nobleman there". The mansion was first used as a residence for the Spanish governor generals as well as the Americans. It was then the official residence of the president when…

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines
spots.desc: Built and opened in the 1900s, the museum showcases significant collections from archaeology, arts, cultural properties, zoology, botany and many more. The National Museum of the Philippines is a government institution in the Philippines and serves as an educational, scientific and cultural institution in preserving the various permanent national collections featuring the ethnographic…

spots.name: Mall of Asia Arena
spots.desc: A large outdoor arena that serves as an alternative venue for Philippine Basketball Association (PBA) games, most concerts, and theatrical performances.

spots.name: Minor Basilica of the Immaculate Conception (Manila Cathedral)
spots.desc: Destroyed and rebuilt several times over, the Cathedral is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Manila and one of the most important churches in the Philippines. The current Neo-Romanesque iteration (consecrated in 1958) is the eighth - or sixth, depending on who's counting - to stand on the site since 1581, succeeding the 19th-century structure that was levelled to the ground during the…

spots.name: Rizal Park (Luneta)
spots.desc: Nearest railway station: United Nations (LRT-1). Manila's green lung, this large urban park stretches from the Quirino Grandstand in the west to Taft Avenue in the east, with the historic walled district of Intramuros bordering it to the north. The park's most famous landmark is the Rizal Monument, a stone obelisk with bronze statuary erected near the site of Philippine national hero José Rizal's…

spots.name: Mount Arayat
spots.desc: A looming inactive volcano that also contains the largest stretch of forested jungle between the Zambales and Sierra Madre Mountains. The mountain is part of a protected reserve known as Mount Arayat National Park. However, access to the area is partially restricted due to rudimentary facilities and landslides that have disrupted the usual hiking trails.

spots.name: San Juanico Bridge
spots.desc: This spans the San Juanico Strait from Tacloban to Santa Rita on Samar Island. At 2.16 km long, it was the longest bridge spanning a body of seawater in the Philippines until the Cebu-Cordova bridge opened in 2022.

spots.name: Mount Isarog
spots.desc: A dormant volcano and a national park open for trekking and mountain biking. Rising 2,000 meters above sea level, this active stratovolcano features forests, waterfalls & hiking.

spots.name: Tabon Caves
spots.desc: The Tabon cave complex consists of 29 explored caves, but there are 200 caves known on Lipuun Point. They are maintained and managed by the National Museum. Diwata Cave and Liyang Cave are open to the public. The Caves were the discovery site of the Tabon Man, one of the oldest discoveries of human inhabitants found in the Philippines.

spots.name: Ongpin Street
spots.desc: is a home to many Chinese herbal stores, restaurants and groceries.

spots.name: Golden Dome Mosque
spots.desc: Quiapo is home to a large Muslim Community, this mosque was built in the 1970s in order of Imelda Marcos for the visit of former Libyan leader Muammar al-Gaddafi, although his visit was cancelled. It is the biggest mosque in Metro Manila and serves the large Muslim community of Quiapo.

spots.name: San Sebastian Church
spots.desc: Built in 1891, this striking Gothic church has steel vaulting, stained-glass windows & 2 towers.

spots.name: Smart Araneta Coliseum
spots.desc: Officially nicknamed the "Big Dome", this is a multi-purpose indoor arena built in the 1960s, and the centerpiece of Araneta Center. The "Thrilla in Manila" match between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier in 1975 was held here; it is also the main venue of Binibining Pilipinas pageants since the 1970s. The arena gets its present name from 2010 when telecommunications giant Smart Communications bought…

spots.name: Mount Makiling
spots.desc: A towering inactive volcano and prime hiking destination shared with the town of Los Baños in Laguna.

spots.name: Pagsanjan Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall with a height of around . The falls is administratively part of Cavinti, but is more accessible upstream from Pagsanjan town proper, hence the insistence of some in Cavinti to name the falls after their town. The trip heading there involves a scenic raft trip through the forested Pagsanjan Gorge along the Bumbungan River or a hike from the Cavinti side involving a climb up a 600-step…

spots.name: Basilica of Santo Niño
spots.desc: A large and venerable church that traces its history to the founding of the convent of the Santo Niño de Cebu in 1565. It contains a statue of the Santo Niño (Holy Child) that is regarded as the oldest religious relic in the Philippines. The statue was presented by Ferdinand Magellan to Queen Juana during the baptism of King Humabon and his wife Queen Juana on 14 April 1521. The natives of Cebu…

spots.name: Mount Iraya
spots.desc: The highest peak in Batanes, with a height of . It is a dormant volcano that is home to endemic species such as the Batanes pit viper. It also serves as a local weather instrument of sorts; clouds obscuring the peak mean that bad weather is expected all over Batan Island.

spots.name: Fort Drum
spots.desc: A heavily fortified sea fort, shaped like a battleship, built by the United States in 1909 as one of the harbor defenses at the wider South Channel entrance to the bay during the American colonial period. It was unique among forts built by the United States between the Civil War and early World War II, both as a sea fort and in having turrets. It was captured and occupied by the Japanese during…

spots.name: Babuyan Claro
spots.desc: The other active volcano in Babuyan Island, it is an massif that last erupted in 1924 and has two craters each measuring between .

spots.name: Mt. Talinis
spots.desc: The second-highest mountain in Negros Oriental at 1903 m, a dormant volcano, one of a group called the Cuernos de Negros (Horns of Negros). It has lakes, waterfalls and a mossy forest as well as a stream with sulfur vents. Local mountaineering groups frequent the mountain.

spots.name: Philippine Sports Stadium
spots.desc: Also part of Iglesia ni Cristo's Ciudad de Victoria complex. The stadium is mainly for football events. It also hosts a blue athletics track.

spots.name: Mount Cagua
spots.desc: The only active volcano in northern Luzon, it is a peak in the Sierra Madre mountains that last erupted in 1907 and has a wide caldera. It is home to hot springs, fumaroles and some endemic plant and animal species such as the cloud rat.

spots.name: Fort Santiago
spots.desc: The former military headquarters of the Spanish colonial government. Although the fort sustained very heavy damage during the 1945 Battle of Manila, several key portions of the compound were subsequently restored - including its iconic gate with a wooden relief featuring Santiago Matamoros (St. James the Moor-slayer), the patron saint of Spain. It is now considered a major landmark and one of…

spots.name: Bataan Nuclear Power Plant
spots.desc: The Philippines first and only nuclear power plant, which never operated (though plans to reactivate it remain). Can be visited by pre-arranged guided tour.
spots.addr: Governor J.J. Linao National Highway, Barangay Nagbalayong

spots.name: Hundred Islands National Park
spots.desc: An archipelago of 123 small, pristine isles, four of which have been developed for tourists. They can be reached via chartered excursion or boat ride from the Lucap wharf outside of Alaminos.

spots.name: BDO Virac Town Center Branch
spots.desc: Master Card/Visa Card ATM.

spots.name: Quiapo Church
spots.desc: Catholic church containing a revered 17th-century statue of Jesus called the Señor Jesus Nazareno.

spots.name: Mount Kitanglad Range Natural Park
spots.desc: Mt. Kitanglad Range Natural Park (MKRNP) is in Northern Mindanao of Philippines.

spots.name: Mavulis Island
spots.desc: The northern-most island in the Philippines, home to native vegetation, coconut crabs, and a garrison of the Philippine military that forms the only human population, albeit on a rotational basis.

spots.name: Camiguin de Babuyanes
spots.desc: An active volcano on the southern tip of Camiguin Island that last erupted in 1857.

spots.name: Fort San Pedro
spots.desc: The smallest Spanish outpost in the Philippines during the colonial era. It has a small museum showcasing the wreckage and treasures from the sunken San Diego galleon from Mexico. The area is scenic with the newly renovated and open-air Plaza Independencia at the entrance.

spots.name: Cebu Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: A church built in 1565 by the first Spanish missionaries in Cebu, seat of an Archbishop who has subordinate Bishops in many cities of the Visayas. It was mostly destroyed during World War II and had been rebuilt a bit differently. Behind the church is a cemetery where several prominent churchmen including Cardinal Rosales are buried.

spots.name: Mariveles Volcano
spots.desc: A dormant volcano with a wide caldera that comprises the southern part of Bataan. It has multiple peaks and ridges that are popular among climbers and hikers such as Mount Tarak.

spots.name: Manila North Cemetery
spots.desc: Manila's largest cemetery. Notable people buried includes Philippine presidents Sergio Osmeña, Manuel Roxas, and Ramon Magsaysay, and actor Fernando Poe Jr. (FPJ). Other landmarks inside is the Mausoleum of the Veterans of the Revolution, dedicated to Filipino revolutionaries who were killed during the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American war, and the Bautista-Nakpil pylon, an Art…

spots.name: Bataan National Park
spots.desc: A protected forest area covering Mount Natib, a dormant volcano with a wide caldera encompassing most of northern and central Bataan.

spots.name: Magellan's Cross
spots.desc: An octagonal building decorated with murals containing a large wooden cross that commemorates the Portuguese conquistador Ferdinand Magellan who planted a wooden cross upon converting the original inhabitants to Christianity. A plaque states that the visible wooden cross contains the original cross, but some historians say the original cross was reduced to firewood by local inhabitants when the…

spots.name: Angono-Binangonan Petroglyphs Site
spots.desc: The Angono Petroglyphs are the oldest known form of art in the Philippines. They consist of 127 human and animal figures engraved on a rock wall, likely carved before 2000 BC.

spots.name: Tubabao Island
spots.desc: Served as the former International Refugee Organization (IRO) campsite for 6,000 displaced White Russians from 1949-1952.

spots.name: Smith Volcano
spots.desc: An almost cylindrical active volcano with a height of that last erupted in 1917.

spots.name: Didicas Volcano
spots.desc: A small volcanic island with an elevation of that repeatedly erupted out of the ocean and sunk before definitively emerging into dry land since an eruption in 1952. It is the most active of the islands' volcanoes and there are tight restrictions on approaching the island, although some who have managed to step on its shores describe the ground as being hot enough to cook a fish on.

spots.name: Minor Basilica and Archdiocesan Shrine of Our Lady of the Assumption
spots.desc: Santa Maria's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in 1765. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 for its unique architecture and its dual purpose as a fortress built on a hilltop to defend the town against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea.

spots.name: Cultural Center of the Philippines
spots.desc: Straddling the boundary with Manila, this building complex showcases Filipino performing arts and culture. The area is also popular for jogging, and families often have picnics here, especially on weekends.

spots.name: Malolos Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in Bulacan, rebuilt in its original style following its burning by Filipino forces during the Philippine-American War. Some visitors confuse the cathedral with Barasoain Church, although President Emilio Aguinaldo did use the cathedral’s convent as his official residence during the First Republic.

spots.name: Bud Dajo
spots.desc: Volcanic cinder cone and the highest point in the province of Sulu. Site of a battle in 1906; see Mindanao#Understand.

spots.name: Marcelo Fernan Bridge
spots.desc: 1237 m long Cable-stayed bridge across Mactan Channel

spots.name: St. Paul's Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia and built by the Augustinians around 1790, this cathedral features a unique design intended to minimize earthquake damage, called "earthquake baroque". Look out for the brass communion handrails forged in China, complete with Chinese characters scrawled by its ancient installers (if you look closely). The eight-sided bell tower is just south of the…

spots.name: Magat Dam
spots.desc: Opened in 1983, it was deemed the largest dam in Southeast Asia at the time and created a reservoir that displaced numerous communities in neighboring Ifugao. Since then it is one of the main sources of irrigation and electricity in the Cagayan Valley Region. The complex and its surroundings have become a favorite recreation spot for residents as well as day-trippers from Santiago. Fishing…
spots.addr: Burgos-General Aguinaldo Road, Barangay General Aguinaldo, Ramon

spots.name: Antipolo Cathedral
spots.desc: A circular Catholic church rebuilt in 1949 following the destruction of its original Spanish colonial building during World War II. Its main draw is a 17th-century wooden statue of the Virgin Mary that attracts pilgrims. The cathedral is popular with travelers who are about to embark on far away trips and other well-wishers and devotees. The actual image is said to have come from Mexico and…
spots.addr: P. Oliveros Street, Barangay San Jose

spots.name: Clark Freeport and Special Economic Zone
Naga Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: The oldest cathedral in southern Luzon. It was built in 1573, and was inaugurated in 1575. It is the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Caceres.

spots.name: Barasoain Church
spots.desc: Erected in 1885, was the site of the very First Philippine Congress on September 15, 1898, and the inauguration of the First Philippine Republic on January 23, 1899. In this church the Oath of Office of Emilio Aguinaldo and Joseph Estrada as Philippine presidents took place. Within the premises of Barasoain Church, there are other historical markers installed by National Historical Commission…

spots.name: Mount Maculot
spots.desc: A dormant stratovolcano beside Taal Lake that rises about above the town. It is a sacred site to ancient Tagalog religion and some Christian pilgrims climb it as a penance.There are guided treks which take about two hours; up to 4 persons hike with a guide. Hiking Mount Maculot is suitable for beginners; the grade is not too steep, except near the summit, and there are rest stops at regular…

spots.name: Mount Batulao
spots.desc: This high inactive volcano is a must-visit for beginners. The scenic views and beautiful mountain range made the experience unforgettable. Highly recommended for those looking to start their hiking journey.

spots.name: Mount Sembrano
spots.desc: An extinct volcano at the head of the Jalajala peninsula that is frequented by hikers due to its proximity to Metro Manila and its commanding views of Laguna de Bay into Talim Island and as far as Mount Makiling, on the southwestern shores of the lake.

spots.name: Manila Ocean Park
spots.desc: Opened in 2008, this is Manila's first major oceanarium. Although not quite as large and well-equipped as some of Asia's more famous oceanaria (including those in Hong Kong and Singapore), it's still a popular attraction among locals and could be a very interesting diversion for families with children. The centrepiece is the Living Ocean exhibit with large aquariums and an underwater acrylic…
spots.hours: 10AM to 8PM on weekdays (last entry 7:15PM), 9AM to 8PM on weekends and public holidays (last entry 8:15PM)

spots.name: Mount Tapulao
spots.desc: At , it is the highest mountain in the Zambales Mountain Range and Zambales province in general. The summit offers views ranging up to Lingayen Gulf in Pangasinan to the north and San Antonio in the southern end of Zambales.

spots.name: Taluksangay Mosque
spots.desc: This colorful mosque is in the barrio of Taluksangay outside the city center.

spots.name: Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park
spots.desc: An extensive protected area covering a large swathe of the Sierra Madre Mountains from the boundary with Cagayan to San Mariano town. Home to the indigenous Agta/Dumagat tribes, endemic species such as the Philippine crocodile, the Philippine eagle, the Isabela oriole, pitcher plants and virgin forests, in addition to peaks that have never been named or climbed by humans.

spots.name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: The historical Roman Catholic church at the downtown, it has a Baroque façade and interior, and houses both the images of the Infant Jesus (Santo Niño) and the Immaculate Conception.

spots.name: Hinulugang Taktak National Park
spots.desc: National park known for its soaring waterfall in a serene, natural setting, plus hanging bridges.
spots.addr: Daang Bakal Road, Barangay Dela Paz

spots.name: Coconut Palace
spots.desc: Coconut lumber & shells were used for this octagonal government building & some of its furniture.
spots.addr: F. Ma Guerrero Street, PICC Complex

spots.name: Balanga Cathedral
spots.desc: The headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church in Bataan and seat of the Diocese of Balanga. Built in 1793, this church was used as an artillery embattlement by the Filipinos during the Battle of Bataan. The cathedral was declared a National Historical Site in 1940.

spots.name: Mount Bongao
spots.desc: Hike

spots.name: Caliraya Lake
spots.desc: A man-made reservoir created in 1939 following the damming of the Caliraya river. A favorite spot for watersports, fishing and camping activities, with an increasing number of Metro Manilans setting up retirement homes along the shore. The lake is shared by the municipalities of Cavinti, Kalayaan and Lumban.

spots.name: Tayabas Basilica
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church designed in a key-like shape. Its nave measures more than in length. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.
spots.addr: Apolinario de la Cruz Street, San Roque Zone 1

spots.name: Pantabangan Dam
spots.desc: One of the largest dams in the country, it is a high structure with a length of holding back of water from the upper reaches of the Pampanga River, sustained by the Pantabangan–Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve that covers the Caraballo mountain range in the towns of Pantabangan and Carranglan in Nueva Ecija, and Aritao, Dupax del Sur and Alfonso Castañeda in Nueva Vizcaya. There is a viewdeck…

spots.name: New Clark City Athletics Stadium
spots.desc: Among the modern sports facilities in the Philippines, the stadium which hosted the 2019 Southeast Asian Games. Its architectural design is inspired from the Mount Pinatubo volcano.

spots.name: Lake Balanan
spots.desc: This is a scenic mountain lake in a protected wildlife area, in Siaton Municipality a few km inland from the town.

spots.name: Tondo Church
spots.desc: One of the most visited churches in the Philippines, it dates back to 1572, and houses an image of the Infant Jesus that was brought from Acapulco in Mexico.

spots.name: Honda Bay
spots.desc: Consisting of several islets with beautiful beaches, Honda Bay is the place to go to for swimming, snorkeling as well as beach and island hopping. Accessible via the Sta. Lourdes wharf which is 25 minutes away from the city. Pumpboats at the wharf can be hired to take visitors to the various islets on the bay. Arrive before 11AM to go island hopping if you require a small boat (1-5 people) and…

spots.name: Ayala Museum
spots.desc: Showcases the rich and vivid history of the Philippines from the earliest times of the Mactan battle to the struggle of democracy in EDSA. Also present are some famous paintings by Filipino painters such as Fernando Amorsolo, Juan Luna and Fernando Zobel. Guided tours are available if booked in advance for large groups.

spots.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: Founded in 1810 as a parish at the present day Universidad de Zamboanga campus, the Cathedral is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Zamboanga (created in 1910 as diocese and elevated in 1958 as an archdiocese). It is known as one of the most modern cathedrals in Mindanao, built in 1998-2001. The cathedral's structure is cruciform, resembling a cross and its facade is patterned after a…

spots.name: SM City Bacoor
spots.addr: Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo Highway corner Tirona Highway

spots.name: Cagsawa Ruins
spots.desc: The picturesque ruins of an old parish church on what was the town of Cagsawa. The original church was built in 1587 until it was burned down by Dutch pirates in 1636. A new church was again built in 1724 until it was destroyed by the devastating 1814 eruption of Mayon.

spots.name: Minor Basilica of Our Lady of Piat
spots.desc: The main landmark and destination in Piat, it was established by the Spanish on a hilltop in the early 17th century, but has been drastically altered, rebuilt and expanded over the centuries to accommodate the increasing throng of pilgrims seeking blessings from the Our Lady of the Visitation of Piat, a 17th-century darkwood sculpture of the Virgin Mary that was imported from Macau and is…
spots.addr: Our Lady of Piat Avenue, Poblacion I

spots.name: Mary Mediatrix of All Grace Parish
spots.local: María, Tagapamagitan ng Lahat ng Biyaya
spots.desc: Church and monastery complex, site of the 1947 Marian apparitions that was not recognized by the Vatican, which has not discouraged a faithful following in Batangas and is supported by the Archdiocese of Lipa, which continues to gather evidence of the apparitions in the hopes of persuading the Holy See to reconsider.
spots.addr: Lipa-Padre Garcia Road, Antipolo del Norte

spots.name: Aguinaldo Shrine
spots.desc: The sprawling house, built in 1849, is the ancestral home of Emilio Aguinaldo, the first President of the Philippines. It is now a museum. It is where independence from Spain was declared on June 12, 1898. The house’s balcony is where the Philippine president annually raises the Philippine flag on Independence Day.The basement has an exhibition dedicated to Aguinaldo’s life and role in the…

spots.name: University of the Philippines, Los Baños
spots.desc: Primarily a university of agriculture. There are some places of interest within its administered area:.

spots.name: Mount San Cristobal
spots.desc: A towering inactive volcano east of San Pablo, along the boundary with Quezon province. Situated alongside Mount Banahaw, a religious pilgrimage site, it is said to be the mountain's "evil twin", having been dubbed the "Devil's Mountain" for malevolent entities said to inhabit its slopes.

spots.name: Angat Dam
spots.desc: Built in the 1960s, it is the largest of the three dams along the Angat River system and is the highlight of the Angat Forest Watershed. While access to the dam itself is restricted, the complex provides wide views of the Sierra Madre mountains.

spots.name: Cape Bojeador Lighthouse
spots.desc: A cultural heritage structure in Burgos established during Spanish colonial times. The lighthouse was first lit on March 30, 1892.

spots.name: Minor Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary of Manaoag
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church that has continuously been significantly expanded and altered over the centuries to accommodate the increasing horde of worshippers wishing to see Our Lady of Manaoag. At the back of the main building are stores selling snacks, and a side-chapel allowing visitors to see the back of the statue up close. There is an extensive candle-lighting area and a small museum featuring…

spots.name: Pescador Island
spots.desc: An island with abundant marine life (pescador is Spanish for fisherman) about 3 km (1.9 miles) off the coast. This is the most common destination for dive trips from Moalboal. The structure of the reef that follows the entire coastline has made the place ideal for scuba-diving, snorkeling and freediving. Divers can enjoy easy access to the reef since the drop off is shallow and close to shore but…

spots.name: Bangan Hill National Park
spots.desc: A historical landmark, it is the location of an annual "Stations of the Cross" held during the Lenten season, with live actors portraying Jesus' suffering, death, and resurrection. Aside from that, it is also visited by hikers, and the hilltop provides a wide view of the surrounding area and the Caraballo and the Cordilleras.

spots.name: MacArthur Landing Memorial National Park
spots.desc: A protected area that commemorates the historic landing of U.S. General Douglas MacArthur at the start of the campaign to recapture and liberate the Philippines from Japanese occupation on 20 October 1944.

spots.name: Mount Guiwan
spots.desc: A high peak believed to be the highest in the Sierra Madre.

spots.name: Escolta Street
spots.desc: See the old art deco style buildings in Escolta Street, this used to be the home of many luxurious fashion brands and slowly declined in the 1970s after the growth of malls.

spots.name: Santo Domingo Church
spots.desc: Large, contemporary Catholic church, with a shrine to the Virgin Mary & an adjacent cemetery.
spots.addr: #537 Quezon Avenue corner Santo Domingo street

spots.name: San Pedro Bautista
spots.desc: One of the oldest churches in the country, housing the bones of the patron saint. There is also a catacomb in the basement of the church where the friars of the past were buried.

spots.name: Mount Santo Tomas
spots.desc: An inactive volcano with a height of . It has some geothermal features and has multiple telecommunications antennas on its summit.

spots.name: Colon St
spots.desc: Brave the cacophonous traffic to see the oldest street in the Philippines with some nice worn-out classical buildings dating back to the American Era. At night, this street transforms into a market with good buys everywhere. Be wary of pickpockets though.

spots.name: The Chinese Taoist Temple
spots.desc: There are many people of Chinese ancestry in Cebu, and several Chinese temples; one is the Taoist Temple. From there you can see a nice view of the city because it is on a hill.

spots.name: Cebu Provincial Museum
spots.desc: The museum is housed in the former Cebu Provincial Detention and Rehabilitation Center, which was once the Carcel de Cebu. Its four Spanish-era buildings made of coral stone contain artifacts relating to the history of Cebu.

spots.name: San Sebastian Cathedral
spots.desc: Bacolod’s main Catholic church, begun in the late 19th century and completed in 1894. Built of coral stone and later covered with cement, it is one of the city’s key landmarks. The cathedral is also known for its Centennial Bells and the nearby Palacio Episcopal.

spots.name: Jaro Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: One of the most significant religious sites in the Visayas. It houses the miraculous image of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria (Our Lady of the Candles), the only Marian image in the Philippines crowned by a pope and Vatican decree, Pope John Paul II in 1981. Across the street stands the iconic Jaro Belfry, which was originally a watchtower before being converted into a bell tower.

spots.name: MassKara Festival
spots.desc: A big annual Mardi Gras-like parade event celebrated every 3rd week of October. Each of the city's barangays (districts) joins the fierce competition for the best-costumed groups, best in choreography, and many others. Lots of food and handicraft stalls, street dancing and an Oktoberfest-like event at the Bacolod Plaza area making the city for a span of a week, a city that never sleeps!…

spots.name: Verde Island
spots.desc: An island which gives its name to the eponymous strait separating Batangas and Mindoro. In contrast to the mainland, this is a mostly unspoiled ecotourism destination and base to explore the marine biodiversity of the waterway.

spots.name: Baclaran Church
spots.desc: This Modernist Romanesque Catholic church completed in 1958 is an important landmark for Baclaran, and provides a serene atmosphere away from the area's gritty side. Every Wednesday, devotees to the Our Lady of Perpetual Help and the international Redemptorist movement flock this church to pray.

spots.name: Parañaque Cathedral
spots.desc: The original church was founded 1580, but were torn down in preparation of the invasion of the Chinese pirate Koxinga. The present cathedral was rebuilt somewhere in the 18th century.

spots.name: Basco Lighthouse
spots.desc: Spiral stairs wind upwards to a 5th-floor deck, popular for its panoramic hill, sea & sunset views.

spots.name: Basco Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Batanes, built during the Spanish era in 1812.

spots.name: Sts. Peter and Paul Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao. The church with the belfry is the biggest Spanish colonial church in Cagayan Valley built by the Dominicans. It was constructed from 1761 to 1767 under the supervision of Fr. Antonio Lobato, OP. The cathedral suffered massive destruction in World War II losing its pipe organ, three wooden retablos, pulpit, wooden choir loft and the painted wooden ceiling…

spots.name: Sangley Point
spots.desc: A former United States Navy station that was turned over to the Philippine Navy and Philippine Air Force. It houses the Danilo Atienza Air Base and Naval Base Cavite; visitors must register first before entering. It is also the site of the future Sangley Point Airport (see #Get in).

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Cathedral Parish of Our Lady of the Pillar
spots.desc: Built during the Spanish era, it is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic church in Cavite and houses a venerated image of the Virgin Mary that is regarded as the most sacred in Cavite. Around the plaza are a few surviving colonial era structures such as the old municipal building and the ancestral residence of Daniel Tirona, whose fierce criticism of Andres Bonifacio during the Philippine…
spots.addr: Imus Plaza, General Castañeda Street, Poblacion III-A

spots.name: Museo ni Jose Rizal
spots.desc: The birthplace of the Philippine national hero, Jose Rizal. It houses the restored colonial-era mansion of Jose Rizal, which contains his memorabilia.
spots.addr: Francisco Mercado corner Jose Rizal Streets, Poblacion 6

spots.name: Sinking Belltower
spots.desc: Part of Laoag Cathedral. Named so because it slowly sinks into the soft soil of the city. A decade ago, the entrance was still tall enough to let a man on horseback enter. Now not even a man could enter.

spots.name: Metropolitan Cathedral Parish of St. John the Evangelist
spots.desc: Dagupan's main Roman Catholic church and one of two seats of the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan. Its modernist structure dates from the 20th century, when it replaced the Spanish-era church building at the back of the compound after it was heavily damaged in the 1990 Luzon earthquake.

spots.name: Lingayen Cathedral
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church that serves as one of two seats of the Archdiocese of Lingayen-Dagupan,.

spots.name: Cebu-Cordova Link Espressway
spots.desc: The longest bridge in Philippines, with toll, running from Cebu City to Córdova (the southern part of Mactan).

spots.name: San Diego Pro-Cathedral
spots.desc: The only pro-Cathedral church outside Metro Manila, its birth was in the 1700s, the church was still made of nipa-palm, bamboo and grass, in the 1800s the church was then made into a wood and stone structure, finally in the 1900s the structure was made into what it is now, the architecture; Lucio Bernasconi (an Italian architect) took churches in his native Italy as an influence and model of the…

spots.name: Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park
spots.desc: A large protected forest area centered on two volcanic crater lakes. The flora and fauna have been considerably degraded, but it's still an interesting daytrip.

spots.name: Sergio Osmeña Bridge
spots.desc: 864 m long truss bridge across the Mactan Channel

spots.name: San Sebastian Cathedral de Lipa
spots.desc: A reconstruction of a 19th century church that was bombed out in World War II, serving as the seat of the Archdiocese of Lipa. It has a narrower nave and higher ceiling than most churches. Its highlights are the cupola, the high altar and the ceiling frescoes loosely based on the Sistine Chapel.
spots.addr: C.M. Recto Avenue corner G. Solis Street

spots.name: Taal Basilica
spots.desc: A fine old church built in Spanish times to replace the one in San Nicolas that was destroyed by a volcanic eruption. The front has a neoclassical facade with lots of columns; the back of the building has high windowless stone walls and looks more like a medieval European fortress than a church. A sign in front of it says it is the largest Catholic church in Asia.

spots.name: Quezon Protected Landscape
spots.desc: It is a protected landscape on the southern end of the mighty Sierra Madre range, which straddles the boundary with Pagbilao. It was founded in 1934 as a national park until it was elevated into a protected area in 2003. It covers 938 of tropical rainforests, home to endemic species of birds, reptiles, mammals, and trees. Inside the park is Mount Pinagbanderahan, where a Philippine revolutionary…

spots.name: Mount Malepunyo
spots.desc: A towering massif west of Tiaong that separates the town from Batangas province.

spots.name: Mount Tagapo
spots.desc: The highest point in Talim Island, with an elevation of , and a popular hiking spot for daytrippers from Metro Manila.

spots.name: Avilon Zoo
spots.desc: The largest zoo in the Philippines in terms of land area and collection of animals.
spots.price: ₱800, concessions for children, elderly and disabled

spots.name: Angat Watershed Forest Reserve
spots.desc: A popular birdwatching site and a biodiversity hotspot containing most of the remaining closed-canopy forests in Central Luzon. The site also covers parts of the city of San Jose del Monte, and the towns of Norzagaray, Angat, San Rafael, and San Miguel, as well as parts of Rizal, Quezon, Aurora and Nueva Ecija provinces.

spots.name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
spots.desc: A sprawling national park that also covers parts of the neighboring towns of San Miguel and San Ildefonso. Famous as the site of the Biak-na-Bato Republic, a proto-state founded by Filipino separatists during the Philippine Revolution against Spain in 1897, it also contains caves, rivers and forested highlands of the Sierra Madre that belie the misconception of Bulacan as a largely flat province.

spots.name: Masjid Shiekh Karimul Makhdum
spots.desc: The Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque building dates from the 1960s. Four old mosque pillars found within the mosque are from the 17th century. According to local lore, the original mosque, built in the indigenous sacred Moro pagoda architectural style, was established in 1380, making it the oldest mosque in the Philippines and in Southeast Asia.

spots.name: Palo Cathedral
spots.desc: This Roman Catholic cathedral was built in 1596 by the Jesuits. It served as a military hospital during World War II, and in 2013, was badly damaged by Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda). Palo Cathedral also hosted Pope Francis' visit to the Philippines, also dedicated to the victims of Typhoon Haiyan.
spots.addr: San Salvador Street corner F. Sevilla Street

spots.name: Ivuhos
spots.desc: A large grass-covered island west of Sabtang inhabited only by free-roaming cows and goats.

spots.name: Museo Pambata
spots.desc: This museum is geared towards keeping children entertained (and informed) through educational hands-on exhibits and special activities. Themed galleries cover a variety of subjects ranging from history to science to art. Don't put a short leash on the kids here: they're expected to touch and play with most of the stuff on show. Admission 100 adults/children. Streetchildren, infants (under 2…
spots.hours: Tue-Sat 8AM to 5PM (Aug-Mar), 9AM to 5PM (Apr-Jul); Sun 1-5PM; closed Mon and holidays

spots.name: Manila Chinese Cemetery
spots.local: Libingan ng mga Tsino sa Maynila
spots.desc: The second oldest cemetery in Manila after La Loma Cemetery and was designated as the resting place for the Chinese citizens who were denied burial in Catholic cemeteries during the Spanish colonial period.

spots.name: SM North EDSA
spots.desc: The second largest mall in the Philippines, one of the world's largest malls, and the first mall of the nationwide SM Supermalls chain, SM North EDSA houses almost 1000 retail stores, services and restaurants within the mall's premises. It was the largest mall in the Philippines from 2008-2011 and 2015-2021.

spots.name: Capones Island
spots.desc: A picturesque island with white sand beaches, stunning views of the mainland mountains and an equally picturesque lighthouse.

spots.name: Basilica Minore of Our Lady of Charity
spots.desc: Agoo's main Roman Catholic church, destroyed multiple times by earthquakes and rebuilt in its present state in 1975. Its main draw is the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Charity. It also has an ecclesiastical museum.
spots.addr: Manila North Road corner Grotto Road, Consolacion

spots.name: Saint Augustine Metropolitan Cathedral
spots.desc: A Gothic-inspired cathedral and is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Cagayan de Oro, since it houses the cathedra (seat) of the Archbishop of Cagayan de Oro. The present-day cathedral was constructed in 1946, after being destroyed during World War II. Inside the cathedral are centuries-old stained glass windows, while outside its main entrance is a wooden cross from 1888, erected by…

spots.name: Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Particularly scenic at night, is by far the largest provincial capitol building anywhere in the entire archipelago. It was built during the American era, and the design is a miniature of the White House.

spots.name: Carbon Market
spots.desc: The largest farmers' market in the city — both a shopping area and a tourist attraction.

spots.name: SM City Cebu
spots.desc: Northeast of downtown. Has a large supermarket.

spots.name: Buntun Bridge
spots.desc: One of the longest bridges in the country at . It is from the city proper and offers an unobstructed view of the Cagayan River. It connects Tuguegarao with western Cagayan, Kalinga, Apayao and western Isabela.

spots.name: Fort San Felipe
spots.desc: Built in 1609, it served as the fortress for the then town of Cavite, but only half of it remains. As an active naval base, permission is required to visit this fort.

spots.name: Lucena City Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Lucena, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1882.

spots.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando
spots.desc: A Neoclassical church that serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Fernando. Originally a wooden church with a thatch roof built in 1754, it was burned by the Filipino revolutionaries under General Antonio Luna, and a Neoclassical church building was built on its place during the American era. It was again burned in 1939, and restored by the Kapampangan architect Fernando…
spots.addr: Consunji St. cor. Gen. Hizon Ave, Santo Rosario

spots.name: Tarlac Cathedral
spots.desc: A Neo-Gothic style Catholic church, rebuilt from one destroyed during World War II. It was built in the late 17th century by the Augustinians, while the present buildings date from late 1940s onwards.

spots.name: Cathedral of St. William the Hermit
spots.desc: The headquarters of the Roman Catholic church in La Union is housed in a Baroque building built during the Spanish era in the 19th century.

spots.name: Plaza de Roma
spots.desc: Bounded by the Manila Cathedral to the southeast, the Palacio del Gobernador to the southwest and the Ayuntamiento to the northeast, this small plot of land is Intramuros' very own plaza mayor (main square). At the centre of the plaza stands a monument to King Carlos IV of Spain, cast in 1808 and erected in 1824 by a colonial government grateful for his having dispatched a shipment of smallpox…
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Andres Soriano (Aduana)

spots.name: Casa Manila
spots.desc: A recreation of a typical upper-class colonial Intramuros home. The interiors are filled with antique furniture, artwork, and other artifacts from the Spanish era, all carefully arranged to illustrate what life was like for wealthy families of that period. 75, 50 students/children.
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Real

spots.name: Cebu International Convention Center
spots.desc: Media center, large plenary hall, exhibition hall and several meeting rooms.

spots.name: Ilagan Sanctuary
spots.desc: national park. Activities include hiking, mountaineering, spelunking and birdwatching.

spots.name: Hacienda Luisita
spots.desc: A 6,435 sugarcane plantation that is the center of landmark decisions on land reform in the Philippines. Straddling the boundaries of the nearby municipalities of La Paz and Concepcion, It used to be a Spanish-owned tobacco plantation until it was turned over to the Filipino-Chinese Cojuangco family (the family of Corazon "Cory" Aquino). An operational azucarera (sugar factory) inside the…

spots.name: Bahay Tsinoy
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the history and contributions of the Chinese-Filipino community. 100, 60 students/children.

spots.name: Old Daet Cathedral
spots.desc: Built by the Franciscan friars in 1611, it is one of the oldest churches in Camarines Norte.
spots.hours: Masses Mon-Fri 6AM, noon, 5:15PM; Sat 6AM, 5:15PM; Sun 5AM, 6:30AM, 8AM, 9:30AM, 3PM (Children's Mass), 4:30PM, 6PM…

spots.name: Cathedral of the Most Holy Trinity
spots.desc: It is a prominent Latin Rite Roman Catholic cathedral. It was erected in 1984 after the Diocese of Daet was created by a Papal Bull in May 27, 1974.

spots.name: Magapit Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: Asia's first suspension bridge, built in 1978. It spans the Cagayan River at Lallo and is long. The hanging bridge links Cagayan and the Ilocos Region by the scenic Patapat Road.

spots.name: Cape Engaño Lighthouse
spots.desc: A Spanish-era lighthouse built on top of a high hill. This was also a filming site for the American reality TV series Survivor. From the complex, multiple islands can be viewed on a clear day, such as Dos Hermanos Island, Didicas Volcano and Camiguin de Babuyanes Island. All visitors must register at Engaño Cove and be accompanied by an accredited tour guide.

spots.name: Tumauini Church
spots.desc: One of the oldest churches in Isabela and a designated national treasure. It contains the only cylindrical bell tower in the Philippines. Its striking red brick facade has intricate carvings and symbols, including an inscription of its construction date of 1784. The church is being nominated for inclusion as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Bayombong Cathedral
spots.desc: Bayombong’s main Roman Catholic Church and the seat of its eponymous diocese. Built during the Spanish era, it was razed by fire twice and lost its belltower in the 1990 Luzon earthquake. With subsequent rebuilding, it is now approximately twice its original size. The cathedral maintains its original Baroque façade, which is similar to other colonials churches in Nueva Vizcaya except that its…
spots.addr: Dela Cruz Street, Don Tomas Maddela

spots.name: Fortune Island
spots.desc: The island is owned by José Antonio Leviste, a former governor of Batangas. Leviste opened the Resort Club on the island in 1995. It was a bad investment (also due to lack of fresh water on the island). In the end the idea of the resort was abandoned. What has left are remnants of the beach cabanas, swimming pool and an acropolis with Grecian pillars and statues on the edge of the island…

spots.name: Lake Sampaloc
spots.desc: The largest of San Pablo's seven lakes, of volcanic origin. Around the lake are Dagatan Boulevard, a lakefront park, floating cottages, and various civic monuments such as that of a giant tilapia fish.

spots.name: Saint Paul the First Hermit Cathedral
spots.desc: An adobe Romanesque Roman Catholic cathedral that forms the center of San Pablo and serves as the seat of the namesake Roman Catholic Diocese of San Pablo which oversees the entirety of Laguna. Built in 1714, it was damaged during World War II, and its façade been restored to its original. Its dome is a landmark of the city.

spots.name: Villa Escudero
spots.desc: Tiaong's main draw is a sprawling family-owned agricultural estate that began in 1872 as a sugarcane plantation before switching to coconuts following a blight. The hacienda was opened as a resort showcasing rural life in 1981 and features a myriad of amenities such as a museum showcasing the landowners' art collection, a reconstructed Spanish-style chapel and ancestral houses, as well as a…

spots.name: Minor Basilica and Parish of Saint John the Baptist
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church that was built on a hilltop, it was significantly expanded in the 1970s and structurally resembles a carton box. The facade, belltower, altar and colored windows are the building's main attractions, while the well-manicured grounds contain a museum, chapels, the Spanish-era bells, and a driveway lined with statues of the Twelve Apostles.
spots.addr: J. Sumulong St., Brgy. San Isidro

spots.name: Minor Basilica and Shrine Parish of Our Lady of the Rosary of Orani
spots.desc: Orani's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Baroque style following the 1938 fire. Since 2019, it is the only basilica in Bataan and houses a venerated Marian image of the Our Lady of the Rosary, also known locally as Our Lady of Orani.

spots.name: Obando Church
spots.desc: Obando's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Spanish-era design following World War II destruction. Unlike most churches, it is dedicated to three patron saints, namely St. Pascual Baylon, St. Claire of Assisi and the indigenous Our Lady of Salambao.The Obando Fertility Rites are performed on Sundays following the 8AM Mass and the feast day of Our Lady of Salambao on May 19.…

spots.name: Bangui Wind Farm
spots.desc: Constructed in 2003 and opened in 2005, this is the first wind farm in the Philippines. Even after the Burgos and Caparispisan wind farms were completed, the Bangui wind farms remain the main tourist attraction in its region.

spots.name: Marcos Museum and Mausoleum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to President Marcos and his achievements, but avoids its excesses. It also used to house the president's preserved remains inside an airconditioned separate mausoleum building, although doubts persisted on whether the wax-looking cadaver on display was the real thing until he was reburied in Metro Manila in 2016, revealing the displayed corpse to be a fake. The dummy remains on…

spots.name: Burgos Wind Farm
spots.desc: The largest wind farm in the Philippines. It is operated by the EDC Burgos Wind Power Corporation.

spots.name: Paoay Lake
spots.desc: A natural lake with no connecting rivers said by folklore to be the site of a sunken community. It has been a national park since 1969.

spots.name: Cathedral Parish of St. Joseph the Patriarch
spots.desc: The first church was built in 1770, but it was rebuilt a few times after being burned to where current church dates to about 1893. It is the seat of the Roman Catholic church in western Pangasinan. Also try People's Park adjacent if you need to stretch your legs.

spots.name: Capul Island Lighthouse
spots.desc: A historic lighthouse on Titoog Point in San Luis on the northern tip of Capul Island. Built in 1896.

spots.name: Northern Luzon Heroes Hill National Park
spots.desc: A ridge that is popular among hikers and motorists for the dramatic coastal views along Manila North Road. While most of the park is located in Santa, its southern tip lies at Barangay Sulvec in Narvacan.

spots.name: Manila Central Post Office Building
spots.desc: Never mind the ill-conceived pink and yellow paint job - this grand Neoclassical structure from the 1920s is a fine exemplar of the massive government buildings that were erected in this part of Manila during the American colonial period. It is the headquarters of the Philippine Postal Corporation (PhilPost). The structure experienced a massive fire last May 2023.

spots.name: Parish of the Holy Sacrifice
spots.desc: Chapel inside the University of the Philippines Diliman campus with distinctive architecture designed by Leandro Locsin, and hosting works from five National Artists. Designated a National Historical Landmark since 2005

spots.name: Bantayog Memorial Center
spots.desc: Monument dedicated to the people who died during the Marcos dictatorship.

spots.name: ABS-CBN Broadcasting Center
spots.desc: The flagship studio of the ABS-CBN media network, built in 1968 and is the Philippines' most advanced broadcasting center.
spots.addr: Eugenio Lopez Jr. Drive, South Triangle

spots.name: EDSA Shrine
spots.desc: Opened in 1989, it is a chapel and monument designed by renowned Filipino architect Francisco Mañosa also commemorating the 1986 revolution

spots.name: People Power Monument
spots.desc: A monument that commemorates the events in the People Power Revolution in 1986.

spots.name: Salinas Natural Monument
spots.desc: The remains of a natural salt spring that stopped producing salt and whose rocks turned from white to gray following the 1990 Luzon earthquake. Despite this, it has managed to maintain its natural settings and is also a wildlife refuge.

spots.name: Bird watching at Candaba Swamp
spots.desc: The best time to go bird watching is on the early morning, around five to seven in the morning when bird activity is at its peak and the heat is not intense. Late afternoons are also a good time for this. Must brings are hiking footwear and clothes, and a good pair of binoculars or telescope. The avid birdwatcher might also want to bring his or her field notebook, pencil and camera. Expect to pay…

spots.name: Bonifacio Monument
spots.desc: This famous landmark of the city is located at the intersection of EDSA, Rizal Avenue, Mc Arthur Highway, and Samson Road. Made by National Artist Guillermo Tolentino, the monument commemorates the first encounter of the revolutionary group Katipunan, lead by hero Andres Bonifacio, with Spanish forces.

spots.name: SM Seaside
spots.desc: A huge mall with a large department store, bowling center, movie theaters, Olympic-size ice skating rink, and 447 shops and restaurants.

spots.name: Bacolod Public Plaza
spots.desc: The Bacolod version of Central park but smaller; fountains are scattered around the plaza and a gazebo stands in the middle. The Unknown Soldiers Monument (also known as Theodore Vinther Monument) is found here. The plaza is used for events like the MassKara Festival and for activities such as Arnis (Filipino martial arts). It is also a hub for joggers and people doing aerobics during the morning.

spots.name: Lion's Head
spots.desc: Limestone sculpture of a lion by the Baguio chapter of the Lions Club. It is carved by Ifugao artist Anselmo Bayang Day-ag and is considered as the Baguio's "entrance marker" for tourists coming from south of the city.

spots.name: St. Gregory the Great Cathedral
spots.desc: The episcopal seat of the Diocese of Legazpi, it was first built by Spanish missionaries as a wooden chapel in 1581. The present church, designed by then governor Don Jose Ma. de Peñaranda, was built in 1839 using volcanic rocks.

spots.name: Ligñon Hill
spots.desc: Pronounced leeng-YAWN, it is a 156 m peak with a nature park at its summit offering panoramic views of the city and Mayon Volcano, and adventure activities like ziplining.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora dela Annunciata Parish Church
spots.desc: An 18th-century church that was built by the Spanish as a missionary outpost to convert the indigenous Dumagat residents.
spots.addr: Boso Boso Road, Sitio Old Boso Boso, Barangay San Jose

spots.name: Fort Stotsenburg
spots.desc: The former headquarters of American cavalry divisions sent to the Philippines during the Philippine-American War. Destroyed in World War II, only its gateposts remains.

spots.name: Manila Memorial Park
spots.desc: Founded in 1964, it is the first cemetery in the Philippines to open to cremations after the Catholic ban was lifted. Among the most notable buried here are Ninoy Aquino, who was assassinated in 1983 upon arrival at Manila International Airport, which was eventually renamed in his honor, Corazon Aquino, the first female president of the Philippines and also of Asia, who died in 2009 due to colon…

spots.name: Star City
spots.desc: The only indoor, air-conditioned amusement park in the Philippines, with over 30 attractions and rides including rollercoasters such as the Star Flyer - the first inverted coaster in the Philippines. Plus, enjoy the country's largest permanent ice entertainment area, Snow World. Within the amusement park complex, you can also find the Aliw and Star Theatres.
spots.price: Ride pass + Snow World = 859; Ride pass only = 699
spots.addr: Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex

spots.name: Solaire Resort & Casino
spots.desc: Opened in 2013 as the first resort and casino constructed in Entertainment City. Solaire Resort and Casino houses 5-star hotels and a casino, as well as a theater and other entertainment facilities.

spots.name: Sacred Mountain National Park
spots.desc: Do hiking and birdwatching at the national park. The 94-hectare (230-acre) national park and protected area was established on August 5, 1965 by Republic Act no. 4190. The park is dominated by Mount Mupo, a 900-foot (270 m) tall extinct volcanic cone. See the small pond featured at the volcano's summit.

spots.name: Our Lady of Peñafrancia Shrine
spots.desc: The original home of Our Lady of Peñafrancia for two centuries. The church was constructed in 1711, as a gift by Rev. Miguel Robles de Covarrubias, the man that brought the devotion of Ina to the Bicol Region. Peñafrancia Shrine, as called by locals, marks the starting point of the Traslacion, or the transfer of the Image of Ina from the Peñafrancia Shrine to the Naga Metropolitan Cathedral.

spots.name: Holy Rosary Minor Seminary and Museum
spots.desc: Oldest seminary in the Bicol Region, it houses the old paraphernalia, and items used by the old Catholic Church, including the documents of Our Lady of Peñafrancia’s verified devotion, and coronation. The Holy Rosary Minor Seminary was built during the time of Bishop Francisco Gainza. It is historical building. Most of its students became the pillars of the Church heirarchy as well as civic…

spots.name: Callao Cave
spots.desc: This 7-chamber limestone show cave features a chapel & numerous rock formations.

spots.name: Cabanatuan Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in central and southern Nueva Ecija, built in its present form following a major fire in the 1970s. Its convent was where General Antonio Luna and his aide were assassinated in 1899.

spots.name: Iba Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in Zambales, built during the Spanish era in the 18th century.
spots.addr: Olongapo-Bugallon Road corner Lesaca Street, Zone 5 Poblacion (Bano)

spots.name: Benguet State University
spots.desc: Educational tours are available for tourists at the regional agricultural university. Tourists can learn about organic farming through tours in the university's demonstration farms and gardens as well as shop for souvenirs

spots.name: Ayuntamiento
spots.desc: Completely rebuilt in 1884 after the disastrous earthquake of 1863, the seat of Manila's colonial-era city council once had some of the grandest interiors in Intramuros. The 1945 Battle of Manila left it a gutted shell, of which only parts of the first storey survived; it then suffered the indignity of serving as a parking lot. A major reconstruction project that started a few years ago is…

spots.name: Cathedral of Santa Catalina
spots.desc: A fine old Roman Catholic church, built under Spanish rule in the 1700s and consequently the oldest stone church in the whole of the province of Negros Oriental. It's dedicated to Saint Catherine of Alexandria who is the patron saint of the city. Her festival is vigorously celebrated around the end of November each year since a Mass celebrating liberation from the Spanish took place in its…

spots.name: Thirteen Martyrs Monument
spots.desc: The thirteen Martyrs of Cavite were Filipino patriots executed by musketry on September 12, 1896, for cooperating with the Katipunan during the Philippine Revolution against Spain. The capital city of Trece Martires in Cavite is named after them. In 1906, a monument to the Thirteen Martyrs was erected at the San Roque district of Cavite City, at the head of then San Roque causeway. Their families…
spots.addr: At the intersection of M. Valentin Street, Lopez Jaena Road, Zulueta Road and P. Burgos Avenue

spots.name: The Plaza
spots.desc: A park built to commemorate Rizal's 150th birthday. Opened in 2011, it houses a statue of Jose Rizal.

spots.name: Cathedral of Saint Michael
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Ilagan, built in 2000. It formally replaced a Spanish-era building in neighboring Ilagan that reverted to being Ilagan's parish church in 2003. Formerly dedicated to Saint Ferdinand, its patron saint was changed to Saint Michael the Archangel in 2013.

spots.name: Punta de Santiago Lighthouse
spots.desc: Built in 1890, it is one of the earliest lighthouses that remain functional up to this date. Since its construction, no ship has ever ran aground within its vicinity.

spots.name: Shrine of Our Lady of Caysasay
spots.local: Simbahan ng Mahal na Birhen ng Caysasay
spots.desc: A pilgrimage site just north of the heritage town containing a venerated image of the Virgin Mary. It is on a low ground; one can descend to it from the historical center city over the with a flight of 125 steps (San Lorenzo Ruiz Steps). The church reopened in 2024 following a major restoration program to undo damage caused by earthquakes and the 2020 Taal Volcano eruption, with the drab modern…

spots.name: Minor Basilica and Parish of Saint Gregory the Great
spots.desc: The only Catholic basilica in Laguna and a national cultural treasure, Majayjay's church burned down several times during the Spanish era, with the last being in 1711. Instead of razing the structure, its priest instead ordered the ruins to be encased inside a -thick layer of brick and plastered in pink, resulting the façade exuding a fortress-like aura. The interior contains an ornate altar and…

spots.name: Nagcarlan Underground Cemetery
spots.local: Sementeryo sa Ilalim ng Lupa ng Nagcarlan
spots.desc: The only cemetery of its kind in the Philippines, it was built in the 19th century on an octagonal layout. It retains its Spanish-era chapel containing a sculpture of the dead Christ, and its underground crypt with the remains of Nagcarlan's high society still inside. Beside the entrance to the compound is a small but informative museum about the concept of death in Philippine culture. An urban…

spots.name: Cagbalete Island
spots.desc: Mauban's main tourist draw is a island northeast of the downtown. It features multiple resorts, white sand beaches and forests.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of Light
spots.desc: Built in 1760, and rebuilt in 1966-68. Pope Francis granted the papal bull of canonical coronation towards its enshrined Marian image in 2017. The altar features a painting of Our Lady of Light by national artist Fernando Amorsolo. Unlike other churches, its entrance is at a transept, as its original Baroque façade leads to the premises of the Cainta Catholic School.

spots.name: Morong Church
spots.desc: Morong's main Roman Catholic church and a designated National Cultural Treasure by the National Commission of Culture and the Arts (NCCA). It was built by Chinese craftsmen during the Spanish era in a unique and intricate neo-baroque architectural style. It is one of a few churches in the Philippines whose belfry is built above its façade.

spots.name: Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar
spots.desc: A living museum housing a growing collection of Spanish-era buildings, which are either reconstructions, replicas or houses dismantled and reassembled from across various towns in the Philippines. The site’s replica of Balanga Cathedral is a favorite wedding venue for those willing to splurge.
spots.addr: Governor J.J. Linao National Highway, Barangay Ibaba

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint Augustine
spots.desc: Baliwag's main Roman Catholic church, built in the 19th century during the Spanish era.

spots.name: National Shrine and Parish of Saint Anne
spots.desc: Hagonoy's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style and retaining its exquisite ceiling art and religious sculptures. It also has an ecclesiastical museum.
spots.addr: M.H. del Pilar Street, Santo Niño

spots.name: Meycauayan Church
spots.desc: This church was built in 1578, originally in barangay Bahay Pare, but was moved to its present location due to attacks from the indigenous Aeta (Negritos). The church survived the Philippine Revolution and World War II, but was destroyed by a fire in 1949 and rebuilt in 1953. It has managed to retain its Baroque facade and belltower, which is connected to the building through an elevated walkway.…
spots.price: Parking fees of PHP30 for cars and PHP20 for motorcycles

spots.name: Gapan Church
spots.desc: Gapan's main Roman Catholic church. Built in 1872, it is the oldest church in Nueva Ecija and is one of the few remaining Spanish-era structures in the province. It also hosts a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.
spots.addr: H. Malgapo corner Delos Reyes Streets, San Vicente

spots.name: Betis Church
spots.desc: The Baroque parish church of Betis district. The original structure was built in 1660, but was damaged by fire and rebuilt in the 1770s. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2001. The church's interior is likened to that of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City. Flash photography is discouraged.

spots.name: Patapat Viaduct
spots.desc: Elevated viaduct hugging the cliff of the North Cordillera Mountain Range along the sea that is sometimes referred to as the "French Riviera of the North". Along the expanse is Mabugabog Falls used for hydroelectric power. The viaduct is part of the Manila North Road (AH26).

spots.name: Minor Basilica of Saint Dominic
spots.desc: Largest Catholic church in the Philippines during the late 18th century, founded in 1773, but had to be rebuilt in 1890.

spots.name: Kawasan waterfalls
spots.desc: The Kawasan water falls (a three step waterfall) is located in the rain forest approximately 20 km south of Moalboal (past Badian). If you take the bus from in front of the public market in Moalboal (near 360 Pharmacy), you can ask the bus driver or ticket collector to drop you off at the right place. The bus ticket from Moalboal to the water falls or vice versa costs 19.00. You also need to pay…

spots.name: Osmeña Peak
spots.desc: This is the best-known hiking area in the region, and the highest peak on Cebu island. The trip from Moalboal town takes about 90 minutes, and if you are going by a bike, do note that some of the roads are rough. Entrance fee is 60. The usual hike can be done in 15-25 minutes with a couple of routes or peak to take. There are some basic accommodations for rent on the hiking trail.

spots.name: Sts. Peter and Paul Cathedral
spots.desc: Constructed in the 1800s, it became the see (central church) of the new Diocese of Calbayog in 1910. Considered to be the biggest church in Samar, the St. Peter and Paul Cathedral was rebuilt and renovated through the years and evolved to a blending of many architectural eras. The structure reveals some are new and some are old. The old dome, the spire and the thick walls are what is left from…

spots.name: Mount Samat National Shrine
spots.desc: Also known as Dambana ng Kagitingan or Shrine of Valour, it is a 92-meter-high War Memorial Cross and a national shrine atop Mount Samat, built to honor and remember the gallantry of the Filipino and American soldiers who fought during World War II. Memorial services are conducted every April 9, which is commemorated nationally as Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valour) and known in the province as…
spots.price: P75 entrance fee, P60 for seniors, disabled and students, P75 parking free for small vehicles and P200 for buses

spots.name: Bocaue Pagoda Festival
spots.desc: An annual fluvial parade, also part of the annual Feast of the Holy Cross, where the Krus ng Wawa, which is believed to have saved an old woman's life who drowned, is paraded on the Pagoda, a gaily structure mounted on large wooden boat (banca), which is then paraded through the Bocaue River.

spots.name: Old Meycauayan Station
spots.desc: One of the stations of the old Manila-Dagupan railway, it also witnessed one of the battles of the Philippine-American War. The station building stands until today, but is slowly crumbling and the station interior is closed to the public. A new station for the North-South Commuter Railway (NSCR) is undergoing construction as of 2026 beside this station, alongside the restoration of the older…

spots.name: Obando Fertility Rites
spots.desc: Literally meaning "Dance in Obando", the practice is believed to have been a Hispanicized version of a precolonial fertility ritual whose subject of veneration was transferred from animist deities to the patron saints of Obando Church. The practice was discouraged and even banned by clergy on multiple occasions due to its syncretic origins, but has since been accepted by the church as an integral…

spots.name: Guadalupe Mabugnao Mainit Hot Spring National Park
spots.desc: Hot springs where cottages and pools have been developed. Life-size statues of saints. Caves

spots.name: Robinsons Place Manila
spots.desc: An urban shopping complex with the usual amenities: food court, cinemas, department store, supermarket, etc. 7 levels, 330 stores. Located near Pedro Gil Station (LRT-1).

spots.name: Plaza Moriones
spots.desc: A linear park placed on the median of Moriones Street, it is dedicated to the Spanish Governor-General Domingo Moriones y Muralla, who designed Manila's sewerage system. It also has a role in Philippine politics, being the location of the first Philippine Labor Day celebrations, and it is designated a "freedom park" where protesters are free to assemble peacefully. Also in the park is a monument…

spots.name: Santa Cruz Church
spots.desc: One of the well known landmarks of Santa Cruz district, named after the Holy Cross, the church was built and administered by the Jesuits up to 1768.

spots.name: Paco Park
spots.desc: Built by the Dominican priests in 1820, this cemetery is where Jose Rizal was buried after his execution in Luneta (also known as Rizal Park) in December 30, 1896. In August 17, 1912, Rizal's remains were exhumed and laid beneath his monument at Rizal Park. A marker can be seen in the location where the remains of Rizal used to be interred. Paco Park is being used as a venue for weddings…

spots.name: Plaza Dilao
spots.desc: During the Spanish colonial era, Plaza Dilao became one of the Japanese settlements in Manila. In 1915, Dilao became a transport center with the operation of the Paco Railway Station. During World War II, intense battle were fought in the area between the Japanese and joint Filipino and American forces. A statue of Justo Ukon Takayama can be seen in this plaza.

spots.name: New Frontier Theatre
spots.desc: Multi-purpose venue opened in 1967, with fast food chains, upscale restaurants and cafés outside.

spots.name: Millennium Transmitter
spots.desc: The 220 m transmitter tower of ABS-CBN, providing strong TV signals around Metro Manila. It is a landmark of the district itself, and is very visible from almost every corner of the Scout Area.
spots.addr: Mother Ignacia Avenue corner Sergeant Esguerra Street

spots.name: Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.desc: Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Davao Oriental, Philippines.

spots.name: TriNoma
spots.desc: Short for Triangle North of Manila, it is a large shopping mall in Quezon City in the Philippines owned by land developer Ayala Land. Opened in 2007, the mall is on the side of Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, near the MRT-3 North Avenue Station in Quezon City, giving significant market competition to the nearby SM North EDSA as one of the largest malls in Manila's metropolitan area.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish Church
spots.local: Simbahan ng Parokya ng La Purisima Concepcion
spots.desc: Santa Maria's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era and hosting a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Minor Basilica and Parish of Saint John the Baptist
spots.desc: Badoc's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period in the 17th century in the Baroque style and housing the venerated Marian image of the Virgen Milagrosa.

spots.name: Binga Dam
spots.desc: A massive hydroelectric complex built in 1960 to control the waters of the Agno River. There is a viewdeck on site.

spots.name: SM City Rosario
spots.desc: The largest mall in Rosario and part of the SM Malls chain.
spots.addr: General Trias Drive corner Costa Verde Access Road, Tejeros Convention

spots.name: Badoc Island
spots.desc: A island with pristine white beaches and rock formations.

spots.name: National Museum/Padre Burgos House
spots.desc: also known as the Ayala Museum, this showcases the memorabilia of martyred priest Jose Burgos. Behind the house is the national museum (formerly the Ilocos Sur Provincial Jail), housing other ethnic and Ilocano artifacts such as artifacts, weapons, kitchen utensils, basketry, costumes, jewellery and Burgos memorabilia. There are also some dioramas showing important events in the history of Ilocos…

spots.name: Syquia Mansion
spots.desc: Vigan residence of President Elpidio Quirino, who married a member of the Syquia family. There are memorabilia inside the residence, including a campaign portrait of Quirino.

spots.name: Baluarte Resort and Mini Zoo
spots.desc: A zoo founded by local politician and businessman Chavit Singson, featuring the usual animals as well as hunting trophies from his safaris in Africa.

spots.name: Parish of Saint Augustine of Hippo
spots.desc: Bantay's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1590. Access to the site has been partially restricted since an earthquake in 2022 that severely damaged the structure.

spots.name: SM City Baguio
spots.desc: A large shopping mall in Baguio. It hosts a SM Supermarket. This mall is unusual among most Philippine malls you generally find because it lacks air conditioning; instead, cooling is provided by Baguio's naturally cool air.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de Gracia Church
spots.local: Simbahan ng Nuestra Señora de Gracia
spots.desc: Built by the Augustinian friars and is inspired by European Baroque. It is named Nuestra Señora de Gracia in honor of the miraculous image of the Virgin Mary that can also be found inside.

spots.name: Ayala Mall
spots.desc: Has several department stores, two supermarkets, a movie theater, lots of restaurants and hundreds of stores. The terraces have a central park-like area and several floors of shopping, mostly restaurants, on either side. The mall is in the Cebu Business Park which hosts the Cathay Pacific office, foreign banks a few consulates, and the Seda hotel. There is now a 2nd Ayala mall at the IT park.

spots.name: Jaro Belfry
spots.desc: One of the few belfries in the country that stands apart from the church. It was constructed by the Spaniards to serve as a watchtower to monitor Muslim invasion from Mindanao. The colonial structure was ruined by an earthquake in 1948 and was restored decades later, in the mid-1990s.

spots.name: Molo Church
spots.desc: Built in 1831, this Gothic-Renaissance church stands as one of the most iconic landmarks of Iloilo. Known as the “feminist church” for its 16 statues of female saints, Molo Church features twin spires, a coral-stone façade, and a magnificent altar. It was visited by Jose Rizal on his way to exile in Dapitan, Mindanao.

spots.name: Calle Real
spots.desc: The city’s historic street, lined with late 19th and early 20th-century neoclassical and art deco buildings. The street has been famous since the Spanish era and once served as the city's main shopping center for more than a century. Eusebio Villanueva Building, a neoclassical building built in 1927, stands as one of the most iconic landmarks along Calle Real. Many other structures are also under…
spots.addr: J.M. Basa Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Camiña Balay Nga Bato
