spots.desc: It was built in 1865 and was designed by the first parish priest of Molo, Anselmo Avanceña, for Don Fernando Avanceña and his wife, Eulalia Abaja. It is now operates as a living museum and restaurant, serving traditional Ilonggo cuisine including tsokolate tablea and local delicacies.

spots.name: Old Iloilo City Hall
spots.desc: Formerly the seat of the city government of Iloilo, the building now serves as the main building of the Iloilo City campus of the University of the Philippines (UP) Visayas.
spots.addr: General Luna Street cor. Infante Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Museo Iloilo
spots.desc: Built in 1971, this provincial museum was the first government-sponsored museum in the Philippines outside Metro Manila. It houses a collection of artifacts, historical items, and exhibits on local culture, as well as temporary art and cultural displays. It’s an excellent place to explore Iloilo’s history, traditions, and artistic heritage.

spots.name: Iloilo River Esplanade
spots.desc: A 10-long well-landscaped linear park along the banks of the Iloilo River. It is considered the longest linear park in the Philippines

spots.name: San Isidro Labrador Convent
spots.desc: Reputed to be the biggest and one of the oldest convents in the Philippines, the Spaniards started construction in 1887 and was completed in 1894. Declared as a historical landmark by the Philippine Historical Commission.

spots.name: SM Cagayan de Oro Downtown Premier
spots.desc: Has a large-screen format theater, a wide variety of restaurants, shops, an SM Supermarket, and a Sky Garden on the 5th floor.
spots.addr: Claro M. Recto Avenue at Osmeña Street

spots.name: Robinsons Cagayan de Oro
spots.addr: Rosario Crescent at Florentino Street, Limketkai Center

spots.name: Pisamban Maragul
spots.desc: Colloquially called the "Big Church" in Kapampangan, it was constructed from 1877 to 1896 by the "Polo y Servicio" labor system, a kind of forced labor imposed on Filipino peasants by the Spanish colonial government. It was used as a military hospital by the U.S. Army from August 1899 to December 1900. Its backyard was the execution ground used by Spanish forces to shoot Filipino rebels and…
spots.addr: Santo Rosario corner Santo Entiero Streets

spots.name: Apung Mamacalulu Shrine
spots.desc: A stone church which is known for hosting the image of Jesus Christ known as "Apung Mamacalulu" (Merciful Lord). The image commissioned in the mid-19th century during the Spanish colonial era, is believed to be miraculous by its devotees.

spots.name: St. Joseph Parish Church
spots.desc: Founded in 1795, this church is built the Earthquake Baroque style. It houses the renowned Bamboo Organ, built in 1825 by Diego Cera, an Augustinian priest.

spots.name: San Diego de Alcala Parish
spots.desc: This parish church, part of Valenzuela's old downtown, was built by locals in 1632 using the polo y servicio system of forced labor. The Spanish-era church was destroyed during World War II, but its old belfry survived.

spots.name: Philippine International Convention Center
spots.desc: the venue of the 1994 Miss Universe Beauty Pageant in Manila.

spots.name: Market! Market!
spots.desc: If you think that BGC is all about expensive, high-end shopping you will be blown away when you step in the Market! Market!, a large shopping mall that besides regular shops, has also a fair share of "air-conditioned street shopping" with all sorts of bargains and even products of dubious origin. In the external part of the mall, the Fiesta Market also contains an open air food court and a small…

spots.name: SM Aura Premier
spots.desc: If the Market! Market! is the shopping mall you wouldn't expect in BGC, the SM Aura is pretty much what you would expect - thin crowds and high-end shopping on its finest, although you can still find some affordable Filipino clothing stores. Even if the expensive shopping does not interest you, the curved L-shaped building is a sight to behold on itself. The Samsung Hall is also contained here.

spots.name: Venice Grand Canal
spots.desc: A shopping mall that is more like a tourist attraction, the Venice Grand Canal mall contains a replica of Venice's Grand Canal and a sight to behold, leaving far behind any "Fake Venices" you may have seen in Las Vegas or Macau. Besides gondola rides, it contains a small size replica of the Rialto Bridge and hosts free family-oriented performances. Still not many shops around, but the…
spots.addr: McKinley Hill Garden Villas, Cluster B, Upper McKinley Rd

spots.name: Okada Manila
spots.desc: It houses a large fountain and a man-made indoor beach.

spots.name: Cuenca Ancestral House
spots.desc: One of the few remaining bahay na bato residences from the Spanish era, the privately-owned house became the first headquarters of the Philippine revolutionary government following the declaration of independence in June 1898 until September that same year, when it was transferred to Malolos, Bulacan. It became the temporary seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Bacoor in the early 1900s when…

spots.name: Casa Real
spots.local: Museo ng Kasaysayang Pampulitika ng Pilipinas
spots.desc: It was built in 1580 as Casa Tribunal and Casa Presidencia of the town gobernadorcillo. It became the Spanish treasury in 1673. Declared National Shrine on October 4, 1965. Now it is the Museum of Philippine Political History.

spots.name: Santa Monica Parish Church
spots.desc: Sarrat's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style in 1724. Access to the site may be restricted due to renovations since 2025 to repair damage caused by earthquakes in 1983 and 2022. The river of Sarrat and the Santa Monica Park in the front make it more beautiful and to relax.

spots.name: Poro Point
spots.desc: A headland containing Poro Point Baywalk and Lighthouse. Also don't miss the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Built as a tribute to the heroism of the soldiers who fought during the last World War, the marker stands at the junction leading to Poro Point.

spots.name: Casa Real
spots.desc: Once the seat of government for Pangasinan, the renovated Casa Real now hosts a museum with 11 galleries.

spots.name: The Cathedral of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary
spots.desc: It's the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Dipolog. Constructed by the Spanish friars of Dipolog on April 15, 1894, records show that the original altar was designed by Dr. Jose Rizal, the sketch of the altar was inspired after that of San Ignacio Church in Manila. The main attraction of the church is the ceiling made of Philippine hardwood.

spots.name: Crocolandia
spots.desc: Witness different sizes of crocodiles, snakes, deer and birds.

spots.name: Paskuhan Village
spots.desc: Christmas-themed park, open all year round

spots.name: Pangasinan Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Neoclassical capitol building.

spots.name: Museo El Deposito
spots.desc: A history museum.
spots.addr: Pinaglabanan Memorial Shrine, Pinaglabanan Street, Corazon de Jesus

spots.name: First monument for José Rizal
spots.desc: The Rizal Monument in Daet was the first monument built to honor José Rizal, and is the oldest surviving such monument in the Philippines. It was designed by Lt. Colonel Antonio Sanz with the help of Ildefonso Alegre of the Philippine Revolutionary Army and through the financial contributions of the locals of Camarines Norte. The three-tiered stone pylon with its square base supporting a triangle…

spots.name: Casa de Segunda Katigbak
spots.desc: The ancestral home of prominent Batangas family, the Casa is a typical "Bahay na Bato" (stone house). It is Spanish Colonial in style, yet tropical in ambiance. It was named after Segunda Katigbak, reputed to be the first love of Dr. Jose P. Rizal, the Philippines' national hero. Casa Segunda was declared by the National Historical Commission as a heritage house for having harbored generations of…

spots.name: Parish and International Shrine of Saint Padre Pio
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic shrine and parish devoted to St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina, with buildings built to local styles. Built as a small chapel along Maharlika Highway, it is now a large complex frequented by devotees around Batangas and surrounding provinces, as well as Metro Manila. It was recognized as an international shrine by the Vatican in 2026.
spots.addr: Gov. Antonio Carpio Avenue, San Pedro

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Church
spots.desc: Baroque church built with coral stones, and completed in 1752. Parts of the original structure have been demolished due to earthquake damage. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

spots.name: Matabungkay
spots.desc: Lian's major tourist destination is the white sand beaches at barangay Matabungkay. It is originally a beach discovered by Germans living in Manila in the 1950s until it became a tourist destination for residents from Manila.

spots.name: Maragondon Church
spots.desc: The town's Roman Catholic church is a Spanish-era structure that is a government-recognized national treasure. It retains its original interiors, except for the pulpit which collapsed in 2025 and is being restored. It was also one of the places in Maragondon where the Bonifacio brothers were detained during the period of their trial and execution.

spots.name: Pagsanjan Arch
spots.desc: One of the few-surviving town gates in the Philippines from the Spanish era, the three-portal structure is a designated National Cultural Treasure that sits directly on the highway from Santa Cruz.

spots.name: Saint Peter of Alcantara Parish Church
spots.desc: The church was built in the 18th century and features elaborate Baroque carvings in its plastered, cream-colored exterior. Its interior consists of an ornate altar, a holy water font carved with a resemblance to a gargoyle, an old painting of the Final Judgement made by artisans from neighboring Paete, and folksy, vibrant ceiling frescoes inspired by Sistine Chapel and the town's devotion to Our…

spots.name: Nuestra Señora dela Natividad Parish Church
spots.desc: Pangil's Roman Catholic church was largely rebuilt following World War II destruction in a more modernist style, resulting in an austere and smooth look. It is known for hosting the Nuestra Señora de la O, a rare venerated image of the Virgin Mary in her pregnant state, and Santo Niño de la O, an equally venerated image of the Christ Child. At the side of the building is a memorial to Charles III…

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Los Baños, dating from the 17th century, although its appearance has been significantly altered by modern cement renovations.

spots.name: Enchanted Kingdom
spots.desc: Opened in 1995, this fantasy-themed amusement park is the city's number one tourist draw, drawing locals and foreigners (generally Chinese and Koreans) alike. The park is built with Filipino values in mind, and not just for amusement and thrill-seeking. Go ride the Wheel of Fate and see the wide views of the city and surrounding area, spin around in the Space Shuttle roller coaster, get wet at…
spots.hours: Mon Tue closed, Wed Thu 11AM-7PM, Fri noon-7PM, Sat 11AM-9PM, Sun 10AM-9PM

spots.name: Twin Lakes
spots.local: Mga Lawa ng Pandin at Yambo
spots.desc: Two of San Pablo's Seven Crater Lakes, situated in close proximity to each other and separated only by a narrow isthmus. These lakes are the most suitable among the seven for recreational activities, including swimming, and offer pristine unspoiled waters. There are camping accommodations nearby.

spots.name: Gumaca Cathedral
spots.desc: Gumaca's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1690. It is also the headquarters of the Diocese of Gumaca.

spots.name: Malagonlong Bridge
spots.desc: A Spanish-era stone bridge along the highway to Pagbilao, built between 1840 and 1850. The bridge is no longer passable and has been superseded by a newer adjacent bridge, but is still in good condition.

spots.name: Binangonan Church
spots.desc: Binangonan's main Roman Catholic church, built in 1792 in the Baroque style and declared a national cultural treasure in 2025. Its highlights are the original Spanish-era altarpieces and a statue of Saint Ursula in the main altar.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint Joseph
spots.desc: Home of the image of San Jose de Baras. The Church was completed by the Franciscan missionaries in 1686. It features a dark and austere interior thanks to its unplastered bricks, lined with a set of original carvings of the Stations of the Cross. Its ceiling remains uncovered, revealing a ribcage-like row of wooden beams supporting the roof.
spots.addr: San Jose Street, Barangay San Juan

spots.name: Masungi Georeserve
spots.desc: A conservation area near the boundary with Tanay which consists of the geological formations of Masungi rock. It is characterized by rugged limestone karst peaks, steep slopes, and surrounding lush montane rainforests. It contains several caves, including the Yungíb ni Ruben (Ruben's Cave), which features stalactite and stalagmite formations.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of St. Mary Magdalene
spots.desc: Home of the ivory processional image of Saint Mary Magdalene. Built in the Spanish era in a Baroque style, its interior features exquisite ceiling frescoes.

spots.name: Baliwag Museum and Library
spots.desc: It was the first town hall (munisipyo or municipio) which was built during the American occupation in 1899. It used to house the municipal government until 1971, when a new town hall was inaugurated. Today, it houses a museum dedicated to the town's history. As of 2026, the museum is closed for renovations.

spots.name: Marcelo H. del Pilar Shrine
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to Marcelo H. del Pilar, an anti-clerical activist who criticized the theocratic influence of Spanish Roman Catholic friars in the 19th century Philippines and advocated for equal rights for Filipinos under the Spanish Crown before shifting to outright independence in his last years. Built on the site of the del Pilar residence, it features a replica of a Spanish-era house that…

spots.name: Ipo Dam
spots.desc: The oldest of the three Angat River dams, built in 1935, and the scene of a battle between Allied forces and Japanese stragglers during the closing stages of World War II in 1945. While access to the dam itself its restricted, a viewdeck provides vistas of the surrounding watershed.

spots.name: Plaridel Church
spots.desc: Plaridel's main Roman Catholic Church, built in its current state by the Spanish in the 18th century in a Baroque style with cream-colored plaster in its facades and gravestones in the interior walls.

spots.name: Minalin Church
spots.desc: Minalin's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period in the Baroque style over a 70-year period from 1764 to 1834 and designated a national cultural treasure in 2001 for its intricately carved Baroque facade.

spots.name: San Guillermo Parish Church
spots.desc: Bacolor's main Roman Catholic church, which also doubles as a memorial to the 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption. The original church building dates back to 1587 but was destroyed by an earthquake, and the present church is from 1897. During a lahar flow from Mount Pinatubo exacerbated by a typhoon in 1995, the church, along with its cemetery became half-buried in lahar, which has since hardened.The…
spots.addr: Don Ceferino Joven Street, Barangay Cabambangan

spots.name: San Agustin Church
spots.desc: The oldest parish church in Pampanga, it has a neoclassical façade and a stone brick structure. The church building and belfry that stands today dates back to 1638. It was declared a National Historical Site in 1952, and an Important Cultural Property in 2013. As of 2026, access to the interior is restricted due to renovations and repairs to undo damage caused by a 2019 earthquake.

spots.name: Capas National Shrine
spots.desc: A memorial for the soldiers who died at the hands of the Japanese in Camp O'Donnell. It houses an obelisk with a central bell, and the shrine is built on what was Camp O'Donnell.

spots.name: Bacarra Church
spots.desc: Bacarra's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and repaired to its current state following heavy damage from an earthquake in 1983. There is an ecclesiastical and local history museum in the convent.

spots.name: Minor Basilica of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino
spots.desc: Sinait's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period in the 17th century in the Baroque style and housing the venerated image of the Santo Cristo Milagroso.

spots.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria Parish Church
spots.desc: Luna's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style in 1690. It houses the venerated image of Our Lady of Namacpacan, a statue of the Virgin Mary that arrived in town when the ship transporting the image to its original destination in Vigan was repeatedly forced to seek shelter in town due to storms along the South China Sea in 1871. The church was declared a national cultural treasure…
spots.addr: Luna-Bangar Road corner Namacpacan Road, Victoria

spots.name: Cape Bolinao Light House
spots.desc: A lighthouse built in 1905 to guard the approaches to Lingayen Gulf from the South China Sea.

spots.name: Calasiao Church
spots.desc: A Spanish-era Baroque Roman Catholic church first built in the 17th century and declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2001.
spots.addr: Mamaradlo co. F. Sison Streets, Barangay Poblacion East

spots.name: Santo Niño Parish Church
spots.desc: Mabini's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1830. It retains its original façade and large parts of its walls.

spots.name: St Raymond of Peñafort Parish Church
spots.desc: An Early Renaissance style Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1830.
spots.addr: Romulo Highway corner Mabini Street, Torres Bugallon

spots.name: SM City Consolacion
spots.desc: A large mall with over 100,000 m2 or a million ft2 of leased area, and over 200 stores and restaurants.

spots.name: Capul Church and Fortress
spots.desc: The Capul Church, built during the Spanish colonial period, is dedicated to St. Ignatius of Loyola and is surrounded by a square fort with bulwarks of dissimilar designs. The church structure was actually the third that was built on the site. The first two structures, made of hard wood and nipa roofs, were razed when Moro pirates plundered the island in 1615 and 1768. In 1781, Fr. Mariano Valero…

spots.name: Lake Tikub
spots.desc: A volcanic crater lake west of downtown Tiaong. It was formed as part of the Laguna Volcanic Field and is an extension of the more famous Seven Lakes of neighboring San Pablo, but is less visited and has few tourist infrastructure apart from two viewdecks.

spots.name: National Shrine of the Divine Mercy
spots.desc: Shrine dedicated to the Divine Mercy, built in 1992 and featuring a giant statue of Jesus Christ.

spots.name: Quipayo Church
spots.desc: A Spanish-era Roman Catholic church.

spots.name: SM City Tanza
spots.addr: Antero Soriano Highway, Daang Amaya II

spots.name: Sub-Parish Church of Santo Cristo
spots.desc: A Spanish-era chapel built in 1881.

spots.name: Mercado Mansion
spots.desc: Bahay-na-bato heritage house painted Mediterranean blue

spots.name: Titay's
spots.desc: Bakery since 1907, famous ringlet cookies.

spots.name: SM City San Mateo
spots.desc: The only mall in San Mateo.
spots.addr: General A. Luna Avenue, Ampid I

spots.name: SM City Manila
spots.desc: Part of the nationwide SM "Supermall" chain, this shopping centre has all of the standard features of an urban mall (including a food court, cinemas, a department store and a supermarket) as well as scores of shops spread out over 6 floors. Located near Central Terminal (LRT-1).

spots.name: Max's Restaurant
spots.desc: A Filipino restaurant popular for its chicken.

spots.name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Dupax del Sur, built in the Baroque style during the 18th century and declared a national cultural treasure in 2001. Beside the convent is a souvenir shop and museum showing church antiquities. The courtyard also features a centuries-old acacia tree.
spots.addr: Aritao-Quirino Road, Dopaj, Dupax del Sur

spots.name: Mabuhay Rotonda
spots.desc: The name was changed during the 1990s. Built in 1948 during the term of Mayor Ponciano Bernardo. Quezon City had been declared the capital of the Philippines on July 17, 1948 and so the monument was built to welcome people to the capital, hence “Welcome Rotonda”.

spots.name: Ali Mall
spots.desc: The oldest standing major shopping mall in the Philippines, built in 1976. It is named in honor of boxing legend Muhammad Ali, who won the famed "Thrilla in Manila" on 1975.

spots.name: Oblation
spots.desc: The iconic statue, sculpted by Guillermo E. Tolentino, that symbolizes the University of the Philippines and its tradition of the Oblation Run.

spots.name: Gateway Mall
spots.desc: The flagship mall of the Araneta Group. Opened 2006.

spots.name: St. Catherine of Siena Parish Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Bambang, built during the 18th century in a Baroque style. With the exception of the ruinous post-colonial porte-cochere, its facade resembles that of Dupax Church.

spots.name: Dalton Pass
spots.desc: It is a rugged piece of terrain where a part of the Caraballo Sur reaches south and joins the Sierra Madre. Because of its strategic importance as the only access between Nueva Ecija and Cagayan Valley, the pass became the scene of much bloody fighting during the final stages of World War II. Japanese Shobu soldiers headed by General Tomoyuki Yamashita tried to hold their positions while Filipino…

spots.name: Nuestra Señora dela Merced Parish Church
spots.local: Parokya ng Mahal na Birhen ng Awa ng Pampanga
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic church serving the swampland barangays of Candaba. It houses the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Mercy of Pampanga, known locally as "Apung de la Merced".

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish Church
spots.desc: Concepcion's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the late 19th century in the neo-Romanesque style. It is one of the few remaining Spanish-era buildings in the province and has ceilings painted with floral motifs.

spots.name: SM City Pampanga
spots.desc: Giant SM mall at the boundary with San Fernando that opened in 2000, with hundreds of shops and restaurants, and the Sky Ranch Pampanga theme park.

spots.name: Archdiocesan Shrine of Saint Vincent Ferrer
spots.desc: San Vicente's main Roman Catholic Church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1795. The site, along with the adjacent town plaza, municipal hall, and a building of the San Vicente Integrated School, which also dates back to the Spanish period, was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2020.
spots.addr: Bantay-San Vicente Road, Poblacion, San Vicente

spots.name: Nielson Tower Historical Marker
spots.desc: The Nielson Airport was built by Laurie Reuben Nielson, a businessman born in New Zealand. It was built in 1937 and served as the control tower and passenger depot of the city's airport. Until 1948. The Nielson Airport was built on a 42-hectare piece of land owned by Ayala y Cia. During World War II, commercial flights were relocated so that Nielson could serve the U.S. Army Air Corps.

spots.name: Casa Gorordo Museum
spots.desc: A well-preserved Spanish colonial mansion constructed largely of wood, set in a pleasant, manicured garden. The lower floor has a collection of old tools, and an A/C room that has changing displays such as art exhibitions. The more interesting upstairs level was the former living quarters of the Gorordo family. It features lovely carved wooden furniture and a wide patio. The kitchen is…

spots.name: Cebu IT Park
spots.desc: Offices, rental and condo apartments; the area has many foreign employees and a good selection of western restaurants. Not much shopping.

spots.name: Negros Occidental Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: The official seat of the provincial government and perhaps the most impressive building in Bacolod City. It served as the headquarters of the Japanese Imperial Army during World War II. The Romanesque-style building stands in landscaped grounds with a park and lagoon, and features Ang Paghimud-os ("The Struggle" in Hiligaynon), a sculpture by Eduardo Castrillo, as well as The Man and the Carabao…

spots.name: San Jose Church
spots.desc: Founded in 1607 by the Jesuits and later turned over to the Augustinians, it is considered the first church in Iloilo City. The church houses the replica of Santo Niño de Cebú, the patron saint of the Dinagyang Festival.

spots.name: Casa Real de Iloilo
spots.desc: The building, formerly the seat of the provincial government of Iloilo, has undergone numerous renovations and additions since it became the seat of the civil government in 1901. It was used as a military garrison by Japanese Imperial Forces during World War II. The building also hosted the Vin d'honneur (wine of honor) for the 117th Philippine Independence Day, led by President Benigno S. Aquino…

spots.name: Molo Mansion
spots.desc: A neoclassical-art deco heritage mansion built in 1926 by Doña Petra Lacson, a matron of the Lacson clan, and Estanislao Yulo Yusay, a prominent lawyer and judge from Molo. The property has been restored and is now owned by the SM Group, housing several cafés, restaurants, and souvenir shops, including Kultura.

spots.name: Nelly Garden
spots.desc: Built in 1928 by the Lopez family, this Beaux-Arts mansion is one of Iloilo’s most elegant heritage houses. The property features sprawling gardens, neoclassical architecture, and preserved interiors showcasing the lifestyle of Iloilo’s early 20th-century elite. The mansion is not entirely open to the public and requires a tour or event reservation to enter, but visitors can still admire its…

spots.name: Lizares Mansion
spots.desc: Built in 1937 by sugar baron Don Emiliano Lizares, this Beaux-Arts mansion features hardwood floors, elegant staircases, and classic architectural details. During World War II, it was occupied by the Japanese army. Today, it houses Angelicum School Iloilo and is occasionally open to visitors. The mansion is particularly popular during Christmas, when it is beautifully illuminated.

spots.name: Casa Mariquit
spots.desc: The 200-year-old ancestral house of Doña Mariquit Lopez, the matriarch of the Lopez clan of ABS CBN. It also serves as a museum of the late Vice President Fernando Lopez, the husband of Doña Mariquit and the patriarch of the Lopez clan. Considered the oldest surviving house in Iloilo City, it is preserved as a museum showcasing furniture, photographs, and artifacts from the Spanish colonial…

spots.name: National Museum Western Visayas
spots.desc: Housed in the former provincial jail, built in 1911, the museum features five galleries on its lower floor and an open gallery on the second floor, showcasing artifacts from across the Western Visayas region.

spots.name: Museum of Philippine Economic History
spots.local: Museo ng Kasaysayang Pang-ekonomiya ng Pilipinas
spots.desc: The national museum narrates the evolution of the Philippine economy, highlighting major industries, historical developments, and Iloilo City’s role as the second-most important city in the Philippines during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
spots.addr: J.M. Basa Street cor. Ortiz Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Iloilo Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.desc: A three-floor art museum full of avant-garde artistic atmosphere. Compared with ordinary artworks, the works here incorporate the contemporary artists' ideas to express to the public. It has five exhibit halls and highlighting works from 42 different artists.
spots.addr: Festive Walk Road cor. Taft Street, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

spots.name: Plaza Libertad
spots.desc: Also known as Plaza Alfonso XII, this central park in Iloilo City Proper is a National Historical Institute site for its role in the Philippine liberation. Surrounding the plaza are key landmarks, including the City Government Center, San Jose de Placer Church, heritage buildings like the Masonic Temple and Lacson Ancestral House, the Botica Lacson ruins, Iloilo Plaza Hotel (now LandBank), and…

spots.name: Graciano Lopez Jaena Park
spots.desc: One of the largest district plazas in the city, it is part of the Jaro Cultural Heritage Tourism Zone, alongside Jaro Cathedral, Jaro Belfry, and surrounding heritage ancestral houses. The plaza features several monuments and memorials, including a new shrine of Patrocinio Gamboa, the World War II Memorial Monument, and the Graciano Lopez Jaena Monument.

spots.name: Molo Plaza
spots.desc: One of the six district plazas in the city, it features statues of Greek goddesses and a monument of Maria Clara. Like Jaro Plaza, it is surrounded by Molo Church and heritage ancestral houses such as Molo Mansion.

spots.name: SM City Cagayan de Oro
spots.desc: Every August and December, SM City Cagayan de Oro holds two Pyro Musical Fireworks shows.
spots.addr: Masterson Avenue at Gran Via Street

spots.name: Jose R. Gullas Halad Museum
spots.desc: A museum that pays homage to the musical heritage of Cebu. This museum is operated under the Tipiganan sa mga Handumanan sa Kanta ug Kinaiyang Sugbuanon (Treasury of Memories) Foundation. In the old building of The Freeman Newspaper.

spots.name: Pinto Art Museum
spots.desc: A museum gallery showcasing works of art from paintings and sculptures of local artists. It is a sprawling property with well manicured gardens and fountains. A perfect backdrop for reflection and learning. The gallery also has a commanding view of Metro Manila. The café catered by Bizu is open during weekends.
spots.addr: 1 Sierra Madre Street, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Ynares Center Arena
spots.desc: Ynares Center is a multi-purpose indoor arena located inside the provincial capitol compound. It is named after the Ynares family, who are prominent politicians in the province of Rizal. The center is a popular venue for various sports events, concerts, exhibitions, and other large-scale gatherings.
spots.addr: L. Sumulong Memorial Circle, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Pamintuan Mansion
spots.desc: A century-old heritage house, which houses the Museum of Philippine Social History since 2015. The museum features exhibits and artifacts related to Filipino daily livelihood and leisure. It was used by the American soldiers during World War II, converted to the Angeles Hotel sometime after the war, and was the satellite office of the Philippine central bank from 1993 to 2009.

spots.name: Museo ning Angeles
spots.desc: Housed in a vintage building located at the "Santo Rosario Historic District", this edifice was constructed in 1922 and served as the Town Hall until 1998. The museum has become the venue of the city's cultural activities be it from the or government sector. Since it opened in 1999, it has been a venue for various activities from exhibits, art classes, concerts, venue for performances and climax…
spots.addr: Santo Rosario corner Santo Entiero Streets

spots.name: Las Piñas-Parañaque Critical Habitat
spots.desc: A rare thing, natural habitat extant in these parts. Here you can find a mangrove trail and marine views.

spots.name: Tanghalang Pambansa
spots.desc: A giant Brutalist theater building that is the center of the CCP complex. It was built in 1969, and the architecture was designed by Filipino architect Leandro Locsin. It houses four theatres for different performance genres.

spots.name: The Dessert Museum
spots.desc: Offbeat museum showcasing large, colorful sculptures of dessert items, plus sweets to sample.

spots.name: Pasig City Museum
spots.desc: Also found in the city center adjacent to Plaza Rizal, this former colonial mansion has been converted into a museum to showcase Pasig's rich history of culture and arts.

spots.name: Bahay na Tisa
spots.desc: Lit. "House of Stone". It is the only remaining "Bahay na Bato" in Pasig City, still owned by the Tech Family and not yet open to public. This house has also been used in many movies relating to Spanish times due to the house's authenticity and rustic appeal.

spots.name: Ibalong Festival
spots.desc: This non-religious festival based on the Ibalong Epic is held in August. It celebrates the epic story Ibalong who was accompanied by three legendary heroes, namely Baltog, Handyong, and Bantong. People parade in the streets wearing masks and costumes to imitate the appearances of the heroes and the villains, portraying the classic battles that made their way into the history of Bicol. The Ibalong…

spots.name: SM City Clark
spots.desc: A major shopping mall at the Clark Freeport Zone under the SM Supermalls chain.

spots.name: City of Dreams Manila
spots.desc: It was planned as the Belle Grande Manila Bay. It is the second resort and casino to be built in Entertainment City. It houses six five star hotel buildings and a casino, as well as an animated movie-oriented theme park named DreamPlay Manila built with collaboration with DreamWorks Animation.

spots.name: Uptown Bonifacio
spots.desc: Mall forming a mixed used development with corporate towers, containing a mix of Filipino and international brands. The dancing fountain in the 4th floor is worth checking.

spots.name: MarQuee Mall
spots.desc: A major shopping mall under Ayala Malls.

spots.name: Mahatao Church
spots.desc: A 19th century Spanish colonial church that was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2001.

spots.name: St. Paul University Philippines
spots.desc: It was founded by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres in 1907, who came to Cagayan upon the invitation of Bishop Dennis Dougherty. The school had its operation in a Spanish Convento, adjoining the Cathedral of Tuguegarao. The institution transferred to its present location in 1934 after it was acquired from the Dominican Order. The entire building complex became hospital and garrison of the…

spots.name: Ilagan Sports Complex
spots.desc: A large modern sports center opened 2015 to replace the older Paguirigan Memorial Sports Complex. It has badminton, basketball, tennis, and volleyball courts, an 8-lane swimming pool, and an IAAF-certified track and field.

spots.name: Zapote Bridge
spots.desc: A historic arch bridge at the boundary with Las Piñas, where two battles during the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American War, the 1897 Battle of Zapote Bridge and the 1899 Battle of Zapote River, occurred. The 1897 battle was a Filipino victory, while the 1899 battle was an American victory (as they used gun boats to devastate the Filipino positions). At the middle of the bridge…

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Solitude of Porta Vaga
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church. Following the destruction of the Ermita, it has since housed the Porta Vaga image, the oldest-known image of the Virgin Mary in the Philippines, dating from the 17th century. Access to the image is through the parish office at the back of the church.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish Church
spots.desc: The first Roman Catholic church in the city, designated a National Historical Landmark by the Philippine government. Originally a chapel for the barrio of Tampus, it served as a Spanish outpost during the Philippine Revolution, and also a concentration camp during the Japanese occupation of the Philippines during Pacific War. Also within the churchyard is a statue of Don Placido Campos, who led…
spots.addr: Don Placido Campos Avenue cor. Camerino Avenue, Poblacion

spots.name: Isabel II Bridge
spots.desc: One of the few surviving Spanish-era bridges in the Philippines, it was the site of one of the earliest victories of the Katipunan against the Spanish during the 1896 revolution. In the middle of the bridge is a memorial plaque designed after the façade of Imus Cathedral with benches. At the approach beside Camp Pantaleon Garcia, the headquarters of the Cavite Police, is a monument to the battle.

spots.name: Alberto Mansion
spots.desc: Historic location of Jose Rizal's first formal schooling previously owned by an uncle of the national hero. It collapsed in 2012, but was expropriated by the city government and restored into a museum and cultural center in 2019.

spots.name: St. John the Baptist Parish
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Calamba, built in the Baroque style and rebuilt after World War II. This was where Jose Rizal was baptized and attended mass in his early years.

spots.name: Bulacan Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Built in the art deco style in 1937, it is one of the few provincial government buildings in the Philippines that survived World War II.

spots.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto Shrine (Graceville)
spots.desc: A pilgrimage site often visited by Roman Catholic devotees during Holy Week, distinguished by its spire and curving ramps around it. However, parts of the main church building are in a dilapidated state, and the ramps have been closed off due to concerns about structural integrity.

spots.name: Camp Pangatian
spots.desc: A former American military camp turned into a Japanese concentration camp for American and Filipino prisoners of war, it was known for the raid at Cabanatuan, one of the largest military operations of World War II in the Pacific. The camp has been turned into a memorial for the prisoners of war detained here, and is also part of itineraries for American war veterans.

spots.name: Pampanga Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: American-era Neoclassical building housing the offices of the provincial government of Pampanga

spots.name: San Nicolas Church
spots.local: Simbahan ng San Nicolas de Tolentino
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in San Nicolas, built during the Spanish era. Its present Baroque structure dates from 1693.
spots.addr: Manila North Road, San Ildefonso, San Nicolas

spots.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Parish
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church that used to be the main place of worship in Salasa until the town center was moved to its present location in 1958.

spots.name: Colors of StoBoSa
spots.desc: Inspired by the favela paintings in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, it is a community artwork formed by paintwork of about two hundred houses in the sitios of Stonehill, Botiwtiw, and Sadjap. It was conceptualized by local artist troupe, Tam-awan Artist Village and was painted by residents of the area as well as volunteers.
spots.addr: Stonehill, Botiwtiw, and Sadjap Sitios in Barangay Balili.

spots.name: San Bartolome Church
spots.desc: Historic Roman Catholic church with a history dating back to 1599.

spots.name: Intendencia (Aduana)
spots.desc: Built in the 1820s and reconstructed after the 1863 earthquake, this building once housed the Spanish colonial government's customs offices and other administrative units. It was damaged during the war but survived to re-enter government service - at one point housing the Central Bank of the Philippines - only to fall victim to a 1979 fire that caused massive destruction. There are plans to…

spots.name: Battle of Pinaglabanan Shrine
spots.desc: Opened 1974, it commemorates the Battle of San Juan del Monte during the Philippine Revolution.

spots.name: Pinaglabanan Church
spots.desc: A Neo-Romanesque church dating back to 1894. It is declared a National Historical Landmark in 1974.

spots.name: Iglesia ni Cristo, Lokal ng F. Manalo
spots.desc: It was the central office for the church administration of the Iglesia ni Cristo 1925–1971. The complex houses numerous Art Deco buildings, most notably its chapel, designed by the architect Juan Nakpil. Viewable from the outside, not open to the public.

spots.name: Filoil EcoOil Centre
spots.desc: Constructed in 2006 as a major sports venue, this serves as the main venue for Premier Volleyball League (PVL, formerly Shakey's V-League), the UAAP games, and is an alternate venue for PBA games.

spots.name: Greenhills Shopping Center
spots.desc: Opened in the 1970s, it is a middle class commercial-residential development with over 2000 shops in 6 mall buildings. Greenhills has over 90,000 visitors a day, and also houses tiangges (flea markets) and a pearl market.

spots.name: Bernardino-Ysabel Jalandoni Ancestral House
spots.desc: Besides from European architecture, what special about the house is that it has been turned into a museum and displays an expensive doll collection, and century-old objects like telephones, chandeliers, etc.

spots.name: Palinpinon Geothermal Plant
spots.desc: This geothermal plant provides electric power for all of Negros Island, Panay, and Guimaras, plus parts of Cebu Province. The power station plaza is closed to visitors at the guard house.

spots.name: SM Center Tuguegarao Downtown
spots.desc: SM Center Tuguegarao Downtown has a gross floor area of almost 37,000 m². SM Supermarket, cyberzone and food and nonfood retail tenants.
spots.addr: Luna Street cor. Mabini Street, Ugac Sur

spots.name: Museo de Baler
spots.desc: Cultural hub showcasing artifacts, paintings, memorabilia & ethnic exhibits of the region.

spots.name: Ma-Cho Temple
spots.desc: Taoist temple. At 7 stories high, it affords views of the sea. Has gardens and fountains too.

spots.name: Palacio del Gobernador
spots.desc: This eight-storey office building was erected in the late 1970s on the site of the Spanish Governor-General's official residence, which was destroyed in a powerful 1863 earthquake that also damaged many other structures in Intramuros. Sadly, the hulking modern building looks almost nothing like its grand 19th-century namesake.
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Andres Soriano (Aduana)

spots.name: Museo ng Katipunan
spots.desc: A local museum on the history of the Katipunan and the 1896 Philippine revolt against Spain, operated by the local government of San Juan, and supervised by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines.
spots.addr: 29 Pinaglabanan Street, Corazon de Jesus, San Juan

spots.name: SM City Dasmariñas
spots.addr: Governor's Drive corner Aguinaldo Highway, Sampaloc 1

spots.name: Robinsons Place Santiago
spots.desc: Has a nice food court on the 2nd floor.

spots.name: Robinsons Townville Cabanatuan & Robinsons Supermarket
spots.addr: KM #111, Brgy. H. Concepcion, Pan-Philippine Hwy

spots.name: SM City San Fernando Downtown
spots.addr: V. Tiomico corner Consunji Streets, Santo Rosario

spots.name: St. Theresita's Academy
spots.desc: A private school.

spots.name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church
spots.desc: Sabtang's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1785.

spots.name: Sabtang Lighthouse
spots.desc: An structure overlooking the northern part of the island and watching the ferries heading to and from Batan Island.

spots.name: Filipino - Japanese Friendship Landmark
spots.desc: A marker erected in 1985 to commemorate the end of Japanese occupation of Bicol and the start of stronger Filipino-Japanese relations.

spots.name: Lal-lo Church
spots.desc: A red brick Spanish-era church that served as the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia until it was transferred to Vigan, Ilocos Sur in 1758, leading to the decline of Lal-lo as an economic hub. Its facade faces the Cagayan River, a reminder of the waterway's previous function as the main artery of transport in the Cagayan Valley.

spots.name: Saint Raymond of Peñafort Parish Church
spots.desc: Rizal's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1617 in a baroque style using stones quarried from the Matalag River. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001 on account of its age and dual function as a fortress against raids by Kalingas and Isnegs from Apayao.

spots.name: Cabagan-Santa Maria Bridge
spots.desc: A multi-arched bridge that took nearly 10 years to build, only to collapse a month after its opening in 2025. After repairs, it reopened a year later to light vehicles. Despite this, the structure retains its imposing look and provides great views over the Cagayan River. Is it visible as far away as San Pablo, more than away.
spots.addr: Cabagan-Santa Maria Road, Barangay Casibarag Norte

spots.name: San Pablo Church
spots.desc: The oldest church in Isabela, built in a Baroque style during the 17th century. Its belfry looms above the town center and is visible as far away as Cabagan.

spots.name: Saint Rose of Lima Parish Church
spots.desc: Gamu's Roman Catholic parish church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in the 18th century.

spots.name: Bauan Church
spots.desc: Founded as a chapel in what is now the town center of Alitagtag municipality, it is a Neoclassical church dating back to 1894, although a botched restoration by parish officials in 2021 stripped the facade bare to the frustration of residents and heritage advocates. The church also houses a giant image of the Holy Cross made from anubing, a species of Artocarpus. It is also known for subli, a…

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Patriarch Church
spots.desc: Baroque-styled church in the middle of town, dedicated to its patron saint and forming the Spanish-era Poblacion. Its highlights are the altar, pulpit and gold-colored ceiling motifs and tiles. There is also an adjacent ecclesiastical museum.

spots.name: Mabini Shrine
spots.desc: The Shrine houses the remains and personal belongings of the revolutionary hero and "Brains of the Katipunan," Apolinario Mabini, who was a native of Tanauan. Mabini is known as the "Sublime Paralytic" who, despite his polio-induced paralysis, fired nationalism in the Filipinos and urged them to unite, with the sheer power of his writings. He wrote fiery articles against Spanish atrocities in…

spots.name: Tanauan Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church of Tanauan, also a National Historical Landmark. The original church was built in 1584, but was destroyed by the eruption of Taal Volcano. The church was rebuilt in 1881, but was destroyed again in World War II and rebuilt in its present form in 1948 while retaining its 1881 facade.
spots.addr: F. Laureana Street corner Mabini Avenue, Poblacion 2

spots.name: Saint Roch Parish Church
spots.desc: Lemery's main parish church, it dates back to 1887, and used to have a Neoclassical façade with two belfries. It was badly damaged by aerial bombing at the end of World War II in 1945, and the façade was replaced by a modernist one in 1968, with the belfries demolished.

spots.name: NHCP Museo nina Marcela Mariño at Felipe Agoncillo
spots.local: Museo nina Marcela Mariño at Felipe Agoncillo
spots.desc: The birthplace of Marcela N. Agoncillo who was known as the maker of the first official Filipino Flag during the Philippine revolution against the Spanish authorities. The different flags of the revolution are also prominently displayed at the site. It is also one of the few places in the country where the Philippine flag must be hoisted 24/7 by law.

spots.name: Casa Villavicencio
spots.desc: Heritage home owned by Gliceria Marella Villavicencio's family, and a site of a meeting of the La Liga Filipina with Jose Rizal and Andres Bonifacio. Open by prior reservation.

spots.name: Indang Church
spots.desc: Indang's central parish church, dating back to 1625. It was originally a chapel, and the present Baroque church, which has galvanized iron roofing and exquisite ceiling and wall paintings, dates back to 1953, rebuilt from the original destroyed during the Philippine Revolution.

spots.name: St. Mary Magdalene Church
spots.desc: One of the oldest churches in the Philippines, construction was started in 1737. It holds Emilio Aguinaldo's baptism certificate and has a finely crafted and gilded altarpiece. The image of its patron saint, Saint Mary Magdalene, has a peculiar mole on its forehead and is placed in a side altar.

spots.name: Baldomero Aguinaldo Shrine
spots.desc: An overlooked heritage house museum dedicated to President Aguinaldo's cousin, who held several positions in his cabinet and was also a distinguished military commander during the revolution. Baldomero and several of his relatives are buried at the backyard.

spots.name: Naic Church
spots.desc: Naic's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era and containing an exquisite altarpiece and interior. At the front is a pedestrian mural showing a map of Cavite.

spots.name: Silang Church
spots.desc: A typical Baroque church dedicated to the Virgin of Candelaria. The original parish church and its attached school was completed 1595 by the Franciscans, but were destroyed by fire in 1603. A new church was built in 1637-39, and dedicated in 1640, and its belfry was damaged by earthquakes in 1880 and repaired in 1989. It became a Spanish Civil Guard (Guardia Civil) outpost against a local…

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine of Saint Augustine and Parish of the Holy Cross
spots.desc: Tanza's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Spanish era and dedicated to the town's two patron saints, the Holy Cross, of which a side altar displays a crucifix in which Emilio Aguinaldo swore an oath as leader of the Philippine revolutionary government in 1897, and Saint Augustine of Hippo, in which another side altar displays a venerated sculpture of the saint, known fondly by locals as…

spots.name: Bonifacio Trial House
spots.desc: A Spanish-era heritage house that was converted into a makeshift courtroom for the kangaroo trial of Andres Bonifacio and his brother by his comrades following a political rivalry with Cavite's own Emilio Aguinaldo in 1897. It now houses a museum explaining one of the most controversial events in Philippine history.
spots.addr: Col. C. Riel Street, Barangay Poblacion 1-A

spots.name: Transfiguration of Our Lord Parish Church
spots.desc: Cavinti's Roman Catholic church was built on the site where the town's venerated image of Jesus Christ was said to have been discovered during the Spanish period. Its baroque facade is made of exposed brick, while its interior has been plastered.

spots.name: San Sebastian Parish Church
spots.desc: Lumban's Roman Catholic church was built in the late 16th century but was finished in its present form during the early 20th century. It features a partially plastered facade colored in orange. Its interior is largely plastered, without much ornamentation.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de Candelaria Parish Church
spots.desc: Mabitac's Roman Catholic church was largely rebuilt following damage from World War II and earthquakes, resulting in an austere look, with only the belltower and altar hinting at its Spanish origins. The church was built on top of Kalbaryo (Calvary) Hill, the highest point in the town center with vistas of the surrounding valley, Mount Sembrano, the Sierra Madre mountains, and Laguna de Bay.…

spots.name: Saint Mary Magdalene Parish Church
spots.desc: Magdalena's Roman Catholic church was built in the Baroque style and features an austere and unplastered facade and interior, along with a statue of Saint Mary Magdalene seemingly bleeding through her eyes while she holds a skull. Its main claim to fame is being a convalescent home for Filipino revolutionary hero Emilio Jacinto during the war of independence against the Spanish, with a small…

spots.name: Saint James the Apostle Parish Church
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic church built during the Spanish colonial era, featuring a Baroque brickwork with Asiatic-like jagged ridges on top. Inside the church are murals by local artist, Luciano Dans namely Langit, Lupa, Impiyerno (Heaven, Earth, Hell) and large murals of Saint Christopher. The murals are designated as national cultural treasures, although some of them are in urgent need of repair due to…
spots.addr: Juan Tinawin Street, Barangay. Nueve (9) Ibaba del Norte

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe
spots.desc: The town's Roman Catholic church, it was rebuilt in its original Spanish colonial-style minus its dome after sustaining heavy damage from World War II-bombardment. It houses a venerated image of Our Lady of Guadalupe that was donated by Mexico. A side chapel contains funeral plaques of residents from the colonial era. A side room to the left of the entrance leads to a parish store selling themed…

spots.name: National Shrine and Parish of San Antonio de Padua
spots.desc: Pila's Roman Catholic church was built in 1849. Its gray brick exterior contrasts with the red brick belltower. Its interior features an ornate altar, multiple gravestones on the walls containing the remains of Pila's high society, and an exquisite statue of the Christ Child

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish Church
spots.desc: A reconstruction of a Baroque church that was built in 1603 but destroyed during the liberation of the Philippines at the end of the Pacific War in 1945.

spots.name: UPLB Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: Biological & zoological exhibits. Hopefully it won't be a field trip day for all the Metro Manila schools.

spots.name: Santa Rosa Arch
spots.desc: 19th-century welcome arch based on Paris's Arc de Triomphe, with the current arch being Art Deco, built in the 1930s. It is a local symbol, found in the city's official seal.

spots.name: St. John the Baptist Parish Church
spots.desc: Liliw's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style with a red façade and ornate altar in 1578.
spots.addr: Entrances:9th corner Gat Tayaw Streets and 8th corner San Juan Streets (for vehicles), Mabini Street (for pedestrians only), Barangay Pag-asa

spots.name: San Bartolome Apostol Parish Church
spots.desc: A Spanish colonial church dating from 1752. It was built in a Baroque style with Moorish-inspired crenellations, and supporting exterior pillars that seemingly wrap around the structure like a cast. Look for the ornate altar and painted wooden carving of the Final Judgement made by carvers from Paete.
spots.addr: J. Lirio corner Mabini Streets and J. Coronado corner E.A. Fernandez Streets (for pedestrians only); P. Zamora Street (for vehicles), Barangay Poblacion III

spots.name: Our Lady of the Angels Parish
spots.desc: It was first built in 1643, but was repeatedly destroyed by a fire and an earthquake. The present church was built between 1687 and 1700. The church's ceiling and interior dome have paintings of archangels, the Virgin Mary, and symbols of heavenly authority.

spots.name: San Luis Obispo Parish Church
spots.desc: A Baroque 18th century church that has a bone relic of its patron saint.

spots.name: Gala-Rodriguez Ancestral House
spots.desc: It is an Art Deco mansion built by the renowned Filipino architect Juan Nakpil for the opulent Gala and Rodriguez families in 1935. It is one of the three houses in Sariaya declared a Heritage Home in 2008.

spots.name: Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church
spots.desc: A Barn-style Baroque church that forms the center of Sariaya's historic downtown. It was first built in 1599; the present stone church building was built in 1748, to replace one destroyed by earthquakes and flooding.

spots.name: Villa Sariaya
spots.desc: The ancestral home of Don Catalino Rodriguez, built in Bahay na Bato (stone house) style. It was built in 1922.

spots.name: San Ildefonso de Toledo Parish Church
spots.desc: A Spanish-era Baroque church that is was designated in 2001 as a National Cultural Treasure Church by the NCCA due to the five rococo-influenced retablos and wood-carvings depicting the stations of the cross.
spots.addr: M.H. del Pilar Street, Brgy. Katipunan-Bayan

spots.name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
spots.desc: Abucay's main Roman Catholic church, established in 1588 and is the oldest in Bataan. The church also doubled a fortress during the Dutch invasion and was subsequently repaired in the Baroque style.
spots.addr: Bataan National Road corner Laon Road, Laon

spots.name: Saint Catherine of Siena Parish Church
spots.desc: Samal's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish period in the 17th century.

spots.name: St. Martin of Tours Parish Church
spots.desc: One of the oldest churches in Bulacan, established in 1578. The church is the home of the Cross of Wawa, a Catholic relic, which is paraded in the Pagoda Festival. Its pointed-edge altarpieces resemble those in medieval European churches.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Nuestra Señora de la Asuncion
spots.desc: Bulakan's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present style in 1812. Unlike most colonial churches in the Philippines, which are Baroque, Romanesque or even Gothic, Bulakan Church is built in the neo-Byzantine style. At a side chapel to the right of the main doorway is an ecclesiastical museum.

spots.name: Calumpit Church
spots.desc: Calumpit's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 17th century. Its facade resembles a wedding cake due to ornamentations made by local artists.

spots.name: San Miguel Arcangel Parish
spots.desc: Barn-style Baroque Roman Catholic church completed in 1868. It was destroyed by a fire in 1896 amid the Philippine Revolution, but was rebuilt mostly in its original style, although the floor level has been raised due to flooding. Today, the church is an important reference point for both locals and visitors. Its main highlights are the gilded altarpieces and the relic and statues of St. Michael…

spots.name: San Isidro Labrador Parish Church
spots.desc: This is where the carabaos during the feast are made to kneel as tribute to their patron saint, St. Isidore the Laborer. This is a 19th-century baroque church located at the Kabayanan or the downtown area (Poblacion). It is also a famous pilgrimage site in Bulacan during the Holy Week or "Kuaresma". The Museo San Ysidro Labrador with its ecclesiastical collection is also situated here.

spots.name: San Miguel Arcangel Church
spots.desc: San Miguel's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 19th century and used as a garrison by opposing sides during the Philippine Revolution against Spain. It houses a statue of Saint Michael the Archangel that was found in the forests outside town and is believed by residents to be miraculous. It is one of a few churches in the Philippines whose belfry is built above its façade. There is a…

spots.name: Sideco House
spots.desc: A two-story private colonial mansion belonging to one of San Isidro's elite families that served as the de facto presidential palace when it was the capital of the First Philippine Republic in 1899.
spots.addr: P. Carmen corner Vallarta Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Santa Catalina Parish Church
spots.desc: Arayat's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Renaissance style during the Spanish era in 1753.

spots.name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church
spots.desc: Macabebe's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt in its original Baroque style in 1904 after it was burned by nationalist forces during the Philippine-American War in 1899. The arson also saw the massacre of 300 residents accused of treason, which explains Macabebe’s subsequent support for the Americans. Despite its relative youth compared to other colonial churches, the place retains a dated air…

spots.name: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish Church
spots.desc: Masantol's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Renaissance style in 1932 with a façade somewhat resembling a trident.

spots.name: San Bartolome Apostol Parish Church
spots.desc: Magalang's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present style in 1866.

spots.name: Sunken Shrine of Our Lady of Lourdes of Cabetican
spots.desc: A Catholic shrine built in the Brutalist style. It was also buried to its roof by lahar flows from Mount Pinatubo in 1995, but was partially excavated in 2005. The structure lost of its height to the volcanic mud, and its interior, which was partially cleared out, exudes a cave-like atmosphere, with the jungle-like altarpiece also carved from lahar.

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
spots.desc: Floridablanca's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the 19th century and repaired following World War II bombing.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Church
spots.desc: The massive parish church of Guagua proper, with its cupola looming across town. The present barn-style Baroque church and belfry dates to 1772, after the original 1587 building was destroyed by fire. Unlike Betis Church, its interior is painted in austere white, with only the pulpit and altarpiece giving away its Spanish origins.
spots.addr: Aurelio Tolentino Street, Plaza Burgos, Poblacion

spots.name: Santa Catalina de Alejandria Church
spots.desc: A Baroque church dating to 1872. It was damaged during World War II, but was restored in the 1980s. Its four-storey belfry was reduced to three storeys by an earthquake in 2019.

spots.name: Pio Chapel
spots.desc: The first known circular chapel in the Philippines, built in 1861. Damaged by the 1991 Pinatubo eruption and a 2019 earthquake, it was controversially repaired in a DIY manner by locals amid limited funds and lack of advice from conservationists.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of San Andres
spots.desc: Masinloc's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1713 using coral stone. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

spots.name: Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
spots.desc: Rock formations created by forces of the ocean on the rocky coast of Burgos, located just a few minutes from the lighthouse

spots.name: Malacañang of the North
spots.desc: President Marcos' official residence in Ilocos Norte, with a veranda overlooking Paoay Lake. Sequestered by the government following his overthrow in 1986, it was turned into a museum about him and his living conditions, although the exhibits mention nothing about his regime's abuses.

spots.name: Saint James the Great Parish Church
spots.desc: Bolinao's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque and Renaissance style during the Spanish era in the 17th century.

spots.name: Saint Ildephonse of Seville Parish Church
spots.desc: This Roman Catholic church was established in 1746 in a Baroque architectural style.

spots.name: Manleluag Spring Protected Landscape
spots.desc: A pair of hot springs tucked in the Mangatarem forest. Over 90 species of birds call this place home.

spots.name: Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church
spots.desc: Church and convent dating to 1619 in the town of Bayambang, a town founded in the 16th century that was fifth capital of the Revolutionary Philippine Republic and which is known for its Malangsi Fishtival (tilapia grilling festival).

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Patriarch Parish Church
spots.desc: Church dating to 1809 in Aguilar, a municipality named after Spanish governor-general Rafael Maria de Aguilar, who ordered its establishment on 16 July 1805 due to sanguine qualities in the area like mineral water and fertile grounds for rice and cattle cultivation.

spots.name: St. Peter the Martyr Parish Church
spots.desc: Sual's main Roman Catholic church. It retains its original Spanish-era facade despite having been destroyed multiple times throughout its history.

spots.name: Kiangan Shrine
spots.desc: A war memorial commemorating General Yamashita's surrender in 1945.

spots.name: Mariano Hamoy House
spots.desc: The preserved house of Don Mariano Balsomo Hamoy, José Rizal's closest friend during his exile, and their family.

spots.name: Tarsier Research and Development Center
spots.desc: Tarsier (Tarsius syrichta) is one of the world's smallest primates, and it is endemic to Bohol. At the sanctuary, a spacious net enclosure keeps a number of Philippine Tarsiers for feeding, captive breeding and display. Here, visitors can observe the Philippine Tarsier in their natural habitat. Within the sanctuary, the Philippine Tarsiers roam freely and all of them have got used to a…
spots.price: Adult 150, senior or student 120, child under 8 free, includes small trek to viewing decks

spots.name: Agas-Agas Bridge and Adventure Park
spots.desc: The main attraction of the town is the country’s tallest viaduct. The Agas-Agas Bridge zipline or what they call "Zipline Leyte" is a twin zip line and one of the longest in the country gliding diagonally above the bridge and the riverine below it.

spots.name: San Antonino de Florencia Parish Church
spots.desc: The oldest church in Uyugan, built during the Spanish era in 1871 and housing a venerated image of Saint Antoninus of Florence

spots.name: Battle of Noveleta historical marker
spots.desc: At the Calero Bridge in November 30, 1896, Filipino revolutionaries led by General Luciano San Miguel were victorious after killing 400 Spanish soldiers led by General Diego de los Rios.

spots.name: Lumot Lake
spots.desc: A man-made reservoir created in the 1940s as an auxiliary to nearby Caliraya Lake. Like Caliraya, it is a favorite spot for watersports, fishing and camping activities.

spots.name: SM City Santa Rosa
spots.desc: A huge two-storey mall with a vast collection of shops and restaurants, cinemas, a department store, and supermarket. Since 2017, it hosts tower blocks housing call centers. Also at the mall grounds is the SRIT (see #Get in).

spots.name: Kamay Ni Hesus Healing Church
spots.desc: Roman Catholic pilgrimage site on the foot of Mount Banahaw, frequently visited during Holy Week. It houses a replica of Noah's Ark, a healing church, family park and pond. Group tours can be organized from Lucena.

spots.name: Saint Anne Parish and Diocesan Shrine
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in eastern Pagbilao, it is home to a venerated image of Saint Anne. The current church building dates from 1960.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway, Sitio Santa Ana, Silangang Malicboy

spots.name: Higantes Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival featuring a procession of giant papier mache figures, which originated as a satirical protest against corrupt landowners and officials during the Spanish period.

spots.name: SM Center Angono
spots.desc: SM Center Angono is the lone SM supermall in Angono. It houses a collection of stores, a large Savemore supermarket, typical fast-food chains, upscale dining, and a cinema.
spots.addr: Manila East Road corner Quezon Avenue, San Isidro

spots.name: Daranak Falls
spots.desc: Derived from the word "dadanak", which means "to flow", describing the falls.

spots.name: SM City Baliwag
spots.desc: Has numerous restaurants, a SM Store (department store), and a SM Hypermarket.

spots.name: Shrine of Saint Andrew Kim
spots.desc: A Catholic shrine dedicated to Andrew Kim Taegon, a 19th century Korean priest who served in the area before returning to his homeland, where he was martyred for his beliefs. The chapel resembles an East Asian pagoda, while the gardens have been manicured on the same lines.
spots.price: PHP20, parking fees of PHP20 for cars and PHP10 for motorcycles, tricycles and bikes

spots.name: Aglipay Mausoleum
spots.desc: Gregorio Aglipay, the founder of the Iglesia Filipina Independiente, is interred here, at the back of the Aglipayan Cathedral of Saint Mary.

spots.name: Batag Island Lighthouse
spots.desc: A historic lighthouse off the coast of the town of Laoang. The light marks the northeastern point of Samar Island. Built in 1907.

spots.name: Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in the city, built in 1796.

spots.name: SM City San Pablo
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway, Riverina Residential and Commercial Estates, San Rafael

spots.name: Saint Bonaventure Parish
spots.desc: Mauban's main Roman Catholic church.

spots.name: Pililla Wind Farm
spots.desc: The first wind farm outside the Ilocos region.

spots.name: Pateros Church
spots.desc: Spanish-era parish church, completed in 1815

spots.name: Rizal's Relief Map of Mindanao
spots.desc: A landscaping work created by Jose Rizal.

spots.name: Langun-Gobingob Caves
spots.desc: The largest cave system in the Philippines.

spots.name: Presidential Car Museum
spots.desc: Museum featuring land vehicles which were owned and/or used by past Philippine Presidents.

spots.name: Old Executive Building
spots.desc: Built during the American colonial era, the emblems of the United States of America are still seen. It was used as official use of the administration of President Manuel L. Quezon until the Marcos' administration. Today it showcases Filipino history

spots.name: Legarda Ancestral Mansion
spots.desc: Showcases Juan Luna's and Felix Ressurecion Hidalgo's paintings. It has a library, clinic and a room for photography equipment.

spots.name: UP Town Center
spots.desc: Open-air shopping mall built over the former site of U.P. Integrated School

spots.name: Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife Center
spots.desc: Houses a zoological and botanical garden, complete with a man-made lagoon for boating activities

spots.name: Eton Centris
spots.desc: Mixed-used development with a shopping mall, lifestyle strip, and call center buildings

spots.name: SM City San Lazaro
spots.desc: Redeveloped from the San Lazaro Racecourse which has moved to Cavite, it is the only large mall in the district, with more than 300 shops, boutiques and outlets. Has a food court, 6 cinemas, and a department store.

spots.name: Art in Island
spots.desc: Interactive art museum where visitors can pose for a picture with 3D paintings in exhibit.

spots.name: Eastwood City Walk of Fame
spots.desc: The Philippines' answer to Hollywood's, it sports a row of stars used to commemorate famous television, film and radio personalities of the country.

spots.name: Fisher Mall
spots.desc: Mall owned by a fishing business in Malabon, and built over an old bus terminal. This mall has plenty of fast food chains and fast food restaurants, but not as crowded as the major ones.

spots.name: Santa Maria de Mayan Parish Church
spots.desc: Itbayat's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1872 but was reduced to ruins following an earthquake in 2019 and subsequent typhoons later that year and in 2025. The ruins can still be seen pending a proposed reconstruction.

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
spots.desc: Ivana's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1795.

spots.name: Saint James the Apostle Parish Church
spots.desc: Iguig's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1787.

spots.name: St. Francis of Assisi Parish Church
spots.desc: GenTri's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1769 and hosting relics of Saint Francis of Assisi.

spots.name: San Agustin Church
spots.local: Simbahan ng Parokya ng San Agustin
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in 1954, faithfully restored to its original-Spanish era design in 1954 following damage brought about by World War II.

spots.name: Saint Peter the Apostle Parish Church
spots.desc: Apalit's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Renaissance Revival style during the 19th century and featuring exquisite ceiling paintings made by local artists and gravestones of prominent residents on the walls. Its large dome is visible from the North Luzon Expressway.

spots.name: ADD Convention Center
spots.desc: A multi-purpose venue with a 100,000-seat capacity, commonly used by the Members Church of God International (MCGI), a homegrown evangelist Christian sect.

spots.name: San Andres Apostol Parish Church
spots.desc: Candaba's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in the 17th century.

spots.name: San Luis Gonzaga Parish Church
spots.desc: San Luis's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a mix of Baroque and Renaissance styles. The turreted and unplastered brick façade itself is unlike the typical flat church exterior found elsewhere.

spots.name: Bamban Bridge
spots.desc: Connecting Bamban with Mabalacat in Pampanga, this long bridge, built over a tributary of the Sacobia River, is commonly used as a photography and filming location for its distinctive concrete and steel arches.

spots.name: Saint John of Sahagun Parish Church
spots.desc: Candon's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in 1710 and featuring exquisite ceiling paintings. As of 2026, the church is undergoing repairs following structural damage caused by an earthquake in 2022.

spots.name: Saint William the Hermit Parish Church
spots.desc: Magsingal's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish period in 1827. It was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

spots.name: Museo de Iloko
spots.desc: A museum of local history and culture, set inside the old colonial-era municipal building. The first floor is partially leased out as commercial space.
spots.addr: Manila North Road corner Cases Boulevard, Santa Barbara

spots.name: Agoo–Damortis Protected Landscape and Seascape
spots.desc: An extensive protected area along the coast of Agoo featuring a mix of beaches, forest and estuarine wetlands.

spots.name: Saint Michael the Archangel Parish Church
spots.desc: Bacnotan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a combined Baroque and neoclassical style during the Spanish era in 1819.
spots.addr: Guerrero Avenue corner Gabaldon Street, Raois

spots.name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentino Parish Church
spots.desc: Balaoan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1864.
spots.addr: Manila North Road, Dr. Camilo Osias

spots.name: Saint Christopher Parish Church
spots.desc: Bangar's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in the 19th century.
spots.addr: Manila North Road corner Boughton Street, Central East No. 1

spots.name: Santa Monica Parish Church
spots.desc: Panay's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1884. Its main highlight is the church bell, which at 10 tonnes, is dubbed as the heaviest in Asia. There is also an ecclesiastical museum.
spots.addr: Iloilo East Coast-Capiz Road, Poblacion Ilaya

spots.name: Bessang Pass Natural Monument
spots.desc: An extensive combined war memorial, national park, and nature reserve covering the Bessang Ridge. There is a memorial to the Battle of Bessang Pass as well as habitats for various flora, mostly moss and pine trees, and fauna. The Tagudin-Cervantes-Sabangan Road passes right through the area.

spots.name: Mount Tabayoc
spots.desc: The second highest mountain of Luzon and the fifth highest in the Philippines, at . It also forms part of the boundary between Kabayan and the municipality of Tinoc in Ifugao province.

spots.name: BenCab Museum
spots.desc: Art gallery featuring modernist works by National Artist Benedicto "BenCab" Cabrera and other artworks he has collected over the years, including indigenous Igorot crafts, contemporary pieces and even erotica. It also has an on-site cafe and manicured gardens. Flash photography and video prohibited.
spots.price: P200, P150 for elderly and disabled, P120 for students, free for children below 4"2

spots.name: Museum of Philippine Maritime History
spots.local: Museo ng Kasaysayang Pandagat ng Pilipinas
spots.desc: The national museum highlights the Philippines’ maritime heritage, featuring shipbuilding, trade, port activities, and Iloilo’s role as a major trading hub.
spots.addr: Muelle Loney Street cor. Aduana Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Brandy Museum
spots.desc: It is the first and only museum in the Philippines dedicated to brandy.
spots.addr: Festive Walk Road cor. Taft Street, Mandurriao

spots.name: Manila Polo Club
spots.desc: Exclusive: you can't order or get water inside if you're only a guest and not a member. Though there's ample parking inside. Comfort room operating and wheelchair accessible.

spots.name: Centrio Mall
spots.desc: From early November to early January, Centrio holds the Magical Nights of Lights, a music and light show located in the garden where thousands of strobe lights are synchronized to well-known Christmas songs.
spots.addr: Claro M. Recto Avenue at Corrales Avenue

spots.name: Panaad Park and Sports Complex
spots.desc: The park surrounding the stadium is filled with eucalyptus trees.

spots.name: Museum Negrense De La Salle
spots.desc: A university museum with exhibits ranging from indigenous woven textiles, plantation-era furniture, religious vestments, santos, and other devotional objects to rotating works by local and international artists on social, cultural, religious, and political themes.

spots.name: GSIS Building
spots.desc: A significant landmark hosting both the Senate of The Philippines and the Senate Museum. Art enthusiasts can see the GSIS Museo ng Sining (GSIS Museum of Art), which showcases a diverse collection of artworks by Filipino artists from the colonial to contemporary period. The museum not only displays historical pieces but also serves as an exhibition space for contemporary Filipino artists.

spots.name: Serendra
spots.desc: Mixed used development with contemporary decoration and several alfresco cafes and restaurants. It links the Bonifacio High Street to the Market! Market!

spots.name: Bacoor Church
spots.desc: The Spanish-era church was first built in the 18th century, but had to be rebuilt several times due to wars and earthquakes. One of the Gomburza, Mariano Gomez, became one of its parish priests until he was arrested in 1872 for alleged involvement in the Cavite Mutiny and was executed at the garrote in Bagumbayan, Manila. There is a historic marker dedicated to Gomez in front of the convent…

spots.name: San Fernando Station
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Himpilang Daang-bakal ng San Fernando
spots.desc: A restored train station along the abandoned Philippine National Railways northern main line. It served as the endpoint of the 102 km Bataan Death March. The restored station houses a well-preserved wooden boxcar used on the "death trains" that carried surrendered soldiers, both Filipino and American, to the rural municipality of Capas in Tarlac.

spots.name: La Trinidad Strawberry Farm
spots.desc: Strawberry-picking may be done at the strawberry farm which is a popular site for domestic tourists. The site is owned by the Benguet State University.

spots.name: Museo ng Muntinlupa
spots.desc: A city-owned museum dedicated to Muntinlupa's history, from its founding to its cityhood. The museum's exterior is eye-catching, being shaped like a traditional fish trap.

spots.name: Saint Ferdinand Parish Church
spots.desc: Formerly the seat of the Diocese of Ilagan, it houses the oldest bells in the province. The church, save for its belfry, was gutted by fire in 2024 and is undergoing reconstruction.

spots.name: Battle of Alapan National Monument
spots.desc: Houses a giant flagpole with the Philippines flag. This site commemorates the Battle of Alapan, where the Philippine flag was first raised during the Philippine Revolution.

spots.name: Aquino Center and Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to assassinated Senator Benigno "Ninoy" Aquno and his wife, Corazon "Cory", who became the first female president of the Philippiines. They have memorabilia, photos, historic items, murals, books and mementos of the Aquinos. The place is well kept and clean.

spots.name: Luisita Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: Designed by renowned architect Robert Trent Jones Sr., this 18-hole championship course has been renovated so you can enjoy it in any weather, all year round.
