There are water areas all around coupled with great landscaping which is breathtaking. It's quite an easy course although wind is sometimes a factor. It is listed in Golf Magazine's Top 100 Golf Courses in the World. There are no crowds, no…

spots.name: Ilagan Japanese Tunnel
spots.desc: tunnel, once used as a Japanese army headquarters.

spots.name: Mandaue Presidencia
spots.desc: Neo-Grecian style building built in 1947

spots.name: Nasugbu Landing Monument
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Pagdaong sa Nasugbu
spots.desc: It commemorates the landing of American liberation forces on January 31, 1945.

spots.name: The White House (Taal)
spots.desc: The stately American colonial “White House” contains a collection of beautiful hardwood antique furniture and personal artifacts. The house is in very good shape. It is preserved by Don Gregorio Agoncillo Foundation in honor of Gregorio’s daughter, Corazon Agoncillo. It seems closed but when you stand in front of the gate long enough, a caretaker appears, let you in and guides you through the…

spots.name: Saint John the Baptist Parish Church
spots.desc: The church was built in the 18th century but was neglected through much of the 20th century when it was downgraded into a chapel due to the government's decision to move the town center of Kalayaan from Longos to San Juan. After recovering its parish status in 1996, the church was gradually repaired. The church's façade, partially covered by moss complimented by the shrub-lined plaza in front…

spots.name: Tatlong Krus
spots.desc: As suggested by its name, the site features three white crosses which was patterned after the cross in Mount Calvary.
spots.addr: Juan Tinawin Street, Brgy. Nueve (9) Ibaba del Norte

spots.name: Narvacan Church
spots.desc: Narvacan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style.

spots.name: Our Lady of Purification Parish Church
spots.desc: Binmaley's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era.

spots.name: Casa Real
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Ang Casa Real
spots.desc: The preserved house and office of the Spanish politico-military governor during Rizal's four-year exile in the town.

spots.name: Lal-lo and Gattaran Shell Middens
spots.desc: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Various sizes of shell middens carbon dated from 2000 BC to 100 AD

spots.name: SM City Cauayan
spots.desc: Two-story SM mall, with a supermarket, cinema, department store, the first Uniqlo outlet in Cagayan Valley, and branches of national restaurant chains. Parking available at 15 for the first 3 hours (100 beyond that).

spots.name: National Shrine of Our Lady of the Visitation of Guibang
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic shrine dedicated to a venerated image of the Virgin Mary found in the barrio in 1905 and believed to be miraculous. The church celebrates its feast day on July 2, during which the highway in front is closed to motor vehicles and non-visitors are directed to use a bypass road skirting the center of Guibang.

spots.name: San Juan Nepomuceno Parish Church
spots.desc: It used to be a simple chapel of the town, first a barrio of nearby Rosario until it was separated in 1848. The church was first built in 1843, until it was destroyed by flooding in 1883. The present church, built from stone, was from 1890.

spots.name: Divine Word Seminary
spots.desc: One of the biggest schools of theology in the Philippines in terms of population and land area, it is also one of the oldest religious institutions in the city. It is run by Divine Word Missionaries also known as SVD.

spots.name: Alaminos Goat Farm
spots.desc: Buy fresh goat milk and other dairy products derived from goat milk like ice cream, and cheese locally known as kesong puti. The farm was established by local goat breeder Valeriano "Rene" L. Almeda in 2005 who pioneered dairy goat farming in the Philippines.

spots.name: Hermano Pule Monument
spots.desc: A shrine to Apolinario de la Cruz, better known as Hermano Pule, who founded the Cofradia de San José, who fought for religious and civil rights during the Spanish colonial era. Pule lead a rebellion from 1840 until his execution in 1841.

spots.name: National Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of Aranzazu
spots.desc: Built in 1596 under the patronage of Saint Matthew the Apostle. It houses a venerated image of the Virgin Mary. The parish store sells a few themed memorabilia.

spots.name: The Old Town of Dapitan
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Ang Lumang Bayan ng Dapitan

spots.name: Metro Manila Horse Turf Club
spots.desc: An horseracing track at the boundary of Malvar and Tanauan.

spots.name: Sta. Lucia Mall
spots.addr: Marcos Highway cor. Imelda Avenue, San Isidro

spots.name: Mariveles Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Mariveles.

spots.name: Katipunan founding site
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Kataastaasan Kagalanggalang na Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan

spots.name: Tandang Sora National Shrine
spots.desc: A national monument and memorial park dedicated to Filipino revolutionary and centenarian, Melchora Aquino. It covers an area of 1,000 m² and features a 10.67-m bronze sculpture. An art gallery is also hosted within shrine grounds which features paintings and other sculptures dedicated to Aquino. It also has a pavilion and stage for events, and a mini-museum dedicated to Melchora Aquino. It was…

spots.name: 11th World Scout Jamboree Monument
spots.desc: Monument created in memory of the 22 Boy Scouts who perished en route to the 11th World Scouting Jamboree in Greece.
spots.addr: Timog Avenue and Tomas Morato Avenue

spots.name: NHCP Museo ni Ramon Magsaysay
spots.desc: A museum on the life of Ramon Magsaysay, the country's first populist president and the first not to have come from the mestizo elite. Housed in his two-story residence, it showcases his personal possessions and other memorabilia.
spots.addr: Olongapo-Bugallon Road corner Sixto Cacho Street, Santa Maria

spots.name: NHCP Museo nina Juan at Antonio Luna
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to the lives of Juan and Antonio Luna, brothers who originated in the town (Juan was born in Badoc while Antonio was born in Manila where his family moved to) and dedicated their lives to upholding Filipino nationalism against Spanish and American prejudices. Juan excelled in realist and romanticist painting, while Antonio made his name commanding Filipino forces during the…
spots.addr: Juan Luna corner Rizal Streets, Garreta

spots.name: Magalawa Island
spots.desc: With its creamy white sand beaches and pristine waters Magalawa Island is perfect for swimming, water and sand sports, boat riding, jetskiing, scuba diving, snorkelling or just relaxing on the beach amidst the crystal clear waters and white sand. Another attractions of Magalawa Island are coral reefs, mangroves and abundant water resources

spots.name: Candon City Arena
spots.desc: A stadium with a seating capacity of 8,000. Opened in 2023, it hosts national-level competitions for indoor sports such as basketball and volleyball.

spots.name: Almeida Watchtower
spots.desc: A stout, Spanish-era watchtower meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

spots.name: Calle Crisologo
spots.desc: It is what Vigan City is known for — streets lined with Spanish Era ancestral houses (with ancient tile roofs, massive hardwood floors, balustrades and azoteas in varying Spanish, Mexican, and Chinese architectural styles) and cobblestone streets, which led to Vigan's inscription in the list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Tourists can buy souvenirs or even ride a calesa (horse-drawn buggy). This…

spots.name: Session Road
spots.desc: The main thoroughfare of Baguio, where most of the city activity is centered. SM Mall and Burnham Park are walking distance. Take a look at the cool robot sculptures and the mascots that sometimes pass by.

spots.name: Ayala Triangle Park
spots.desc: Behind the Philippine Stock Exchange, the Ayala Triangle Park is surrounded by restaurants and cafes.
spots.addr: Paseo De Roxas Avenue corner Makati Avenue corner Ayala Avenue

spots.name: Palawan Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Center
spots.desc: Formerly the Crocodile Farming Institute, and still referred to by locals as the "Crocodile Farm," is a tourist attraction and a national research institute devoted to crocodiles. About 30 to 40 minutes from the city center, the Croc Farm also has a mini-zoo, which features some of Palawan's endemic species of wildlife. The place is open from about 8:30AM to about 4:30PM. From Rizal Avenue you…

spots.name: Ugong Rock
spots.desc: A 75-foot (22-m) limestone formation in the middle of farmlands and karst forests located near the Underground River. Main activities in the site include spelunking and zip line.

spots.name: Palawan Museum
spots.desc: This is an old museum that is not very well maintained or labeled but which has a number of interesting pieces. It is well worth a visit on a rainy day.

spots.name: Iloilo Customs House
spots.desc: Built in 1916, it is a neoclassical structure designed by American architect Ralph Harrington Doane. It stands as the second largest and second oldest American-era customs house in the Philippines, following those in Manila and Cebu.
spots.addr: Muelle Loney Street cor. Aduana Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Barako coffee
spots.desc: At least two of Calabarazon's provinces, Batangas and Cavite, produce a variety of coffee called kapeng barako. This is neither arabica nor robusta, but a different variant (Coffea liberica) that grows on a tree rather than a bush and has a lower caffeine content. At one time it was a major crop, especially in the area around Lipa; in the late 19th century it was exported, and commanded a premium…

spots.name: Island hop and Snorkel in Hundred islands
spots.desc: Rent a motor banca (pump boat) for the day, hop between islands and snorkel to your hearts content

spots.name: Mestizo District
spots.desc: offers a wonderful glimpse into the Philippines' colonial past. The ancestral houses were mostly built by Chinese traders using a mixture of local, Asian and Spanish architectural styles. Movie fans recognize the streets from the movie Born on the Fourth of July. If someone looks closely, there are still evidence left from the shooting, e.g. signs in Spanish but hastily and thinly painted over…

spots.name: Plaza Salcedo (Luneta Park Musical Dancing Fountain)
spots.desc: west of the cathedral features a 17th-century monument to Juan de Salcedo, and was also the site of resistance leader Gabriela Silang's public hanging in 1763. Also within the site at the lagoon is the Vigan Dancing Fountain. This Korean-engineered attraction is the first of its kind in the country, and rivals the Bellagio Water Fountains in Las Vegas, Nevada.

spots.name: Plaza Burgos
spots.desc: is a favorite hang out for locals and is also used for staging major public events. It has also food stalls selling local snacks, especially the empanada. It is next to Vigan Cathedral and dedicated to the memory of Father Jose Burgos. Depending on the weather, the streets surrounding it (except for the street adjacent to the Empanadaan) are closed off to motorized traffic every Saturday and…

spots.name: Crisologo Museum
spots.desc: used to be the home of assassinated Congressman Floro Crisologo and wife Carmeling, former governor of Ilocos Sur. It contains Crisologo memorabilia.

spots.name: Barangay Pagpartian
spots.desc: Where the great conquistador Juan de Salcedo landed when he arrived in Vigan through the Mestizo River. Also the site of the city slaughterhouse, built during the Spanish Era (for which the barangay is named).

spots.name: Hidden Garden
spots.desc: A wonderland of greenery, with a mini-snack bar nestled in the middle.

spots.name: Quema House
spots.desc: The residence of the Quema family, considered by sociologist Fernando Zialcita as most representative of 18th-century Philippine architectural style.

spots.name: Mindoro Beach
spots.desc: The only seaside tourist spot in the city, just adjacent to Vigan Airport.

spots.name: Simbaan A Bassit
spots.desc: This cemetery chapel found at the southern end of Quezon Avenue has a bell-gable design, the only one of its kind in the Ilocos Region. The chapel's name is an Ilocano term meaning "small church."

spots.name: Museo Nueva Segovia
spots.desc: Just adjacent to the Cathedral is the Archbishop's Palace of the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia, which dates from the 16th century during the Spanish era - the oldest archbishop's residence still in use in the Philippines. It was completed in 1793 after seven years of construction. It features sliding capiz windows and cut-out decorations with floral motifs. It has a back entrance that leads to the…

spots.name: Bantay Watchtower
spots.desc: The belfry of Bantay Church, built during the Spanish era on a hilltop and physically separated from its church as part of its double function as a lookout for pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015. Access to the site has been restricted since an earthquake in 2022 that severely damaged the…

spots.name: Our Lady of Hope Parish Church
spots.desc: Caoayan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in the 19th century.

spots.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria Parish Church
spots.desc: Santa Catalina's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era.
spots.addr: Vigan-Santa Catalina Road, Poblacion, Santa Catalina

spots.name: Vigan City Fiesta
spots.desc: The Bigueños celebrate the Longganisa Festival every January 22 in accordance to the cityhood of Vigan. With a colorful street dancing competition along the Calle Crisologo, this festival features one of the city's products, the very well-known Vigan longganisa. On the 25th, Vigan celebrates its town fiesta in honor to its patron saint, Saint Paul.

spots.name: Viva Vigan! 'Binatbatan' Festival of the Arts
spots.desc: Every first week of May, Vigan plays host to visitors for this festival featuring painting and product exhibits, a calesa parade, and other cultural activities.

spots.name: Semana Santa
spots.desc: St. Paul’s Metropolitan Cathedral is the venue of religious rites during Holy Week. The Good Friday procession features decorated carrozas bearing life-size statues of Spanish vintage. On Easter Sunday, the dawn celebration depicting the Resurrection of Christ, called "Sabet", is a scene to behold.

spots.name: Raniag Festival
spots.desc: A Halloween celebration wherein there are colorful and lighted floats paraded around the city.

spots.name: RG Jar Factory
spots.desc: Vigan is famous for its burnay jars that have been used as storage material for various wares since the precolonial era. This venue makes these jars, which are made of carabao-kneaded clay and fire-blasted in a huge kiln and allows visitors to try their hand in making their own jars.

spots.name: Camangaan
spots.desc: A barangay of Vigan known for its concentration of shops and manufacturers, usually old women, weaving the traditional Ilocano Abel textiles.

spots.name: Vigan Public Market
spots.desc: Visitors can purchase delicacies like Vigan Longanisa (native pork sausages) and bagnet (deep-fried crispy pork); and Ilocano handwoven abel cloth.
spots.addr: Alcantara corner Jose Singson Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Insiang's Empanada
spots.desc: Insiang's is a small street side empanadahan with a couple of tables set up by the sidewalk.
spots.addr: Salcedo corner De Los Reyes Street

spots.name: Diversion Food Bazaar
spots.desc: A variety of food is offered: from local dishes to Korean style, desserts and shakes.

spots.name: Calle Brewery
spots.desc: Cool place in the centre of Vigan serving craft beer and food.

spots.name: Casa Vicente Restaurant
spots.desc: Casa Vicente serves fusion dishes of International and Ilocano cuisine.
spots.addr: V. De Los Reyes and Bonifacio Streets

spots.name: Burnham Park
spots.desc: Go for a walk or go rowing on Burnham Lake. Visit the Rose Garden or have fun with the kids in the Burnham Park Playground.

spots.name: Camp John Hay
spots.desc: This former R&R facility for American military personnel during the American occupation was turned over to the Philippine Government in 1991. Now under the auspices of the Bases Conversion & Development Authority (BCDA), Camp John Hay is a sort of country club complete with an 18-hole golf course, horseback riding and camping, among other activities. A condotel is in operation. Renovations in the…

spots.name: Mines View Park
spots.desc: Enjoy the view of the beautiful mountain scenery with other various attractions... And that's just it. This place is more of a tourist trap. The scenic view is honestly mediocre - with lots of houses dotting the hills; not too breathtaking. There are lots of vendors selling plants and souvenirs. Probably the best place to buy garden plants in Baguio, but there is no need to hastily buy souvenirs…

spots.name: Igorot Stone Kingdom
spots.desc: A contemporary stone attraction made through the traditional method of riprap and reinforced with concrete. Made from the concept of an Igorot child's fantasy of castles, the Igorot Stone Kingdom is meant to showcase Igorot culture and folklore.

spots.name: St. Francis Xavier Seminary Bamboo Educational Demo Farm (Bamboo Sanctuary)
spots.desc: Here you can find a beautiful bamboo sanctuary and demo farm. It was wonderful seeing various species of bamboo.

spots.name: Wright Park
spots.desc: Tranquil natural area full of trees, where visitors can walk, jog or rent horses to ride.

spots.name: The Mansion House
spots.desc: The President of the Philippines summer home features manicured lawns & gardens open to the public.

spots.name: Baguio Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Popular botanical garden featuring a variety of plants & colorful flowers, along with native huts.

spots.name: Philippine Military Academy (PMA)
spots.desc: Located at Fort Gregorio del Pilar on Loakan Road, visitors Philippine Military Academy History, Traditions & General Information to the City of Pines are welcome to explore the grounds, view the cadets performing their drills, and explore the PMA museum and walk around its manicured grounds to see vintage tanks and other historical military weapons.

spots.name: Panagbenga Park
spots.desc: This family-friendly outdoor space has trees, flowers & stone sculptures, plus a butterfly preserve.

spots.name: Laperal White House
spots.desc: Considered to be haunted, this house built in the 1930s houses Filipino bamboo & wood artworks. After Dec 2022, the house has been turned into an upscale fine-dining restaurant called "Joseph's". Ask around if it is still possible to visit without necessarily dining.

spots.name: Baguio Museum
spots.desc: Small museum with displays & artifacts related to local indigenous groups & the history of the city.

spots.name: Valley of Colors
spots.desc: Massive artwork made up of a tightly packed cluster of hillside homes painted in bold colors.
spots.addr: Baguio - La Trinidad - Bontoc Rd, Pico

spots.name: North Haven Spa
spots.desc: Aside from the usual Thai, Swedish and combination massage, you can have a Baguio strawberry, Benguet coffee or Cordillera rice scrub, an indigenous head massage or the Dagdagis or Kolkolis, the region’s traditional foot massage using runo sticks to stimulate the soles of the feet.

spots.name: Good Shepherd Convent
spots.desc: Peanut brittle, strawberry jam, sesame crunch and ube (purple yam) jam. They ration some products to one to two jars per customer only, so if you want to buy lots of products, it might be better to bring everyone with you to buy.

spots.name: Baguio City Night Market
spots.desc: Around 11PM, when the normal hustle of the city cools down, the night market takes to the street. Buy clothes, shoes, and accessories at low prices. Make sure to bring a tumbler of coffee to fight off the cold as you peruse their goods.
spots.addr: Harisson Road, Session Road, and surrounding streets

spots.name: Kurio Gift Shop
spots.desc: Souvenirs: t-shirts, keychains, magnets, notebooks, planners, tumblers, bags, sticky notes, memo pads, greeting cards, etc. Temporarily closed as of September 2023.
spots.addr: 3rd Flr. Porta Vaga Mall, Upper Session Rd

spots.name: Café by the Ruins
spots.desc: Quaint ambience, hearty salads, pastas and juices and good coffee or tea.

spots.name: 113 Wagner Café
spots.desc: Private home dining by reservation only. Book through the link.

spots.name: Jollibee
spots.desc: The most well-known Filipino fastfood chain of all, Jollibee can boast of over a thousand stores in the Philippines and more than 300 stores around the world. Typical fastfood fare for the most part, but the burger dressing will taste different (read: sweet) to most foreigners. For something a little different, try the pancit palabok, which is a vermicelli dish with an orange sauce.

spots.name: Greenwich Pizza
spots.desc: The second of Jollibee corps' trifecta of fastfood chains, Greenwich Pizzas are your typical fare, but once again with the slightly sweeter than usual tomato sauce. Some seasonal offerings may be on offer though, like the sisig pizza, so check the menu.

spots.name: Chowking
spots.desc: The Filipino version of Chinese food, also owned by Jollibee. For good sampling of their food, try the Lauriats, which feature a viand (beef, pork, chicken), rice, pancit (fried noodles with meat and veggies), siomai (dumplings), and buchi (a sweet rice ball covered with a sesame-based coating.

spots.name: Tapa King
spots.desc: Tapaking is where you get the ubiquitous tapsilog (fried beef strips, fried garlic rice, and egg), which is popular breakfast fare, along with other local delicacies.

spots.name: GotoKing
spots.desc: This is a fast-growing chain where you go to get the localized version of congee called goto and lugaw (rice porridge), with different kinds of toppings like chicken, roasted garlic, egg, etc.

spots.name: Mang Inasal
spots.desc: A relative newcomer, Mang Inasal brings a variety of barbecue called "inasal" into Metro Manila from the smaller city of Bacolod (further south in the Visayan region). They offer other grilled meats, and soups like sinigang (a sour, tamarind based soup).

spots.name: Goldilocks
spots.desc: The place to go for your baked treats and sweets like mamon (a spongy round cake), polvoron (a tightly packed powdery treat) ensaymada (bread baked with cheese and sugar), and host of other delicacies for those with a sweet tooth. A must try savory treat is their fresh lumpiang sariwa (light and fresh spring roll with peanut sauce).

spots.name: Victory Central Mall Caloocan
spots.desc: Sprawling mall with 800 shops & eateries, including a food court, plus an indoor amusement center.

spots.name: Pandayan Bookshop (Caloocan Branch)
spots.desc: Pandayan Bookshop, founded in 1993, is a 40-store chain spread across Central Luzon, Cagayan Valley, Calabarzon, and northern Metro Manila. The usual size of our stores is around 200 square meters.
spots.addr: #1403 Rizal Ave Ext, Grace Park East

spots.name: Amber-Caloocan Branch
spots.desc: Takeout restaurant for the best Palabok, Spaghetti, Pichi-Pichi.

spots.name: Greenbelt Chapel
spots.local: Santo Niño de la Paz Chapel
spots.desc: The church is popular for church-goers, most people find it relaxing though because of the park around it. The church is surrounded by trees and a fish and lily pond is on the side of the chapel. The Greenbelt Chapel might be the most relaxing chapel in the Philippines. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is also found here.

spots.name: Ninoy Aquino Monument
spots.desc: Erected in honor of the late Filipino senator, Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino, who was the husband of late Philippines president. Corazon Aquino.

spots.name: Yuchengco Museum
spots.desc: The museum was created to house the art collection of Secretary Alfonso T. Yuchengco, and highlight his distinguished career as a businessman, diplomat, collector, philanthropist, patron of the arts, and advocate for education in the Philippines. The museum’s primary goal is to foster a greater public appreciation of the finest in Filipino and Filipino-Chinese visual arts and creativity. The…
spots.addr: RCBC Plaza, Corner Ayala Avenue and Senator Gil J. Puyat Avenue

spots.name: Filipinas Heritage Library
spots.desc: Has an astounding collection of books that date back to the Spanish period. Serious scholars of the time period will love it, but anyone with even a remote interest in old books and history should give it a visit.

spots.name: Makati Museum
spots.desc: Old colonial building displaying some local historical artifacts & photos.

spots.name: Greenbelt Park
spots.desc: Greenbelt Park is a small park designed to be a complement to the surrounding Greenbelt Malls. An artificial duck pond and stream can be seen here, as well as the Greenbelt Chapel for Catholic services. Greenbelt Park is also a good place to sit, people watch and see the more multicultural side of Metro Manila.

spots.name: Legazpi Active Park
spots.desc: A small, well-kept park along Legaspi Street. On Sunday mornings the Legaspi Market opens, where you can get fresh organic foods, delicacies, sweets and other assorted souvenirs.

spots.name: Salcedo Park
spots.desc: Another small park along Legaspi Street. Similar to the Legaspi Market, on Saturday mornings the Salcedo Market opens.

spots.name: Washington Sycip Park
spots.desc: Compared to Legazpi Active Park this park is far more tranquil with a lot more greenery. The trees are quite lovely, the pond is quaint, plenty of spaces to sit & eat a meal; plus, large enough for a moderate paced walk.

spots.name: Glorietta
spots.desc: It is one of the biggest malls in Metro Manila. Aside from shopping and dining, it has indoor facilities such as a kids' playground and an activity center for concerts and shows. Its tenants include Adidas, Aldo, Cole Haan, Lacoste, Mango, Marks and Spencer, Nike, Puma, and Zara.

spots.name: Greenbelt
spots.desc: The one stop for high-end stores. Dining options include walk-in restaurants and fast food chains; fast food chains are found in Greenbelt 1, while restaurants are located in Greenbelt 2, 3 and 5.

spots.name: Power Plant Mall
spots.desc: A four-level complex in the heart of Rockwell Center that has shops, international and local restaurants, and cinemas.

spots.name: Salcedo Weekend Market
spots.desc: In the heart of the Business Center District is the Salcedo Park. Every Saturday, vendors take over part of the park to sell their specialty items. There are ornamental plants, organically grown vegetables, bakery products, lechon from Cebu, etc. Be sure to come early for the full experience.

spots.name: Jolibee
spots.desc: A growing fast-food chain in the country serving fried chicken, burgers, fries, sundaes, etc.

spots.name: Yellow Cab Pizza
spots.desc: One of the Philippines' most successful pizza franchises that has gained its market share with good value for money, lots of toppings and imported cheese.

spots.name: Sbarro
spots.desc: Yes, it's a chain store but where else are you going to find Chicago-style deep dish? Nowhere. Sbarro's it is. Their pastas are also filling and tasty.

spots.name: California Pizza Kitchen
spots.desc: It is what it is. If thin crust is your taste, head here. Dine in, take away or delivery.

spots.name: Shakey's
spots.desc: Great traditional thin crust pizzas and a family restaurant.

spots.name: Apartment 1B
spots.desc: Comfort foods with a twist, served in a bistro-style setting. Highlights include French onion soup and cream cheese samosas. Though the prices (410 average starter; 670 average sandwich; mains from 690 for Mango BBQ Chicken, to 3,550 for the Steak Frites) come out on the high side of mid-range dining options, Apt. 1B is well worth it.
spots.addr: One Lafayette Square, 132 L.P. Leviste Corner Sedeno St., Salcedo Village

spots.name: Persia Grill
spots.desc: The Legaspi location is directly across the entrance to Greenbelt 5, at the corner of Dela Rosa Street. Highly recommended.

spots.name: Circles Event Café
spots.desc: Offers an array of continental, oriental, à la carte and buffet selections in a relaxing ambiance.
spots.addr: Makati Shangri-La Hotel, Ayala Ave. cor. Makati Ave.

spots.name: Cibo
spots.desc: Italian restaurant with several branches, most notable at Shangri-la Plaza Mall in Mandaluyong and Glorietta 4. Their pasta dishes and panini sandwiches are great. Don't miss the very refreshing fresh red grape shake.

spots.name: Hossein's Persian Kebab
spots.desc: The restaurant was founded in 1985. Serves authentic Indian, Arabian and Persian cuisine. Halal certified. Very overpriced. Go to Persia Grill.

spots.name: Sentro 1771
spots.desc: Casual dining restaurant serving Filipino cuisine. Popular dishes include the tomato and kesong puti (native white cheese) salad, sizzling tofu and corned beef sinigang (corned beef in tamarind broth). They are known for their coffee pie.

spots.name: Old Manila at The Peninsula Manila
spots.desc: Fine French dining. Experience the luxuriousness of the place and its cuisines. Impeccable service and the best food awaits you.

spots.name: Sala
spots.desc: Modern European restaurant. Wonderful fine dining restaurant, with two choices of set menus, attentive and friendly service, and a small and tasteful interior decor.
spots.addr: Locsin Building, 6752 Ayala Ave. cor. Makati Ave

spots.name: UMU Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers authentic Japanese cuisine such as the sushi and sashimi bar, teppanyaki, and bento box.
spots.addr: Dusit Thani Hotel, Ayala Center, Arnaiz Avenue

spots.name: Blackbird Makati
spots.desc: Elegant art deco restaurant with a spiral staircase serving grilled meat, seafood, pasta & curries.

spots.name: Museum Cafe
spots.desc: Kind of a swanky joint. Usually featuring live music. It's common to see well-heeled expats sipping mimosas at noon.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, Ayala Museum, Makati Ave corner Dela Rosa Street (adjacent Greenbelt 3 and 5)

spots.name: University of Santo Tomas
spots.desc: This university is oldest and first university in Asia and the Philippines. It was used as a camp by the Japanese during their occupation where the imprisoned about 10,000 people even though it only can hold 4,000.

spots.name: Bahay Tsinoy
spots.desc: One of Manila's well-known museums; see Chinese biographies and their contributions in the history of the Philippines.

spots.name: Museo Pambata
spots.desc: A children's interactive museum, the first of its kind in the Philippines. Opened in 1994, Museo Pambata is the dream come true of Nina Lim-Yuson, who was inspired by the Boston Children’s Museum to open up a similar facility in Manila.

spots.name: Manila Zoological and Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Has since reopened after heavy renovations. The Manila Zoo covers an area of 0.055 km². Accessible via LRT-1 Quirino station.

spots.name: Club Manila
spots.desc: In a streamlined Art Deco style, the lounge competes with the MIASCOR Lounge for the title of NAIA's best lounge. One of two pay lounges at Terminal 1, it has a Wi-Fi bar, a buffet spread and a shower. The lounge is also known for its large fish tank. Access is free to American Express Platinum and UnionBank Gold and Platinum cardholders, BPI "Preferred Banking" clients, BDO Diamond Rewards…

spots.name: Pacific Club Executive Lounge
spots.desc: The larger of the two lounges at Terminal 3, it has a modern ambiance with ample seating, a large buffet spread and a shower room. Access is free to Priority Pass, DragonPass, BPI SkyMiles Platinum, and Citibank Prestige and PlatinumMiles cardholders, SkyTeam Elite Plus members, and business class passengers flying on Delta Air Lines and KLM.

spots.name: PAGSS Lounge
spots.desc: It has a native feel. Reading materials, a buffet spread and business facilities are available, but no bathrooms. There is a separate buffet with halal-certified food. Access is free to The Club Card, Priority Pass and Diners Club cardholders, BPI "Preferred Banking" clients, BDO Diamond Rewards members, and business class passengers flying Air Niugini, Asiana Airlines, China Airlines, China…

spots.name: Skyview Lounge
spots.desc: Formerly known as the MIASCOR Skyview Lounge, it is known for its tasteful decor and its delicious buffet spread, although the spread is not as plentiful as the MIASCOR Lounge at Terminal 1. While it is the smaller of the two pay lounges at Terminal 3, there's lots of seating and outlets, and it also has a shower. Access is free to Priority Pass, Priority Access Club, AmEx Platinum, Citibank…

spots.name: The Wings Transit Lounge
spots.desc: It has multiple sleeping facilities and is available to the public for a fee. Sleeping facilities include reclining lounge chairs, a small capsule hotel, twin rooms that can fit two people and a single family room that can fit four people. Twin rooms and the family room are outfitted with bunk beds. Access to shower facilities are made available when purchasing a package that includes either a…
spots.price: Lounge Chairs 700; Capsule unit 1000; Twin Room 1800; Family Room 3200 (these rates are for a maximum stay of 7 hours…

spots.name: Bo's Coffee
spots.desc: A local coffee chain known for its large selection of pastries, it has branches at Terminals 1 and 3.

spots.name: Goldilocks
spots.desc: The airport store of the Philippines' largest bakery sells a variety of pastries, pies and sweets, including their famous ensaymada and mamon.

spots.name: Grand Kitchen
spots.desc: Serving traditional Filipino carinderia (traditional eatery) fare, it has branches at Terminals 2 and 3.

spots.name: Jollibee
spots.desc: The Philippines' largest fast food restaurant has branches at Terminals 1, 2 and 3. Serves typical American fast food fare, but with a Filipino twist.

spots.name: Kaishu Express
spots.desc: This restaurant is a sister to Kaishu, said to be one of Manila's best Japanese restaurants.

spots.name: Le Bistro
spots.desc: Known for its entirely locally-sourced sustainable coffee and organic salads and sandwiches, it has branches at Terminals 2 and 3.

spots.name: Little Vin-Vin's
spots.desc: This restaurant serves food in the style of the local carinderias, with branches at Terminals 2 and 4. It is the only restaurant in Terminal 4. Food here, however, is severely overpriced relative to what is being served.

spots.name: Raku Hokkaido Ramen House
spots.desc: A decent Japanese restaurant in Terminal 3 best known for their gyudon and, of course, their Hokkaido ramen. One of the more popular restaurants in Terminal 3, it is often full.

spots.name: Seattle's Best Coffee
spots.desc: Starbucks' sister chain has a branch at Terminal 3. Unlike other dining options at NAIA, prices here are the same as in other Seattle's Best Coffee branches outside the airport.

spots.name: Starbucks Coffee
spots.desc: The Philippines' largest coffee chain is one of the newest offerings at Terminal 1, serving coffee and cold drinks, as well as other coffee shop fare.

spots.name: Tim Horton's
spots.desc: This Canadian doughnut chain has a couple of dozen locations in Metro Manila, including one at Terminal 3's foodcourt. They serve brewed filter coffee, not espresso; many Canadians consider it far superior to Starbucks.

spots.name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast
spots.desc: This Singaporean chain has one of its four branches in the Philippines at the airport, where it serves both its famous kaya toast and a number of traditional Singaporean dishes.

spots.name: Christian Ventures Bookstore
spots.desc: This bookstore, which has stores at Terminals 1, 2 and 4, sells novels, travel guides, maps and periodicals in addition to Christian literature.

spots.name: Cora Jacobs
spots.desc: Known as the "pioneer of Philippine handbag design", its airport store has a variety of items from its collection on sale.

spots.name: National Book Store
spots.desc: The Philippines' largest bookstore has two stores in Terminal 3: one each at the International and Domestic Wings. It has a good selection of books and periodicals, and has a nominal school supplies section.

spots.name: Mixed Lifestyle
spots.desc: A trendy clothing store in Terminal 3, it carries Team Manila merchandise, which make good souvenirs.

spots.name: Preclaro's Souvenirs
spots.desc: This souvenir shop has a variety of Filipino souvenirs, but it is better known for the giant, purple morion (a localized Roman soldier found in Marinduque) statue standing outside the entrance.

spots.name: Tesoro's Philippine Handicrafts
spots.desc: A famous retailer of Filipino handicrafts and souvenirs, it has stores at Terminals 1 and 3.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Airways Parish
spots.desc: This is the official airport church and NAIA is probably the only airport in the country, if not the world, with one. A large statue of the Virgin Mary stands on an island across from the church, at the corner of NAIA Road and Ninoy Aquino Avenue.
spots.addr: Chapel Rd cnr Ninoy Aquino Avenue, Parañaque

spots.name: Shrine of Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus
spots.desc: The church of Newport City and the seat of the Military Ordinariate of the Philippines, it is a popular venue for weddings. Its dome is visible from all parts of the airport complex.

spots.name: Philippine Air Force Aerospace Museum
spots.desc: Founded in 1974 as the Marcos Museum, today it's a modern museum showing the history of the Philippine Air Force and Philippine military aviation, as well as general aerospace science. A collection of historic PAF aircraft is on display outside the museum in the Aircraft Park, including the now-retired F-5.
spots.addr: Andrews Avenue cor. Sales Road, Pasay

spots.name: Villamor Golf Club
spots.desc: Host to the Philippine Masters several times, it is a relatively flat course, but still challenging because of the trees, the terrain and the occasional strong wind. Some golfers claim it to be the best course in Metro Manila.

spots.name: Crocodile Park
spots.desc: The park serves as a breeding center of crocodiles and houses also a small zoo, with daily animal shows on the central stage. Possibilities to feed crocodiles, tigers and some other animals for a fee. Ticket includes an entrance to Butterfly Park (8AM-5PM) and K'Mindanawan Village (not a real village, but one for tourists, fire show on F-Su 5:45PM-6:30PM).
spots.addr: Riverfront Corporate City, Carlos P. Garcia Highway

spots.name: Eden Nature Park
spots.desc: About 50 km from Davao, Eden Nature Park is close to the town of Toril. It's in the mountains so it's cooler than Davao City. It has nice walks, restaurants, horse riding and a Sky-Rider thing and lots more. It's a pretty good day out and well worth the trip from Davao.

spots.name: Jack's Ridge
spots.desc: This was a hangout for Japanese Forces during World War II. It is now a tourist spot in Davao City, where you can have a scenic view of Davao City (especially during the night). There is a restaurant, a pool, bars, cottages, and a trail up and down the ridge, where you can enjoy your stay.

spots.name: Philippine Eagle Center
spots.desc: See the Philippine eagle, one of the largest eagles in the world, and one of the most endangered. The center is home to about 30 Philippine eagles. Aside from eagles, it is also home to other birds and animals as well as raptors in a simulated forest environment.

spots.name: People's Park
spots.desc: A public park located along Legazpi Street. A park where people people gather around, enjoy the stroll crossing bridges,exercising around the walkway which circles the park, seeing man-made waterfalls, beautiful plants, etc. It is more enjoyable as the sun goes down and at the night.

spots.name: San Pedro Cathedral
spots.desc: This cathedral, built in the 19th century, is the city's main cathedral. It is across from City Hall.

spots.name: Shrine of the Holy Infant of Jesus
spots.desc: A shrine that is up a hill with views across Davao in which you can unwind, relax, and reflect. There are mass celebrations once in a while per day. A lot of people visit this place during Sundays.

spots.name: Dabawenyo Museum
spots.desc: No photos except on few recent paintings and a separated room.
spots.hours: 9AM-6PM, closed on Sun and some holidays

spots.name: Forest Hill Resort
spots.desc: One of the most visited inland resorts in Davao city. Has a very nice big swimming pool and is very clean.

spots.name: Camp Holiday Resort and Recreation Area
spots.desc: For the 100 day fee you get the use of swimming pools, nipa huts, open cottages and a seaside veranda. Very clean.
spots.addr: beside Samal Ferry Wharf Samal Island

spots.name: Wake Board Park
spots.desc: One of Asia's largest wakeboard parks. Great place for day trips, or rent locally to extend your stay.

spots.name: Gaisano Mall of Davao
spots.desc: This is the largest Gaisano mall in the Philippines. Cinema tickets from 120 per person.

spots.name: Taco Boy
spots.desc: Mexican food. There are also Taco Boys in Gaisano Mall in Tagum, Matina Centerpoint, Ateneo de Davao University, SM Lanang, SM Ecoland, and Nccc Mall.
spots.addr: JS Gaisano,Gaisano mall of Davao, SM city. Abreeza Mall

spots.name: Albertos Pizza Davao
spots.desc: Garden express pizza. Also does breakfasts. Free delivery with no minimum order required.

spots.name: Jenny Fried Chicken JFC
spots.desc: You find Jenny Fried Chicken fast foods all over Davao city. They also sell grilled chicken for 22, pork chop 25, cassava cake 12.
spots.price: Soft drinks from 12, a cup of rice 8, chicken and rice meal 35

spots.name: Barbecue Boss
spots.desc: Five pork barbecue with all the rice you can eat. Cold beers from 35. Has a garden where you can drink beer at night.

spots.name: Knight's Cafe
spots.desc: Knights Cafe offers a choice of local and Western dishes at its pool side bar and restaurant. WiFi and swimming is free if you buy food/drinks. Feast of Fish&Chips to Kinilaw and from traditional English breakfast to pizza. Good place to meet and get lots of local knowledge.

spots.name: Ellen's Tuna Queen
spots.desc: Serves the original pritong paksiw buntot ng tuna formerly at Petron Bajada, sinigang silik ng malasugui, beef calderetta, laing, kinilaw (tuna), lechon kawali and tuna sisig. Grilled steaks (lamb chops, beef prime ribs, burger steak) are also served. Try the latest Tuna Sisig na Pizza and the creamy halo-halo at its best.
spots.addr: South Street Dbp Village, Matina, Davao City

spots.name: Basti's Coffee
spots.desc: Basti's is a cafe in Victoria Plaza, with an entrance outside as well as through the food court. They brew great coffee, and they ask you to pick between 'mild' and 'strong'. They also have pastries including an interesting durian cheesecake. Davao is a no-smoking-in-public-places city so smokers might find it useful to know that there is an enclosed and air-conditioned smoking section in Basti's.

spots.name: Archdiocesan Shrine of the Black Nazarene
spots.desc: A shrine dedicated to the Black Nazarene located in the heart of the city. The Minor Basilica of the Black Nazarene in Quiapo Church decided to move the replica statue of the Black Nazarene to Nazareno Parish Church, so that Nazarene devotees from Mindanao do not have to travel to Manila for their annual pilgrimage.

spots.name: Santuario Eucaristico
spots.desc: Formerly the Archdiocesan Shrine of the Holy Eucharist, Santuario Eucaristico is a shrine dedicated to St. Peter Julian Eymard, Apostle of the Eucharist. Along the rear, semi-circular wall of the shrine are intricately-designed Mosaic Stations of the Cross, while above the secondary entrances/exits are stained glass windows depicting the Stations of the Eucharist. These stained glass windows are…

spots.name: Carmelite Church
spots.desc: The area surrounding the monastery is also the residence of several religious orders, including the Discalced Carmelites, as well as the St. John Vianney Theological Seminary. Carmelite Church contains an image of the Santo Niño, or Holy Child which is said to be miraculous.

spots.name: Divine Mercy Shrine
spots.desc: Its focal point is a statue of Jesus as the Divine Mercy overlooking Macajalar Bay. The site attracts many pilgrims every Divine Mercy Sunday, one week after Easter Sunday, as well as during solemnities and other feast days throughout the year.
spots.addr: Divine Mercy Hills, PSB-Ulaliman, El Salvador City

spots.name: Gaston Park
spots.desc: A circular park named after Segundo Gaston, a former pre-war Municipal Mayor of Cagayan de Oro, and is a favorite place to unwind for many Kagay-anons, especially during Sundays. This was the site of the first Spanish settlement established in 1622 and was the main plaza during the era, even becoming an execution ground for Spanish criminals. During the Philippine-American War, Gaston Park was a…

spots.name: Du-aw Kagay-an Park
spots.desc: The park was proposed by Mayor Pablo Magtajas after 120 Kagay-anons returned home from the United States and Canada in August 1987, a year following the end of Martial Law. It is also the place where the Birhen sa Kota sa Cagayan de Oro (Our Blessed Lady of the Holy Rosary) was said to have appeared, saving the early settlement from invaders. Every August during the City Fiesta, the park serves…

spots.name: Plaza Divisoria
spots.desc: It was built in the early 1900s as a town divider (hence the name Divisoria) or fire breaker after a great fire that almost burned down the entire town. The park is dedicated to local and national heroes.

spots.name: Vicente de Lara Park
spots.desc: Situated in front of the Provincial Capitol of Misamis Oriental with age-old mahogany trees that provide a therapeutic canopy for the promenades. The park is a popular jogging area during the morning. This is also the site of the Press Freedom Monument and a Sculpture of the Province of Misamis Oriental.

spots.name: Museo de Oro
spots.desc: Exhibits artifacts dug from Huluga Cave, and a repertoire of Bukidnon and Maranao cultures that have survived the ravages of time.
spots.addr: Xavier University-Ateneo de Cagayan, Corrales Avenue

spots.name: Museum of Three Cultures
spots.desc: It houses a gallery of Maranao antiquities from Tugaya, Lanao del Sur; a gallery of ethnohistory which shall display Cagayan de Oro history, Butuan archaeological artifacts, lumad arts and crafts from the Hiligaynon and Manobo cultures, and a treasure of Christian lowland artefacts of Northern Mindanao; and an art gallery and coffee shop promoting the local visual arts of Mindanao.

spots.name: City Museum of Cagayan de Oro
spots.desc: The museum was opened in 2008, but the water tower was completed in 1922, and survived World War II. It houses photos of people who contributed to Cagayan de Oro over the years, and life and events from yesteryear.

spots.name: La Castilla
spots.desc: A museum of Philippine household heirlooms and antiques. This is the Rodolfo and Elsa Pelaez family memorabilia administered by Liceo de Cagayan University.
spots.addr: Liceo de Cagayan University, R.N. Pelaez Boulevard

spots.name: Cagayan de Oro Tourism Showhouse
spots.desc: Showcases the products from Cagayan de Oro and the province.

spots.name: Plaza de Los Heroes
spots.desc: A memorial park dedicated to the heroes of the Three Battles of Cagayan de Oro during the Philippine-American War.

spots.name: Gardens of Malasag Eco-Tourism Village
spots.desc: This is in a reforested area in Malasag Hill. This 7-hectare village has replicas of tribal houses in the region and a panoramic view of Macajalar Bay. It is owned by the government and managed by the Philippine Tourism Authority. The views are well worth the short drive up the hill.

spots.name: Macahambus Hill, Cave and Gorge
spots.desc: An underground cave with a 130 ft circular gorge. The ravine is thick with various species of plants and huge trees. It is the site of the historical battle between Kagay-anons and American soldiers during the Philippine-American War (1900).

spots.name: Catanico Falls
spots.desc: The falls contain huge boulders, rapids, cascading falls and a natural pool.

spots.name: Kagay-an Resort
spots.desc: Previously called Lawndale Spring, it is usually packed with families and groups on weekends lounging in the cold springs.

spots.name: High Ridge
spots.desc: It is open to the public for outdoor picnics, and known for its commanding view of downtown Cagayan de Oro.

spots.name: Monigue Cave
spots.desc: The cave entrance is flowing water from an underground stream.

spots.name: Cogon Public Market
spots.desc: The largest of the city's markets covering a number of blocks. Cogon Market is also the terminal for jeepneys going to far-flung barangays to the south of the city, and those going to Bukidnon.

spots.name: Bigby's Café & Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant chain that has its roots in Cagayan de Oro, Bigby's specializes in international cuisines, with each of its branches displaying memorabilia from around the world.

spots.name: Yakimix
spots.desc: A Japanese, Korean and Chinese buffet restaurant with all you can eat promos.
spots.addr: G/F Cagayan Town Center, Captain Vicente Roa Street at Antonio Luna Street

spots.name: R.T. Lim Boulevard
spots.desc: You can visit the place early in the morning for brisk walking or jogging or in the afternoon for its famed sunset view. You can also spend some time at night eating Balut (a fertilized duck embryo that is boiled and eaten with vinegar and salt).

spots.name: Fort Pilar Shrine
spots.desc: Founded in 1635 as a garrison during the Spanish period, the Fort Pilar serves as a present day open-air shrine. Built as La Fuerza Real de San Jose, the fort is now named after and dedicated to Our Lady of the Pillar, the patroness of the Archdiocese of Zamboanga. Its image is embossed at the altar (which was then an entrance of the fort).
spots.price: Free, although you are encouraged to buy candles for 10

spots.name: Fort Pilar National Museum
spots.desc: Fort Pilar also houses a National Museum branch inside the fort. You can appreciate the glorious past of Zamboanga as a Spanish city here in the museum. It also has record of inhabitants and antique items of the early time. It also exhibits paintings, natural marine life and cultural memorabilia. Excellent air conditioning.

spots.name: Old Normal School Building
spots.desc: Also known as the Western Mindanao State University (WMSU) Social Hall, the building was built during the American Era and was the center of education for most of Mindanao. It houses the College of Education of WMSU and is also the site where most cultural presentations are held. It also houses a museum.

spots.name: Pasonanca Park
spots.desc: Traversed by a gently rippling stream, this park is the only one of its kind in the country. It abounds with trees, flowering plants, ferns, shrubs and 600 different species of orchids. Mindanao Governor John J. Pershing started the construction of Pasonanca Park in 1912. He sent for a parksman in the United States, Thomas Hanley, to prepare the plan and direct its execution. There is a treehouse…

spots.name: Plaza Pershing
spots.desc: Plaza Pershing honors American general John Joseph "Black Jack" Pershing (1860 –1948) who defeated Muslim insurgents in the region.

spots.name: St. Ignatius of Loyola Parish Church, Tetuan
spots.desc: Records shows that at the start, there was a small chapel constructed on a lot. Owned by Don Balbino Natividad, a permanent resident of Tetuan. (The Natividad is one of the biggest clans in the Parish spread throughout the city up to the hinterlands and reputed to be large property owners. Members held various positions in the government and parishes. At least one became a Jesuit priest.) In…

spots.name: Sta. Cruz Island
spots.desc: The Great Santa Cruz island is known for its pink sand beach and sand bar, while the Little Sta. Cruz Island is a typical white beach, with pulverized-like sand. It is also a diving site and is host to a lagoon, a Muslim burial site and a badjao/samal community.
spots.price: Environmental Fee: P20 + P5 (Terminal Fee) Boat Fees: P1000/boat (good for up to 10 pax) Cottage Rental Fee: Small (10…

spots.name: Yakan Weaving Center
spots.desc: Host to the only Yakan community in the city, the center is just across the famed La Vista de Mar beach resort at the border of Barangay Upper Calarian and Sinunuc and along the National Highway. You can witness the local people weaving intricately hand-woven clothes on giant looms as well as traditional brasswares.

spots.name: Zamboanga City Hall
spots.desc: The construction of this building started in 1905 and it was completed in 1907, built by the US government for the American Governors of the area. Today, this serves as the City Hall of Zamboanga City where the Mayor holds office.

spots.name: Zamboanga Golf Course and Beach
spots.desc: Known to be the "oldest golf course" in the Philippines. It was established during the American Occupation and is overlooking the Basilan Strait. It also is host to a public swimming resort managed by the Philippine Tourism Authority.

spots.name: Bathe in Pasonanca's natural pools
spots.desc: Bathe in Pasonanca's natural swimming pools- where water flows freely from the mountains to 3 pools- Rotary Pool, Wee-wee Pool for Kids, Tanada Pool.

spots.name: Sta Cruz Island
spots.desc: Swim and scuba diving in a pink sand beach in an unspoilt island

spots.name: Visit Abong Abong Park
spots.desc: Climb the hill and do the Stations of the Cross during Holy week or any day of the year, visit the Scout Camps, the tomb of the unknown soldier and Mayor Cesar C. Climaco.

spots.name: Mangroves Boat Tour (Sta. Cruz Grande Island)
spots.desc: While Grande Santa Cruz Island allures with its pink radiance, its beauty goes beyond appearances. It also keeps a trove of natural wonders. On the other side of the island is a lagoon fully adorned with mangroves, nourishing wildlife and promoting biodiversity.
spots.price: Boat to Yellow Boat Tour Jump-off: P300/boat (up to 10 pax) Yellow Boat Rental: P300/boat (good for 2 pax) Tour Guide…
spots.addr: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)

spots.name: Vinta Rowing
spots.desc: The vinta is the traditional outrigger boat that is common in Mindanao, especially in the areas of southern Mindanao, Sulu archipelago, and the Zamboanga peninsula. It is famous for its vividly colorful rhombic sail, adding a splash of color to the waters of Sulu Sea.
spots.price: P300/boat (good for up to 10 pax) P100 (good for up to 10 pax)
spots.addr: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)

spots.name: Little Sta Cruz Island & Sandbar
spots.desc: Sitting northwest of Santa Cruz Grande Island, Little Santa Cruz Island is like a quick dash of paradise off the coast of the Zamboanga peninsula. The most recognizable feature of the island is the sandbar trailing on the easternmost point.
spots.price: P300/boat (good for up to 10 pax) P100 (good for up to 10 pax)
spots.addr: Paseo del Mar (Santa Cruz Island Ferry Terminal)

spots.name: Once Isla Cruise (11 Islands)
spots.desc: A steadily rising tourist attraction is Once Islas (11 Islands), a string of islands and islets off the eastern coast of Zamboanga City. Not all islands are open to the public, but those that are accessible are great for swimming, sunbathing, and further exploring. There are designated snorkeling spots for those who want to take a peek into the underwater scene. Bisaya-Bisaya, Baung-Baung, and…
spots.hours: Mon-Thu Sat Sun 7AM – 3PM; Fri closed; the schedule might change without prior notice, so check first before going

spots.name: La Vista del Mar Beach Resort
spots.desc: A private resort popular with city dwellers, close to downtown. It has well-manicured and lushly-appointed gardens and a beautiful view of the Basilan Straight water and Santa Cruz Islands in the distance. The resort owners need to do a better job at cleaning the beach sand daily, along with the water that sometimes get covered with garbage in some areas from leftovers by picnickers.

spots.name: KCC Mall de Zamboanga
spots.desc: The biggest mall in Zamboanga with a wide variety of shops. Huge indoor mall near the airport featuring a variety of stores, casual eateries, and a cinema.

spots.name: ABC Bakery and Restaurant
spots.desc: This bakery is one of the cleanest bake house in Zamboanga City. Their Pan Mongo is designated by the Department of Tourism as pasalubong ng bayan for tourists who visit the city.

spots.name: Alavar's Seafood House
spots.desc: Beyond the extraordinary cuisine, Alavar Restaurant provides a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects the unique spirit of Zamboanga.

spots.name: Village Family Restaurant Zamboanga
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in Filipino cuisine. Good grilled chicken, garlic rice and sisig will impress you at the first bite. Village Restaurant has good beer among its drinks.

spots.name: Island Bubble Tea
spots.desc: Pearl Shakes (25 flavors), Belgian waffles, fries. Perfect place to have merienda. Wi-fi zone.

spots.name: Myrna's Bakeshop
spots.desc: Serves delicacies like cakes, pastries, pasta and drinks (coffee and shakes).

spots.name: Taza Coffee Company
spots.desc: The only specialty café and coffee roaster in Zamboanga City
spots.addr: Makenter Building, Mayor Jaldon Street, Barangay Canelar

spots.name: Iwahig Penal Colony
spots.local: panandang pangkasaysayan ng Iwahig Penal Colony
spots.desc: A good example of a true correctional institute, the Iwahig Penal Colony is more of a farming community rather than a prison. Inmates often live with their families and are allowed to toil their farms to earn a living. Carving out handicrafts is also a common preoccupation and mahogany handcarvings are a good buy for tourists. The colony is about 35 minutes from the city center.

spots.name: Butterfly Garden
spots.desc: With native Palawan butterflies is about half-way to the Croc Farm (above) and along the same road. Open 7 days a week from 8AM to 5PM. Entry is 50.

spots.name: Our Lady of Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: A very beautiful church that is decorated in blue and white.

spots.name: White Beach
spots.desc: The only beach in town. Not as clean as it used to be and no longer white or pristine. But if you want to meet some of the locals and have a few drinks (alcoholic) then it's a great place. Just walk down and buy a few beers from the take away store and walk around the huts and you will be invited to join a group at a table. Lots of fun for an international traveller - if you have a great time…

spots.name: Rizal Avenue
spots.desc: Puerto Princesa's main commercial strip where one can find various shops, banks, restaurants, and budget inns.

spots.name: Langogan Reef
spots.desc: New Coral reef protected by city ordinance and three falls, the largest of which is around 50 m, 5 km from the barangay.

spots.name: PSU Museum
spots.desc: This is a one room museum located inside a university building. You should ask for specific directions at the front gate, because not everyone knows about the existence of the museum. The museum is located in one small room but is clean, organized, and well-maintained, with an enthusiastic and helpful staff member.
spots.hours: Closed from noon to 1PM for lunch

spots.name: Plaza Cuartel
spots.desc: Historical place, a must see site. It is the restored ruins of an old garrison where Japanese soldiers burned 143 American prisoners of war inside a tunnel and stands as a grim reminder of World War II.

spots.name: Robinsons Mall
spots.desc: It has a Robinsons supermarket. There is also a food court, bakeries, and assorted electronics stores.

spots.name: A&A Seafood Palace
spots.desc: Seafood prepared by a Hong Kong chef. Authentic Chinese cuisine.

spots.name: Ditchay's
spots.desc: French cuisine and can be a very welcome alternative for those longing to eat something else than local food after a long trip. The little restaurant lets you dine in intimate ambiance while you may chat to both the cook and the owner. The menu includes a variety of French foods like coffee & tea, paté rillettes, confit, soupes, salades, tapenades, grillades, fruits de mer, porc, boeuf, poulet…
spots.addr: Manalo Ext. before Island Divers, Bancao Bancao

spots.name: Divine Sweets
spots.desc: Great cakes (45-90), coffee, shakes, etc. They also serve food (untested). Wifi if you order

spots.name: Kinabuchs Grill and Bar
spots.desc: A sports bar and grill and a magnet for tourists and other visitors. The food is really good and customers can play pool or watch live sports.

spots.name: KaLui Restauran
spots.desc: Amazing food and ambiance. Can get quite busy so a reservation can't hurt. Seafood is the specialty and the daily seafood special for two is 395.
spots.hours: Opens at 6PM for dinner, closed some holidays

spots.name: Artisan’s
spots.desc: Owned by a British expat and his Filipina-American stepdaughters.

spots.name: Carpe Diem Villas & Resort Restaurant
spots.desc: Open-air restaurant set in a tropical garden inside Carpe Diem Villas & Resort. Serves French-inspired dishes alongside Filipino and international options, with a daily breakfast buffet, à-la-carte lunch and dinner, and cocktails. Open to both hotel guests and outside visitors. Walk-ins are welcome.
spots.price: Breakfast buffet ₱750; approximately ₱400–1,500 per person for lunch or dinner
spots.addr: F. Ponce de Leon Road, San Pedro, Puerto Princesa, Palawan 5300

spots.name: Cafe Nori
spots.desc: Serves Japanese cuisine with fusion and variety of Filipino and American cuisine. Also available are fruit shakes, coffee & frappuccinos.

spots.name: Reggae Pulse Bar
spots.desc: Cool reggae bar serving ice-cold beers, beer towers/buckets, cocktails and mixed drinks. Free WiFi, a stylish & relaxing VIP bamboo lounge.

spots.name: Danao Adventure Park
spots.desc: Extreme/eco/educational adventure park that offers various activities for all ages. It boasts a sky-ride, zip-line, river tubing, caving and trekking activities.
spots.price: Rates vary depending on choice of package or activity

spots.name: Rizal Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Paintings and sculptures by local artists and antiques donated by wealthy Cebuanos.

spots.name: Yap-Sandiego Ancestral House
spots.desc: Another historic house, this one from the 17th century, with hand-carved furniture and a garden. It does indeed look old/cryptic.

spots.name: Jesuit House Museum
spots.desc: Yet another heritage house museum, this one the residence of a Jesuit from around 1730. Inside looks like a Spanish galleon.

spots.name: Sugbu Chinese Heritage Museum
spots.desc: Small exhibit hall on Chinese heritage in Cebu. This building (the Gotiaoco Building), also has a mural of the Magellan's Cross shrine and other Cebu highlights on its backside.

spots.name: Heritage of Cebu
spots.desc: A massive and particularly detailed monument showcasing the heritage of Cebu from the old Spanish to the American colonial era.

spots.name: Jumalon Butterfly Sanctuary And Art Gallery
spots.desc: Where you can go to see Lepidoptera and other entomology exhibits, including a butterfly and art garden, although it's pretty scrunched in to an urban environment.

spots.name: Temple of Leah
spots.desc: Neo-grecian temple built onto the mountainside to memoralize Leah Villa Albino Adarna, the wife of a local entrepreneur family and grandmother of actress Ellen Adarna. Also contains displays of upper-class furniture and souvenirs from their travels.

spots.name: Tops Lookout
spots.desc: This sits at the top of the Mt Busay and has an unobstructed view of the entire city at night. A few shops and restaurants stand along the way for a short stop. Taxi drivers may want as much as 1000 for a trip to Tops, so the best way to get there is by mountain bike. This is a world class climb and on any given day, Cebu's bikers are humping the 45-minute to 1-hr trek filled with switchbacks and…

spots.name: Sky Experience Adventure
spots.desc: The tallest building in the city. Adventure seekers may head to the top floor to experience a breathtaking view of this modern city and its environs. You may also opt to join in the Xtreme Rides that puts you on the edge of the city, or you may walk around the edge of the building (don't worry, safety cables are attached) to experience this for a fee.

spots.name: Abellana Cebu Sports Center & Public Swimming pool
spots.desc: Full-size Cebu City Council-run outdoor swimming pool 50 m by 25 m. Has ten lanes. There have been reports of people getting ear infections using this pool.
spots.addr: 179 R R Landon Road off Osmmena Blvd

spots.name: Robinson Mall Fuente
spots.desc: A bakery on the ground level is popular for coffee. The mall has a food court and supermarket.

spots.name: Elizabeth Mall
spots.desc: Has a supermarket, travel agents, cellphone shops, and lots of places to eat.

spots.name: Colonnade Mall
spots.desc: The biggest air-conditioned mall in downtown Cebu. Has a discount supermarket, two bake shops, bank, two money exchanges, many cell phones shops, a pharmacy, a food court and a two-screen cinema.

spots.name: HSBC Bank (UK)
spots.desc: Has the only Mastercard and Visa card ATMs in Cebu without a fee for overseas cards. Also the only ATMs in Cebu where you can take out up to 40,000 per time.
spots.addr: G/F Philamlife Center, Cardinal Rosales Avenue corner Samar Loop

spots.name: Fully Booked
spots.desc: A modern bookshop with a good selection of imported fiction and non-fiction books, a smaller collection of books about the Philippines and an in-shop café.

spots.name: National Book Store
spots.desc: Bookshop chain with local and foreign books, academic texts and stationery.
spots.addr: Locations: Ayala Center, Mango Avenue; and SM City Cebu

spots.name: Book Sale
spots.desc: Used books and magazines, mostly imported from the UK & US. It may take some searching but there are often gems to be had.
spots.addr: Locations: Elizabeth Mall; Park Mall; Robinsons, SM City, Gaisano

spots.name: Robinsons Fuente food court
spots.desc: Lower ground floor near the supermarket. Good bakery and coffee shop.

spots.name: Ayala Terraces
spots.desc: Many restaurants including several foreign chains such as Burger King, Army-Navy, Starbucks and TGI Friday's, Filipino chains, and many non-chain places.

spots.name: Alberto's Pizza
spots.desc: Offers a good and rather affordable locally made thin crust pizza. Has branches all over Cebu.

spots.name: S & R New York Pizza
spots.desc: Freshly baked New York-style pizza, fried chicken, cheeseburgers and fries, salads.
spots.addr: Ayala & SM City Malls & Tafa East Gate Tower

spots.name: The Philly Sports Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: An expat sports bar, serving Western & Filipino food. Excellent choice of imported beers & ciders from Europe in their beer garden. Happy hours beer is from 45. Very good English breakfast for 199 pesos.
spots.addr: 53 AJ King Bulg General Maxilom Avenue

spots.name: Our Place Pub & Restaurant
spots.desc: Established 1978. Meet other expats from all over the world. Good British & European food at a great prices. Sells beer for only 70.

spots.name: Price Mansion
spots.desc: CAP Building served as the residence and headquarters of General Douglas MacArthur for three months.

spots.name: Philippine-Japan Commemorative Peace Park
spots.desc: Stone's throw away from city hall. It was donated by the Tokyo Survivors Associations in honor of soldiers and paramilitary personnel who perished in the area.

spots.name: The Maria Kanon Madonna of Peace Shrine
spots.desc: Near the city hall. Carved out of a rare Miyagi rock and fashioned by Japanese sculptor Shiniche Tani.

spots.name: Calvary Hill
spots.desc: Larger than life statues of Jesus Christ and other personages, in tableaux, depict Christ's sacrifice and sufferings.

spots.name: San Juanico Bridge
spots.desc: It is one of the longest bridges in the Philippines. It connects the city to the third biggest island of the Philippines, Samar. The bridge spans 2.14 km and is one of the major tourist spots in the city.

spots.name: The People's Center and Library
spots.desc: It houses volumes of books from the US and Europe and other countries.

spots.name: Subiran Regatta
spots.desc: It is a race of one-man native sailboats with outriggers locally called "subiran" along scenic and historic Leyte Gulf. The race is done without using a paddle but only skills and techniques to manuever the sail.

spots.name: Iron Dinosaurs (vintage steam locomotives)
spots.desc: Locomotives were used in Bacolod to transport sugarcane from the fields to the azucareras (sugar factories), thus they were part of making Bacolod the sugar bowl of the Philippines.

spots.name: Bacolod City Hall
spots.desc: A modern civic building with a neoclassical-style facade, including prominent columns and a large fountain in front.

spots.name: St. Jude Thaddeus Shrine
spots.desc: This relatively new church is dedicated to St. Jude Thaddeus, patron saint of lost causes. It is notable for its richly decorated, gold-toned Baroque-style altar, ceiling mural, and Divine Mercy shrine.

spots.name: Carmelite Monastery
spots.desc: This Carmelite church and monastery is known for its quiet, contemplative atmosphere. Visitors may leave prayer requests, and the monastery also has a shop selling religious items and souvenirs.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Church and Seminary
spots.desc: This church is notable for its European-inspired architecture, high ceilings, and tall spire, which give it a Gothic Revival look. It also has side chapels dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Barangay Sang Birhen Parish Church
spots.desc: This chapel, designed by Archbishop Norman Campus, is notable for its extensive shellwork. It features Leticia Sia Ledesma’s Barangay Sang Birhen ("Village of the Virgin"), a mosaic made from 95,000 shells, as well as other shell-made images of saints, Stations of the Cross, and altar pieces created from a further 30,000 shells.

spots.name: Pope John Paul II Monument
spots.desc: Marks the site where Pope John Paul II celebrated Mass for thousands of Bacolodnons.

spots.name: Negros Museum
spots.desc: Housed in the former Provincial Government building, The Negros Museum traces the history of Negros Occidental from its beginnings through the colonial era, the rise of the sugar industry, the revolution, and the province’s cultural development. It also features material on past governors and murals by Negrense artists, and serves as a venue for exhibitions by Filipino artists.

spots.name: Bacolod Art District
spots.desc: A city block with art galleries, restaurants, and cafés. The galleries showcase the work of local artists.

spots.name: Christmas Village
spots.desc: This private display is the result of many years of collecting figurines and related items. Its miniature Christmas village features intricate hand-painted details, including cliffs, lakes, and mountains, all made by the owner. Photography is not allowed, but souvenir photos and postcards are available.
spots.addr: San Juan St and San Sebastian St

spots.name: Negros Forests and Ecological Foundation Inc.
spots.desc: A movement of concerned citizens to conserve the forests of Negros Island as well as animals that are under threat of extinction. Visit the foundation and see their rare warty pigs, leopard cats, spotted dear, bleeding heart pigeon and many more animals, most of which are endangered. Help the foundation by adopting an animal or tree, or by becoming an NFEFI volunteer.

spots.name: Mt. Kanla-on Natural Park
spots.desc: A possible day trip, this is a nature park surrounding the Kanlaon Volcano. Many waterfalls and a spectacular area for birdwatching, featuring species such as the bleeding-heart pigeon and the endangered Negros fruit dove.

spots.name: Bacolaodiat Festival
spots.desc: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) celebrated by the Filipino-Chinese community in Bacolod. This is held in the Provincial Lagoon. Bacolaodiat is derived from the words "Bacolod" and "Laodiat"; a Hokkien word meaning "Celebration".Rows of stalls serving Chinese cuisine form "chopsticks alley". Live bands play, there are displays of Chinese culture, and a cookfest is also held.

spots.name: Holy Week
spots.desc: This religious event is held either in March or April is considered as one of the most important events in Christianity. Witness Cenaculo/Senakulo reenactments of the Passion of Christ, Du-aw — a Hiligaynon tradition of veneration of Christ's Crucifix and his Dead Body and Visita Iglesia — a Catholic tradition of visiting 7 churches and praying at each church.

spots.name: Panaad sa Negros
spots.desc: Held annually in either March or April in Bacolod, is considered as the "mother of festivals" in the province of Negros Occidental. It represents the festive nature of the Negrense, commences with a mass, which is then followed by banners and displays of every town and city in Negros Occidental, and showcases of provincial products, from food to handicrafts. Firework displays at night also are…

spots.name: Negros Occidental Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: This golf club has 18-holes, with a panoramic view of the Mount Mapara and Patag.
spots.price: 18 holes: 2200 weekdays; 3000 holidays/weekends. 9 holes: 1650 weekdays; 2300 holidays/weekends. Caddie and umbrella…

spots.name: Yuang Thong Temple
spots.desc: A Mahayana Buddhist temple. If you haven't seen Tai chi before, this is your chance.
spots.hours: Tai chi sessions on Sundays from 07:00 to 08:30

spots.name: Caribbean Water Park
spots.desc: This water park features Negros Occidental’s first and largest water slide. It has a main pool, a kiddie pool, a jacuzzi, two large slides, and a pirate-ship replica for children to explore. Function rooms, locker rooms, huts, and air-conditioned rooms are also available for rent.

spots.name: Buro-Buro and Bocal-Bocal springs
spots.desc: Located just outside of Bacolod, the Buro-Buro and Bocal-Bocal springs are popular for their cool spring water despite the name Bocal-Bocal, which suggests boiling. The site has both an artificial swimming pool and a natural pool, as well as small waterfalls near the main pool where visitors can sit under the falling water. Huts are available for rent, and the area is popular for family outings…

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: A good option for affordable souvenirs such as local handmade products, sweet delicacies and uga (dried fish). Be sure to bargain.

spots.name: Libertad Market
spots.desc: Great place to buy fresh fruit and produce, particularly at its eastern corner.

spots.name: Ayala Malls Capitol Central
spots.desc: Another popular mall, right behind the Provincial Capitol, it features multiple restaurants, a supermarket, and a small park right in front of the entrance.

spots.name: 888 Chinatown Mall
spots.desc: Sells dirt-cheap goods, such as imitation name-brand clothing.

spots.name: SM City Bacolod
spots.desc: The largest mall in the city. Just like any other SM Supermall in the Philippines, it has its large department store, grocery store, famous brand stores, restaurants, and a cinema. It is also one of the few SM malls of the country that has its own convention center.

spots.name: ANP Hub
spots.desc: Sells high-quality local handicrafts, albeit at higher prices.
spots.addr: S Capitol Rd and Gatuslao St

spots.name: Jojo Vito Designs Gallery
spots.desc: Locally made maskara, lighting, wall art, furniture, refrigerator magnets, etc. You can even paint your own maskara!

spots.name: Bong Bong's Pasalubong
spots.desc: More popular than Merci Pasalubong, however they have fewer products. Their specialty is their piaya and barquillos. They have many locations in Bacolod.

spots.name: Merci Pasalubong
spots.desc: Merci's specializes in piaya, biscocho, and napoleones. They have a number of locations around Bacolod.

spots.name: Manokan Country
spots.desc: A row of stalls and restaurants serving cheap local fare, and the home of the original chicken inasal recipe.

spots.name: Ting-Ting's Native Restaurant
spots.desc: Bacolodnon cuisine. The place is open air and fresh air fills the open air area which is suitable for brunches and lunches.

spots.name: Pala-Pala Market
spots.desc: Buy fresh seafood in the wet market then go to a restaurant nearby and have it cooked. From oysters to crabs to blue marlins.

spots.name: Calea
spots.desc: Residents of Iloilo take the trip to Bacolod just to taste their irresistible cakes.

spots.name: Cafe Bobs
spots.desc: Must-tries include their gelato, mini-cakes, and coffee-shakes.

spots.name: L'Kaisei Express
spots.desc: L'Kaisei has a smaller branch in SM City Bacolod Mall which is much more accessible and affordable. Serves typical Japanese cuisine, sushi, and bento boxes.

spots.name: Kuppa
spots.desc: Their Spanish chocolate and milk is delicious. The gelato is worth trying too.

spots.name: Mu Shu
spots.desc: Restaurant and bar that serves Asian fusion cuisine. Try their pritchon or pritong lechon. Has a good sampling of Southeast Asian dishes such as pad Thai, Hainanese chicken, and nasi goreng.

spots.name: Quan
spots.desc: Quan's is a one stop shop for local delicacies, from napoleones to kutsinta. They also serve meals such as ciabatta pizzas and lasagna.

spots.name: Bob's
spots.desc: One of the oldest restaurants in Bacolod, the restaurant serves authentic Filipino cuisine within a beautiful interior.

spots.name: Italia Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves pizza straight from the brick oven, as well as a range of pasta dishes and steaks. Also offers a good variety of fine wines. Italia is a regular venue of several art exhibits of both local and national artists.

spots.name: 21 Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves authentic Filipino cuisine including great seafood which is harvested from a specially-built aquarium.

spots.name: Cafe Uma
spots.desc: Pricey, but the portions are large and delicious. Serves international cuisine.

spots.name: L'Kaisei
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant with reasonable prices and a relaxed atmosphere.

spots.name: Gypsy Tea Room
spots.desc: Beer, cocktails, and appetizers are served here. Shisha is also available, along with henna, tattooing, and palm reading, giving the place a Middle Eastern feel.

spots.name: Mu Shu
spots.desc: By day an Asian restaurant, by night a nightclub, as chairs and tables are moved aside to create a dance floor; dancing often continues until sunrise.

spots.name: WaterWorld Iloilo
spots.desc: The first and largest waterpark in Western Visayas, it offers a fun and refreshing getaway for families and friends. It features thrilling water slides, wave pools, and play areas for kids, making it an ideal destination for all ages.
spots.addr: Datu Sumakwel Street, Alta Tierra Village, Jaro

spots.name: El Dorado Waterpark
spots.desc: A family-friendly waterpark with pools designed for both kids and adults. Guests are welcome to bring their own food and drinks, making it perfect for picnics and casual weekend outings.

spots.name: Vertex Bouldering Iloilo
spots.desc: The first indoor climbing gym in Iloilo City, it offers a challenging yet beginner-friendly space for those who want to experience the thrill of wall climbing. It’s a great place to train, exercise, and meet fellow climbing enthusiasts.

spots.name: Iloilo Golf Driving Range
