spots.desc: A relaxing spot to practice your golf swing, this driving range caters to both beginners and seasoned players looking to sharpen their skills in a laid-back environment.

spots.name: Iloilo Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: Known as the oldest golf course in the Philippines, this beautifully maintained 18-hole course offers scenic greens and a peaceful atmosphere. Although located outside Iloilo City, it’s easily accessible via jeepneys, taxis, and private vehicles, making it a convenient escape for golf enthusiasts.

spots.name: Deca Wakeboard Park
spots.desc: It offers an exciting wakeboarding experience for both beginners and pros. It’s situated just outside Iloilo City but remains easily accessible by public and private transport. The park also provides training sessions and a relaxing area for spectators.

spots.name: The Boat Club Iloilo
spots.desc: A riverside leisure spot where visitors can dine, relax, and enjoy scenic cruises along the Iloilo River. Private boat rentals and chartered trips are available, including leisure cruising and selected trips toward the Iloilo Strait and Guimaras.

spots.name: SM City Iloilo
spots.desc: The largest shopping mall in Iloilo City under the SM Supermalls chain, featuring a wide range of local and international retail stores, a department store, supermarket, cinemas, food courts, and numerous dining options. It serves as a major lifestyle and entertainment hub, conveniently located near the Iloilo Business Park and transport terminals.

spots.name: Festive Walk Mall
spots.desc: A modern lifestyle mall within the Iloilo Business Park, known for its open-air Festive Walk Parade, high-end shops, cafés, and nightlife spots, managed by Megaworld Lifestyle Malls.

spots.name: Robinsons Iloilo
spots.desc: A major shopping mall in the downtown area, offering a department store, supermarket, cinemas, and a wide selection of shops and restaurants, managed by Robinsons Malls.

spots.name: SM Delgado
spots.desc: A smaller, centrally located SM mall in the downtown area, popular for quick shopping, groceries, and easy access to the city’s historic core.
spots.addr: Delgado Street cor. Valeria Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: MaryMart Center
spots.desc: A shopping center in the downtown area known for small retail stalls and affordable local boutiques, frequented by locals.

spots.name: Gaisano City Iloilo
spots.desc: A shopping mall offering budget-friendly shopping, groceries, and basic dining options, part of the Gaisano Capital Group.

spots.name: Robinsons Jaro
spots.desc: A shopping mall in Jaro with retail stores, a supermarket, a department store, cinemas, and dining options, managed by Robinsons Malls.

spots.name: Shops at Atria
spots.desc: An outdoor, open-air mall known for its trendy restaurants and cafés, under Ayala Malls.
spots.addr: Donato Pison Avenue, Atria Park District, Mandurriao

spots.name: Ponsyon by Breakthrough
spots.desc: Offers a more modern take on traditional Ilonggo seafood dishes, including sizzling prawns and crab platters.
spots.addr: Plazuela de Iloilo, Benigno Aquino Avenue, Mandurriao

spots.name: Dayneto's Seafood Grill & Restaurant
spots.desc: Casual dining spot popular for grilled fish, squid, crabs, and steaks.

spots.name: Samurai Talabahan Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Known for fresh oysters and a variety of oyster dishes with Japanese-inspired sauces.
spots.addr: Benigno Aquino Avenue Service Road, Mandurriao

spots.name: Punot Restaurant
spots.desc: Local favorite serving affordable seafood platters alongside modernized Ilonggo dishes.
spots.addr: Riverside Boardwalk, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Griller's Oyster House
spots.desc: Specializes in grilled talaba and other shellfish, cooked to order—steamed, baked, in hot chili, crispy fried, or sizzling.
spots.addr: Riverside Boardwalk, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Ocean City Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Family-friendly spot serving classic Filipino seafood dishes.
spots.addr: General Luna Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Spring Palace Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves traditional Ilonggo-style seafood and features a temperature-controlled live seafood aquarium—the only one of its kind.
spots.addr: Doctor Rizalina V. Bernardo Avenue cor. Boardwalk Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Buto’t Balat Restaurant
spots.desc: Known for its grilled crabs, shrimp, and native-style seafood cooking.

spots.name: Nato & Helen Native & Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves authentic Ilonggo seafood favorites in a casual, local setting.

spots.name: Waterfront Seafood & Cocktails
spots.desc: Combines fresh seafood with a lively, modern dining atmosphere, perfect for groups and nightlife vibes, with access to the Iloilo River Esplanade.
spots.addr: General Luna Street, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: The Granary
spots.desc: All-day dining restaurant offers a blend of Ilonggo and international cuisines in a modern setting.
spots.addr: Richmonde Hotel Iloilo, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

spots.name: Jardin Mediterranean Cuisine
spots.desc: A garden-themed restaurant serving authentic Mediterranean dishes, including Greek, Italian, and Moroccan cuisines.
spots.addr: Riverside Boardwalk, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Muelle Deli and Restaurant
spots.desc: Known for its selection of steaks, pastas, and deli items, this restaurant offers a contemporary dining experience with a view of the Iloilo River.

spots.name: Troi Oi
spots.desc: An authentic Vietnamese restaurant featuring traditional dishes in a setting adorned with Vietnamese-made furniture and lacquerware.
spots.addr: Riverside Boardwalk, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Barrio Inasal
spots.desc: A local favorite offering juicy chicken inasal and other Filipino dishes like sisig and sinigang na pompano.
spots.addr: Maria Clara Avenue, Aurora Subdivision, Iloilo City Proper

spots.name: Ramboy's Lechonan and Restaurant
spots.desc: Famous for its crispy lechon manok and a variety of Filipino comfort foods.

spots.name: The Mango Tree Restaurant
spots.desc: A garden-themed restaurant offering a serene dining experience with a menu featuring Filipino and international dishes.

spots.name: Theo's Restaurant and Bakery
spots.desc: Offers a range of baked goods and comfort food, perfect for casual and modern dining.

spots.name: Bavaria German Restaurant & Inn
spots.desc: A popular spot for families and gatherings, this restaurant serves authentic German flavors, including dishes like sausages and schnitzels.

spots.name: Patpat’s Kansi House
spots.desc: Known for its version of the Ilonggo dish kansi, a sour beef soup, in a casual setting inside an ancestral house.

spots.name: MO2 Ice Bar
spots.desc: A vibrant place for karaoke, billiards, dancing, drinks, and food, catering to both small groups and families.
spots.addr: Glicerio T. Pison Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: JLK Music Bar
spots.desc: Known for its lively atmosphere, neon lights, and a wide selection of drinks.
spots.addr: San Jose Street, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: The Cave Superclub And Music Hall
spots.desc: A premier nightlife destination offering live music performances and a dynamic clubbing experience.
spots.addr: City Times Square, Gaisano Iloilo City Center, Mandurriao

spots.name: Bourbon Street Bar and Grill
spots.desc: A stylish bar and restaurant offering American-Filipino fusion dishes, craft cocktails, and a cozy ambiance. Their Festive Walk branch is particularly appealing, featuring a balcony dining area with views of the bustling street.
spots.addr: The Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Drink SLS
spots.desc: A chic lounge with stylish interiors, curated cocktails, and a lively atmosphere. It's a go-to spot for those seeking a sophisticated night out.
spots.addr: Festive Walk Parade, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

spots.name: Bottle Ground
spots.desc: A dynamic resto-bar known for its vibrant ambiance, affordable cocktails, and a nostalgic playlist featuring '80s and '90s hits.
spots.addr: Festive Walk Parade, Iloilo Business Park, Mandurriao

spots.name: Madge Café
spots.desc: A historic café known for its traditional brewed coffee, since 1940.

spots.name: Glory's Café
spots.desc: A traditional brewed coffee since 1948, now run by its third generation.

spots.name: Bluejay Coffee & Co.
spots.desc: A contemporary café known for its specialty coffee, minimalist design, and a selection of baked goods.
spots.addr: Pacencia L. Tijam Avenue, Smallville Business Complex, Mandurriao

spots.name: Monkey Grounds Coffee
spots.desc: A hip café with a jungle-themed interior, serving specialty coffee and light bites in a relaxed setting.

spots.name: Capilay Spring Park
spots.desc: A natural spring fed swimming pool in the centre of San Juan. A favourite with the locals at weekends.

spots.name: San Juan Beach
spots.desc: Lots of beach resorts and great for snorkelling and scuba diving.

spots.name: Cambugahay Falls
spots.desc: Impressive 3-tiered waterfalls just outside Lazi. Great for swimming.

spots.name: Century Old Balete Tree
spots.desc: Supposedly enchanted old tree covered in hundreds of roots and vines.

spots.name: Kagusuan Beach
spots.desc: Noted for its picturesque seascape and rock formation, it is situated below a cliff and accessible by concrete staircase.

spots.name: Salagdoong Beach
spots.desc: Favourite with the locals and great for swimming and snorkelling. There are also water slides and places to dive into the sea. On the way to the beach you'll be passing Salagdoong Forest Reserve, which a manmade forest with Molave trees.

spots.name: Mt. Bandilaan National Park
spots.desc: It hosts the highest peak in the island. It takes about 5-10 minutes to get to the top of the mountain from the road. The path is not well maintained. On the way there are a couple of Stations of the Cross.

spots.name: Cantabon Cave
spots.desc: Takes 1.5 hr to walk through and you need to register in the town before venturing inside. Local guide required (they hang around the cave) as the cave is locked up.

spots.name: Aberration Dive Club
spots.desc: Offers filled scuba tanks (650 each) for certified divers and easy diving without dive center connections.

spots.name: Villa Marmarine
spots.desc: 3 km north of Siquijor going towards Larena. Good food, maybe the best on the island.

spots.name: Kawayan Holiday Resort
spots.desc: 2 restaurants; main restaurant touts international cuisine next to the "Infinity" swimming pool and lounge area around the pool.

spots.name: Donato House
spots.desc: Ancestral house.

spots.name: Mindoro Beach
spots.desc: The main stretch of beach in Vigan.

spots.name: Vigan Longganisa & Bagnet by Dang Arce
spots.desc: For take out only.

spots.name: First Sinanglaoan
spots.desc: Filipino beef broth soup, must try!

spots.name: Six Bros. Bar and Grill
spots.desc: Great Filipino home-cooked meal.

spots.name: MILA'S Empanada and Okoy
spots.desc: serving empanada & okoy.

spots.name: Kennon Road Viewpoint
spots.desc: one of the best panoramic sights in Baguio City.

spots.name: Pine Trees of the World Park
Teacher's Camp
spots.desc: One of the most haunted place in the Philippines.

spots.name: Museo Kordilyera
spots.desc: Ethnographic museum.

spots.name: Sky Ranch Baguio
spots.desc: Amusement park.

spots.name: Ambiong Nature View Deck
spots.desc: Hiking area.

spots.name: Porta Vaga Mall
spots.desc: Also hosts a Robinsons Supermarket.

spots.name: Good Taste Café & Restaurant
spots.desc: Chinese cuisine

spots.name: Pizza Volante
spots.desc: Traditional Italian pizza and pasta.

spots.name: Punchy Palate Gastropub
spots.desc: Filipino food.

spots.name: Som Tam
spots.desc: Thai restaurant.

spots.name: Tajimaya Charcoal Grill
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant.

spots.name: Tres Reyes Islands
spots.desc: A chain of three islands off the coast of Gasan.

spots.name: San Roque Cathedral
spots.desc: A Catholic church.
spots.addr: A. Mabini St, corner 10th Ave, Poblacion

spots.name: Thai-To Taosit Temple
spots.addr: #113 M. H. Del Pilar Street, Grace Park East

spots.name: Ung Siu Si Buddhist Temple
spots.desc: Temporarily closed as of September 2023.

spots.name: Green Paddle (Caloocan City)
spots.desc: Table tennis facility.
spots.addr: Unit 31 Grace Park Commercial Complex, 4th Avenue, corner A. Del Mundo Street

spots.addr: General Luna Street corner Espina Street

spots.addr: Rizal Ave Ext, Grace Park East

spots.name: Perry's Chicken House
spots.addr: 159 12th Ave, Corner 8th St, East Grace Park

spots.name: Padi's Point Restaurant and Bar
spots.desc: Serves Filipino, grill, seafood, Spanish dishes.
spots.addr: Grandz Commercial Building, McArthur Highway, Calle Cuatro

spots.name: SamgyupSalamat
spots.addr: Morning Breeze Subdivision, Manila North Road

spots.name: Tong Yang-SM City Grand Central Branch
spots.addr: Level 3, SM City Grand Central, Grace Park East

spots.name: JT's Manukan Grille
spots.desc: Owned by Filipino veteran actor Joel Torre.

spots.name: Tutong’s Laksa-Caloocan Branch
spots.desc: Asian restaurant.
spots.addr: Filipino Building, 2F plaza, Libis Espina Street

spots.name: Orient Pearl Seafood and Restaurant

spots.desc: Has a statue of Jose Maria Peñaranda, the first governor of Albay. Around the park is Legazpi City Hall, Albay Capitol and St. Gregory the Great Cathedral.

spots.name: Battle of Legazpi Pylon
spots.desc: A 16 m high monument built to commemorate the defeat of Filipino fighters by American forces in 1900. The pylon marks the site of a bloody battle during the Philippine-American War and World War II.

spots.name: Kapuntukan Hill
spots.desc: Provides a view of the Embarcadero, the Port District, Albay Gulf, and Mayon Volcano.

spots.name: Acosta-Pastor House
spots.desc: Built in 1883, it is the ancestral home of Don Alejo Acosta, who served as a capitan de barrio. It remains the property of Acosta's descendants, and has been turned into a museum

spots.name: Bahay Pamahalaan, Lungsod ng Batangas
spots.desc: The historic city hall which has been renovated in 2009 with a newer facade.

spots.name: Batangas Provincial Capitol Building
spots.desc: A Neoclassical capitol building housing the office of the governor of Batangas. First built in 1926, it was destroyed by bombing twice, during World War II and in 1950. Around the façade is a tall flagpole, the provincial seal of Batangas, a marble terrace, and two fountains
spots.addr: Jose P. Laurel Highway, Kumintang Ibaba

spots.name: SM City Batangas
spots.desc: Opened in 2005, it hosts a large department store, hundreds of shops, and movie theaters. It underwent expansion that added more restaurants, and a Kidzoona children's play area. Also has a SM Supermarket. The rear parking lots hosts terminals for jeepneys headed south to as far as Ilijan.

spots.name: Bale Herencia
spots.desc: Built in 1860, it is a picturesque house with the unsavory reputation of having been built for the mistress of a parish priest. The current owners have leased the place to various restaurants, food stalls, and other businesses like salons and computer shops. The antique architecture, however, is still preserved.
spots.addr: Lakandula St. corner Santo Rosario St

spots.name: Lily Hill / Goddess of Peace Shrine
spots.desc: Lily Hill is the highest point in the Clark area with an elevation of 32 meters (105 ft). The name of the hill, is the anglicized form of the word "lili" in the local language of the Aetas which means "lost". It was used as an outpost by American soldiers, and later by the Japanese during World War II. In 1998, the Goddess of Peace Shrine was set up, which has a large statue as its centerpiece…

spots.name: Pasig Cathedral
spots.desc: In the city center, this stone church has been around since the early 1700s and serves as a religious city landmark.

spots.name: Capitol Mosque
spots.desc: One of the city's noted mosques. The beige place of worship is located within the Lanao del Sur Provincial Capitol Complex.

spots.name: MSU Golf Course
spots.desc: Play golf or relax at the MSU Golf Course, a 9-hole course laid out on the gentle greenery of Mindanao State University.

spots.name: Bicol Heritage Park
spots.desc: Has a statue of General Simeon Ola. Site at the Camp Simeon Ola headquarters featuring monuments, including one of General Ola.

spots.name: Legazpi City Museum and Library
spots.desc: Deals with the history of Legazpi. Well-maintained place with a high standard. The sculptures, paintings, historical photos and dioramas are especially interesting.

spots.name: Liberty Bell
spots.desc: Housed on a concrete dome structure. This bronze bell was a gift from the Americans (the 158th Infantry Regimental Combat team of the US 6th Army) command led by Brig. General Hanford Macnider and Captain Hoomer Mcgee) in 1945 after the liberation of the city from the Japanese occupiers. A side note within is inscribed "Whenever oppression knocks at your door, feel free to ring this bell".

spots.name: Pinarik Viewdeck
spots.desc: Offers a truly breathtaking experience that captures the essence of natural beauty. Nestled amidst lush landscapes and towering trees, this vantage point provides an unparalleled panoramic view that leaves one speechless. The vast expanse of rolling hills and valleys is adorned with vibrant hues, creating an awe-inspiring canvas that changes with the light of the day. The serenity of the…

spots.name: Headless Monument
spots.desc: It is dedicated to the unknown heroes who died in the Japanese occupation of Legazpi City during World War II.

spots.name: Ibalong Heroes Monument
spots.desc: A monument named after the complete Bicolano folk epic Ibalong. Based on another Asian epic the Ramayana and was allegedly narrated by an ancient sage called Kandunung. The three heroes of the story, Baltog, Handyong, and Bantong are featured as relief with their names in the ancient Baybayin characters on each post.

spots.name: Legazpi Boulevard
spots.desc: A picturesque seaside road along the city's southern coastline with wide promenades, bike lanes, monuments such as the statue of Miguel López de Legazpi, JCI Legazpi Tourism Marker and the Freemason Obelisk, restaurants, cafés, and pubs.

spots.name: The Obelisk
spots.desc: A monument which is built as a joint project between the city government and Masonic Lodge No. 61.

spots.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe Shrine (Legazpi City)
spots.desc: It features life-sized depictions of Stations of the Cross and a huge statue of the Virgin of Guadalupe at the summit.

spots.name: St. Raphael the Archangel Church
spots.desc: The original church was built in 1834 under the auspices of Pedro Romero, but was destroyed during the liberation of Legazpi by Allied forces in 1945. A more modern church was rebuilt in its place. Notable features include an altar table made of a single block of hardened lava rock.

spots.name: Plaza Rizal
spots.desc: It has a fountain and a monument to José Rizal, the country's national hero, sculpted by National Artist Napoleon Abueva in 1966.

spots.name: Sawangan Park
spots.desc: Very nice place to relax, just do a simple walk or jog around the area. The park is so clean. No mosquitoes and smells good even if the area is near the port. There are food kiosks and you can enjoy eating with your friends or family

spots.name: Albay Gulf Landing Monument
spots.desc: Built in 1995 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Landing of the Allied American Forces in Legazpi City.

spots.name: Albay Park and Wildlife
spots.desc: A picnic grove and a zoological park combined. Quaint city park hosting a diverse array of wildlife, including crocodiles, pigs & eagles.

spots.name: Giant Statue of Nuestra Señora de Salvacion
spots.desc: A towering religious monument dedicated to Our Lady of Salvation, a patroness celebrated for protection and blessings among local devotees.

spots.name: Padang Memorial Cross
spots.desc: A monument dedicated to the victims of Typhoon Durian ("Reming") in 2006, which destroyed parts of the city. The location is right beside the highway. There are no parking spaces available except for the highway's shoulder. Visitors should take extra precaution alighting from their vehicles as there are lots of fast moving vehicles on the highway. There are no trees at all to hide under when the…

spots.name: Imelda Park
spots.desc: Has pavilions, a playground, and a basketball court. Also at the park is Mag-Ilusyon, a metal sculpture by artist Eduardo Castrillo, commissioned in 1976.

spots.name: Our Lady of Perpetual Help Parish Church
spots.desc: It is also known as the Redemptorist Church and Our Lady of Perpetual Help is the patron.

spots.name: Embarcadero de Legazpi
spots.desc: A marina-inspired waterfront lifestyle hub, commercial and entertainment center in the city's port area. It also hosts the first Duty Free Philippines store in Bicol.

spots.name: Yashano Mall Legazpi
spots.desc: They have fast food, resto, food kiosks, and cellphone accessories.
spots.addr: Terminal Road 1 Corner, F. Imperial Street

spots.name: SM City Legazpi
spots.desc: A 140,000-m² mall, which also hosts the central bus station.

spots.name: 1st Colonial Grill
spots.desc: A well known restaurant in the area that is famous for inventing the Sili ice-cream, a chili-infused ice-cream that is a core part of Bicol cuisine. There are three branches in Legazpi: SM Legazpi, Pacific Mall, and near the Bicol University College of Education.

spots.name: BIGG'S Diner
spots.desc: A famous fast food chain in the Bicol region serving various comfort Western and Filipino foods.

spots.name: Sol at Hotel Areca
spots.desc: A high-end restaurant that is part of Hotel Areca, serving both high quality local and international cuisine. Hotel guests have a 10% discount.

spots.name: Pinyasan Formosa Festival
spots.desc: Named after the delicious sweet Formosa Pineapple, it lasts a week and a half in mid-June with parades, street stalls and nightly entertainment.

spots.name: Central Plaza Mall
spots.desc: Central Plaza Mall provides enjoyment to people seeking casual leisure time or just simply entertainment.

spots.name: Jardin En Ville (Garden in the City)
spots.desc: Newly opened Japanese, European and American themed Restaurant. They served different variety of foods from their menu plus instagrammable place.

spots.name: Buntod Sandbar
spots.desc: A 10-minute boat ride from the city will take you to Buntod Sandbar, which vanishes during high tide.

spots.name: Dunoy Lake
spots.desc: An isolated lake reachable only by a four-hour hike or by motorcycling on a single-lane trail, it is home to the endemic Philippine crocodile, which was rediscovered in the area in 1999. An observation tower provides sightseeing opportunities for the reptile as well as endemic birds.

spots.name: Bambanti Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival celebrating Isabela's culture. Most major events are held at the amphitheater at Queen Isabela Park.

spots.name: Kayapa Quad Peak
spots.desc: A nice loop hike that goes over the ridgeline of the four peaks in the area - Mt. Tugew, Mt. Kuban, Mt. Cabo, and Mt. Sadjatan. The hike is around long and takes approximately 5-6 hours, excluding breaks. The starting point is at the Alang-Salacsac Barangay Hall. A guide, available at the barangay hall, is required, in addition to the entry and environmental fees. The barangay also provides some…

spots.name: Assemblyman Rafael Recto People's Park
spots.desc: Provincially-maintained park, with wide grassy spaces and mini-amphitheatre

spots.name: Borbon-Rosales House
spots.desc: Dating back to 1870, it was the ancestral home of the Borbon family, as well as the Rosales family, where the former archbishop of Manila, Cardinal Godofredo Rosales, is part of

spots.name: Laurel Park
spots.desc: A fenced circular park dedicated to the historical contributions of the Batangueños (people of Batangas). Inside the park is sculptures representing the five Batangueño virtues of nobility, bravery, industriousness, wisdom, and beauty, as well as
spots.addr: National Highway cor. Telecom Road, Kumintang Ibaba

spots.name: Monte Maria Batangas
spots.desc: Constructed in 2013, this Catholic pilgrimage site includes the Santo Niño Chapel (a replica of the Church of Our Lady Victorious in Prague) and the 90 m statue of the Virgin Mary, the Mary, Mother of All Asia, which will become the largest in Asia. The location in the coast also provides views of Puerto Galera and Verde Island.

spots.name: Museo Puntong Batangan
spots.desc: Opened in 2006, it presents the city's cultural heritage and history, as well as the history and culture of Batangueños.

spots.name: Plaza Mabini
spots.desc: A Spanish-era downtown plaza in Poblacion, named in honor to revolutionary Apolinario Mabini. The present plaza dates to 1915, and was redesigned in 2004 by the firm of renowned Filipino architect and urban planner Jun Palafox. It has a monument to Apolinario Mabini, pedestrian space with sunrays design, dancing fountains, playground, a covered amphitheater, flower stalls, souvenir shops, and…

spots.name: Batangas City Sports Complex
spots.desc: Has a 20- by 50-meter 8-lane swimming pool, running track and basketball courts.

spots.name: Batangas Coliseum
spots.desc: Multi-purpose arena, sometimes hosts professional league games held in Batangas, as well as local sports events and concerts.

spots.name: Bay City Mall
spots.desc: Owned by a local retail company, it is a local favorite. It houses a Citimart department store and supermarket, a National Book Store, numerous ukay-ukay outlets, Jollibee and Chowking, and other local businesses.

spots.name: Citimart
spots.desc: Owned also by the retailer owning Bay Mall, this is a large department store building with a supermarket below. The department store remains closed, but it hosts a Greenwich and a Chowking restaurant.

spots.name: Nuciti Central
spots.desc: A more upscale shopping mall, owned by the same retailer running Bay Mall, with mid-range restaurants and several food kiosks, with a Citimart Supermarket (opened 2023) that replaced the Robinsons Supermarket. Has a PNB ATM.

spots.name: Unitop
spots.desc: A local favorite, with its own supermarket, in the basement. It sells household items, clothes, and groceries.

spots.name: Xentro Mall Batangas
spots.desc: Opened May 2018. Single-story mall with some shops and restaurants. The Savemore supermarket that used to be here has been closed since 2024.

spots.name: Batangas City Public Market
spots.desc: An important marketplace for the city for years since the 1900s, it hosts small services, clothing stalls, and local meat, fish and produce. It also has some small restaurants specializing in the regional cuisine and a McDonald's ice cream stall. Parking is also available at a fee of 10.

spots.name: Julian Pastor Memorial Market
spots.desc: A newer public market built to the south, with separate buildings for the wet and dry sections.

spots.name: Bafoo's
spots.desc: Specializes in the Batangueño favorite, lomi, but also serves other regional dishes. It now has branches in Pallocan West (near Calumpang Bridge) and Kumintang Ibaba (near University of Batangas).

spots.name: Batangas City Restaurant formerly known as Canton Restaurant
spots.desc: Best noted for their affordable pancit and chop chicken. Location is also not too far from downtown shopping areas.

spots.name: Ho Tsai
spots.desc: One of the first Filipino-Chinese restaurants in the city. Serves Filipino-Chinese fast food like pansit, lomi and mami, as well as common Filipino favourites, like Filipino-style spaghetti, fried rice and pulutan dishes.

spots.name: Hungry Hippo
spots.desc: Small hamburger restaurant with stall below and tables above. Another branch exists in SM Batangas.

spots.name: Mirellis Diner
spots.desc: Little sit-in restaurant serving Filipino and Western meals, including burgers, sandwiches, pancit, silog, and others.

spots.name: Nung Ru Thai
spots.desc: Owned by a Filipino who lived in Thailand, this is only one of a few restaurants that serve Thai and Indian cuisine in Batangas.

spots.name: Mr. Kimchi
spots.desc: Korean dining, complete with hot pot, barbecue, and soju, within the downtown at a reasonable price.

spots.name: Taza Mia!
spots.desc: Part of local coffeeshop chain, serving coffee and pastries.

spots.name: Big Mike's Grill House
spots.desc: Serves sizzling favorites like sisig, bangus and gambas. You can also try their house style baby back ribs, fried rice, and burger.

spots.name: F. Baylosis Crispy Pata
spots.desc: Houses the city's favorite crispy pata and chicken, for locals and tourists alike. There is also a wide variety of Filipino dishes and sides, starting at 190. The restaurant has an ambient atmosphere and friendly staff, and prices of meals are reasonable. You can eat with the sounds and voice of an acoustic guitar player. Private karaoke rooms are available for rent for those who want a feast…

spots.name: Wanam sa Bukid
spots.desc: Serves various Filipino favorites, such as chop suey, miki noodles, fried chicken, fried lumpia (spring rolls), and crispy pata.
spots.addr: Doña Romana Building, National Highway, Gulod Labac

spots.name: Jocas Lomi Haus
spots.desc: Open-air eatery specializing in lomi, Batangas's major contribution to the Filipino cuisine.

spots.name: Appleville Resto-bistro
spots.desc: Serves a variety of Filipino dishes, but its specialty is its beef caldereta and tadyang. Previously known as A&M restaurant before its refurnishing (August 2024).

spots.name: Al Goto King
spots.desc: Small and often crowded restaurant, specializing in bulalo and goto. The restaurant has parking spaces beside.

spots.name: Forkie's
spots.desc: Restaurant serving a fusion of Filipino breakfast and American fast food. Previously known as Brand X Burgers.

spots.name: Cafe de Alps
spots.desc: Bus-themed restaurant and cafe, serving Western and Filipino dishes. Ciudad Food Park and along with it, Cafe de Alps has long been closed as of December 2024.
spots.addr: Ciudad Food Avenue, Diversion Road, Alangilan

spots.name: Jhorjanes
spots.desc: Specializes in the lomi and bulalo recipes, but they also serve local seafood, chicken, and vegetable dishes.

spots.name: Jovita Cafe
spots.desc: Casual restaurant not far from 3 nearby hotels, and another branch near SM City Batangas. They serve coffee, pasta, pastries, and other. This is the only place in town that serve bagel sandwiches.

spots.name: The Other Place
spots.desc: Filipino-themed restaurant serving common local fare. Relocated to P. Burgos due to a fire accident in 2023.

spots.name: D' Brothers Sports Bar
spots.desc: Sports-themed restaurant and bar, perfect place to talk, drink, and watch sports. Popular among locals and foreigners alike

spots.name: BP Generic Express
spots.desc: Local pharmacy chain with numerous branches in Batangas City

spots.name: Generika
spots.desc: Part of nationwide chain with numerous branches in Batangas City and nearby municipalities. Provides low-cost medicines and blood pressure check.

spots.name: South Star Drug
spots.desc: Most of this nationwide chain's locations have been converted to Chavez Pharmacy branches.

spots.name: Aguinaldo Shrine
spots.desc: The National Shrine of the Philippines, where the Philippine Declaration of Independence from Spain took place on June 12, 1898. A staple for field-tripping schoolchildren for Metro Manila.

spots.name: Malibiclibic Falls
spots.desc: A Hidden Falls below the grasslands of Cavite. Malibiclibic Falls is a result of a convergence between three rivers flowing from Magallanes, Aguinaldo, and Maragondon. Millions of years of three-river pounding a 100-m high cliff, the water found its way through it; thus creating a waterfall. This river was awarded as the cleanest river during the 2004 National Search for the Clean Inland Bodies…

spots.name: Pink Sisters Convent
spots.desc: It was established through the Society of Divine Word, Holy Spirit Missionary Sisters and Holy Spirit Adoration Sisters, all founded by Saint Arnold Janssen. The nuns’ presence in the chapel gives the place an even more sacred ambiance. A visit is the chance to see nuns praying 24 hours a day — although they can only be seen behind the iron grilles of the altar.
spots.addr: Holy Spirit Drive in Barangay Maitim

spots.name: Mystical Cave
spots.desc: Show cave with guided tours through stalactites, stalagmites & other intricate limestone formations.
spots.addr: 25 Masinag, Marilaque Highway, Barangay San Jose

spots.name: Sumulong Park
spots.desc: A paved park hosting vendors, busking mascots and a small weekend farmers market.
spots.addr: M.L. Quezon Street, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Antipolo Skate Park
spots.desc: The biggest skate park in the Philippines. Skateboarding, biking and BMX can be done here.
spots.addr: Provincial Satellite Auditing Office, Marcos Highway, Brgy. Inarawan

spots.name: Alay Lakad
spots.desc: Literally means Offering Walk, it is a penitential walk from Quiapo Church in Manila to Antipolo Cathedral to commemorate the feast of Our Lady of Antipolo. It is a major religious affair, drawing in up to six million pilgrims climbing the heights leading to downtown Antipolo.
spots.hours: Maundy Thu and the first Tue of May

spots.name: Antipolo Triangle Mall
spots.desc: The place has government offices (PSA, SSS, Pag-ibig), banks, ATM, and medical facilities; parking is good.

spots.name: SM City Masinag
spots.desc: Has an e-trike terminal for those heading to downtown Antipolo and a minibus terminal servicing Teresa, Morong, Baras, Tanay and Pililla.

spots.name: iMall Antipolo
spots.desc: Its lot formerly housed the public market until transferring to Sumulong Highway.
spots.addr: M.L. Quezon Street, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Victory Park and Shop
spots.desc: Beside the Antipolo Cathedral and the Sumulong Park. Includes the Pasalubong Center at the side. Has an e-trike terminal for those heading to SM Masinag and LRT Antipolo Station.
spots.addr: P. Oliveros Street, Barangay San Isidro

spots.name: Super Metro Antipolo
spots.desc: Hypermarket. Its parking lot doubles as the jeepney terminal to Cubao.
spots.addr: P. Oliveros Street, Barangay Dela Paz

spots.name: Kamayan - Tamerlane's Ihaws
spots.desc: The place gives a feel of typical and homey Filipino canteen. Like everyone's welcome to enter and just eat good food. Their food is also really good.

spots.name: Sakura Circle
spots.desc: If you want to eat any various Asian cuisine this is a must try too.

spots.name: Mogu Tree Noodle House
spots.desc: The place is small very basic seating, but the food is good! Must try their noodles, with toppings and noodles of your own choosing, and 3 different types of soups.
spots.addr: Beverly Hills Drive corner First Avenue

spots.name: 21st Century Girls Cafe
spots.desc: If you are a BTS fan/army, you'll really love this place. The design, services, foods are all great. Though the place is small, but it made them more Instagramable.

spots.name: Churches of the province
spots.desc: Pampanga is host to many old and beautiful churches. The oldest and largest of which is the Lubao Church, which was built in 1570 and boasts a fine altarpiece. The most beautiful, however, is the Betis Church which is often tagged as the "Sistine Chapel of the Philippines" because of its painted wall and ceilings, and its sumptuous retablo. The Bacolor Church is famous for being buried up to its…

spots.name: Trek Mt. Pinatubo
spots.desc: Mount Pinatubo erupted in 1991 and is now open for tourism. It has an elevation of 1,485 m (4,872 ft) and a beautiful crater lake where you can swim. This trek can be done as a day tour if you leave very early on the morning.

spots.name: Bird watching at Candaba
spots.desc: The best time to go bird watching is on the early morning, around five to seven in the morning when bird activity is at its peak and the heat is not intense. Late afternoons are also a good time for this. Must brings are hiking footwear and clothes, and a good pair of binoculars or telescope. The avid birdwatcher might also want to bring his or her field notebook, pencil and camera. Expect to pay…

spots.name: Founders' Residence
spots.desc: Located at the heart of Santo Rosario, it is the oldest building in the city. It was built in 1824 by the city founder, Don Ángel Pantaleón de Miranda, and his wife, Doña Rosalia de Jesus, and was inherited by their only daughter, Doña Juana de Miranda de Henson. This house, which is made of high stone and an ornate gate, nostalgically symbolizes the glorious past of Angeles amidst the…

spots.name: Post Office Building
spots.desc: It is a building that was constructed in 1899 for the purpose of depositing religious statues and carriages of the Catholic Church, hence the name Deposito. It was also used as the headquarters of the 11th Film Exchange U.S. Army from 1946 to 1947 and was then used as a jailhouse for recalcitrant U.S. troops during the Philippine–American War. On February 6, 1967, the Angeles Post Office moved to…

spots.name: Holy Family Academy Building
spots.desc: Holy Family Academy Building was once a convent and was served as a military hospital of the U.S. Army in 1900. It was later used as troop barracks, officers' quarters and arsenal by the Japanese Imperial Military Forces in 1942.

spots.name: Center for Kapampangan Studies
spots.desc: A museum inside the Holy Angel University showcasing the history and culture of the Kapampangans, the main ethnic group in Pampanga. It also has an art gallery featuring modernist works by National Artist from Pampanga Vicente Manansala, and a section dealing with Mount Pinatubo. Its libraries house more than 4,000 volumes.
spots.price: free, but guests must register before the security guards at the university’s entrances beforehand

spots.name: Expo Pilipino
spots.desc: An exposition center opened in 1998 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the declaration of Philippine independence. It features a 35,000-seater covered amphitheater.

spots.name: Bayanihan Park
spots.desc: A park at the Clark Freeport Zone near SM City Clark shopping mall. It features the "Salakot", a large pavilion structure named after the native hat of the same name due to the shape of its roof.

spots.name: Chapel of the Holy Guardian Angel
spots.desc: The main chapel of the Holy Angel University. It is noted for its contemporary white facade which has an unconventional structure for modern churches. It is dedicated to the Guardian Angel, which is the patron of both the school and the city of Angeles. It also hosts an image which was commissioned in the Spanish colonial era in 1830 by Don Angel Pantaleon de Miranda.

spots.name: Mount Arayat Trek
spots.desc: Available November through May. Prices range: day trips (minimum of 3 persons, 800 per person) and overnight trips (minimum of 3 persons, 2500 per person).

spots.name: Clark International Speedway
spots.desc: Reserve a day for motorsports activity at the Clark International Speedway, a 4.19 km permanent race track. No walk-ins allowed. Closed Mondays.

spots.name: Angeles Fried Chicken
spots.desc: The oldest restaurant in Angeles City, offers a wide array of food. Locally famous for its juicy chicken (crispy or regular) with coleslaw and gravy. Also popular: gambas, sisig, calamares,Japanese fried chicken, pancit canton, bihon, clubhouse sandwich, iced tea.

spots.name: Tequila Reef Cantina
spots.desc: Authentic Mexican cuisine, barbecue chicken & ribs, New Orleans “Cajun” specialties, steaks, burgers, sandwiches and Filipino food.
spots.addr: Corner of A. Santos and Real Streets

spots.name: Camalig
spots.desc: A local restaurant open since 1973 known for "Armando's Pizza" which is billed as "the national pizza". It is purported to be made in-house using classic homegrown Pinoy pizza recipe. Camalig has a selection of 18 pizza flavors. It is housed inside a historic structure built in 1840 by Don Ciriaco de Miranda, the first gobernadorcillo of Angeles, and was used as a grain storehouse. It was…

spots.name: Clark Lomi House
spots.desc: A large eatery inside Clark airbase serving a variety of Filipino local food. Prices are affordable and food tastes good. They have indoor and outdoor area dining. Parking is huge.They also serve coffee, fruit shakes, milktea and hot or iced coffee.

spots.name: My Lola Nor's Meryendahan
spots.desc: Every dish is surprisingly delicious and authentic. They have short orders for merienda and lunch servings. All food is cooked very distinctively. Tidtad capampangan (dinuguan/pork blood stew), pork sinigang, fresh lumpia (the crepe is hand-made, smooth and soft) with peanut sauce (amazing), pancit luglug (the serving is generous), batirol (everyday Christmas!) and their batirol shake.

spots.name: Mi Amor
spots.desc: Highly recommend place for those who love singing but have a wallet friendly budget.

spots.name: The Coffeeshop Restaurant and Rooftop Hotel
spots.desc: The Coffeeshop Restaurant was built in April 1984 and remains one of the most popular restaurant in Barrio Barretto. It is well-known as the "Home of the Jumbo Tacos" and is located a few meters from several beach resorts. It serves local and international cuisines at affordable prices.
spots.addr: #2-3 Rizal Street, Barrio Barretto, corner National Highway, Olongapo City

spots.name: Quirino Skyline/Tirad Pass
spots.desc: designated a National Shrine, this pass was the site of a battle led by a young general named Gregorio del Pilar against revolutionary forces led by hero Emilio Aguinaldo

spots.name: Benguet Museum
spots.desc: Provincial museum containing ethnographic materials relating to the indigenous people of Benguet.

spots.name: National Museum-Kabayan Branch Museum
spots.desc: Kabayan Museum is established to protect and care the Kabayan Mummy Caves in the province. Mummy Caves are one of the country's national cultural treasures. It is a burial caves that holds mummies sited in Kabayan especially in the Timbac Caves. The building is placed in a lot donated by citizens who value the culture of the Ibaloi and the Kankanaey. It is a one-story building and a basement…

spots.name: Attend a kanyaw
spots.desc: This is an Igorot practice, Visitors can easily be in one during Benguet Day, or the Adivayan Festival.

spots.name: Gabaldon Hall
spots.desc: Historical school building, constructed as one of the "Gabaldon Schools" during the American occupation in 1907. It is now part of Las Piñas Central Department of Education's Las Piñas school division office.

spots.name: Lara House
spots.desc: Ancestral house that once housed the Las Piñas General Hospital and Las Piñas's municipal hall. It now hosts a small barbershop below.

spots.name: Mary Immaculate Parish Church
spots.desc: A nature-themed Roman Catholic parish church built by Filipino architect Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa. The current church is rebuilt in the original style from the original church destroyed by fire during a New Year's Day fire caused by a misfired firework.

spots.name: Palazzo Verde
spots.desc: Luxurious church used as a wedding venue by many personalities. The inside is off-limits, but you can take selfies with a carriage outside or you might shot the church from the outside. It has a small chapel, Notre Dame de Vie Chapel, just across Zapote River.

spots.name: Southlinks Golf Club
spots.desc: A links golf course inside an affluent subdivision. Locker rooms are available, but there is no WiFi access. Golfing is rather difficult due to the surrounding area.

spots.name: Car-Free Weekends
spots.desc: Bikers and joggers flood the 2.5 km tree-lined dual-carriageway avenue often named "Daang Reyna", which serves as an alternative route to San Pedro, every weekend morning. It's possible to bike the whole road in 16 minutes, from near Palazzo Verde into the roundabout outside the Amore subdivision and back. Bike rental is available for the activity. Biking and jogging continue till sunset, but…

spots.name: Evia Lifestyle Center
spots.desc: Small shopping mall with Italian-style architecture, opened 2013, It has a variety of shops and restaurants, including its major anchor shops, H&M and Uniqlo.

spots.name: SM Southmall
spots.desc: Major SM mall with a variety of food options. Opened in 1999, it is the first large SM mall in southern Metro Manila. Since 2012, it has been renovated and it retail space has been further expanded. Just beside it are some office blocks with dining and shops below.

spots.name: Our Lady of Abandoned Parish
spots.desc: Our Lady of Abandoned is the patron saint of Marikina. This is a large church renovated in 2013.

spots.name: Marikina River Park
spots.desc: Beside the Marikina River, this river park hosts the Annual Christmas Tiangge usually starts at November and ends at January. Many people used to bike, jog and walk here. You can see here the Our Lady of Lourdes Pagoda, Chinese Temple, Marikitna, Senior Citizen Gazeebo, Roman Park, Sto. Nino Skating park. It also features bars and restaurants

spots.name: Riverbanks Center
spots.desc: A business center beside the Marikina River. It is a center for leisure, entertainment and shopping, it contains E-COM Center, Riverbanks Mall, Arcade Center, Marikina Convention Center, Museums, River Park, Carnival, Amphitheatre.

spots.name: Marikina Shoe Museum
spots.desc: The Shoe Museum traces the history of shoe industry in Marikina. It houses traditional Filipino footwear and 1,500 shoes from the famous Imelda Marcos collection. The museum holds shoes of several famous people including a pair of shoes from each president of the Philippines in chronological order. Other noteworthy shoes are those of celebrities, ambassadors, political figures and even…

spots.name: Kapitan Moy House
spots.desc: It is the Cultural Center of Marikina, features the Convention Center and Restaurants Kapitan Moy Building, situated in Marikina, Metro Manila, the Philippines, is the 200-year-old house of Don Laureano Guevarra, known as the founder of the Marikina shoe industry

spots.name: Marikina Market Mall
spots.desc: It is located at the Poblacion, features wet and dry market, has 3-floor commercial building
spots.addr: W. Paz Street cor. J.P. Rizal Avenue

spots.name: Philippine Science Centrum
spots.desc: Philippine Science Centrum (PSC) is a premier hands-on science center museum in the country recognized by the Department of Education, Department of Science and Technology and the Department of Tourism as an ideal venue for educational field trip destination where visitors are encouraged to touch, twist, play, hear, see the interactive exhibits displayed. PSC is open to pre-school to college…

spots.name: Marikina Sports Center
spots.desc: an Olympic-size swimming pool, a 400-m track oval, a sports building, an indoor gymnasium and several courts.

spots.name: Industriya Marikina
spots.desc: An old shoe factory turned restaurant and events venue. Wooden furniture, shoe forms and empty bottles form part of the place’s modern and industrial design. They serve international cuisines including American, Japanese, Italian and Filipino.

spots.name: Bun of Brothers
spots.desc: The newest addition to the ‘Brothers’ chain of restaurants, which includes Burrito Brothers and Kebab Brothers (and soon to open Breakfast Brothers). Bun of Brothers is a small build-your-own burger joint serving all-American burgers, hotdogs, fries and refreshments.

spots.name: Battle of Don Galo monument
spots.desc: Parañaque locals led by Don Galo, who became the namesake of the barangay nearby, helped the Spaniards to ward off an attack by the Chinese pirate Limahong off Manila Bay, but the waters nearby is now buried by land reclamation since the 1970s.

spots.name: DreamPlay Manila
spots.desc: The characters from DreamWorks films feature at this state-of-the-art center for kids' activities.

spots.name: GG 999
spots.desc: I didn’t expect to enjoy this game so much It’s simple, fun, and actually pretty addictive.

spots.name: SM City Sucat
spots.desc: The first mall by the SM mall chain at the south of Manila, it has two buildings, connected together by a skybridge across C-5 Road Extension. Building A has a SM Hypermarket, and is larger, while Building B houses the anchored department store.

spots.name: Duty Free Philippines Fiestamall
spots.desc: Duty Free Philippines' flagship store, sits just 200 meters from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 1. This shopping haven boasts an extensive selection of foreign items, including chocolates, cigarettes, liquor, electronics, sporting goods, and supermarket items.

spots.name: Harbour Square
spots.desc: Surrounded by a variety of dining shops, offering a diverse culinary experience. Visitors can enjoy a picturesque view that showcases yachts from the Manila Yacht Club against the stunning backdrop of the Manila skyline. A perfect spot for relaxation and appreciation of the city's charm.

spots.name: SM MOA Eye
spots.desc: Riders of this huge Mall of Asia Ferris wheel with night lighting can take in city & bay views.

spots.name: J.W. Roadway Bridge
spots.desc: Go here during the morning and the afternoon for the stunning view of the area.

spots.name: SM By the Bay
spots.desc: This amusement park offers a delightful experience with a Ferris wheel, bumper cars, and other thrilling rides. Adjacent to it is an esplanade overlooking Manila Bay, providing a stunning view for witnessing the sunsets. Along the area, visitors will find a plethora of dining options to savor, making it an ideal destination for a fun-filled day with scenic views and delectable meals.

spots.name: Manila Bay Breakwater
spots.desc: Stunning view of Manila Bay, Roxas Boulevard's Skyline, Bataan Province.

spots.name: Cartimar Shopping Center
spots.desc: Similar to Manila's famous Divisoria, this bustling shopping area specializes in selling imitation products of well-known brands, primarily shoes, often imported from China. Here, visitors can explore a plethora of shops offering a wide range of affordable options. Besides the imitation goods, the area also hosts pet stores and plant shops, catering to those in search of even the most exotic…

spots.name: SM Mall of Asia
spots.desc: This enormous mall was constructed on reclaimed land. As of mid-2026 Wikipedia ranks it the largest in the Philippines and sixth largest on Earth. It features a wide array of mid-range and high-end stores and restaurants. In addition to shopping, the mall offers various attractions, including a large arena that frequently hosts concerts, a science museum with numerous interactive exhibits, a…

spots.name: Newport Mall
spots.desc: This mall offers a high-end shopping experience with luxury shops and dining. Located within the mall is the Newport Performing Arts Theatre, known for its musicals and various events. Additionally, there is a casino for those who enjoy gaming. Surrounding the mall, you'll find prestigious hotels such as Marriott, Hilton, and Sheraton. Conveniently, these hotels are connected by a bridgeway…

spots.name: Varona Vegetarian Health Foods
spots.desc: A canteen that caters to vegetarians and vegans, offering plenty of delightful options. With a focus on plant-based cuisine, visitors can indulge in a variety of vegetarian and vegan-friendly dishes. Additionally, they also boast an extensive selection of high-quality mock-meats, providing a diverse range of meat alternatives for those seeking a flavorful plant-based experience.

spots.name: Seaside Dampa
spots.desc: a popular seafood market, visitors can explore the market and purchase their desired seafood. For added convenience, there are nearby restaurants that offer cooking services, allowing you to have your freshly bought seafood prepared to your liking. Moreover, the area boasts some lively bars and KTV spots, providing ample entertainment options for a fun-filled evening after indulging in delicious…

spots.name: The Singing Cooks & Waiters Atbp
spots.desc: At this restaurant, you'll be immersed in an ambiance of joy and constant singing from the passionate cooks and waiters, creating a truly unique and lively atmosphere. Indulge in delicious Filipino cuisine that tantalizes the taste buds and showcases the country's rich culinary heritage. The staff goes above and beyond, frequently joining guests on the floor, singing, and dancing, epitomizing the…

spots.name: House Manila
spots.desc: an electrifying nightlife experience at the nightclub within Newport World Resorts, conveniently located just steps away from the hotels. A popular choice among travelers staying in the area, this vibrant nightclub awaits you at the basement of the Holiday Inn Express.

spots.name: Ellipsis
spots.desc: This nightclub is a hotspot among college students, particularly those from the nearby De La Salle University. This vibrant venue comes alive on weekends and days leading up to holidays, drawing crowds seeking an exciting and lively nightlife experience.

spots.name: The Victor
spots.desc: The Victor is a 60-m steel art installation which depicts the victory of the global Filipino. At night, it can be lit up with various colours & can be seen in the city's northern Barangay Rosario.

spots.name: Maybunga Rainforest Park
spots.desc: Visitors can enjoy flower viewing, boating or swimming. As a green space, it offers a respite from the hustle & bustle of the city; it's also where local events are held.
spots.price: Entrance is free but certain attractions require payment

spots.name: Tiendesitas
spots.desc: This unique shopping complex appears in the form of Philippine Native Houses. There are many bargain shops in this area, and the unique motif also offers a pleasant experience for tourists. The barbecue stalls here are great too.

spots.name: Estancia
spots.desc: A shopping centre located in the mixed-use Capital Commons development.
spots.addr: Meralco Ave. and Camino Verde Dr

spots.name: Manila American Cemetery and Memorial
spots.desc: The largest American World War II cemetery in the World, containing 17,206 graves representing U.S. soldiers who died fighting Japanese forces during the Pacific War. Besides the graves, it contains a chapel, monuments, sculpted gardens and a museum with 25 mosaic maps depicting U.S. battles in the Pacific, making the area well worth a visit. Photo ID is required for entrance.
spots.hours: Daily 9AM-5PM except Christmas and New Year

spots.name: The Mind Museum
spots.desc: The top science museum of the Philippines, with stunning architecture and showcasing 5 main galleries with interactive exhibitions.
spots.addr: JY Campos Park, 3rd Avenue, Bonifacio Global City

spots.name: Burgos Circle
spots.desc: A traffic circle and a public park surrounded by skyscrapers and by alfresco restaurants, cafes and bars, described as a "window to the Parisian lifestyle in the heart of Manila". In the center of the circles lies "The Trees" art installation by Reynato Paz Contreras, and bronze and brass sculpture representing three interlocking trees forming a done.

spots.name: Forbestown Road
spots.desc: Linked to the Burgus Circle, Forbestown Road is probably one of Manila's most beautiful and pleasant streets, containing plenty of greenery and mixed used developments with several alfresco restaurants, cafes and bars.

spots.name: Uptown Parade
spots.desc: Next to the Uptown Mall, a two-floor "dining mall" with several alfresco restaurants and some clubs.

spots.name: Tuscany Private Estates
spots.desc: It may sound a bit of joke to have a place named "Tuscany" just next to the "Venice Grand Canal" (and the next project in the area is named "Florence"). Regardless, it is a beautiful mixed used development in Neoclassical style, with plenty of options of alfresco restaurants and cafes facing the Upper McKinley Road.

spots.name: Libingan ng mga Bayani
spots.desc: Cemetery for the Filipino soldiers who perished in the World War II, as well as for national heroes and former presidents, including Elpidio Quirino, Carlos P. Garcia, Diosdado Macapagal and Ferdinand Marcos. It contains several monuments, such as the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and memorials to Korean and Vietnamese soldiers who died in the Philippines.

spots.name: Saint Anne Parish Church
spots.desc: Church built in Baroque style in 1587. In the old cemetery of the parish lies the Simborio, a dome-shaped funerary chapel build in the 1700s.
spots.addr: 18 Gen. A Luna St, Sta. Ana

spots.name: BGC Arts Center
spots.desc: One of the few dedicated facilities in BGC for concerts and cultural events.
spots.addr: 26th Street corner 9th Avenue, Bonifacio Global City

spots.name: Samsung Hall
spots.desc: Indoor theatre and convert venue located at SM Aura Premier (see #Buy).

spots.name: MO_Space
spots.desc: Contemporary exhibitions, shows and performances from emerging artists.
spots.addr: 3rd floor, MOs Design Bldg, B2 9th Avenue, Bonifacio High Street

spots.name: scatter hitam
spots.desc: Good quality contemporary art exhibitions from local and foreign artists.

spots.name: Gondola ride at the Venice Grand Canal
spots.desc: Obviously the Venice Grand Canal mall (see #Buy) isn't Venice, but the price of a gondola ride here is also a small fraction of the "real thing". Plus the atmosphere surrounding the fake canal is lively, especially in the evening.

spots.name: Bonifacio High Street
spots.desc: An open air shopping mall shaped as a vibrant pedestrian street occupying 3 blocks in the heart of BGC, and one of the area's most popular attractions. Besides a variety of shops, bars, restaurants, and a cinema it contains a park which often hosts contemporary art exhibitions and other events.

spots.name: Fully Booked
spots.desc: Fully Booked's flagship store on Bonifacio High street contains 4 floors of books, magazines, and art supplies. Most books are in English, but there is a small foreign language section.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, B6, Bonifacio High Street

spots.name: BENCH Cafe
spots.desc: Cafe in the second floor of the Bench flagship store in Bonifacio High Street. Offers Filipino comfort food with a twist and with affordable prices. Don't expect superb service though. Their Halo-Halos are definitely worth trying.

spots.name: Fiesta Market food court
spots.desc: The Fiesta Market located in the external area of the Market! Market! shopping mall contains a food court offering a range of street food.

spots.name: Conti's Pastry Shop and Restaurant
spots.desc: The BGC branch of the famous Conti's pastry shop, famous for its mango bravo, sans rival and ensaymada. This branch seems specialised in take-outs so don't expect great service from the sit-in restaurant.

spots.name: Las Flores
spots.desc: An authentic Spanish bistro from the popular Andilana group of restaurants in Barcelona, popular for its tapas and paellas.

spots.name: Locavore BGC
spots.desc: Locavore is where laid-back Filipino grub meets trendy urban chic. This eatery and watering hole marries a slick industrial charm with an open bar, boasting an array of delectable drinks.

spots.name: Manam Netpark
spots.desc: The menu is filled with comfort food and the Filipino classics! Simply delicious!

spots.name: Indus Modern Indian Kitchen
spots.desc: Indus is a veritable oasis of sumptuous Indian cuisine located in the bustling heart of Metro Manila. This fine dining establishment takes pride in offering an authentic Indian dining experience with a touch of modern sophistication.

spots.name: George and Onnie's - BGC
spots.desc: George and Onnie's has got the welcoming service and flavorful Filipino cuisine down to a T, though a touch more culinary wizardry and an indoor pet-friendly policy could push it into the realm of restaurant legends.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, World Plaza, 4th Avenue corner 31st Street

spots.name: Arkong Bato
spots.desc: A stone arch built by the Americans in 1910. It served as a boundary marker for Bulacan (where Valenzuela, then Polo, belonged), and Rizal.

spots.name: Libingan ng mga Hapon
spots.desc: cemetery for the thousands of Japanese soldiers killed during the final years of World War II.

spots.name: Dr. Pio Valenzuela Museum
spots.desc: The ancestral home of Pio Valenzuela, one of the leaders of the Katipunan and the namesake of the city, then the town of Polo. It is now fully renovated as of September 2023.
spots.addr: Kapitan Vililia corner Pascual Deato Street

spots.name: Valenzuela City People's Park
spots.desc: A park beside the Valenzuela City Town Center and City Hall of Valenzuela in McArthur Highway.

spots.name: South Supermarket-Valenzuela City
spots.desc: South Supermarket has many to offer and you can eat, grocery, do arcade or have a massage.

spots.name: Little Beijing Chinese Cuisine
spots.desc: Now a local chain, with a branch in Marilao. Dim sum, congee, soups, noodles, and rice, and some Filipino-Chinese dishes.

spots.name: Kuya J's Restaurant
spots.desc: Kuya J is comprised of favorite Filipino food that has affordable prices, great taste, and excellent service. They cater to families and groups, offering them a casual dining experience. “Our type of cuisine is Filipino, essentially what your mother would cook because she loves you.

spots.name: Kuya Bob Pares/Mami On the Go
spots.desc: Decent tasting and very affordable Pares in Valenzuela. Better to dine here early, their best sellers are usually out of stock.

spots.name: Twin Forts
spots.desc: at the peak of San Andres and Santiago hill, constructed by the Spanish in the 1640s. It is now a declared National Cultural Treasure under the protection of the Philippine government through the National Museum of the Philippines. There is a strenuous climb up the stairs to reach the forts situated at the summit of the hill; however, the reward is well-worth it as it affords a magnificent view…

spots.name: Bangsamoro Museum
spots.desc: Museum at the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex, showcasing the history and culture of the Bangsamoro region.

spots.name: Old Cotabato City Hall
spots.desc: The Old Cotabato City Hall which was built in the built in the 1940s was designed by National Artist for Architecture, Juan Arellano. It is now hosts a small museum as well as the visitor information center of the city.

spots.name: Pagana Kutawato
spots.desc: Pork-less menu featuring native and local foods: fresh seafood - tuna, other fishes, crabs, large shrimp, and other shellfish.
spots.addr: Rufo Manara Street Rosary Heights XI

spots.name: Rebecca Buffet
spots.desc: Kare-kare (buntot ng tuna), inihaw na panga, kilawin, fried chicken, shrimps, sinigang na isda, sweets, cookies, unlimited rice.

spots.name: Moncado Colony
spots.desc: Named in honor of Hilario Camino Moncado, a Filipino, leader, an organizer, author of books and lecturer of humanities. He graduated with honor at the age of nine at India College of Mystery and Psychics. Moncado monuments and wild animals monuments can be found here before the late Dr. Mahid Miraato Mutilan formerly a mayor of the city.

spots.name: Aga Khan Museum of Islamic Arts
spots.desc: A museum featuring the arts and culture of the Moro and Lumad people of the Mindanao, Sulu and Palawan region. It was opened in 1962 as the one-room University Museum, and the expanded museum opened in 1969. It touts itself as having the biggest Philippine Muslim collection in the country. The Aga Khan, the namesake of the museum, sponsored the construction of the museum building. Historical…

spots.name: King Faisal Mosque
spots.desc: The biggest mosque in the city. It is noted for following a color scheme of green, the traditional color in Islam and is associated by the Quran to the state of living of those in Paradise and its architectural details such as the metalwork pattern of its minaret, the painted petals on its dome and the name of "Allah" on top of its spires.

spots.name: JECOs Cafe
spots.desc: One of the city's most known dining outlets located at the MCU Commercial Center. Serves various snacks and desserts.

spots.name: Balangay Shrine Museum
spots.desc: Graveyard of the Balangay 1 dated 320 AD. This wooden plank-build and edge-pegged boats measured an average of 15 meters in length and 3 meters wide across the beam. Nine balangays have already been discovered in Ambangan, Libertad sites. Three have been excavated and others are still in situ.

spots.name: Butuan Regional Museum
spots.desc: This museum is the repository of historical and cultural materials and artifacts that proves Butuan's prehistoric existence and rich cultural heritage. There are two exhibit galleries. The Archaeological Hall and Ethnological Hall specimens of stone crafts, metal crafts, woodcrafts, potteries, goldsmith, burial coffins, and other archaeological diggings are exhibited. At the Ethnological Hall are…

spots.name: Bood Promontory 1st Easter Mass Eco Park
spots.desc: This historic site is where Magellan and his men erected a cross and celebrated the 1st Mass on Philippine Soil on March 31, 1521. It is the highest elevation and promontory overlooking the whole of Butuan bay then. Today, the indigenous “Hadlayati Tree” still abound lording over a Clonal nursery and tree park, and the serpentine Masao River (El Rio de Butuan) amidst fishponds and archaeological…

spots.name: Banza Church Ruins
spots.desc: This site was one of the old poblacion of the city. The church built here in 1625 by the Recollect Friars was reduced to ashes in 1753 by Moro pirates. What remains of this church is its bell tower banyan (balete) trees. Now enveloped by as the most beautiful church in the region before its destruction. Today, it is the oldest ruin of a stone church in the entire island of Mindanao.

spots.name: Magellan's Landing Site
spots.desc: Every year on March 31, the city celebrates Mazaua Discovery Day to commemorate a historic milestone, the 1st Easter Mass on Philippines' soil on 1521, celebrated by Ferdinand Magellan. No matter what, Butuanons proclaim with pride that such historic event took place in Butuan, not in Limasawa.

spots.name: St. Joseph Cathedral
spots.desc: This is like an iconic landmark for Butuan, even though there are Catholic churches everywhere in the Philippines. Also there's the opportunity to see the Filipino flag flying from a tall mast in Guingona Park across the way.

spots.name: Delta Discovery Park
spots.desc: Zip-line course through the tropical hills and swimming pool.

spots.name: Flavored otap
spots.desc: Buy flavored otap (a Filipino delicacy) with flavors Durian and Ube.

spots.name: Balangay souvenirs
spots.desc: Models of Balangay (an ancient boat used by first native Filipinos) are particularly popular as souvenirs.

spots.name: Sunken Cemetery
spots.desc: The eruption of Mt. Vulcan from 1871 to 1875 buried parts of Catarman, including the town's cemetery. A large cross was built above the site of the old cemetery in 1982, as a reminder of the power of Mother Nature.

spots.name: Guiob Church Ruins
spots.desc: The church, built out of coral stones, was also affected by the 1871 eruption of Mt. Vulcan. A chapel has since been built within the ruins, where Mass is also held on a regular basis.

spots.name: Sto. Rosario Church
spots.desc: The church was built in 1882 using coral stones. It has undergone renovations over the years using indigenous and sustainable materials, including bamboo for the walls and columns, wood, and coconut materials. The apse is also covered with multicolored adobe stones.

spots.name: Arden Hot Springs
spots.desc: Make a nighttime visit to these hot springs. It is the perfect time for a warm soak or swim. Drinks are served at the resort.

spots.name: Katibawasan Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall at 50 m. There are a few picnic benches and the water is cold and refreshing. A must-see!

spots.name: Mantigue Island
spots.desc: An islet with beautiful white sand and crystal clear waters off the coast of Maninog.

spots.name: Fiesta
spots.desc: Talk to the locals and see if there is a fiesta happening on the island. It is a must-do!

spots.name: Mount Matutum
spots.desc: An active volcano, approximately 5.7 km from Acmonan, Tupi, South Cotabato. Adjacent volcanic edifices are Landayao, Tampad, and Albulhek to the west of the volcano, and Magolo to the north. There is a well-preserved 320-m-wide crater at the volcano's summit. The crater is breached by three gorges and has a 120-m-deep, densely forested floor. The great view of Matutum is seen in Barangay…

spots.name: Klaja Ecopark
spots.desc: An ecological preservation park 15 km (9.3 mi) off the central business district on the north-east side of city in Barangay Conel. Klaja Karsts Land derived its name from “Kalaha” ("frying pot") as it looked like one due to the surrounding towers of karsts formation naturally formed millions of years ago. It produced natural waterfalls and caves. Opposite is the ranch and camping ground of Nopol…

spots.name: Gen. Paulino Santos Museum
spots.desc: In the Notre Dame of Dadiangas University, it is the first formal museum in the city. It showcases the memorabilia of General Paulino Santos and the first settlers of the city who flocked to the area now known as General Santos City. It also features cultural artifacts of South Cotabato province.

spots.name: Sanchez Peak
spots.desc: 800-foot high mountain peak accessed by trails with panoramas of General Santos City.

spots.name: Baluan Balut Park
spots.desc: Good place to eat balut with family. The ambiance is good. A 5-minute drive from city proper.

spots.name: Queen Tuna Park
spots.desc: Lawned city park on Sarangani Bay with beachside cabanas & a number of trees for shade.

spots.name: Kalilangan Festival
spots.desc: General Santos City celebrates the Kalilangan every month of February. "Kalilangan" means festival, festivity or jubilation. It is a social gathering marked by exchanging of amenities among traditional leaders, elders, allies and subordinates in varying tones. In a broader perspective, Kalilangan projects a positive and dynamic meaning for it engulfs the artistic, humane and altruistic aspects of…

spots.name: Tuna Festival
spots.desc: Thanksgiving and festivities are being celebrated annually through its Tuna Festival during the Last week of August and the first week of September highlighting on its main industry which is the Tuna fishing. This is also in line with the celebration of the city's charter anniversary which falls every 5 September and is also being set as the culmination day for the Tuna Festival. Aside from…

spots.name: Yaman Gensan
spots.desc: Yaman Gensan is an annual event in Gensan that celebrates and promotes local entrepreneurs. It is celebrated in July. Tuna products, T'nalak, Malong and other tribal objects are shown and sold.

spots.name: Paskuhan sa Gensan
spots.desc: The city celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, in this event. It is celebrates from December 17 to the countdown of New Year, Colorful lanterns, giant Christmas tree and Gensan Barangay Christmas House competition are in the event as are Paskuhan sa Gensan Street Dancing, choir group and Christmas Dance.

spots.name: Sto. Niño Patronal Fiesta
spots.desc: This one-day celebration in the city is celebrated every 15th of January. It is the same as the Sinulog Festival in Cebu City. Colorful amphibians, Sr. Santo Niño's Grotto and street dancing. This annual and patronal festival is celebrating in Barangay Bula.

spots.name: Chicken Hauz
spots.desc: Very casual atmosphere but if you try out their famous "garlic chicken", you will crave more.

spots.name: Fagioli
spots.desc: Coffee. The ideal time to visit is during mid-afternoons when it isn't crowded. nice ambiance. Bring along your laptop as the whole place is Wi-Fi enabled.
spots.addr: Petron Gasoline Station, Jose Catolico Ave., Lagao

spots.name: Lanai1687
spots.desc: A beautifully landscaped place in Barangay Kapatan. Looks out over Sarangani Bay, Mt. Matutum & GenSan in the distance. Steaks, prawns & other seafoods, Filipino dishes are on the menu.
spots.addr: Km 1687 on Glan highway from GSC

spots.name: Marasa Grill
spots.desc: Serves lutong bahay and grilled meat and seafood. It also accepts catering for all occasions. It is open for breakfast and lunch.

spots.name: Rolands Steak House
spots.desc: Well worth a visit. Casual atmosphere but the service is good.

spots.name: Blugre Coffee
spots.desc: The atmosphere is very comfortable with jazz music. Good desserts and light meals to go with espresso coffees, teas, iced-blended drinks, and excellent fresh-squeezed lemonade.

spots.name: Tatay Pepe's Restobar
spots.desc: Enjoy live entertainment nightly, rain or shine- beginning 9:30PM to 1AM with acoustic modern, alternative and contemporary music and a few love songs.

spots.name: Carlos P. Garcia House
spots.desc: The residence of the former Philippine President and his family in Tagbilaran, it has been converted into a museum featuring presidential memorabilia. Much of the house's original furniture has also been preserved, including the former President's bed and work desk. While admission is free, a donation box is set up by the entrance.
spots.addr: A. Hontanosas cor. F. Rocha Sts., Poblacion II

spots.name: Casa Rocha-Suarez Heritage Center
spots.desc: Built sometime between 1800 and 1830, it is one of the oldest standing structures in Tagbilaran, and one of the few remaining trading villas in Bohol. Owned by the Rocha-Suarez family, it was converted into a museum in 2005, with several of the family's furniture, heirlooms, personal effects and mementos, accumulated over five generations, on display.

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines, Bohol Branch
spots.desc: It was the Escuela La Niña, and then becsme the Provincial Library of Bohol. The museum was opened in July 2008 after moving from the Carlos P. Garcia House. The museum has exhibits on the wildlife, traditions and culture of Bohol, the island's geological history, as well as a room featuring paintings from students throughout the province.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: Plaza Rizal
spots.desc: Formerly the Plaza del Principe, it is the traditional center of the city. A monument to José Rizal stands in the center, while a monument to Carlos P. Garcia stands to the east. A replica of the Chocolate Hills is located to the west beside the Rizal monument.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: President Carlos P. Garcia Memorial Park
spots.desc: The largest park in the city, it fronts the site of the future new Provincial Capitol of Bohol. A large monument to Carlos P. Garcia is located in the park's center.

spots.name: Site of the Blood Compact
spots.desc: One of the city's most famous tourist attractions. This is a sculpture commemorating the Sandugo (blood compact) made between Datu Sikatuna and Miguel Lopez de Legazpi in 1565, with a wonderful view of the Bohol Sea and coastal mangroves. 100 m to the east is a marker erected by the now-National Historical Commission of the Philippines in 1941 for the same event.

spots.name: St. Joseph the Worker Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Diocese of Tagbilaran, it is one of the six original churches of Bohol established by the Jesuits in 1595. The current church structure however dates back to the mid-1800s, after the original church burned down.

spots.name: BQ Mall
spots.desc: This four-storey building has a movie theater, a BQ supermarket, several stores, and its own small department store with a large souvenir section.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: Island City Mall
spots.desc: The largest mall in the city, it has several shops, a movie theater, a department store and a large Alturas supermarket. The mall is also the terminus for a number of jeepney routes within the city and to neighboring towns.

spots.name: Plaza Marcela
spots.desc: This mall is the closest shopping center to the airport and seaport. Has a Alturas supermarket

spots.name: Tagbilaran City Square
spots.desc: The smallest of the city's malls, it promotes itself as Tagbilaran's version of the Greenhills Shopping Center in Manila. It is built on the site of the old Tagbilaran Public Market, which moved to the city's northern outskirts beside the Island City Mall. The two-storey mall has several computer and mobile phone stores, and wholesale products on the second floor.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: Chicken Ati-Atihan
spots.desc: The main competitor to Jo's Chicken Inatô, this open-air restaurant serves Filipino dishes alongside its special grilled chicken.

spots.name: Garden Café
spots.desc: This restaurant is owned and operated by the Philippine chapter of the International Deaf Education Association (IDEA), and true to its ownership, most of the employees are members of the local deaf community.
spots.addr: Juan S. Torralba Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: JERAC's Pizza
spots.desc: This pizzeria is home to Tagbilaran's largest pizza, measuring 22 inches (around 600).
spots.addr: G/F Gallares Court, Graham Ave. cor. Ma. Clara Wharf Rd., Cogon

spots.name: JJ's Seafood Village
spots.desc: Located along the shores of Tagbilaran Bay, this restaurant specializes in several cuisines, though true to its name, it serves many seafood dishes. The "village" also has conference facilities, a pool and a small hotel inside (850 for a double room).
spots.addr: Knights of Columbus Drive, Poblacion II

spots.name: Jo's Chicken Inatô
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in chicken inatô, the Cebuano version of the more-well known chicken inasal found on Negros. They also serve Boholano versions of Cebuano delicacies, such as binakhaw (local kinilaw, or vinegared fish), as well as standard Filipino fare.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia East Ave. cor. S. Matig-a St., Poblacion I

spots.name: Shiang MaNou
spots.desc: Serving mostly traditional Cantonese dishes, this is one of two upscale Chinese restaurants in the city. It however also has a selection of budget meals for 75.
spots.addr: J. Borja cor. C. Gallares Sts., Poblacion II

spots.name: Sweet Home Café
spots.desc: This quiet café is tucked away from the main downtown area. They serve coffee shop staples (i.e. cakes and pastries), and mains.
spots.addr: J. Borja cor. Remolador Sts., Poblacion II

spots.name: Club Sphere
spots.desc: Run by the Metrocentre Hotel and Convention Centre, it is the only nightclub in Tagbilaran, specializing in dance hits. Visiting DJs play here when they visit the city. The club is small though, with only a maximum capacity of 100 persons.
spots.addr: Carlos P. Garcia Avenue, Poblacion II

spots.name: Masskara Festival
spots.desc: A big annual Mardi Gras like event celebrated every 3rd week of October in Bacolod. Each of the city's barangays (districts) joins the competition for the fiercely competitive best costumed group. Lots of food and handicraft stalls, street dancing and beer at the Bacolod city plaza area. "Masskara" means "Mask" in Hiligaynon and Tagalog. The use of colorful masks with large smiles represent the…

spots.name: White Beach
spots.desc: This is what most people are here for, but there are environmental rules and the beach is a challenge for people with disabilities. It is a lovely stretch of powdery white sand against azure water, it's also the commercial center of the island. The long beach is divided into three sections, Station 1, Station 2, and Station 3. Station 1 is the northernmost and has the widest beachfront, where…

spots.name: Puka Beach
