spots.desc: A quiet stretch of white sand along the northern tip of the island, Puka Beach is an image of what most people expect on a tropical island: white sand, azure water, and relatively empty. This is where locals gather the small puka shells for some of the jewelry that is sold on the island so expect the sand to be more coarse than on White Beach. The water tends to be a little rougher on this side…

spots.name: Baling Hai Beach
spots.desc: This is a quiet little cove just north of Diniwid Beach, where you can enjoy swimming, snorkeling and dining in a relaxed, peaceful environment. There are some fantastic views from the clifftop restaurant. Baling Hai is often included as a stop-off on an island boat tour.

spots.name: Bulabog Beach
spots.desc: Come there on a windy days to see kiteboarders doing high jumps and crazy tricks.

spots.name: The Bat Cave
spots.desc: You will see in several tour guides and maps of Boracay something called the Bat Cave, which houses many small insectivorous bats (the larger fruit bats roost in the trees on the hillside above Punta Bunga Beach), and locals will be more than happy to accompany you there for a fee, or "tip". The cave is on the western-end of the island and down several dirt roads. The guide will then take you on…

spots.name: Freestyle Academy Kitesurfing School
spots.desc: Offers lessons from beginner to advanced. All instructors are IKO-certified.

spots.name: Hangin Kite Center
spots.desc: The island's first kite center. Offers lessons from beginner to advanced. All instructors are IKO-certified.

spots.name: Isla Kiteboarding school
spots.desc: The biggest school on Boracay. Very passionate about kitesurfing and very professional.

spots.name: Pinas Kite Boarding
spots.desc: Locally owned kite-boarding shop, offers courses from level 1 to 3. All instructors are IKO-certified.

spots.name: Bella Isa Salon & Spa
spots.desc: A little spot on the beach in Station 3 with upscale decor and professional staff. They provide a full range of services including massage, facials, foot spa, and hair services.

spots.name: Tirta SPA
spots.desc: — found in Sitio Malabunot, Manoc-Manoc, area. Indian treatments in a stunning environment. Friendly and helpful staff. It is a good idea to compare prices between Tirta Spa, Mandala Spa, and Shangri-La Boracay to find the best deal.

spots.name: Ariel's Point
spots.desc: Ariel’s Point is an affordable eco-adventure destination for Boracay travellers who want to experience the natural splendor of the Philippines and meet fellow travellers. Located 30 minutes away from Station 1 by outrigger boat, Ariel’s Point allows travelers to enjoy a wide array of adventurous activities such as cliff diving (the destination has five different platforms ranging in height from 3…
spots.price: 2000 for round-trip boat transfer, a BBQ buffet, unlimited drinks (bottled water, beer, soda, rum), and access to cliff…

spots.name: Parasailing
spots.desc: Take a parasailing tour around the island, to explore quiet beaches and snorkel sites. Ask your crew to organize a romantic BBQ on the beach with fresh grilled seafood, if you like. Cruise back at sunset to experience breathtaking views.

spots.name: Motorbiking
spots.desc: It is worth hiring motorbikes or scooters out to explore the island, as there are other beautiful beaches on the other side of the island that are even better for snorkeling that will be completely deserted. Hire them for a couple of days and you should get a discount. The roads are a bit dodgy, and some are still being constructed, but it's a good laugh and better than plunking yourself on a…

spots.name: Horseriding
spots.desc: Horse riding is a fun activity in Boracay. Get off the beaten path and experience villages and scenery most other visitors don't get to see. All levels of experience are catered to. Ask a tricycle to take you to the Boracay Horse Riding Stables.

spots.name: CityMall Boracay
spots.desc: A new shopping mall with a big Savemore supermarket and many fast food outlets.

spots.name: Kolai Mangyan Fudhaus
spots.desc: Good local cafe serving Filipino cuisine. Excellent value and quality. Good reviews.

spots.name: Andok's
spots.desc: Andok's, which has 5 locations, sells rotisserie and fried chicken as well as favorite Filipino dishes.

spots.name: D'Talipapa Market
spots.desc: Fresh seafood market with relatively cheap prices. Around the place are a variety of food stores that offer to cook for you. You can buy fresh seafood, etc., right near the stores, then have the stores cook it for you however you like. For example, you can get crabs for 400 for 1 kg opposed to buying in restaurants that charge 200 per 100 grams. However, most of the seller are quite pushy and…
spots.price: scallops 300/kg, lobster 1000, fish steak 150. Cooking prices 100-200

spots.name: Smoke
spots.desc: A very good budget eatery. Local dishes, meat and seafood dishes, omeletes and excellent sandwiches are on offer. Most meals cost around 120 and are all cooked fresh. If you are around between 11AM and 2PM you get a free drink of iced lemon tea with every rice meal.
spots.addr: down one of the alleys opposite Lemon cafe in D'Mall

spots.name: Jammers
spots.desc: Up and running for more than 8 years, amazing burgers, hotdogs, fruit shakes, etc. A lot of negative reviews, people say it's overrated.
spots.addr: on the front beach of D'Mall

spots.name: True Food
spots.desc: Offers fiery Indian cuisine that will awaken the tastebuds. The place is cozy with straw mats and over-sized cushions. The staff is polite and very accommodating. For those who enjoy the spicier side of life, try the tandoori chicken.

spots.name: The Sunny Side Cafe Restaurant
spots.desc: Good place to have a breakfast. Very high ratings on rating sites.

spots.name: Lemoni Cafe
spots.desc: This place serves a variety of breakfasts, lunches and light meals. The service and presentation is excellent.

spots.name: Dos Mestizos
spots.desc: This restaurant is the brainchild of respected Boracay chef & restaurateur Binggoy Remedios and his close childhood friend, Jose Ramon Valdes Nieto. Both owners have Spanish ancestors, hence the name "Dos Mestizos". This restaurant serves a selection of excellent tapas and is located between stations 2 and 3, behind the Tourist Center.

spots.name: Aria
spots.desc: Delicious Italian food. If they don't give you the spicy olive oil bottle on the side for your custom made pizza, make sure you ask for it.

spots.name: Hama
spots.desc: A Japanese restaurant located at the D'Mall and just across The Hobbit House.

spots.name: Fridays Boracay
spots.desc: All day dining, themed dinner, Friday night buffet, seafood grill, plus 3 cultural dance shows every week with fire dance.

spots.name: Heidiland Deli
spots.desc: Next to the main plaza at the D'Mall Phase IV is a fully air-conditioned European style deli selling all kinds of deli food as cheeses, cold cuts, salami, yoghurt, wines, etc. Locally famous for reasonably priced sandwiches, other stuff is usually expensive.

spots.name: The Hobbit Tavern
spots.desc: With great food, drinks and live music, this place is the best of the Hobbit House chain. The main draw is the midget staff, however.

spots.name: Valhalla Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: In the mall is a refurbished steakhouse with a varied and interesting menu.

spots.name: Kasbah
spots.desc: Authentic Moroccan cuisine serving exquisite tagines and couscous.

spots.name: Bamboo Lounge
spots.desc: Serves a good selection of Chinese food in a relaxed beachfront setting. Quite average reviews.

spots.name: Manana
spots.desc: Serves large portions of tasty Mexican food. Guacamole is only available when avocados are in-season despite what the menu says. Average reviews left by customers.

spots.name: Obama Grill Bar-Restaurant
spots.desc: Steak restaurant, opened April 2009. Some say it's expensive and the portions are small.

spots.name: Ole
spots.desc: A great place to go for Spanish tapas and other specialties. Beware - the main courses are enormous!

spots.name: Tilapia 'N Chips
spots.desc: Visit this place for good beer-battered fish and chips. They also serve Asian and Western style fish dishes, burgers, sandwiches and soup at this modern, airconditioned restaurant. Take out also available.

spots.name: Titos (Resto & Grill)
spots.desc: Serve modern Filipino cuisine that combines the casual comfort of a home cooked meal with the relaxed sophistication of fine dining. Drop by for a quick snack or a delicious meal and enjoy the live music coming from Pat's Creek and Bom Bom Bar.

spots.name: Deparis Beach Resort
spots.desc: One of the first European restaurants on the island, the first in fact to have chocolate mousse and Italian pizza when the island was without electricity in the early 1980s. Owned by the infamous and eccentric Frenchman Roger Deparis who has lived on the island since his backpacking days, it is a throwback to the old island style of mismatched decorations and heavy foliage.

spots.name: Cowboy Cocina
spots.desc: Serves tasty steaks, ribs and other grilled dishes, and arguably the best burgers in Boracay.

spots.name: Cyma
spots.desc: Excellent food and service at this Greek restaurant. Try the mezedes combination, the spinach and artichoke fondue and the chicken souvlaki.
spots.addr: in the new part of the D'mall

spots.name: Real Coffee
spots.desc: Serves a variety of pancakes, sandwiches, omelettes, baked goods and salads as well as freshly brewed coffee. The mother-and-daughter owners also get repeat customers who have been going there for years. They are also famous for their lemon muffin cupcakes, which are very much in demand.
spots.hours: 7AM-7PM, take away shop downstairs works till 9PM

spots.name: Starbucks
spots.desc: Of the coffee shops of this famous chain. On the other side, it's extremely small cafe without even places to seat.

spots.name: Bom Bom Bar
spots.desc: A native-style beach bar that often has live music. It's a popular hang out for artists and musicians.

spots.name: Charlie's Steakhouse & Diner Restaurant
spots.desc: This bar is a long-time favorite on Boracay with live bands that play covers. Customers are invited to sing with the bands.

spots.name: Cocoloco Beach Resort
spots.desc: An attractive beach bar and restaurant that also serves tasty food. You can enjoy your drink by the beach, under the coconut trees, and there's a pool table in the bar too. Several years ago it started offering bungalows for rent as well.

spots.name: Juice Bar
spots.desc: Offers top notch cocktails and a variety of "sneaky smoothies". with a wide open courtyard opening up to the beach it tends to fill up by around 11PM but still very comfortable. The crowd is a nice mix of locals and foreigners. Great staff and charming bartenders. There was a report in 2016 that it was closed.
spots.addr: right between Boracay Regency and Boat Station 2

spots.name: Bei Kurt und Magz Restaurant
spots.desc: Run by friendly Bavarian Kurt and his wife Mags. It's a very popular spot to meet and chat, and one of the few places on the island serving draft beer. Serve German and Filipino food.

spots.name: Nigi Nigi Nu Noos
spots.desc: A popular, centrally located spot to have a cool drink and enjoy a little people-watching. The manager is an expat. It is a hotel as well.
spots.addr: between boat stations 2 and 3, three minutes walk north of the tourist center

spots.name: Red Pirates Pub
spots.desc: A native style beach bar (Angol, near boat station 3) with a relaxed and friendly atmosphere and good selection of fruity cocktails as well as affordable ice cold beer. It's a good place to meet other travelers and chat, and on weekends, selected weekdays and full moon nights there is live music and an all-you-can-eat beach BBQ and buffet (Fridays).

spots.name: Shantal's Resto Bar
spots.desc: Revered, family-owned cantina on the beach with great value homemade food. The menu offers a bit of everything and the friendly staff will go out of their way to make you feel right at home. Has a popular Happy Hour from 2PM-8PM, offers one of the best beachside and sunset views on the island, and bumps a non-stop soundtrack of the best in electronic, hip-hop, R&B/soul, and reggae music.
spots.addr: Station 3 at the pathway to Dave's Straw Hat Inn, Morenos, and Escurel

spots.name: Experience Dinagyang
spots.desc: Step up to the beat, enjoy the sound of drums and bare feet stomping into the pavement in perfect unison, and join the locals dancing in the streets with a bottle of beer. The Dinagyang Festival is celebrated every 4th Sunday of January in Iloilo.

spots.name: Paraw Regatta
spots.desc: Claimed as the oldest traditional craft in Asia, the Paraw Regatta is a race among seafarers on colorful sailboats called Paraws in the Iloilo Strait between Guimaras Island and the city of Iloilo. The present-day paraw managed to maintain its original design from the sailboats of the first settlers from Borneo who were in search of a peaceful home in 1212 AD. Surviving centuries, the paraws have…

spots.name: Balangiga Massacre
spots.desc: Every 24 September, the locals in Balangiga town celebrate the 1898 massacre in which the native Balangigans rose up and attacked the abusive American soldiers stationed in their town. The celebration includes a reenactment of the massacre. After the uprising, the sole surviving American soldier made his way back to nearby fort Base (American fort). The Americans immediately dispatched a regiment…

spots.name: Balaan Bukid Shrine
spots.desc: Hike to the 14 stations of the cross. Take a ferry bound for Jordan Wharf in Ortiz Port (Iloilo City). From Jordan Wharf, take a tricycle ride to the foot of Balaan Bukid. It's a 30-45 min hike to the top. During the Holy Week (Easter), there are special trips that transport visitors directly to the foot of Balaan Bukid.

spots.name: Guisi Light House
spots.desc: From Guisi Beach, follow a trail 15 minutes uphill to the Guisi Lighthouse for a great view of the beach. At the top of the hill are the ruins of a Spanish-colonial outpost and the rotting remains of the metal lighthouse structure.

spots.name: Trappist Monastery
spots.desc: An ornate cross-shaped church, with sections both for the monks (in the middle) and lay visitors (on the sides). A gift shop sells souvenirs and sweets.

spots.name: Roca Encantada
spots.desc: A summer house built on top of a huge rock, possessing a magnificent architectural design, overlooking the Legendary Seven Isles or Siete Picados and fascinating beautiful seascape of the northern part of Guimaras Strait. It was built as a pledge of the great Lopez matriarch, Doña Precentacion Hofeliña Lopez in 1910. It was declared by the National Historical Institute as a Heritage House or one…

spots.name: National Mango Research and Development Center
spots.desc: If you want to learn more about the sweetest mangoes of Guimaras, go here. The ideal month to visit it towards the end of summer where the mangoes are ripe and they offer picking activities. The arrangement of the mangoes are also very good for pictorials.

spots.name: Capitoguan Beach
spots.desc: Guimaras has a number of secluded beaches without road access, and Capitoguan is one of them. To get there,The beach operators charge a 50 pesos per person admission fee. If you have packed a tent with you, you pay 200 PHP fee to set up the tent overnight. There are also a few simple cabins which can be rented for 1500-2000 pesos per night. Amenities include a water pump, and a toilet which can…

spots.name: Mango Fruit Stalls Pasalubong
spots.desc: Come and visit the mango fruit pasalubong delicacies. Let's taste the sweetest mango here in Guimaras Island!

spots.name: Karangahan Falls
spots.desc: Has a deep catch basin ideal for swimming.

spots.name: Our Lady of Fatima Church de Legazpi City
spots.desc: A modern church with a semi-circular nave built in 1999.

spots.name: A. Bichara Silverscreens and Entertainment Center
Pacific Mall
spots.desc: Has a Metro Gaisano supermarket and a cinema.
spots.addr: F. Imperial St, Legazpi Port District

spots.name: Ayala Malls Legazpi

spots.name: Jose Maria Panganiban Monument
spots.desc: It is a monument dedicated to the Bicolano hero Jose Maria Panganiban, who was an active member of the La Solidaridad Propaganda movement during the waning days of Spanish Colonial Rule.

spots.name: Heroes Arch
spots.desc: A monumental arch that served as the entrance to the Spanish-era Port of Cavite.

spots.name: School of Rizal Site and Museum
spots.desc: Preserved Spanish-era schoolhouse, where Jose Rizal did his formal education between 1869 and 1871. Declared a National Historical Site, it used to be a private residence, until it was expropriated by the city government and turned into a museum.

spots.name: Balanga City Hall
spots.desc: A Neoclassical building which houses the city government offices. Beside the main building is a preserved water tower, and at nighttime, it is flooded with light.

spots.name: Plaza Lucero
spots.desc: A little plaza built on where Antonio Luna, a Filipino general during the Philippine-American War, was assassinated. A statue of Luna in horseback is erected on the spot where he was killed.
spots.addr: Rizal Street and Del Pilar Streets, Nabao

spots.name: Santa Cruz Marker
spots.desc: This is the oldest landmark in the city dating back to May 3, 1905, marking the safe landing of migrating Boholanos settling near the mouth of Dipolog River.
spots.addr: Intersection of Rizal Avenue and Martinez Street, Central

spots.name: Casa Bernedo
spots.desc: Casa Bernedo is a two-story ancestral house, originally owned by the then influential Bernedo family of Dipolog, now a museum and Center for the Culture and the Arts in the city.
spots.addr: Arellano Street corner Ranillo Street, Dipolog City

spots.name: Explore Dipolog Landmark
spots.desc: Opened in November 2019 which features the slogan of the same line, and it is near the Dipolog Watchtower.

spots.name: Basco Rolling Hills
spots.desc: Scenic hilly area offering views of the ocean and Mt. Iraya, with grazing cows, goats & other animals.

spots.name: Chawa View Deck
spots.desc: A perfect place to watch the sunset. Romantic sunset viewing. Highly recommended for sunset lovers.

spots.name: Rakuh A Payaman (Marlboro Country)
spots.desc: Scenic trails through rolling hills & lush meadows offering sweeping views of a rugged coast & sea.

spots.name: Casa Napoli Pizza
spots.desc: Best, real handmade pizza in Batanes! Handmade crust made from scratch, good mozzarella, and awesome flavor.

spots.name: Harbour Cafe-Basco
spots.desc: They serve a mixture of Filipino and Italian food. Try out their pasta and pork Sinigang.

spots.name: Cafe du Tukon
spots.desc: Great food and view, a must visit when you go to Batanes compete with outdoor and indoor dining.

spots.name: HiroJoy Cafe
spots.desc: Don't be fooled by the carinderia/eatery set up of this place. This is the best restaurant in Basco!

spots.name: Angela Manalang Gloria House
spots.desc: An old two-storey house that was once the residence of Angela Manalang Gloria, a poetess who was born in Guagua, Pampanga in 1907 and died in Tabaco in 1995.

spots.name: Tabaco Church
spots.desc: Completed 1750, it is one of the two heritage churches in Albay that are designated as National Cultural Treasures.

spots.name: Ishi Aya
spots.desc: Specializes in Japanese cuisine, but they also serve Filipino, Malaysian and Indonesian cuisine and fusion dishes.

spots.name: Basilica of Our Lady Of Peñafrancia
spots.desc: Established in 1985, it is the new home of Our Lady of Peñafrancia where the Traslacion starts when her image is led into procession around the city streets then brought to the cathedral.

spots.name: San Francisco Church de Naga
spots.desc: Established in 1578, it is the first church in the region built by the Franciscan Friars. The surrender of the Spanish forces to the Bikol revolutionaries Elias Angeles and Felix Plazo took place here on September 18, 1896. The church was reduced to rubble by the heavy bombing of Naga in World War II, and the church remained in ruins until the present new edifice was constructed.

spots.name: Christ the King Church Naga
spots.desc: Solemn chapel inside the campus just a short distance from the city's main cathedral. The interior is light and airy but for me, the most interesting is the portrayal of Jesus' image stylized as Filipino/Bicolano in the stained glass windows.

spots.name: Malabsay Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall near Mt. Isarog. It can be accessed by hiking in the Panicuason trail or through the Stonehouse Gardens Resort. Accessed by a trail, this picturesque waterfall is a popular destination for relaxing & swimming.
spots.addr: Panicuason Road, Mount Isarog National Park

spots.name: Nabontolan Falls
spots.desc: Rests within the protected area of Mt. Isarog National Park and accessible through the Panicuason trail, this waterfall offers a breathtaking refuge from the busy city life and allows one to commune with nature. It is seldom visited by mountain climbers, hikers and picnic-goers because of its rough trail.

spots.name: Naga City Ecology Park
spots.desc: An ecological park in Brgy. San Felipe, at the foot of Mount Isarog. It is a five-hectare sprawl of tropical greenery, the park showcases various exotic plants, palms, an eco-walk maze, topiary garden, an orchid and mini-forest. Walkways, lawns, and pavilions provides for family picnics, stroll, and undisturbed appreciation of nature's beauty.

spots.name: Panicuason Hot Springs Resort
spots.desc: Hot springs attraction in the city. Located at the bottom of a forest river ravine accessible via a private road, this resort is smack at the center of the teeming rain forest of Mt. Isarog. The resort is a sight to behold, a virtual jungle paradise of ancient trees and giant ferns minus the wild animals. The resort is composed of several natural pools with temperatures ranging from a cold 20°C…

spots.name: Haciendas De Naga
spots.desc: It is a master-planned resort community designed by renowned green development architect, Felino Palafox, Jr. The resort offers a golf course, adventure park, and a variety of accommodations.

spots.name: Penafrancia Resort, Inc.
spots.desc: It is one of the oldest resorts in the city. Since its development in 1970, it has maintained its services and reputation in the city as one of the first resorts in Naga. Great resort that is good for Retreats, Reunions and other activities, almost pure fresh water..there are many pools fit for all ages.

spots.name: Fr. Miguel Robles De Covarrubias Monument
spots.desc: It is a monument in the plaza of Our Lady of Peñafrancia Shrine, the old home of Our Lady of Peñafrancia. It was constructed, along with the stage, to commemorate the 300 years of the Our Lady of Peñafrancia, the patroness of Bicolandia. It also depicts of how Fr. Miguel Robles de Covarrubias brought Ina to the Bicolanos.

spots.name: Nueva Caseres Plaza
spots.desc: Also known as the Oragon Monument, is a monument constructed by the local government of Naga City to commemorate Naga City's long history, and its charter anniversaries. The monument depicts Nueva Caceres during the Spanish Period. The yearly foundation day of Nueva Caceres is held in the monument.

spots.name: A La Virgen Milagrosa Monumento
spots.desc: In front of the Universidad de Santa Isabel is a historic monument built by the Daughters of Charity that is the management of the Universidad de Santa Isabel and is a major component of Catholic life. The monument commemorates the thanksgiving of the nuns after World War II in which that they were saved from the impending danger.

spots.name: Sto. Niño Monument
spots.desc: It is a monument located It is a monument unveiled by the Archdiocese of Caceres to commemorate the patronage of Santo Niño in the Archdiocese, being centered in the parish.
spots.addr: Santo Nino Memorial Park, Balagtas Road

spots.name: Jesse Robredo Monument
spots.desc: His burial site is at Eternal Gardens Naga City at Balatas Road where the Peñafrancia Basilica Minore is located and near to the monument. It is a commemorative monument to honor the late Jesse Robredo who was Naga City Mayor from 1988 to 2009. He was a great example of good governance in the country.

spots.name: Quince Martires Plaza
spots.desc: It is the monument at the heart of Naga's Central Business District I. It commemorates the martyrdom of 15 people from Naga who oppose Spanish Regime. It was on January 4, 1897 or barely 5 days after the National Hero –Dr. Jose P. Rizal – was executed when the 11 prisoners from Bicol were also executed on the same field in Bagumabayan (now Luneta). The four others had either died in prison as a…

spots.name: Padre Jorge Barlin Plaza
spots.desc: It is the only monument constructed to commemorate Bishop Jorge Barlin, the first Filipino bishop, which was from Baao, Camarines Sur.

spots.name: Plaza Quezon
spots.desc: It is the largest plaza in Naga City. It is where the Regional Civic Parade, Voyadores Festival, Military Parade are done in September during the festivities of Our Lady of Peñafrancia. It is also where international artists and showbiz caravans are held when visiting the city.

spots.name: Plaza Rizal
spots.desc: is the oldest plaza and monument in Naga City. It is the centerpiece of the Rizal Park which was the former park of the old Camarines Sur Provincial Capitol. It has Jose Rizal and some angels in the monument. Majority of trade fairs held in the city are sometimes done in the plaza. The plaza is also adjacent to the Plaza Quezon.

spots.name: LCC Mall Naga City
spots.desc: The Mall is recovering from its customers that previously lost due to the opening of SM. They have now a lot in the store having shopping. Likewise tenants are also improving which means that they are recovering.

spots.name: Chef Buster Cuisine
spots.desc: Great food! Affordable prices. A must-try restobar when you're in Naga City. Their meals are delicious and reasonably priced. Chef Buster's All Meat Pizza is a must-try. Rice meals, sizzling platter meals, pizza and fruit shakes are all delicious. They also serve beer which is great with pizza. Thank you Chef Buster for the great food.

spots.name: Burgbox
spots.desc: The burgers in BurgBox are unique and outrageously delicious. From the fresh ingredients to the juicy meat, it is one of the best burger places in Naga City.

spots.name: Tapsi Terminal
spots.desc: If you are looking for a budget friendly restaurant, you are in the right place. They have unli soup and man there cucumber pitcher serving size can accommodate 5 persons! The location is also strategic, the ambiance is okay.

spots.name: Feliciana Kuchen
spots.desc: Crab Mango Wrap, Beef Nachos, Crispy Fried Chicken, Chicken Wings, Lemon Butter Sauce, Stir Fried Prawn, Banana Shake, Seafood Tomato Pasta, Pumpkin Soup, Balsamic Vinaigrette Salad, Rice Platter, Fresh Cucumber Juice, Pork BBQ w Natong, Pot Roast, Shrimp Sinigang, Squid Salpicao, Baby Back Ribs.

spots.name: Starmark Cafe at Royale Emelina
spots.desc: Rice meals, Beef Yakiniku, the crispy pork Tonkatsu, beef teriyaki, and had a taste also of their fish fillet in a lemon sauce, it is so yummy and pleasant to the mouth. As for the drinks it's all okay too.

spots.name: La Playa's Pot and Coffee Bar
spots.desc: Rice in a bowl Pork-chop, Fried Chicken, Grilled Liempo/Burger/Fries/Coffee/Shakes.

spots.name: F3's Riverside Food Park
spots.desc: This is a simple drinking and billiards place in Naga City. Cheap beer, cheap Billiards table, friendly staff. Chill ambiance.

spots.name: Cellar Wine Bar Kitchen Deli
spots.desc: Quaint little resto tucked away from busy Magsaysay Avenue. Good steak and reasonably priced wine.

spots.name: Mangrovetum
spots.desc: Nice walkway. Good place to stretch your legs and do some walking.

spots.name: Villa Bayot
spots.desc: An old ancestral house made of iron and wood. Inside, there are antique religious articles, some believed to be miraculous.

spots.name: Rodeo Masbateño Grand Arena
spots.desc: The Only Rodeo arena in Asia with complete fixed structure including stockyard, bleachers, rodeo corral, clinic, VIP stage and rodeo office and activity center.

spots.name: St. Anthony of Padua Cathedral
spots.desc: The place is clean and organized. The sound system they used for the mass is clear and loud enough for the gatherers. They have electric fans everywhere so you can be comfortable while attending the mass.

spots.name: Sorsogon Provincial Museum and Heritage Center
spots.desc: There are guides on each station who will explain to you what's in the gallery (they're not experts as most of them are interns from senior HS or college doing immersion.

spots.name: Nono's Bakery - Yema Buko Pie
spots.desc: A must-visit bakeshop in Sorsogon if you’re a fond of cakes and pastries. Try their Yema Buko Pie, it’s one of the best. It’s really appetizing and I’m sure you’ll love it too.

spots.name: The Chancery Coffee Shop, Bookstore & Religious Store
spots.desc: Right beside the Fatima Church is this well decorated and good coffee shop in town. The price is affordable, and you have a good venue to chat and talk small or big talk topics.They are also selling supported locally produced products on display.

spots.name: St. Hyacinth Church
spots.desc: An elevated historic chapel established in 1604, 100 years older than the Sts. Peter and Paul Cathedral. American soldiers during the Philippine-American War used it as headquarters in 1899. St Hyacinth is the patron saint of the city whose feast is celebrated every August 15 coinciding with the Pav-vurulun Festival. The oldest brick structure in the city is the first parochial building built by…
spots.addr: Mabini Street corner College Avenue, Barangay Centro 8

spots.name: Cagayan Provincial Museum and Historical Research Center
spots.desc: This is a general museum that houses an extensive collection of artifacts, antiques, ethnography, trade wares, heirloom pieces and liturgical works of the province and fossils of animals that once roamed the valley. The museum houses extensive data on the discovery of Callao Man by the National Museum of the Philippines. Since 2023, it is housed in the old provincial jail, which in turn used to…

spots.name: Horno Ruins
spots.desc: A Spanish-era brick kiln located at Barangay Bagumbayan. This was used to fire bricks to be used for various structures during the Spanish colonial era in Tuguegarao such as the Tuguegarao Cathedral and the San Jacinto chapel. It is found beside a basketball court.

spots.name: Cagayan Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: The headquarters of the provincial government of Cagayan, housed inside a sprawling gated complex.

spots.name: Blue Lagoon
spots.desc: the place is beautiful, gatorade blue water, you have to hike for 20-30 min to the river, cave exploration 'was' optional.

spots.name: Rizal Park
spots.desc: The old town square, flanked by the Cagayan Museum and Tuguegarao Cathedral. At the center is an ornate monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal.

spots.name: SM City Tuguegarao
spots.desc: has a gross floor area of almost 90,000 m². Anchor tenants are SM Store and SM Supermarket. The mall also has cinemas, a foodcourt, Cyberzone, and amusement center.

spots.name: Mall of the Valley
spots.desc: One of the city's two public markets, run by the Xentro Malls chain since 2011.

spots.name: Pan de Cagayan Baguettes and Pizza
spots.desc: Pan de Cagayan is a family-owned restaurant by Babaran Family. It serves pizza, baguettes, pasta and many more!

spots.name: Tambayan Panciteria
spots.desc: Their pancit has many toppings, like chicharon bulaklak, karahay, and chorizo. You can even add more like siomai, longganisa and others. One of the best pancit in Tuguegarao.

spots.name: Cherry's Pansiteria
spots.desc: This is where the local go-to place for pansit batil patong.

spots.name: Adrinel's Barbeque Corner
spots.desc: Classic Filipino comfort food served at its best. Good choice to eat here everytime.

spots.name: Integrated Farmers' Cooperative - Dairy Processing Center
spots.desc: Sells dairy products such as candies and flavored milk, along with other Cagayan delicacies.

spots.name: Bonifacio Park
spots.desc: Houses a statue of Andres Bonifacio. It is also a common site for demonstrations.

spots.name: Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Ilagan plant
spots.desc: There are guided tours where visitors can see the mechanized process of how Coca-Cola is produced.

spots.name: Giant rocking chair
spots.desc: This, the largest in the world, was constructed within 29 days with a cost of 175,000.

spots.name: Queen Isabela Park
spots.desc: In front of the Provincial Capitol, it hosts concerts and various booths during the Bambanti Festival and has a pond, an amphitheater, and a monument to Queen Isabella II of Spain, after which the province was named.

spots.name: Isabela Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: A monumental office complex. In the courtyard is a statue of the province's longest serving governor, Faustino Dy Sr. At the back is the governor's official residence, known simply as Balai (House).

spots.name: Isabela Museum and Library
spots.desc: Housed in the old provincial capitol building, the museum has a collection on the province's history and culture.

spots.name: Isabela Sports Complex
spots.desc: A massive stadium with a track and field course. During the Bambanti Festival, this hosts the street-dancing competition involving teams from the different municipalities of Isabela.

spots.name: Capital Arena
spots.desc: A stadium with a seating capacity of 10,000. Opened in 2024, it hosts national-level competitions for indoor sports such as basketball and volleyball.

spots.name: Bambanti Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival celebrating Isabela's culture. Most major events are held at the amphitheater at Queen Isabela Park.

spots.name: Ilagan Public Market
spots.desc: There are some carinderias outside. Meat section may smell like cigarette smoke due to many vendors openly smoking.

spots.name: Northstar Mall
spots.desc: Two-story mall with a cinema, a Savemore supermarket, a McDonald's, and a hotel (see #Sleep. While air-conditioned, it may feel hot though inside.

spots.name: Superior Restaurant
spots.desc: One of the best Pansit Guisado in the City of Ilagan, Isabela. Superior Restaurant serves also delicious Pinoy recipes like Igado, Pork Adobo, Adobong Pusit, Lechon Kawali and more.

spots.name: Dom Dom
spots.desc: Egyptian restaurant owned by an Egyptian national. Some specialties such as Koshary require pre-order for at least a day in advance.

spots.name: Calvary Hills and The Chapel of Transfiguration
spots.desc: The place offers a pilgrimage venue for the Holy Week where life-size Stations of the Cross are presented from the foot of the hill going all the way up to the top where a Chapel was so designed to face the rising sun. The Chapel of Transfiguration offers pilgrims a commanding silence befitting a place of worship and can also be utilized for masses and retreat venues. A life-size image of Our…

spots.name: Balay Na Santiago
spots.desc: This used to be a barangay hall called Palacio del Barrio located at Calao West. Balay na Santiago houses the city museum and city library. This also serves as a multi-purpose function hall for art and music exhibitions and different occasion. The building itself is of the bahay na bato style popular during the Spanish colonial era.

spots.name: Santiago Concrete Water Tank
spots.desc: This concrete water tank has been a landmark in Santiago City since the early 1970s. It is almost 30 meters high, and towers over the whole city, visible from almost anywhere. It was constructed through the help of then Congressman Delfin Albano of the lone district of Isabela, and under the leadership of then Mayor Dodo Miranda. It was turned into a colorful mural and is now considered a City…

spots.name: Museo de Pattaradday
spots.desc: This museum at houses collection of artifacts, relics, dresses and antique furniture showing the culture and traditions that are typical in this region of Northeastern Luzon. Temporary closed as of September 2023.

spots.name: Katerina's Homemade Goodies
spots.desc: Has a wide variety of cakes and pastries that suits everyone's taste.

spots.name: Chang Noi Food House
spots.desc: Thai restaurant, Very tasty, flavorful and authentic Thai food. The prices are very reasonable.

spots.name: Bossjuan Kitchen
spots.desc: Good food, night band, good service. The service and food are worth the price.

spots.name: Sea wall Samonte Park
spots.desc: The park is located along the coast of Bacoor Bay and offers a stunning view of the sunset. The sea wall is decorated with colorful murals and sculptures that reflect the culture and history of the Filipino people. The park also has a playground, a fountain, a gazebo, and a stage where various events are held. The park is clean, well-maintained, and safe for visitors of all ages.

spots.name: Ramon Quijano Samonte Park
spots.desc: The main green space in the city, it is contiguous with Plaza Soledad and contains the clock tower, the Ermita, and a small aviary featuring exotic bird species, particularly rare chicken breeds. Cavite City Hall is at the north end of the park.

spots.name: Ermita de Porta Vaga Historical Monument
spots.desc: The chapel housing the Porta Vaga image stood on this site until it was destroyed by World War II bombing, although fortunately, the Porta Vaga image was safely hidden away in Manila. This is a miniature of the original chapel's facade to keep the history alive most especially to the locals. However, parts of the monument have been vandalized and partially dilapidated.

spots.name: Ladislao Diwa Shrine and Ladislao Diwa Historical Marker
spots.desc: This shrine is a historical landmark dedicated to Ladislao Diwa, a pride of Cavite City. This is locked most of the time but you can still visit and look from outside of the gate. The landmark is Cafe Antix, just make a turn and you’ll see this.

spots.name: Santa Monica Belltower
spots.desc: The only intact part of the Spanish-era Augustinian Recollect church that was destroyed during World War II. It is a towering red-brick structure that sits in the middle of a slum.

spots.name: New Chefoo Restaurant
spots.desc: Chinese x Filipino fusion foods. Affordable price and serving is good for 2-3 persons already. This was established in 1945.

spots.name: Asao Grill and Steak House
spots.desc: Steaks, grilled dishes, and sizzling plates, partnered with fried rice. They have some signs in both English and Cavite City Chavacano on the door. The name is from the Chavacano rendition of Spanish asado (roasted).

spots.name: kommonkind
spots.desc: Ancestral house turned into coffee shop. They also have thrift store and photo studio inside.

spots.name: Ciudad Cafe
spots.desc: A stellar cafe located before Samonte Park near Cavite City's City Hall, this cafe is quite the marvel especially during their night hours. Amazing food with a wide variety of choices.

spots.name: Daño Street
spots.desc: A scenic winding street, which overlooks Dasma's remaining patch of open fields. During Christmas season, it becomes a pedestrian-only street and a flea market (tiangge)

spots.name: Museo De La Salle
spots.desc: A unique cultural museum dedicated to the preservation of Filipino high culture and lifestyle, as well as the history of the De La Salle schools system.

spots.name: Promenade des Dasmariñas
spots.desc: A riverside park opened in 2019, at the tributaries of the Imus River.

spots.name: The District
spots.desc: Neighborhood mall. Has a Metro department store and a Toys R' Us location.

spots.name: New Cavite Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Opened in 2025, the complex replaced a previous office at the back of SM Trece Martires that became too cramped. The new building is a massive and imposing edifice whose design is inspired by the Aguinaldo Shrine in Kawit, complete with a towering spire at its center. At the front are large bronze statues of Cavite's own Emilio Aguinaldo and his main rival for leadership of the Revolution, Andres…

spots.name: St. Jude Thaddeus Parish Church
spots.desc: A modernist yet airy and cheery church featuring curved ceilings, painted windows and a large sculpture of the crucified Christ reclining on its back at a 45-degree angle in the altar.

spots.name: Plaza Rizal
spots.desc: It is near the church San Isidro Labrador Parish, The Historic Alberto Mansion (maternal house of Rizal), The Sentrong Pangkultura ng Biñan and more. Rizal monument believed to be a work of the National Artist Guillermo Tolentino.

spots.name: Museo ng Biñan
spots.local: Sentrong Pangkultura ng Biñan, Cultural Center of Biñan
spots.desc: A Spanish-era warehouse that was converted into a school and later the municipal hall. After local government offices moved to a larger complex in barangay Zapote in 2010, the building has hosted the city museum and a cultural center.

spots.name: Shrine and Parish of San Isidro Labrador
spots.desc: Biñan's main Roman Catholic church, built in its present modernist state in 1970 after being destroyed multiple times since the Spanish era by fires, natural disasters and wars. Its belfry is a copy of a Spanish-era original that was destroyed by lightning in 1870.

spots.name: Splash Island
spots.desc: Prime water park with long, winding slides and an artificial wave pool. It is frequented by Manila locals, and was once a common filming location for some Filipino movies. Outside food and drinks are not allowed, and you are required to buy them in-park, albeit at extortionate prices.

spots.name: Biñan Day
spots.desc: A three-day festival to commemorate Biñan's cityhood, liberation from the Japanese, and its original founding.

spots.name: Puto Latik Festival
spots.desc: Held every May 15-23, it showcases Biñan's local delicacy, Puto Biñan (or Putong Latik)

spots.name: Pavillion Mall
spots.desc: Managed by the retail arm of real estate giant, Ayala Corporation, it has fast food and some upmarket chain restaurants, various shops, and a Puregold supermarket.

spots.name: Central Mall Biñan
spots.desc: A three-storey mall with some fast-food chains, and a Savemore supermarket.
spots.addr: Jeepneys headed for Olivarez stop/terminate here

spots.name: St. Polycarp Parish Church
spots.desc: The city's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 18th century and restored in the 2020s. A few 19th-century bells are displayed at the side, while in front, a memorial commemorates the 35 people killed at the churchyard during an agrarian revolt known as the Sakdalista Uprising in 1935.
spots.addr: P. Burgos Street, Barangay Poblacion Uno

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine of San Vicente Ferrer
spots.desc: The city's second Roman Catholic church, containing a revered image of Saint Vincent Ferrer.

spots.name: Calamba Baywalk
spots.desc: This is also the jump-off point for the ferry that goes to Calamba island in Laguna de Bay. There are food stalls here from which you can buy quick meals and refreshments.

spots.name: Republ1c Wakepark
spots.desc: A wakeboarding park inside the Nuvali development in Canlubang

spots.name: SM City Calamba
spots.desc: Huge SM mall, providing a refuge from the cacophony of the Calamba Crossing area.

spots.name: Walter Mart Makiling
spots.desc: Has some fast food restaurants and shops, an Uno department store, and supermarket.

spots.name: Ippon Yari
spots.desc: Authentic Japanese dining, including common Japanese fare like bento, ramen, sushi, tempura and shochu. Tables have tatami mats.

spots.name: Quezon Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: A grand Neoclassical building that houses the provincial government offices of Quezon province. It dates back to 1908, and is a National Historical Site. Perfect place to get your photo with Quezon marker sign.

spots.name: Governor's Mansion
spots.desc: The official residence of the governor of Quezon, built during the Spanish period.

spots.name: Lucena Perez Park
spots.desc: Small green space honoring former governor Don Filemon Perez with stone monuments and a playground.

spots.name: La Casa de Cafe
spots.desc: Foods are affordable and delicious, Pasta, Baby Back Ribs, Fries, etc.

spots.name: Special Lomi Batangas
spots.desc: This place offers quick-served, hot, tasty Lomi Batangas. It is a big and affordable serving of noodles, egg, meat, topped with chicharon, all in a thick, viscous and seasoned soup.

spots.name: Bosschito Roasted Chicken
spots.desc: Grilled Porkchop and Grilled Liempo are equally delicious! Serving size was fair, price was affordable, and grilled aroma was very appetizing.
spots.addr: Old Manila South Road corner Bonifacio Drive

spots.name: The Green Bowl
spots.desc: Green Bowl refreshingly offers healthy food choices in a city where vegetable dishes are hard to find.

spots.name: Kentouka
spots.desc: This is a good place if want to try to experience Japanese ramen. Have the Tonkotsu and Tantanmen a try and you'll definitely like it.

spots.name: Doña Aurora Aragon-Quezon House
spots.desc: Modest, historic house museum owned by the family of Aurora Quezon, First Lady from 1935–1944.

spots.name: Ermita Hill
spots.desc: Tromba Marina was the name given to the destructive tidal wave that struck Baler on December 27, 1735. This monstrous wave caught everyone off-guard when it arrived around 2:00 AM. The town was devastated in seconds and many lives were immediately lost. Seven families managed to survive the great blow of the tidal wave and found their safe haven in Ermita Hill. The ones who made it through were…

spots.name: Cemento Beach
spots.desc: Known for its chill atmosphere, this secluded, rocky beach is a popular destination for surfers.

spots.name: Diguisit Beach
spots.desc: Popular for picture-taking, this picturesque coral beach features pebbly sand & unique boulders.

spots.name: Ditumabo Mother Falls
spots.desc: Popular waterfall with a cold-water pool at its base, reachable by a lush 45-minute nature trek.

spots.name: Tromba Marina Sculpture
spots.desc: Tromba Marina was the name given to the destructive tidal wave that struck Baler on December 27, 1735. This monstrous wave caught everyone off-guard when it arrived around 2:00 AM. The town was devastated in seconds and many lives were immediately lost. Seven families managed to survive the great blow of the tidal wave and found their safe haven in Ermita Hill. The ones who made it through were…

spots.name: Balete Tree (Millenium Tree)
spots.desc: A balete tree locally called "Millennium Tree" in Barangay Quirino, Maria Aurora is claimed to be the largest of its kind in Asia. It is estimated to be about more than 600 years old and 60 metres (200 ft) tall with its roots about 10 metres (33 ft) to 15 metres (49 ft) in diameter.

spots.name: Buencamino View Point
spots.desc: This place is really beautiful and majestic scenery of Aurora Memorial National Park.
spots.addr: Nueva Ecija - Aurora Road, San Luis

spots.name: Aurora Province Welcoming Arch
spots.desc: This place is the gateway to Aurora, If you are looking for a nice fun of sight seeing this place is highly recommended. The place is suited for exploring the mountains and road cycling, Now the most visited area in Bongabon .

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines - Baler
spots.desc: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, with exhibits on Aurora's natural history and culture.

spots.name: Sabang Beach
spots.desc: Relaxed beach featuring strong waves suitable for surfing, with a peaceful vibe.

spots.name: Cemento Beach
spots.desc: Known for its chill atmosphere, this secluded, rocky beach is a popular destination for surfers.

spots.name: Lipit Beach
spots.desc: It's a nice sandy beach. Big waves are good for surfing. It's facing the Pacific Ocean.

spots.name: Kusina Luntian
spots.desc: Filipino restaurant in Nipa Hut (traditional Filipino house).

spots.name: Bay's Inn
spots.desc: It has a restaurant by the beach, good value Filipino-western style meals.

spots.name: Bahia de Baler Garden Resort & Restaurant 1
spots.desc: More expensive than its neighbor, Day's Inn, but a bit more classy too.

spots.name: Balanga Wetlands
spots.desc: A wetland area along Manila Bay which sees migratory birds annually.

spots.name: Bataan Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Rebuilt from an older building destroyed during World War II, it has a historical marker commemorating the fall of Bataan in 1942, and the struggles of Filipinos and Americans to defend democracy.

spots.name: Bataan World War II Museum
spots.desc: Housed in a former school building where the US field commander, Major General Edward King signed the instrument of surrender of Allied forces in Bataan to the Japanese, it contains artifacts and dioramas of World War II events such as subsequent death march and surrender monument.

spots.name: Plaza Mayor de Ciudad de Balanga
spots.desc: This plaza is a spectacular representation of how it is to live during that era. The Gothic architecture, peaceful surroundings.

spots.name: Bataan Tourism Park
spots.desc: an extraordinary place, a park where you can be relieved from stress. best photography place.

spots.name: Death March markers
spots.desc: The Bataan Death March passed through the center of Balanga, as marked by the life-size white obelisks lining the original route along Bataan National Road.

spots.name: Newstar Shopping Mart - Balanga
spots.desc: Great place to find cheap priced items, from clothing, shoes, and house tools to appliances. It has huge parking space.

spots.name: Denbell's Fastfood and Snackhouse
spots.desc: Filipino restaurant. Delicious, home-style cooking that has survived the test of time.

spots.name: Cheenok's
spots.desc: Barbecue restaurant. One of a kind! The best BBQ place in Bataan.

spots.name: Sampalukan Restaurant
spots.desc: Delicious Pinoy food, prepared just like a hearty homecooked meal. Staff are welcoming and helpful.

spots.name: Joyous Tangway Restaurant
spots.desc: They have good Filipino dishes with good serving portions. Great place to stay also if you want to have beer and hang out at night. The location is accessible and can be reached easily even when commuting.

spots.name: Wooden Leaf Cafe
spots.desc: Health food restaurant, The best place to eat healthy veges salads, healthy sandwiches and healthy fruit shakes or fruits smoothies the best world class food.

spots.name: Jeepney Restaurant
spots.desc: It's a nice concept to be able to dine inside a jeepney. They serve Filipino food like kare-kare, sisig, okoy, inihaw etc.

spots.name: The Yard
spots.desc: Serves Pizza, pasta, western, Asian and fusion dishes. A highlight is the panizza.

spots.name: Bulacan Provincial Capitol View Park
spots.desc: City park with many flagpoles and monuments to local heroes.

spots.name: Museo ng Republika ng 1899
spots.desc: Housed in the convent of Barasoain Church, the museum tells the story of the First Philippine Republic.

spots.name: Kalayaan Tree
spots.desc: A more than 100-year old Siar tree named after the Filipino word for freedom for having existed during the First Philippine Republic.
spots.hours: depends on the compound’s opening hours

spots.name: Plaza de la Gobierno Militar
spots.desc: A colonial residence that was converted into a military garrison during the First Philippine Republic. It now houses the local offices of the power utility MERALCO and the house itself is only open if you have an electricity-related concern, but guards don't mind tourists taking pictures inside the compound.

spots.name: Santa Isabel de Unggaria Parish Church
spots.desc: A Mudejar-style Roman Catholic church built in 1863 that hosts a venerated image of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary.

spots.name: Bistro Maloleño
spots.desc: Opened in April 2013, Bistro Maloleno is a casual dining restaurant serving heritage Bulacan dishes derived from recipes compiled by one of the province’s leading food historians. It also serves standard Filipino fare and individual plates, along with a tie-up from a neighboring cafe, Le Jardin.

spots.name: Kaytitinga Falls
spots.desc: The way to Kaytitinga Falls is not well-developed that leads to non-accessibility of the trail. There are also no public toilets or showers in the area.

spots.name: St. Joseph the Worker Parish Church
spots.desc: SJDM's main Roman Catholic church, built in the 19th century and repaired to its original style despite being burned thrice in the Philippine Revolution, World War II, and the Huk Rebellion in 1950.

spots.name: People's Park of San Jose Del Monte City
spots.desc: SJDM's main recreational area containing an athletics stadium.
spots.addr: Santa Maria-San Jose del Monte Road, Sapang Palay Proper

spots.name: Padre Pio Mountain of Healing
spots.desc: A hilltop Roman Catholic shrine featuring a statue of Padre Pio accessible by climbing 150 steps.

spots.name: VS Orchids
spots.desc: The biggest orchids nursery and ornamental plants farm in Bulacan, measuring .

spots.name: Nueva Ecija Old Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: A neoclassical capitol building designed by the American architect and urban planner E. William Parsons. It used to house the government offices of the Nueva Ecija provincial government until it was relocated to the new capital at Palayan.

spots.name: Cabanatuan City Public Market
spots.desc: Very big public market with stores selling meat, fruits, vegetables and dry goods. The famous Longanisa of Cabanatuan is available inside.

spots.name: Kinnobuta Ramen House - IEKEI Ramen
spots.desc: If you want to eat an authentic Japanese cuisine, this is the best place to go!
spots.addr: #31 General Tinio Street Extension, corner St Joseph Avenue

spots.name: KC's Grill & Restobar
spots.desc: The ambience is relaxing, and the service is good. The ihaw ihaw food is delicious.

spots.name: Vicenticos
spots.desc: Great Filipino food showcasing the best of Cabanatuan. Food is authentic. It tastes as if it has been prepared the way that your lola would prepare it.

spots.name: Kamayan Food Park Main Branch
spots.desc: Authentic Filipino foods. The restaurant is completely outdoors and good for large groups and boodle fights. Also serving hot coffee, iced coffee, and milk shakes.
spots.addr: between 19th and General Tinio Street Extension

spots.name: Annapoorna
spots.desc: An Indian restaurant serving dishes from both the north and south of the country. Has vegetarian-friendly options. All their fish dishes use cream dory.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway, Hermogenes C. Concepcion Sr

spots.name: Tomo's Bar and Restaurant
spots.desc: Amazing place with wide variety of food and drink choices of excellent quality.
spots.addr: General Tinio Street Extension, Kapitan Pepe

spots.name: Governor Macario Arnedo Park
spots.desc: Historical and good for unwinding even though the place is simple.

spots.name: Heroes Park
spots.desc: This is a must visit landmark as it is full of history and heroes. Inside the compound are statues of Filipinos national heroes, mostly those born in Pampanga

spots.name: Museum of Philippine Arts and Culture
spots.desc: A privately-owned museum featuring Philippine art, religious artefacts and other items about Filipino culture.
spots.hours: 10AM-5PM, closed Mon, by appointment for group tours only Tue and Sun
spots.price: PHP300, PHP240 senior citizens and disabled, PHP200 students
spots.addr: MacArthur Highway, Ramar Village, San Agustin

spots.name: Crucifixions at San Pedro Cutud
spots.desc: Realistic reenactment of the crucifixion of Jesus on Good Friday, where penitents, usually men, are crucified on a hill.

spots.name: Bren Z. Guiao Sports Complex and Convention Center
spots.desc: A giant arena with a seating capacity of 30,000 people, used for conventions, concerts, sports, beauty pageants

spots.name: Funside Ningnangan-San Fernando Branch
spots.desc: Very affordable place if you want high quality seafoods. It's super Pinoy.

spots.name: Aling Lucing Sisig - San Agustin
spots.desc: the inventor of the famous Sisig (grilled and diced pork face).

spots.name: The Royal Place by JPS
spots.desc: America/Italian food restaurant. This place offers foods and beverages. it also caters for small events in their second floor as long you put a reservation.

spots.name: Souq Pampanga
spots.desc: Filipino food restaurant. Try the Lechon Kawali Kare-Kare, Okoy, or Crispy Sisig.

spots.name: Café Amazon-San Fernando Pampanga
spots.desc: The cafe has the most delectable Mille cake on this side of San Fernando, Pampanga. Layers of crepe between crème and mangoes, it’s a light airy cake that is different than your usual sponge. A must try when you have the chance! The coffee selection was good.

spots.name: Tarlac City Plazuela
spots.desc: The work they made in the plaza was exquisite. If you're in Tarlac City, try to stop by as admission is free and you'll be glad you did, especially the kids.

spots.name: Kart City
spots.desc: Two outdoor karting tracks, with an attached eatery and bar.

spots.name: Fortune (Hongkong) Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Authentic Chinese cuisine. Lots of parking space behind the restaurant.

spots.name: Razon's by Glenn
spots.desc: serving palabok, sisig with rice, lumpia, kare-kare, halo-halo.

spots.name: Conti’s Bakeshop & Restaurant - TarlacCity
spots.desc: Superb options of dine-in meals not only for takeout pastries and cakes. Prices speak well with the quality of their food.
spots.addr: Lot 16-22 Block 22, McArthur Hiway, Brgy, San Sebastian

spots.name: Tessie's Grills & Roasters Restaurant (TG&R)
spots.desc: Eat all you can. They serve many veggie dishes, making them vegetarian-friendly enough.

spots.name: D&C Cuisine
spots.desc: Filipino food restaurant. A mix of sumptuous and delicious meal offerings. Great place with upscale feel and worth-it value for money. Staffs are warm and welcoming. Place can be busy but still manageable. Highly recommended.

spots.name: Betty's Special Native Cakes
spots.desc: Food is good and the ambiance is great. Serving time for the food is not that long. They have a wide variety of choices for the menu and you can tell by the taste that they serve fresh ingredients.

spots.name: Zambales Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: The seat of the provincial government of Zambales, built with a slightly neoclassical façade.

spots.name: The Bakery by SE
spots.desc: Pastry shop with sit-down tables and menu that includes cakes, burgers and soup.
spots.addr: J. Gonzales Street corner Magsaysay Avenue, Zone 4 Poblacion (Sagapan)

spots.name: Ulo ng Apo Monument
spots.desc: A monument of a head of a chieftain in the middle of a roundabout in Rizal Avenue. According to local folklore, the area was once ruled by a benevolent chieftain who was known as "Apo" who was beheaded by rival tribes. The monument features the namesake of Olongapo (particularly from the phrase "Ulo ng Apo" or Apo's head).

spots.name: Marikit Park
spots.desc: A park beside the SM City Olongapo Central. At its entrance is a concrete mural/relief dedicated to Filipino workers, and a model of a RA-5 Vigilante aircraft. The park also has a children's playground.

spots.name: Bat Stop II
spots.desc: A hotspot for seeing bats, The best time to visit is sunset.

spots.name: Hellships Memorial
spots.desc: It’s a nice memorial to read about its history. The memorial does a great job conveying the history.

spots.name: The Hands that Freed the Nation
spots.desc: A historic monument, commemorating the Magnificent 12 Senators of the Republic of the Philippines who stood up and said "no" to the military bases in Olongapo and ended the foreign military presence in the country.

spots.name: Children of the Sun Returning
spots.desc: Symbolises the past event on how the volunteers saved the Subic Bay from the Mount Pinatubo eruption, transforming the former Navy Base.

spots.name: Spanish Gate
spots.desc: The old Spanish Gate at Subic is the remnant of the naval installation established by the Spanish colonial authorities in 1885. Two cannons straddle the gate as a reminder of its military past. Two markers are installed on both sides of the gate giving information about its origin. One can visit the gate with no special permission needed and it is generally open to the public.

spots.name: Waterfront Park
spots.desc: Morning or evening walk, jog, bike, picnic, play frisbee or badminton, etc. This is definitely a good place to be.

spots.name: Boardwalk Divers
spots.desc: Run by George AngDyPay, an experienced TDI and PSAI technical rebreather instructor. Set up to cater to both recreational and technical divers it has quickly become the dive center of choice for most tech divers. Guiding is done by local staff members who are all trained as divemasters and technical wreck guides. Accommodation is at the nearby hotels, Herbie's Mansion, Boardwalk Inn, and Mango…

spots.name: Scuba Tech Philippines
spots.desc: Runs PADI and TecRec technical courses from a luxury dive boat based in Subic Freeport Zone. The instructor, Andy Davis, is a highly qualified and experienced UK-trained instructor with PADI, SSI, BSAC, and DSAT TecRec. Daily scuba diving trips are offered to the wrecks and reefs of Subic Bay. These trips can be tailored to fulfill diver requirements at any level. Accommodation can be booked at…

spots.name: JEST Camp
spots.desc: Jungle survival training. Learn how to survive the harsh jungle environment through the courses that they offer.
spots.addr: J.E.S.T Camp, Upper Mau, Cubi-Triboa, Subic Bay Freeport Zone

spots.name: Inflatable Island
spots.desc: An beachside amusement park dealing with just about every floaty imaginable (unicorns, castles, dragons, etc).

spots.name: SM City Olongapo Downtown
spots.desc: Formerly known as 'Olongapo City Mall', the SM City Olongapo is a mid-sized flagship shopping mall by SM Supermalls in Olongapo.
spots.addr: Magsaysay Drive cor Gordon Avenue, Asinan

spots.name: Olongapo Public Market
spots.desc: The city public market sells souvenirs including native crafts, as well as local food products such as "kakanin".

spots.name: Brettos Deli - Olongapo Branch
spots.desc: A meat shop. They sell good meats, such as steaks, chicken sausage, and ground beef. as it is one of the few places that has imported US meat.

spots.name: American Hardware
spots.desc: Carries lots of useful things. All their products are imported from the US. They have lots of items that are very rare in the Philippines. American Hardware also runs the only car wash in Subic Bay.

spots.name: Royal Duty Free
spots.desc: The biggest department store in Subic. They carry imported and local housewares, cooking items, snacks, and branded clothing. Most of the items are surplus so they're actually cheaper. Has an extensive selection of cigarettes and perfumes.

spots.name: Ayala Harbor Point Mall
spots.desc: The first Ayala Mall development in the province of Zambales. This sprawling mall offers a wide variety of shopping, dining and entertainment choices. It also has its anchor stores such as Puregold Supermarket, Timezone (gaming arcade), Abenson Appliances, and four Ayala Cinemas. VIP lounges are available to special members so they could take a quick rest in the middle of their shopping or while…
spots.addr: Rizal Highway, CBD, Subic Bay Freeport Zone

spots.name: Royal Duty Free Hypermarket
spots.desc: A mini version of Royal Duty Free which is a stone's throw away from Harbor Point, this store offers duty free grocery items, clothing/apparel and other imported goods.

spots.name: Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: This place is good for vegetarian people.The food here are so delicious at a cheaper price.

spots.name: Texas Joe's House of Ribs
spots.desc: Chophouse restaurant. Smoked meats and ribs. Numerous barbecue sauces. Attentive service.

spots.name: Xtremely Xpresso Cafe Restaurant
spots.desc: A casual bistro style restaurant that serves breakfast, lunch and dinner The cafe is known to serve Italy's no. 1 coffee, Lavazza, and is famous for its unique collection of Italian menu.

spots.name: Coco Lime Restaurant
spots.desc: Subic Bay's beloved restaurant that offers a variety of Filipino and international dishes. Famous for its Pineapple Rice. The place is always full so always be ready to go there early to save a seat.

spots.name: Sakura Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Known by the locals as the authentic Japanese restaurant in Subic. They serve fresh sashimi and a variety of sushi choices.
spots.addr: Lot 5 Time Square Bldg.Corner Sta.Rita Rd. Subic Bay Freefort Zone and a branch at Harbor Point Mall

spots.name: Magic Lagoon Bar
spots.desc: Magic Lagoon Restaurant is near a man-made lagoon where you can catch your own fish and ask the staff to cook it for you. An ideal place for family outings and group activities.

spots.name: Baguio Craft Brewery Subic
spots.desc: Offers draft beer and beer on tap (Stella Artois or Heineken). This concept originated in the northern city of Baguio and features local beer brews and international selections.
spots.addr: Riverwalk, Harbor Point Ayala Mall, Subic Bay Freeport Zone

spots.name: Pier One Bar and Grill
spots.desc: Entertainment and dining. They have live bands, a dance floor and sports bar. They also offer a wide variety of dishes and beer food. Order beers by the bucket or try to get those beer towers. Located in the waterfront, sea breezes keep the place cool and airy.

spots.name: Museo Ilocos Norte
spots.desc: Small museum showcasing artifacts & other items exploring local & regional culture & heritage.

spots.name: Ilocos Norte Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: The headquarters of the provincial government of Ilocos Norte.

spots.name: Laoag City Hall
spots.desc: Here you can see the LAOAG letter sign. The building is an old Spanish type.

spots.name: Marcos Museum
spots.desc: A museum on the life of president Ferdinand Marcos, who was born in Sarrat in 1917.

spots.name: Dap-ayan ni Lawiswis
spots.desc: Try the Laoag Empanada along Rizal Street near Provincial Capitol.
spots.addr: #30-B East F. Siazon Road, Stanta Maria

spots.name: Macy's Diner
spots.desc: An American 1950s inspired restaurant. Serves most of your favorite American, Chinese, & Filipino foods.
spots.addr: Gen Segundo Ave. cor M.H. del Pilar St

spots.name: La Tabacalera Food Park
spots.desc: La Tabacalera is a new dining and lifestyle center in Laoag, the capital city of Ilocos Norte. There were a handful of food and retail shops.

spots.name: Kasay Marine Sanctuary
spots.desc: It features a 50-year-old giant clam. Formerly Wallace Air Station, this 101 hectares of base land at the end of Poro Point in San Fernando was acquired in 1903 for the United States Cavalry. It was the home of the 848th Aircraft Control and Warning Squadron which provided logistics and administrative support to other radar detachments under its chain of command. Turned over by the United States…

spots.name: Heroes' Hill
spots.desc: This is a nice diversion if you like climbing a staircase to see not much at all.

spots.name: Pindangan ruins
spots.desc: Spanish church ruins from 1764 looked after by Carmelite sisters.

spots.name: La Union Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: Landscaped gardens featuring orchids and aviary specimens, maybe a monkey or two.

spots.name: San Fernando City Plaza
spots.desc: Includes the Battle of San Fernando Marker at the northwestern portion of the Town Plaza with an inscription as to the account of how the Battle was started and won, enabling the establishment of the United States Army Base Base M at Poro Point which was eventually used as a build up area for the projected invasion of Japan.

spots.name: Bacsil Ridge
spots.desc: The Ridge constituted the East Flank of the 121st Infantry of the United States Armed Forces in the Philippines, Northern Luzon (USAFIP NL) during the Liberation in 1945.

spots.name: The Cliff of Poro
spots.desc: See the beautiful coastline alone with the sunset. Be careful.

spots.name: La Union Pasalubong Center
spots.desc: A well-managed government pasalubong center featuring local products of La Union province, some items are comparatively cheaper than in Vigan. Has clean restrooms. Artworks are also exhibited.

spots.name: The Northern Point Food Paradise & Skatepark
spots.desc: This food park is perfect for late night dinners, meetings, dates, chill hangouts, etc. In front of the place is a skatepark and it adds character to the establishment.

spots.name: Max's Restaurant
spots.desc: Filipino restaurant chain popular for its fried chicken served with banana ketchup.

spots.name: Magsaysay Fish Market and Landing Center
spots.desc: The fish industry in action. Here you can probably see some of Dagupan's much-acclaimed milkfish and other dainty creatures that dwell in the brackish water.

spots.name: Dagupan City Museum
spots.desc: Some say it's just the Dagupan mayor's office, but, hey, maybe you'll get to shake his hand and get your picture taken with him. There is a little choo-choo parked out front.

spots.name: Ciudad Elmina Restaurant
spots.desc: Quirky but serene setting where you get to eat right next to tilapia fish farms. Also, a good place to try pigar-pigar.

spots.name: Kuya Max
spots.desc: One of the original local restaurants in the area. They offer great pangasinan and ilocano dishes with a very reasonable price.

spots.name: Big Boy
spots.desc: Chain of family-friendly diners serving breakfast, burgers & other American comfort food.

spots.name: Urduja House
spots.desc: Named after the legendary woman Urduja, this is the official residence of the Governor of Pangasinan.

spots.name: Lingayen Public Market
spots.desc: You will find many different things to buy from here at a very cheap price. Sweets, seasonings, spices, fish, fruits, general house items like toiletries etc. and lots of other things, if you are into buying authentic small things as souvenirs, this place could be great for that too.

spots.name: Mesa de Amor
spots.desc: Great food. Has a very nice and relaxing ambiance; naturally and well-ventilated. There are a lot of antiques.

spots.name: Yani's Kitchen Ph
spots.desc: They serve very good tasting pizza. Cozy and quiet. Love this place.

spots.name: Bell Church
spots.desc: A Chinese temple situated in Barangay Balili in La Trinidad. It features Chinese architecture and is a known place of worship for Chinese residents and tourists. It is located near the town's boundary with Baguio.

spots.name: La Trinidad Strawberry Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival dedicated to the town's strawberry industry celebrated sometime between February and March.

spots.name: The Master's Garden
spots.desc: A where one can learn about organic farming. The facility is the first training center established in the region dedicated to organic farming.

spots.name: La Trinidad Trading Post
spots.desc: The biggest marketplace for highland vegetables in the country. Tourists may purchase vegetable products at the La Trinidad Trading Post at a cheaper price at this marketplace.

spots.name: Calajo
spots.desc: Calajo is a restaurant which primarily serves local Benguet cuisine. "Calajo" means "Welcome" in the Ibaloi language.

spots.name: Museum of Cordilleran Sculpture
spots.desc: The Museum of Cordilleran Sculpture was founded by George and Candida Ida Schenk over 30 years ago, and evolved from a small antique store in Manila, into dream to preserve a culture that is slowly dying. There are over 1,000 pieces in the collection of the museum, ranging from large-scale, carved wooden Bululs, masks to smaller scale figures, textiles, utilitarian objects, and composite objects.…

spots.name: Hot Spring
spots.desc: A geothermal hot spring next to a river can be reached via walking across rice terraces starting from Hungduan Elementary School. The road to the school however is not yet paved. Arrangements to visit will likely need to be made in town.

spots.name: Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort
spots.desc: Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort is on a six hectare lot in a pine forest above downtown Banaue. It has large grassy areas, picnic shelters, swimming pools, and a large function hall. This would be an ideal place for a school or other organization to have training sessions or meetings.

spots.name: Banaue Museum
spots.desc: Natural history museum. Very small museum. Interesting things to see about Ifugao Culture, attire, handicraft, etc. Good to visit. High steps/stairs to reach the entrance to the museum, then another stairs to the lower level.

spots.name: ATM
spots.desc: There are no ATMs in Banaue. The nearest Visa Card ATM is at the PNB Bank ATM in Lagawe, a one-hour Jeepney ride from Banaue. The nearest Master Card ATM is at Metro Bank in Solano, a 2½-hour jeepney ride from Banaue. There is also a PNB Bank Visa Card ATM in Bontoc.

spots.name: Almost ATM
spots.desc: At this restaurant, you can withdraw cash from your credit card, but 10% fee!

spots.name: Sanafe Lodge & Restaurant
spots.desc: Indoor and al fresco dining on a wide veranda with great views. Filipino, Asian & Western dishes. Set meals start at 140.

spots.name: Ilob Village Inn
spots.desc: Native Ifugao house with restaurant, surrounded with rice terraces. You can also request to see a traditional Ifugao show.

spots.name: Kiben
spots.desc: Local eatery. Good local food provided by friendly family. Main dishes usually 50, sometimes 40. Tea and coffee 10.

spots.name: Naneng Heritage Village
spots.desc: The oldest barangay of Tabuk, it served as the town center during the American era. It is one of the few settlements in the Cordilleras with a mostly intact colonial center with two-story houses made of wood mostly dating from the 1920s, with the Chico River and the Cordilleran peaks as a backdrop. Expect to be invited to participate in the traditional rituals and chores of the Kalinga villagers…

spots.name: Nambaran Cemetery
spots.desc: Established in 1986, the cemetery is a stopover for motorists coming from Tuguegarao who are attracted by the various and sometimes wacky sculptures and artworks on top of the graves to commemorate those interred, ranging from everyday tools to signify the deceased's occupation to beloved pets and even liquor bottles to commemorate their favorite vices.
spots.addr: Sitio Ileb, Barangay Nambaran, Mountain Province-Tabuk-Enrile-Cagayan Road

spots.name: Saint William's Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic Church in Kalinga, built in an austere modernist style with a triangular facade.

spots.name: Patiking Tunnel
spots.desc: An arch blasted through solid rock along a curve of the highway overlooking the gorges of the Chico River.

spots.name: Chico River Dam
spots.desc: A scaled-down version of the otherwise ruinous Chico Dam project of the Marcos regime that provides irrigation for the region. While access to the dam itself is restricted, a viewdeck along the highway provides panoramas of the structure and the surrounding river valley.

spots.name: Dalimuno Half-tunnel
spots.desc: A section of highway blasted the side of a limestone hill, with views of the Chico River on one side and a rock ceiling directly above in a semi-arch.

spots.name: Gessang Tunnel
spots.desc: A section of highway blasted through the side of a limestone mountainside to create a hollowed-out arch.

spots.name: Mount Talama
spots.desc: A hill with a viewdeck at its summit offering commanding views over Tabuk's downtowns. The best views are said to be during sunsets.

spots.name: Daguitan Kan Tangkib Eco-Village Agri Farm
spots.desc: An agritourism resort with coffee plantation and swimming pool.

spots.name: Xentro Mall Tabuk
spots.desc: A mall built as part of the redevelopment of the Bulanao Public Market.

spots.name: Alberto's Pizzeria and Ristorante
spots.desc: Fusion western and indigenous Kalinga cuisine. The restaurant also makes their own pizza dough by hand.

spots.name: Cornelius Farmville
spots.desc: A fruit farm on a steep mountain slope. They also sell home-made smoked meats (kiniing, kussassut and etag).

spots.name: Skyridge Grill and Chill
spots.desc: A restaurant on the Mount Talama massif serving casual meals.

spots.name: National Museum - Marinduque-Romblon Area Museum
spots.desc: Perfect place to learn the warm and thriving culture of Marinduque. It is a must visit.

spots.name: Dampalit Megadike Bike Trail
spots.desc: Dampalit Megadike Bike trail is a Park, Beautiful Place to shoot sunset 5PM to 6PM.

spots.name: Belly's Restaurant
spots.desc: Sea foods/Sisig/Kare-Kare/Pancit, etc. the venue has a very romantic ambiance, very relaxing and food menus' were afforable yet so yummy and tasty.

spots.name: San Felipe Neri Parish Church
spots.desc: Built in 1863, it is dedicated to the city's patron saint, Philip Neri. It also served as a strategic location for the revolutionaries during the Philippine Revolution, where the Katipunan group established an outpost to relay information to other revolutionaries.

spots.name: Archdiocesan Shrine of the Divine Mercy
spots.desc: It is a small church but quite beautiful. It is cozy and comfortable as the place is air conditioned. Because of its size, the atmosphere is solemn and peaceful. Seats are limited and so it is best to come much earlier than the time of your preferred Mass schedule. Parking may be a problem especially during mid-morning Masses on Sundays.

spots.name: Policarpio Street
spots.desc: Once a quiet residential street, it becomes a seasonal tourist attraction for its Christmas displays, a tradition which started in 1980.

spots.name: Shangri-la Plaza
spots.desc: The Shangri-La Mall is located right across from the EDSA Shangri-la hotel, making it convenient for any traveller staying there. Aside from all the amenities (restaurants, grocery, electronics, etc.) a shopping mall has, it also features a connecting bridge to Line 3 for those that want to take mass transit. The mall's cinema occasionally features foreign film festivals.
spots.addr: EDSA corner Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong City

spots.name: Galileo Enoteca
spots.desc: A charming Italian Enoteca or wine bar/deli that is tucked away in the heart of Mandaluyong. A rane of Italian pastas, sausaes, and cheese await you if you can find it! (best use a taxi). Roughly 200 per person.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, Reyes Gym Calbayog corner Malinao Streets

spots.name: Bánh Mì Kitchen - Mandala Park
spots.desc: Banh Mi Kitchen is all about traditional and international flavors all in a crunchy Banh Mi. We serve delicious Banh Mi's made from fresh and healthy ingredients. We also serve authentic Vietnamese Coffee, refreshing teas and juices to compliment your Banh Mi Kitchen experience.

spots.name: Wendy's
spots.desc: We are committed to giving you fresh, delicious meals every step of the way. Sounds simple right? Quality is our recipe. That’s our secret to make sure that anytime is the best time for Wendy’s.
spots.addr: S & R Shopping Mall, 514 Shaw Blvd, Pleasant Hills

spots.name: Shawtime Bar And Restaurant
spots.desc: Good food at reasonable prices, and some good music. All the comedy is in Tagalog, though the comedians will throw in some English if there are foreigners in the crowd. Part of a chain with at least three other locations, all in suburban areas of Metro Manila.

spots.name: Postigo del Palacio
spots.desc: Built in 1662, renovated 1782-83. On 30 Dec 1896, national hero José Rizal was taken through this gate en route to the place of his execution, in what is known today as Rizal Park (see related entry on the district sub-page for Ermita).

spots.name: Baluarte de San Diego
