spots.desc: Dating from the 17th century, this formidable bastion surrounds the remains of the round fort of Nuestra Señora de Guia, the first stone fort built in Manila. Severely damaged during the Second World War, the Baluarte de San Diego was restored in the 1980s and is now a major tourist attraction.

spots.name: Puerta de Isabel II
spots.desc: Built in 1861, this was the last gate to be opened in Intramuros' walls under Spanish rule. A fine statue of Queen Isabel II of Spain stands in front of the gate.

spots.name: Light and Sound Museum
spots.desc: Using images, sounds, and animatronics, the museum takes visitors on a journey through Philippine history under Spanish rule. The facility is housed in a building whose facade reproduces the appearance of the old mother house of the Beaterio de la Compañía de Jesús, which stood on the site until its destruction during the Second World War. 100 per person for groups of 10 or more; smaller groups…

spots.name: San Agustín Museum
spots.desc: Adjacent to the San Agustín Church (see Churches, above), this museum's very impressive - if rather poorly labelled - collection includes Spanish colonial-era ecclesiastical vestments, sacred vessels, religious art, manuscripts, and other important cultural artifacts. The building itself is steeped in history, fashioned out of the surviving portions of a monastery that was heavily damaged during…
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Real

spots.name: San Ignacio Church
spots.desc: Built by the Jesuits and consecrated in 1889, the church's magnificent interiors were completely destroyed in 1945. There are plans to restore the ruined building for use as an ecclesiastical museum.

spots.name: ECJ Building
spots.desc: The external appearance of this post-war building closely mimics that of the Augustinian Provincial House, an extension of the nearby San Agustín convent that was built on the site in the 19th century and destroyed by fire in 1932.

spots.name: Club Intramuros Golf Course
spots.desc: A few years after the Americans took over from the Spanish in 1898, the fetid, swamp-like moat around Intramuros was drained and filled in. The newly reclaimed land was later covered with grass, spiced with a few sand pits and sprinkled with water traps. Result: a 4,326 yd, 18 hole, par 66 greensward that wraps around the city's ancient walls and makes for an interesting (if rather short) golfing…
spots.addr: Bonifacio Drive cor. Aduana Street, Port Area

spots.name: The Silahis Center
spots.desc: Handmade Filipino goods and folk art. Other departments within the same showroom feature fine art, antiques, and books.

spots.name: Bistro Marinero
spots.desc: The menu features a mix of Western and local dishes. Special "payday" buffets, combo meals, etc.
spots.addr: General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio) cor. Santa Potenciana

spots.name: Ristorante delle Mitre
spots.desc: Features simple, hearty Filipino meals inspired by the favourite dishes of the country's bishops and clergy. The culinary team is supervised by a nun who formerly served as a cook to a prominent local cardinal, and the walls are decorated with portraits and mementos of senior clerics, perfectly in keeping with the sacred atmosphere of the San Agustín area.
spots.addr: CBCP Building, 470 General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio)

spots.name: 9 Spoons
spots.desc: Contemporary interiors, access to a roof deck and splendid views. The restaurant serves both international dishes and local specialities. Buffet breakfast daily, buffet lunch on weekdays.
spots.addr: 9th Floor, The Bayleaf Intramuros, Muralla cor. Victoria

spots.name: Barbara's
spots.desc: Housed in a Spanish colonial-style building a stone's throw from San Agustín Church, this centrally located restaurant serves traditional Filipino and Hispanic fare in an old-style setting.
spots.addr: Plaza San Luis, General Luna (Calle Real del Palacio)

spots.name: Ilustrado
spots.desc: Mainly Filipino-Spanish cuisine: rellenong bangus (stuffed milkfish), paella, and other traditional dishes. Fine dining in the heart of the walled city.

spots.name: Cioccolata – Churros Café
spots.desc: Nothing like some good old-fashioned churros con chocolate to relive colonial days. Also offers a selection of more contemporary beverages, sandwiches and desserts.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, The Bayleaf Intramuros, Muralla cor. Victoria

spots.name: Starbucks
spots.desc: No matter where you go, you can't escape Starbucks. Sits not far from the historic Puerta de Isabel II, the last gate built in Intramuros.
spots.addr: 15-A Puerta Isabel II, Muralla cor. Magallanes

spots.name: Insular Life Corporate Center
spots.desc: Office complex with glass-covered twin towers. Has a viewing area on the 34th floor.

spots.name: Bayanan Baywalk
spots.desc: Part of city lakeside development with an elementary school, park and boulevard. Provides a view of Laguna de Bay, but is blocked by kangkong (water spinach) plantations.

spots.name: Ayala Malls South Park
spots.desc: Redeveloped from former Nestle warehouses, it is part of the South Park District development, which includes condominium towers and a call center building. Opened in December 2016, it has fast-food restaurants, a food court, and various shops. Has a Robinsons supermarket and department store.

spots.name: Festival Alabang
spots.desc: Mall constructed as part of the Filinvest City redevelopment. Festival Alabang houses department stores, two supermarkets, two indoor amusement parks, and a variety of restaurants and shops. An expansion area includes a Landmark department store, various restaurants and cafes, and a park along the Alabang River, which bisects the new buildings.

spots.name: New Muntinlupa Public Market
spots.desc: Alabang's farmers' and flea market, with tiangges selling dry goods such as clothes and houseware.

spots.name: Alabang Town Center
spots.desc: Built over where the Boom na Boom amusement park once stood, it is the core of the Ayala Alabang development, with more high-end retailers and restaurants. This mall a Spanish-inspired central park, mostly lined with fine dining restaurants and some shops. Its major anchor stores are a Rustan's and a Metro Gaisano department store.

spots.name: SM Center Muntinlupa
spots.desc: Small community mall with fast-food restaurants, cinemas, and a few shops. Has a SM Hypermarket and Ace Hardware. Parking is free, and expect the parking lots to be full, especially on weekend sales.

spots.name: Molito Lifestyle Center
spots.desc: Molito is a luxury lifestyle center that features 5-star restaurants. They have a park-like center area with a small fountain for customers to sit and walk around.

spots.name: Ho Chai Lai
spots.desc: Authentic Chinese cuisine, including dim sum, noodles, and congee.

spots.name: PRLAN Cafe
spots.desc: Despite its name, it features various Filipino recipes, with an offer for a meal two dishes and one rice. Also has a general store, and three kiosks. Meal starting at 60.

spots.name: Taiyaki
spots.desc: Japanese fish-shaped cakes, with a choice of mung bean or custard filling

spots.name: Wing Bites
spots.desc: Offers unlimited chicken wings. There are no spoons or forks available, so you can enjoy either eating by hand using plastic gloves or with your bare hands.
spots.addr: Edna Duran Building, 163-A National Road, Tunasan

spots.name: Sansó Museum
spots.desc: A small, private museum focusing on the artistic legacy of Juvenal Sansó.

spots.name: San Juan City Agora Market
spots.desc: The largest public market in the city, with a mixed-use commercial/retail area on the ground level, and the market below. At the street level, there is a supermarket, fast food restaurants and a drug store.

spots.name: Santolan Town Plaza
spots.desc: Santolan Town Plaza, is a small, upscale mall in San Juan with a supermarket, cinemas, office spaces, and several dining and service establishments.

spots.name: Little Baguio
spots.desc: A gastronomic enclave of restaurants and homey, food establishments tucked around the intersecting streets of Wilson, P. Guevarra, J. Abad Santos and V. Cruz in San Juan, and named after the territorial barangay of Little Baguio. The establishments in this area serve a variety of cuisines, and ambiance may range from formal, sit-down restaurants, to hole-in-the-wall food specialists, to casual…

spots.name: Recess Food Alley
spots.desc: A neighborhood "food court" with concessionaires offering local and foreign comfort food, especially for the budget conscious. Originally, the main market were students from nearby schools, but since 2020, has evolved as a venue for affordable "food trips.".

spots.name: Oriental Mindoro Heritage Museum
spots.desc: One of the best locally managed museums in the country. The name of the place is fitting as it will truly give you a glimpse of the proud heritage and culture of Oriental Mindoro. There is no boring corner.

spots.name: Cathedral of Santa Isabel de Portugal
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Basilan and Prelature of Isabela, built in 1960s modern-art style with a distinctively Classical Roman mosaic for an altar wall.

spots.name: Kaumpurnah Mosque
spots.desc: Historic seat of Islamic faith and teaching in Basilan, can be seen as you enter the Isabela Channel.

spots.name: Panam Pangan Island
spots.desc: Panampangan Island is an island in the municipality of Sapa-Sapa, Tawi-Tawi.

spots.name: Fat Lips Surfshop
spots.desc: Offers new/used/rental surfboards, apparel, and surf accessories. They also arrange island hopping and other tours.

spots.name: Philtranco
spots.desc: Buses run the Manila-Davao City route via AH26. The bus from Manila leaves from Pasay at 3PM and arrives at 4:30PM, one day after, while the return service leaves Davao City at noon and arrives at about 8:45PM.

spots.name: Mapawa Cave
spots.desc: Unique rock formations approximately 20 feet high stand out against a backdrop of dense coconut trees and nipa palms (Nypa fruticans) and covers an area of . Also a known burial ground. Not too distant is another rock formation called tamulayag that resembles a giant vase with trees perched on top.

spots.name: Manjagao Mangrove Forest
spots.desc: A vast mangrove forest around Manjagao Island is a sanctuary to various species of fish, marine life, birds and bats.

spots.name: Buenavista Cave
spots.desc: A three kilometer cave with three entrances located in Hikdop Island. From the main entrance in Pagkawasan, Buenavista, visitors wiggle through a collapsed boulder into a grand chamber complete with what locals call the Kings Throne. A knee-deep pool culminates the subterranean trek approximately 100 meters from the main entrance. It has an array of impressive stalactites and stalagmites and is…

spots.name: Surigaonon Heritage Center
spots.desc: A small collection of ancient burial coffin jars and antique Chinese kitchenware are showcased in this museum. Some of the artifacts were unearthed at an archeological dig in Panhatungan, Placer. It also contains a significant collection of various rocks and minerals found in the province.

spots.name: Bitaugan Whirlpools
spots.desc: These maelstroms of various dimensions are almost all occurring during ebbtide. They have a characteristic behavior to pull, twirl, and suck into their vortices anything that comes near them. They are called magic whirlpools due to their peculiar behavior to appear and disappear at certain nature-designated time intervals. The appearance of Pahibongan, as they are called locally, are usually…

spots.name: San Pedro Cantiasay Footbridge
spots.desc: This wooden footbridge is among the country's longest at 391 meters, connecting Sibale and Nonoc Islands.

spots.name: Luneta Park
spots.desc: Host to annual events, gatherings, and concerts for over a hundred years, it is a Spanish-style park with few acacia trees fronting the Surigao Cathedral. The new Children's Park Playground is under rehabilitation in May 2018 and publicly opened in June.

spots.name: Mindanao SAGA Flying Club
spots.desc: The Mindanao SAGA Flying Club (MSFC), at the Mati National Airport in Barangay Dahican, is an ultralight aircraft flying facility that offers trial flights and flying lessons. The Quicksilver aircraft has an open cockpit, giving the passenger an unrestricted view of the landscape.

spots.name: Secluded Beach Resort
spots.desc: This resort offers access via steps to Pujada Bay for kayaking, swimming, and freediving. A small cafe offers simple drinks and meals. Tent camping and lodging also available

spots.name: Amihan Beach Park
spots.desc: Dahican public beach access. ₱50 for parking may be charged.

spots.name: Macaraeg-Macapagal Ancestral House
spots.desc: The only house in Mindanao where two Philippine Presidents resided: the father-daughter Presidents Diosdado Macapagal and Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. In 1994, upon the instigation of Diosdado, the lot where the house stands and a two-hectare cocoland nearby were donated to the City Government of Iligan for the purpose of developing the place into a tourist destination with a memorabilia of the…

spots.name: Mr Beefy Burger
spots.desc: Hawaiian cheese 36. Ham egg 40. Bacon egg 40. Cheese burger with egg 40.

spots.name: Archdiocesan Marian Shrine of the Birhen sa Cotta
spots.desc: Locally known as the Cotta Shrine. A shrine dedicated to Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception and of the Triumph of the Cross of Panguil Bay, locally known as the Birhen sa Cotta. The shrine is located at the south wall of the Fuerte de la Concepcion y del Triunfo and is a known pilgrimage destination in the city.

spots.name: Fuerte de la Concepcion y del Triunfo
spots.desc: Called "Fort of the Conception and of the Triumph" in English. Established in 1756, this fort is the oldest structure in the city. Inside in the fort is a garden, with a museum displaying artifacts from the fort and the city. On the southeast bastion is a lighthouse.

spots.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: Built from the remains of the original parish church after the earthquake of 1955. This cathedral was designed by National Artist for Architecture, Leandro Locsin. His simple style of squares, circles, and half circles are evident throughout the external and internal designs of the church. Alterations to the façade of the cathedral were performed later. The cathedral is home to the wooden image…

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Pipe Organ
spots.desc: The only existing pipe organ in Mindanao, and one of only a few anywhere in the Philippines. It was Father Sean Lavery, an Irish-Columbian priest in charge of music at the cathedral, who first thought of the idea of an organ at Immaculate Conception. Funds were raised through donations and a musical extravaganza, organized by the parish, to buy the pipe organ. Father Lavery requested the aid of a…
spots.addr: inside the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception

spots.name: Bukagan Hill
spots.desc: At the top of the hill is a bell tower that houses four great bells, named "St. Peter", "St. Marien", "St. Joseph", and "St. Michael". They were originally purchased by Bishop-Prelate Patrick Cronin, D.D. for the Metropolitan Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception. However, the bells weigh 7 tons and were found to be too heavy and too large for the cathedral's belfry. Given the recent costs of…

spots.name: Geege Mall, Robinsons Supermarket
spots.desc: Has a McDonald's and a cinema, among other notable stores inside the mall.

spots.name: Kasanaya Cave
spots.desc: Has large stalactites, 400 m down the cave's mouth. It also has an underground river in it.

spots.name: Kansal Falls
spots.desc: This waterfall is one of the cleanest in Asia. Its water, coming from Mount Apo, is also the source of the city's water supply

spots.name: Mount Apo
spots.desc: Kidapawan serves as the main jumping point for hikes to this mountain. There are two trails: one which ends at nearby Magpet and another ends at Santa Cruz, across through Davao del Sur.

spots.name: Timpupo Festival
spots.desc: Named after the Cebuano word for "harvest", it celebrates the annual harvest of exotic fruits grown in the city.

spots.name: Gaisano Grand Mall & Gaisano Supermarket
spots.desc: A wide selection of retail outlets with many fast food places.

spots.name: KCC Mall of Marbel
spots.desc: Has a supermarket in the first floor and a department store from the 2nd to 4th floors.

spots.name: ONAY Museum
spots.desc: A museum that pays homage to Zamboanga del Norte's own General Alexander Badong Yano, the first Mindanaoan and the 38th Chief-of-Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.
spots.price: Free upon request from City Tourism Office

spots.name: Sungkilaw Falls
spots.desc: A serene, multi-tiered waterfall nestled in lush forest, known for its cool, clear waters and peaceful, uncrowded atmosphere. Standing at 25-feet tall, it’s a hidden natural retreat near Dipolog, ideal for quiet relaxation and nature trips.

spots.name: Cogon Eco-Tourism Park
spots.desc: A nature-focused recreational area featuring wide open cogon grasslands, scenic viewpoints, and simple outdoor activities like hiking and picnicking. It offers a peaceful escape where visitors can enjoy fresh air and panoramic views of the surrounding countryside, and immerse in the traditional Subanen way of life.

spots.name: 3,003 Steps to Linabo Peak
spots.desc: A steep nature trail leading to a scenic summit, featuring 3,003 steps lined with Stations of the Cross that symbolize Christ’s journey. It is especially popular during Holy Week, when devotees climb the path for reflection, prayer, and panoramic views at the peak. Arrange for a tricycle or a motor sikad (single-ride motorcycle) to take you there.

spots.name: Alvenda Hilander Farm
spots.desc: Hilander Farm is a new tourist destination in Dipolog City. It takes 2-3 hours by multicab to reach the place, its kinda rough road when you reach Center place in Mutia, going to the said place. The place have nice native and antique style of the house, swimming pool for kids and for adults with nice and cool overflowing water. They also have a zipline.

spots.name: Lee Plaza City Central
spots.desc: Three-story shopping mall with a Jollibee, Chowking, Mang Inasal, and Watsons as main tenants. With ample parking space at the basement.

spots.name: Dipolog Center Mall
spots.desc: Three-story shopping mall with supermarket, department store, and food court.
spots.addr: Rizal Avenue corner Padre Burgos Street, Miputak

spots.name: CityMall Dipolog
spots.desc: Has SM SaveMore Supermarket, Ace Hardware, Watsons, and many fast food and retail outlets.

spots.name: Hiraya Pasalubong Shop
spots.desc: They sell bottled food products, snacks, and handcrafted souvenirs from Zamboanga del Norte producers and manufacturers.

spots.name: D'Food Hub and Events Center
spots.desc: A hawker center-style food court where you can enjoy balut or boiled fertilized egg, street food, and the sunset view from the Sulu Sea.

spots.name: Jo's Chicken Inato
spots.desc: Try their BBQ with unlimited rice, Chicken Tinola in Coconut Shell, and Halo-halo in Coconut Shell.
spots.addr: Bonifacio Street corner C.P. Garcia Street, Central

spots.name: Cafe Nicasio
spots.desc: Named after one of Dipolog's pioneers, they serve coffee, all-day breakfast, and more.
spots.addr: General Luna corner M. H. del Pilar Streets, Estaka

spots.name: Alberto's Pizza Dipolog
spots.desc: Offers a good and rather affordable locally made thin crust pizza.

spots.name: Grandma's Best Restaurant and Bakeshop
spots.desc: Serves Filipino dishes, scrumptious comfort foods, and various cakes and pastries. Also serves breakfast meals all-day. Catering needs? Grandma's Best accepts catering services at very affordable prices with spacious amenities.

spots.name: Biaño's Pizza
spots.desc: Serving pizza, spaghetti, potato fries, chicken, rice toppings, milkshakes, desserts, and beer.
spots.addr: General Luna corner Martinez Streets, Central

spots.name: Morgia's BBQ House Main Branch
spots.desc: One of the oldest restaurants in Dipolog (opened in 1980), it serves grilled barbeque and other popular Filipino meals, in addition to coffee and cakes for special occasions.

spots.name: Seven Treasures
spots.desc: Serving Filipino, Chinese, Japanese, Indian, Thai, European, and Western dishes.
spots.addr: GF Top Plaza Hotel, Echavez Street, Central

spots.name: 1988 Bistro and Bar
spots.desc: Serving Filipino, Chinese, Japanese, Indian, Thai, European, and Western dishes.

spots.name: Barra Barista Coffee Co.
spots.desc: Brewed coffee, frappes, fries, waffles, sandwiches, salads, and more. Perfect place to enjoy yourself or with good friends with air-conditioned shop and Wi-Fi connection.

spots.name: Pagadian Rotonda
spots.desc: It is a park within a large roundabout between two of the city's major streets. Every night, the park has dancing fountains which are accompanied by music, and during the Christmas season, it hosts illuminated Christmas displays, with themes that change annually.

spots.name: El Dive
spots.desc: This small dive center will offer you relaxing and long dives (departure at 8AM, come back at 4:30PM) among the colourful aquatic life of Bacuit Bay. The Japanese Yoshi Ohtsuka is the manager, he is the one who will welcome you there. He has about 20 years of experience in the diving industry, so he knows what he is talking about. The staff can speak at least English, French, Tagalog and…

spots.name: Deep Blue Dive Seafari
spots.desc: Jose and Diana from Deep Blue Seafari are the founders of the El Nido to Coron dive seafari. This 4-day trip includes 14 dives, camping on the exotic beaches and bonfire nights. Besides the seafaris, Deep Blue also offers fun dives and PADI courses.

spots.name: El Nido Adventure Scuba
spots.desc: SSI and PADI open water and advanced dive courses are offered.

spots.name: Island Hopping
spots.desc: There are many island hopping tour companies throughout El Nido. They all offer similar tours and prices; therefore it is not necessary to shop around for the best tour company or price. You may want to check a few different companies to see how empty or full their boats are. All tours leave between 8 and 9AM.

spots.name: Island Hopping & Kayak Tours
spots.desc: The El Nido Boutique & Artcafe is a kayak tour operator and rents out kayaks, stand up paddle boards, snorkel equipment and bicycles.

spots.name: Palawan Divers
spots.desc: Palawan Divers was the first certified PADI dive resort in town. Professional and friendly staff serving beginners to experienced divers.

spots.name: Submariner Diving Center
spots.desc: Submariner Diving Center is a diving center operated by the German PADI master scuba diver trainer, Ronny Oliwka. Submariner is a certified PADI Dive Resort and certified Aqualung Partner Center that offers a high standard in diving and education as well as diving gear branded by Aqualung and APEKS. The staff is highly qualified to international standards. Habibi Restaurant & Shisha Cafe is on…

spots.name: El Nido Boutique & Artcafe
spots.desc: El Nido T-shirts printed in their own artshop, souvenirs, handicrafts, postcards, books, photo supplies and cameras, snorkel gear, swimming clothes and beach wear, sarongs, dresses, jewelry, suntan lotions and drugstore items, wine and liquors, bags and backpacks, hammocks.

spots.name: Botanica Cafe
spots.desc: A third wave coffee shop popular for its coffee and its breakfasts. It has an in-house bakery making cakes, pastries, cookies, and bread.

spots.name: Art Cafe
spots.desc: A beautiful, well-established restaurant with very good food such as seafood, salads, steaks, pizzas, spaghetti, homemade bread, cakes and fruit shakes and very good coffee. They have live music several nights a week. Free Wi-Fi all day.

spots.name: Habibi Restaurant & Shisha Cafe
spots.desc: Good food and beverages, and they are the only shisha bar in Palawan. Drinks are made with fresh ingredients, pizzas are also popular. The full bar offers all varieties of premium drinks. The owner frequently visits the local market to find the best/freshest fish available. Free Wi-Fi, widescreen projection television, and games. The vibe is warm and friendly. The restaurant is ideal for groups…

spots.name: The Alternative
spots.desc: Offers tasty & health-conscious food at good prices. Also has a pair of scenic beach-perched "nests" available for dining.

spots.name: El Nido Corner
spots.desc: Great beachfront restaurant with a Danish owner. Try the fresh catch of the day.
spots.addr: North end of the beach in El Nido

spots.name: Mount Manghilaw
spots.desc: outside town is popular as a trekking destination; there is a large cross near the top.

spots.name: Gaisano Capital Mall Danao
spots.desc: Department store & supermarket. there is also a Gaisano shoppers outlet mall Oliver street.

spots.name: Lapu-Lapu Monument
spots.desc: Lapu-Lapu was a local hero whose forces killed Ferdinand Magellan during the Battle of Mactan in 1521. A small marker to Magellan is nearby.

spots.name: The Jungle Restaurant and Entertainment
spots.desc: Filipino and international food with a cultural show involving dances from the Philippines and other countries. The best involves the Fire Dancers.
spots.hours: Noon-midnight, open 7 days a week with lunch show at 12:30, and dinner shows at 6:30, 8, 10PM

spots.name: Upside Down World Cebu
spots.desc: A variety of upside-down optical illusions located within the Park Mall.
spots.addr: 2nd Floor Unit A 204-205-206 City Time Square Phase 2 Mantawi Int'l Drive, Tipolo, Mandaue City, 6014 Cebu, Philippines

spots.name: Lake Danao
spots.desc: In the mountainous part of northern Ormoc. Ideal for family get-aways, fishing, picnics and sight seeing. The place has a natural ambience with floating cottages and boat rentals for those interested in boating and getting around the lake.

spots.name: Pardi's Grill
spots.desc: A restaurant that serves Filipino and grilled foods. Ideal for family dining.

spots.name: Ormoc Barbecue Park
spots.desc: At the bay area, the place is festive at night and offers pork, chicken and hotdog barbecue at affordable prices. They serve soft drinks and beer as beverage.

spots.name: Ikea
spots.desc: Refreshment parlor that serves snacks and is famous for their cake products and halo-halo.

spots.name: Mayong's Snack Haus
spots.desc: An affordable snack bar at the shopping district in Ormoc City. Beside the establishment is Quality Bakeshop that sells bread and cakes

spots.name: Sals Bar and Restaurant
spots.desc: Filipino restaurant, à la carte style but has a "sutukil" method in which the customer points to an array of raw seafoods, meat and vegetables and suggest the cook to have his meat either "sinugba" style (grilled), "tuwa" boiled or "kilaw" to eat raw by marinating in vinegar and coconut milk.

spots.name: Gil's Grill
spots.desc: Grilled fare and seafood. They are known for their Su-tu-kil or sugba, tuwa and kinilaw.

spots.name: Bistado Karaoke Bar
spots.desc: Karaoke bar in private rooms ideal for family and barkada gatherings at an hourly rate. They serve beer and wine at the bar. They also have a comedy bar every Thursday night.

spots.name: Buenos Aires Mountain Resort
spots.desc: Used once as a hideout during the World War II. An Ideal site for a family vacation, it has a hostel, cottages and swimming pools.
spots.addr: Barangay Ilijan, 28 km east of Bago City

spots.name: Kipot Twin Falls
spots.desc: Stunning waterfalls located in the hills, its waterfalls inspire poets and musicians alike and its view attracts local tourists as well as foreign tourists, Swim its waters and take a massage under the waterfalls.
spots.price: Entrance fees cost low as 10 and cottages cost 100

spots.name: The Quiet Place Farm Resort
spots.desc: After a tired and hectic day, go have a spa and massage in the Quiet Place Farm Resort, not only it offers spas but also accommodations.

spots.name: Manuel Severino Hofilena Ancestral House
spots.desc: The ancestral house is home to the world's smallest doll. It also displays ancient artifacts from the 15th century and a collection of Ramon Hofilena.

spots.name: Balay Negrense
spots.desc: Home of the French descent family; the Gaston family, who helped in experimenting Sugar cane production in the province. After the death of their father; Victor Gaston, the family abandoned the house and fell into ruins but during the 1970s concerned people showed their support and repaired the house. The architecture is a typical example of "Bahay na bato" or House of stone, with…

spots.name: Silay Public Plaza
spots.desc: The center of the city. If you are a family, this place is the best place to walk and enjoy with ease.

spots.name: Mt. Patag
spots.desc: A hiking/mountain climbing adventure you can experience with some resorts you can stay.

spots.name: The Mansion
spots.desc: A well-preserved heritage house wherein antique materials can be found.

spots.name: El Ideal Bakeshop
spots.desc: Inside an old Silay building, serves Filipino/international cuisine (try the lumpiang ubod) as well as offering baked goods like piaya, meringue and barquillos. You can also find the famous Guapple Pie, made of guavas, the local version of apple pie.

spots.name: Mang Inasal
spots.desc: Also serves its grilled chicken here, and customers who dine on the second floor get an excellent view of some of Silay's heritage architecture.

spots.name: Silayushi Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: The only Japanese restaurant in Silay City, serving sushi and other Japanese cuisine.

spots.name: Bell Tower
spots.desc: This is the oldest surviving structure in the city, a relic of the long Spanish occupation of Negros Island. It used to be a watchtower to warn the locals against marauding pirates from Mindanao. The first two storeys date from the mid-1700s with the structure above that added later. Its largest bell is engraved with a date of 1818.

spots.name: Silliman University Hall
spots.desc: Built in 1902-1903, this is the oldest U.S. structure in the Philippines still standing. Its architecture is reminiscent of the Stick Style or Victorian type of architecture that characterized U.S. buildings in the late 19th century. On the east or ocean side of the hall is a bronze bust of Horace Silliman.

spots.name: Luce Auditorium
spots.desc: Considered the cultural center of the South. Named for the American Luce family, media magnates who owned Time, Life and other magazines. The tin ceiling was salvaged from an old theater in New York.

spots.name: Marine Laboratory Museum
spots.desc: Houses the second-largest whale bone collection in the world.

spots.name: Silliman University Church
spots.desc: A Protestant church with some fine stained glass windows. Like the university, it was set up by American Presbyterian missionaries, but its outlook today is very ecumenical; it describes itself as "a church ministering to all Sillimanians, regardless of their denomination and religious affiliations".

spots.name: Silliman University Anthropology Museum
spots.desc: The Anthropology Museum houses some Philippine artifacts that were excavated from many parts of the country dating back hundreds or thousands of years.
spots.price: Base rate 40 for locals, 60 for others, with discounts for children and seniors. Rates double on weekends or holidays

spots.name: Silliman Zoo
spots.desc: It conserves endangered Philippine native animals which are rarely seen; eg, spotted deer, warty pigs and crocodiles. Well worth the 10 entry fee. They also need financial support. It's a 15-min walk from the city center or a 8 pedicab ride.

spots.name: Volcanic Road
spots.desc: Get up close and personal with some sulphur vents along the roadside

spots.name: Cheeki Diver
spots.desc: private Dive Guide for diving Dumaguete, Dauin, Siquijor and Apo-Island​.

spots.name: Bravo Golf Course
spots.desc: Beautifully kept 18-hole course with plenty of shade trees and Zebu cattle has a view of the sea and an air-conditioned club room. Quarterly green fees are 15000 while 'walk-ins' pay 750 for 9 holes, 1250 for 18 holes M-Th rising to 1000 & 1500 at weekends. Caddy fees are 175 or 275, golf cart rental 400 or 650, an umbrella girl 120 or 180 and golf set rental 650 or 650 for 9 or 18 holes…
spots.addr: San Antonio Barangay Rd, Pancil, Looc, Sibulan

spots.name: Cang's Department Store
spots.desc: Moderate prices with UnionPay, Visa, JCB and MasterCards accepted, this is a good option for a weekly grocery shop on the ground floor since the basement car park is both free and underutilised. There is a food court on the top floor and the Filomena Cafe 2 (of Bethel Guest House fame) accepts cards too. Purified and cooled water is available free of charge from a self-service drinking fountain…

spots.name: Lee Plaza & Supermarket
spots.desc: Main department store in the city centre with a large supermarket in the basement; accepts Visa, JCB and MasterCard. Two bakeries, ground floor and basement; the basement one may be the only place in town with bagels. Food court on top floor.

spots.name: Robinson's
spots.desc: Supermarket, bakery (with seating & coffee) and drugstore on ground floor. Appliances and hardware store in basement.

spots.name: Open air market area
spots.desc: Many small stalls, mainly selling cheap clothing and tourist items. Some street food as well.

spots.name: AAC Tech
spots.desc: Computers, Apple products from laptops to i-Pods, other gadgets.

spots.name: Unitop Department Store
spots.desc: Generally cheaper than Lee or Robinson, popular with locals.

spots.name: YanYan Baking and Culinary
spots.desc: Primarily supplies bakers with all imaginable and unimaginable ingredients, but also carries an interesting selection of other hard-to-find groceries.
spots.addr: corner of Mabini St and Santa Rosa St

spots.name: Silliman Farm
spots.desc: A 24-hectare (60-acre) farm run by the university's College of Agriculture. High-quality milk and eggs, sometimes other products including turkeys.

spots.name: Citi Mall
spots.desc: Has a Savemore supermarket. Watsons pharmacy, Ace hardware, and many fast food outlets. Coffee shop.

spots.name: Dumaguete market
spots.desc: Around this market is the best place in town to look for small services: key cutting, shoe or bicycle repair, tailors, manicure.

spots.name: Bakery
spots.desc: A range of espresso variants and baked goods, done well enough that the regulars include a group of European French speakers. One of very few places in town that sell bagels. Cheapest brewed coffee downtown at 36, though some people prefer Scooby's at 50 for larger cups and better chairs.

spots.name: Chow King
spots.desc: A chain offering moderately-priced Chinese (mainly Cantonese) food. Pork or beef fried rice, with four shui mai (small noodle-wrapped pork items) and a soft drink, 99.

spots.name: Filomena Cafe
spots.desc: A very hygienic, air-conditioned cafeteria-style place with a good selection of reasonably priced dishes. Their vegetable fried rice is particularly tasty. All-you-can-eat buffet on Friday evenings for 200. Visa and MasterCard are accepted. They give a 20% discount on most things for seniors with Philippine ID, such as the government ACR card which many longer-term visitors have.

spots.name: Food Net
spots.desc: Food Net are a chain with several locations around town. They have cafeteria-style service, Filipino food, moderate prices and a largely student crowd. A basic meal — meat dish, veggie dish, rice, soft drink — is about 90.

spots.name: Gyro Monsters
spots.desc: Cheap and tasty shawarma; the best seller is beef or chicken shawarma wrapped in pita at 30, or 35 with cheese. The most expensive thing on the menu is shawarma rice for 50; two of the sandwiches are a better buy.If you expect shawarma as you would find it in the Middle East, you will be disappointed here. For that, at slightly higher prices, walk a block north to Mediterranean Food (Turkish…

spots.name: Scooby's
spots.desc: Scooby's is a chain with various locations around town. Their brewed coffee at 50 is both a larger serving and (at least for some tastes) better quality than most coffee offered on Rizal Boulevard at 70-120. They also have all the usual variations on espresso, several types of herbal tea, a range of mostly western-style baked goods, and moderately-priced mostly Filipino hot foods. There is a…

spots.name: Wah Crepe
spots.desc: A small stand selling coffee, crepes, waffles & fruit shakes. All are freshly made and good quality; plum crepes and avocado shakes are remarkable. Best buy is a combo, shake plus waffle. It is only one of a group of food stands, so ordering a shake here and getting food elsewhere is possible.The place is popular with the town's resident foreigners; it gets more younger ones and fewer drunks than…

spots.name: Tom 'n Tom's Coffee
spots.desc: Part of a chain, large with nice decor. Has good air conditioning, free Wifi, and a good selection of both baked goods and variations on the theme of espresso. Prices might be considered good by tourists but are high by local standards.

spots.name: Just Do Eat
spots.desc: Large, with much seafood on the menu. Popular with Asian tourists. The city's resident foreigners more often go to Lantaw, listed at #North of the center.

spots.name: Bo's Coffee
spots.desc: A national chain with several locations in Dumaguete, serving mainly coffee & baked goods. Prices are high by local standards.

spots.name: La Residencia Almar
spots.desc: (listed under #Sleep) has three upmarket restaurants. All are somewhat expensive, and all have some customers who consider them worth it. There is also a moderately priced burger bar.

spots.name: Don Atilano
spots.desc: Spanish decor & menu, steaks a specialty. All-you-can eat lunch buffet Friday & Saturday, 339.

spots.name: Das Bürgery
spots.desc: Small, clean & modern. Menu is limited — only burgers, fries and soft drinks — but quality is good & prices are quite reasonable for what you get. No beer and not much seating, so do not plan an evening here; just grab a burger then go elsewhere for the beer.

spots.name: Hamburg joints
spots.desc: Two small cheap places with mostly Filipino customers, one with BBQ chicken as well as burgers. The burgers are not nearly as good as in the tourist restaurants on the Boulevard, and they are smaller as well, but then they are about a quarter the price. The waitress who brings you the expensive burger elsewhere quite likely eats here on her breaks.

spots.name: GameOn Sportsbar
spots.desc: Small and plain compared to other places, with no a/c but many fans, big-screen TVs for sports, sometimes live music.

spots.name: Sans Rival
spots.desc: One of the oldest cake shops in the city. They occupy a pair of buildings on a corner with the cake shop in the smaller one on the side street and "Sans Rival Bistro" on Rizal.

spots.name: Sans Rival cake shop
spots.desc: Offers baked goods (surprise!), drinks, and some pasta and salad dishes.

spots.name: Sans Rival Bistro
spots.desc: The bistro offers a broader range including a half dozen breakfast options at 200-odd. All-you-can-eat breakfast buffet on Sunday 7:30-10AM for 285.

spots.name: Chin Loong
spots.desc: Good Chinese (Cantonese) food, with reasonable service and prices. Large covered patio.

spots.name: Casablanca
spots.desc: European food, elegant décor, and a good wine list. Their patio is above street level and has a wall, so customers here are not bothered by beggars or street vendors as often as at other establishments.There are several breakfast options starting at 230, all including unlimited coffee and a glass of juice. The American breakfast at 295 is bacon, two eggs, bread, and some fried tomatoes and…

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: Chain convenience store with a few tables; the best-selling item is a large soft ice cream cone for 15. It also sells soft drinks, snacks and cigarettes; for those it is more expensive than supermarkets but cheaper than the bars. The chain is expanding; there are several other locations around town and more coming.

spots.name: Paseo Perdices
spots.desc: A building with two floors, built on the location of the Perdices family home; one family member was the provincial governor and has one of the town's main streets named for him. There are two levels, and the lower level has a large shaded central courtyard.

spots.name: Yellow Cab Pizza
spots.desc: Part of a chain. Delivery available; they use yellow scooters.

spots.name: Max's Restaurant
spots.desc: Part of a chain. Their specialty is fried chicken. Breakfast from 7:30AM.

spots.name: Gabby's Bistro
spots.desc: Second location; the first one is an in-house restaurant at Hotel Florentina.

spots.name: Why Not?
spots.desc: One-stop shopping? Restaurant, deli, disco, karaoke, cyber cafe, billiard room, and travel agent under one roof. Beer here is sometimes among the cheapest in town, at 42 in the restaurants in the afternoon, but higher at other times and 90 at the disco.

spots.name: Le Chalet
spots.desc: Salads, pasta, other types of European and American food, with decent quality and prices. Inside with a/c or patio. The current chef is from Milan but the menu emphasizes German and Swiss specialities. There are also a few Thai dishes, competently done, for those who prefer something spicier. All-you-can eat breakfast buffet on Sundays, 331.

spots.name: Chiccos Deli
spots.desc: Selling meats, wines, cheese & chocolate, with many imported European items. Has a bakery with good croissants and pretzels. There are few tables inside and a small patio in front. Both offer the same menu as Le Chalet, but many customers just come for coffee or beer.

spots.name: Why Not? disco
spots.desc: A lively and very loud disco, popular with both travellers and locals, and well known as a pick-up bar. A mix of people come for the dancing, for flirting, or to find a partner for the night or longer. Prostitution is present but not the primary character of the place. The occasional drunken brawl is not unheard of. Attitudes among resident foreigners range from enthusiastic regulars to those who…

spots.name: Honeycomb Tourist Inn
spots.desc: (listed under #Sleep) has a restaurant with a large patio area out front, with live music most evenings. Around the side is a small Japanese restaurant, and inside the building a disco and a sports bar.

spots.name: Allegre
spots.desc: A large restaurant offering mainly Italian and Filipino dishes. Highest prices in town for pasta.Pool table downstairs, table is in better shape than at the one at Why Not? and there are usually fewer players competing for it.

spots.name: Starbucks
spots.desc: Another place for coffee and baked goods at prices that are high by local standards.

spots.name: Gerry's Bar and Grill
spots.desc: A fine old house renovated in 2018 to become a large restaurant. Part of a large chain with reasonable quality but some unreasonable prices.

spots.desc: Part of a chain that advertises "Mexican-inspired" food. They offer that, various pizza and pasta dishes, and other western dishes; most of it is done competently. Good soups 59, burrito 139 (quite good, provided you tell them not to put lettuce in it!), pizza from 165, small but good steak 300. The best-buy drink is bottomless iced tea at 58. Other dishes, such as the "nachos" (overpriced chips…

spots.name: Captain Ribber's
spots.desc: The specialty is ribs, but they have a range of other dishes.

spots.name: Jo's Chicken Inato

spots.name: Poppy Coffee and Cupcakes

spots.name: Harbour City Dim Sum
spots.desc: Many types of dim sum, plus various soups and rice or noodle dishes.

spots.name: Cafe Antonio
spots.desc: Fantastic wide-ranging menu, very reasonable prices, lovely chilled out studenty vibe and a great building to host it. Quite honestly a breath of fresh air in the Philippines. Wonderful coffee too!

spots.name: Mediterranean Food
spots.desc: Good Turkish kebabs and donair. They have distinctly unexciting hamburgs for 30.

spots.name: Mifune
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant. All-you-can eat buffet 333, Tu & Sa evenings.

spots.name: MELs Cafe
spots.desc: This place serves and advocates healthy food, has a certified nutritionist supervising the food. It is small and a bit difficult to find, but worth the trouble. Serves great four season themed salads, a variety of scrumptious sandwiches and unique rice meals like CoFFeeCHoP (pork chop marinated in coffee) or their cheesy delightful fish dish called 'cheesy dory' a favorite among the locals. You…
spots.addr: 2nd Floor UTH Bldg, Sta Catalina St., near Cnr Locsin St

spots.name: Pasta King
spots.desc: Pizza and many pasta dishes, done very well. Pasta in two serving sizes, around 179 or 319. The small one will be enough for most people, perhaps with a soup or salad if you are quite hungry.

spots.name: Roti Boss
spots.desc: Indian and Malay food. Small, no a/c, a limited menu, and rather slow service. It is well worth putting up with these minor annoyances, though, since the food is good and prices moderate.

spots.name: Halang Halang
spots.desc: Excellent Sichuan food, authentic so much of it is very spicy.

spots.name: Fish153
spots.desc: Korean restaurant and grocery store. Neighborhood has a few other restaurants and some guesthouses.

spots.name: Panda Ice Cream House
spots.desc: Locally-produced fresh fruit ice cream. Try the fried ice cream! This is a chain with several locations in Dumaguete and a few in nearby towns.

spots.name: Flip-Flops Restobar
spots.desc: Large shaded patio, big TV with sports, live band Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Open mic on Tuesdays, acoustic performances or karaoke other nights.

spots.name: Happy Jack's Restobar
spots.desc: Restobar serving cold drinks and both Asian and Western food. Full meals plus a mix and match bar snack menu. Billiard and poker tables plus live music on a couple of nights.

spots.name: Octagon Sports Bar
spots.desc: Big-screen TV mostly showing sports. Live music and 250 all-you-can-eat BBQ on weekend evenings.

spots.name: Pastry Dream
spots.desc: Offers wide a variety of European pastry, like eclairs, fruit tarts and French macarons. They also have refreshments and coffee.

spots.name: Hayahay Bar
spots.desc: Large and popular. Often has live music, reggae every Wednesday. There are several separate places selling food within the complex; one has good pizza and another offers fine Jamaican food.

spots.name: Lantaw
spots.desc: A large place with upmarket Filipino food, much of it seafood. Popular with prosperous locals and with seafood-loving foreigners. Possibly the best place in town to take a Filipina out to dinner; she will probably both like the food and be impressed by the decor.

spots.name: Cafe Racer
spots.desc: A diner in the style of mid-20th century America. Decor includes some old cars and a gorgeous motorcycle; the bar is built inside an old VW van. Menu to match; decent burgers, small but excellent milkshakes, etc. Live music sometimes.

spots.name: Low & Slow
spots.desc: A fairly large place with nice decor, offering both American and Filipino styles of barbecue. Prices are reasonable. BBQ is good, burgers decent but nothing special. Margueritas are awful; have a milkshake or 50 beer.

spots.name: Tarbush
spots.desc: Two Lebanese brothers running a small place for Middle Eastern food. Good shawarma and juices.

spots.name: Cafe Mafioso
spots.desc: Another Italian place, good quality and cheaper than most of the others, with pasta dishes around 140.

spots.name: Ayla's Breakfast Restaurant
spots.desc: A good variety of breakfast dishes, including some less common ones like eggs benedict or biscuits & gravy, plus a few other things like chile con carne. They rent the space from the municipality which sets limits on their prices, so they have the cheapest beer in the region at 40.

spots.name: Pacos
spots.desc: A tiny stand with a few tables and good Mexican food, owned by Americans. Ayla's will not complain if you sit at one of their tables and buy beer from them but get food from Paco's.

spots.name: La Cocina by Beth
spots.desc: Run by a Filipino chef who trained in Mexico . If you like flavorful food, there are Mexican dishes. Cold drinks and margaritas, fresh lemonades, the only air conditioned restaurant in the town with a perfect view.

spots.name: Kamalig
spots.desc: A large semi-outdoor (covered patio) place with live music, Filipino BBQ and some other food, and beverages.

spots.name: Lighters Galore
spots.desc: A wide selection of lighters and cigarette cases.They have a range of electric lighters from around 250 up to 1800. These are not supposed to be disposable and do not burn a fossil fuel (recharged via a USB port), so arguably they are rather green. Also convenient, completely windproof and unlikely to set hair or beard afire. However, they are generally not a good buy, except perhaps for a cheap…

spots.desc: Vaporizers, spare parts, and a good range of liquids for them

spots.name: Kalibo Cathedral
spots.desc: During the Ati-atihan festival, don't forget to visit the Kalibo Cathedral and witness the Catholic faithful get a brief respite with the "paeapak" or the massaging of a small Santo Niño (Christ Child) statuette onto the devotees.

spots.name: Latte Coffee Cafe
spots.desc: Between the rotunda and the airport is Latte, a swanky, western-friendly coffeehouse and restaurant. Like most upscale restaurants in Kalibo, the service will be extremely polite but sometimes incompetent and often slow.

spots.name: Euro- Asian Bakery & Coffee Lounge
spots.desc: One place definitely worth checking out is Euro-Asia Bakery, located down the street from the plaza past the gay-friendly nightclub Mezzanine. It has a variety of breads without sugar added, plus brewed coffee. They serve a decent but unspectacular American-style breakfast with tea, eggs, ham, and toast.

spots.name: Evelio Javier Freedom Park
spots.desc: A park dedicated to Antique Governor Evelio Javier, who was assassinated in 1986. There is a marker that reads "A fitting tribute to a man who has done so much, not only for the people of Antique, but the entire Filipino nation, in pursuit of justice, freedom, dignity, democracy and peace" at the spot where he is shot dead. The circumstances behind Javier's assassination remains unknown, but he…

spots.name: Malandog River Park

spots.name: Barangay Culasi Lighthouse

spots.name: Ang Panublion Museum

spots.name: Sumlang Lake
spots.desc: Offers a peaceful retreat where calm waters mirror the majestic Mayon Volcano, creating a soothing atmosphere ideal for relaxation, reflection and scenic photography.

spots.name: Marian Orchard
spots.desc: Serene Roman Catholic pilgrimage site in the middle of rainforest, most frequented every Holy Week as part of Visita Iglesia itineraries. There is a chapel, Stations of the Cross, Our Lady of Lourdes grotto, carillon bell, and rows of statues of various saints. Souvenirs and food are available near the chapel and carillon bell.

spots.name: Giant egg marker
spots.desc: Welcome monument showcasing the town's egg production industry.

spots.name: Fantasy World
spots.desc: theme park, though incomplete and closed to the public. It has been once used in some local fantasy-themed television dramas in the 2000s. This is, however, a common stopover for picture-taking by tourists travelling from Tagaytay to Taal.

spots.name: Fule Mansion
spots.desc: An sea-green old mansion noted for its ornate façade. Its fence is adorned by statues of lions and eagles. A small but interesting number of heritage houses can be seen in the vicinity of the residence, particularly along J.P. Rizal and Del Pilar Avenues.

spots.name: Natalio Enriquez Mansion
spots.desc: A 19th-century Beaux-Arts mansion built by a former governor of Quezon, Natalio Enriquez. It is declared a Heritage House by the Philippine government in 2008.

spots.name: Flaming Sword
spots.desc: This is a landmark depicting a hand holding a flaming sword up in the air, which symbolized the Filipino patriots' courage and gallantry as they face the adversary and threats to their democracy and freedom. The ESPADA was inaugurated on April 8, 1967.

spots.name: Santo Domingo Death March Marker
spots.desc: A marker in Barangay Santo Domingo dedicated to the victims of the Death March near Capas's abandoned train station.

spots.name: Chavayan
spots.desc: The main draw in Sabtang, it is a community (barangay) composed of houses built in the traditional Ivatan way and composed of stone and thatch roofs in the southern part of the island. It is where most postcard images of Batanes are taken.

spots.name: Santa Rosa de Lima Chapel
spots.desc: Chavayan's Roman Catholic chapel, built with a Baroque facade and a thatched roof during the Spanish era.

spots.name: Chamantad-Tinyan Viewpoint
spots.desc: An elevated sport along the National Road with views of the surrounding cliffs, coves and roaring ocean, set amid a background of rolling hills and grasslands. Beware of droppings from grazing goats and cattle.

spots.name: Savidug
spots.desc: Like Chavayan, it is a barangay in the east-central section of Sabtang composed of traditional stone houses that also forms the typical postcard pictures of Batanes.

spots.name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Chapel
spots.desc: Savidug's Roman Catholic chapel, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era.

spots.name: Savidug Idjang
spots.desc: The idjang is an Ivatan word for the elevated and fortified settlements that existed in Batanes before Spanish colonization. The one in Sabtang, situated on a triangular-shaped hill, has been the one most extensively studied by archaeologists.

spots.name: Morong Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of white sand on the northeastern shores of the island.

spots.name: Mayahao Arch
spots.desc: A naturally-formed rock arch along Morong Beach that is the most photographed natural attraction in the island.

spots.name: Mutchung Viewpoint
spots.desc: A cliffside promontory with commanding views into the Pacific Ocean and a large "I Love Uyugan" sign.

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines - Batanes
spots.desc: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, with exhibits on Batanes' natural history and culture. It is housed in a former radar station used by the US Coast Guard during the Cold War.

spots.name: Alapad Hills and Rock Formation
spots.desc: A section of highway carved through a limestone cliff overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Most tourists take photographs beside a road marker that reads "Blow UR Horn".

spots.name: St. Rose of Lima Parish Church
spots.desc: Constructed by the natives in 1660 under the supervision and control of Franciscan Missionaries.

spots.name: Cagraray Island
spots.desc: With plenty of virgin white sand beaches and home to Misibis Bay, a luxury resort.

spots.name: Sula-Bariw Integrated Farm
spots.desc: a fishing ground and has a kayaking adventure at Barangay Sula.

spots.name: Hoyop-hoyopan Cave
spots.desc: Windy ancient caves used as a WWII refuge & typhoon shelter with bats, stalactites & stalagmites.

spots.name: Albay Farmers Bounty Village
spots.desc: It is a 15-hectare, one-stop farmers' complex that serves as a learning facility, recreation, entrepreneurship, and tourism site.

spots.name: Japanese Tunnel
spots.desc: An L-shaped tunnel used as an arsenal by the Japanese Imperial Army during the World War II. It measures 40 m long and around 2.1 m deep below the ground. It was built by Japanese during WW2. Interesting place to visit once you’re at Quituinan Hills (it is included in the price). Short walk down (10 m). The tunnel is on the left. Up front is the decoy.
spots.addr: D. Nieves Street, Barangay Tinago, Camalig

spots.name: Saint John the Baptist Parish Church
spots.desc: Camalig's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era.

spots.name: FarmPlate
spots.desc: Brings a lively countryside experience through its wide-open landscapes, farm-to-table dining, and engaging activities that highlight the richness of Bicolano agriculture and local culture.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de la Porteria
spots.desc: A baroque church built on volcanic lava. It has a perfect view of Mayon Volcano that seems to be a wall paper pasted beside the church.
spots.addr: Santa Maria Street, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Green Lava
spots.desc: A grassland at the foot of a gully of Mayon Volcano accessible only via an all-terrain vehicle (ATV) tour.

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines - Bicol
spots.desc: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, featuring artefacts on Bicol's natural history, art, ethnography and culture.

spots.name: Guinobatan Museum
spots.desc: A local history museum with an equestrian monument to Simeon Ola in front.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Assumption Parish
spots.desc: Guinobatan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1895.

spots.name: Jovellar Underground River
spots.desc: Dry caving and underground river adventure experience. Short hike are expected. There are caves and rock formations. Life jackets, local guides and boatmen are available.

spots.name: Villa Miranda Farm and Resort
spots.desc: A farm offering firsthand picking of different varieties of fruits and vegetables.

spots.name: Kawa-Kawa Hill
spots.desc: Kawa-Kawa (or formerly Lunad) is a hill with a 6 crater, that looks like a giant cauldron, or kawa in the local language of Albay Bikol, and serves as both an ecotourism site and a pilgrimage site. People who climbed this hill described it as a huge amphitheater, a sliced coconut, or a hill without a top. From a distance, it looks like an ordinary hill, but up there, you'll feel its uniqueness…

spots.name: Malison Spring Resort
spots.desc: You can get a majestic view of Mayon Volcano and Malison Lake from this resort, where you can also fish or boat.

spots.name: Hobbit Hill
spots.desc: A Lord of the Rings-themed viewpoint with rolling hills, walking spots and panoramic views of Mount Mayon and Mount Masaraga.

spots.name: Kuyang's Grill
spots.desc: Run by Marcelo Garcia, is a full dining restaurant with an al fresco patio and banquet area, a large kitchen, a menu of local food favorites.
spots.addr: San Roque Street, Barangay San Roque

spots.name: Berman Ice Cream Haus
spots.desc: Halo-Halo ice cream (ice cream sandwich), Banana split, halo-halo, tapsilog, and pancit are available.

spots.name: PitoGo Café by Chef Muel
spots.desc: a popular seaside dining spot known for its unique, premium homemade empanadas.

spots.name: Oas Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic Church in Oas, built in the 19th century but with a façade spruced up and incongruous with its surrounding structures.

spots.name: Saints Peter and Paul Parish Church
spots.desc: Polangui's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1654.

spots.name: 101 Department Store
spots.desc: Most things can be found there at an inexpensive price. It's also air-conditioned for a comfortable shopping experience.

spots.name: LCC Express Mart Daet
spots.desc: Great place to buy your groceries. Available wide variety of good products.

spots.name: Bonux Chicken Unli Rice
spots.desc: They cater different foods ranging from the famous "silogs" to "inasals" to sizzling platters.

spots.name: Jocelle’s Restaurant & Music Lounge
spots.desc: Great ambiance and good food. Also a fun place to celebrate gatherings. Really enjoyed from their KTV.

spots.name: Auroras Cuizzines
spots.desc: The food here is quite expensive but still affordable. Their menu's is worth your money as they are so deliciously made. The staff are courteous, attentive, and accommodating.

spots.name: Hoogpaan
spots.desc: Hoogpaan stands as a delightful culinary discovery, offering not just great food but an experience perfectly framed by the stunning views of Bagasbas. The location, right in front of Bagasbas Beach, adds a unique charm to the dining experience.

spots.name: Leo's Cuisine
spots.desc: Nice and cool restaurant in Daet, Camarines Norte which erected along the Bagasbas Boulevard.

spots.name: Tinawagan Hills Campsite and L-Farm
spots.desc: Popular elevated getaway for camping, cool mountain air, and 360-degree views of surrounding volcanoes and peaks like Mount Isarog and Mount Mayon.

spots.name: Hinulid Church
spots.desc: A small religious shrine hosting an image of the dead Christ (Santo Entierro). It is a popular pilgrimage spot in Bicol, particularly during Maundy Thursday and Good Friday.

spots.name: Caramoan Kayaks
spots.desc: Rents out hobie kayaks as well as tents and sleeping bags in case you like to camp overnight on some islands

spots.name: Mount Iriga
spots.desc: An extinct volcano, its last recorded eruption was January 4, 1614 which formed Lake Buhi. It has an elevation of 1196 m with Ilian Hill sits toward the bottom a few kilometers above barrio San Nicolas. After the 1614 eruption, a 500 ft deep gully from the summit was formed. Wild berries and local pine trees (agoho, pronounced ah-goo-HAW) grow abundantly due to the rather cold environment.

spots.name: Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
spots.desc: Once the supposed home of a witch (aswang) later became the place where the reenactment of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ in the hill of Calvary hence the name Calvario. During World War II, the Japanese Imperial Army took advantage of its strategic location of having a good view of the town proper, used it as a garrison. It is here where countless Irigueños who opposed their presence suffered…

spots.name: Tinagba Park
spots.desc: Built to honor and commemorate the Lady of Lourdes. What was used to be the old children's park just below the church, became this beautiful park designed for everybody but more so for the children, the future of Iriga.

spots.name: New Social Hall
spots.desc: Local farmers sun-dried their rice grain prior to milling. Local and neighboring basketball teams competed every summer. Special events and social gatherings as New Year's Eve masquerade balls were held here for many years. But during the monsoon season one could almost go swimming.; This new, sheltered building, hosts the same activities and more, sporting activities, social gatherings, special…

spots.name: Ilian Hill
spots.desc: At the bottom of Mount Iriga in Barangay San Nicolas, this promontory provides a panoramic view of Iriga City, Baao and Bato Lakes.

spots.name: Inorogan Chapel
spots.desc: The chapel was built by a local philanthropist to commemorate the miraculous escape from the death and destruction by inhabitants during Mount Sumagang's eruption in 1614. The miracle is attributed to the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary whose image as Our Lady of Angustia was said to have been found at the present chapel site by Agta hunters.

spots.name: Bulalacao Hill
spots.desc: During Holy Week, the hill transforms into a vibrant hub of local tradition, where faith, community, and the natural beauty of Bicol converge.

spots.name: Olaño's AlFresko Restaurant
spots.desc: Attached to Olaño's Guesthouse, offering al fresco dining, an outdoor pavilion, and nipa huts.
spots.addr: Zone 5, J. Luntok Street (General Ocampo Street), Poblacion

spots.name: Kamp Hayahay
spots.desc: It is highlighted as a potential ecotourism park featuring natural scenery and a relaxing environment for visitors looking to unwind.

spots.name: Balang Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall at the foot of Mt. Isarog and is the last falls of the "eight falls in one river". It can be accessible through hiking from the Bongcao trail at Barangay Curry.

spots.name: Sabang Beach
spots.desc: The coastal tip of San Jose's shorelines, frequented by tourists and travellers bound to Caramoan Peninsula.

spots.name: John Aldrin Beach
spots.desc: this serene white sand beach is about an hour's drive from the town proper and features bamboo rafts (balsas), picnic areas, and swimming.

spots.name: St. Clare of Assisi Parish
spots.desc: The town's oldest parish church, dating to 1794. Feast day is every August 12.

spots.name: Virac Town Center
spots.desc: Supermarket, department store, boutiques, restaurants, cafe, etc.

spots.name: Whale Shark Interaction
spots.desc: Swimming with whale sharks. Register at the Visitor's Center located at Barangay Dancalan. Shark watchers are assigned a Butanding Interaction Officer and have to follow strict guidelines. All whale shark tour boats are provided by the center inclusive of an interaction guide called a Butanding Interaction Officer or BIO. Some resorts can do pre-booking for a minimal service fee. Price is 300…

spots.name: Frontier Whale Shark Tours
spots.desc: Leads guided whale shark tours every year from February to May with experienced naturalists as guides. The guides enter the water with the group and are experts at maintaining a safe approach to the sharks. Tours start in Manila and include domestic flights, all transfers, resort accommodation and full meals.

spots.name: Bicol Dive Center
spots.desc: Dive center is just across from the tourist center. Offers dive course & day trips to San Miguel Island and Manta Bowl, island hopping and snorkeling, the price is 4500 for 3 dives (minimum of 4 divers)and give special rates for big groups. Gear is in good condition, the boat is spacious and the people are really friendly. Accepts cash payments only. Dive shop is open year round.

spots.name: Frontier Scuba
spots.desc: Leads guided whale shark tours every year from February to May with experienced naturalists as guides. Tours start in Manila and include domestic flights, resort accommodation and meals.

spots.name: Giddy's Place PADI Dive Resort
spots.desc: Open year round. It is the only PADI accredited facility in Donsol and the only one with Philippine Commission on Sports Scuba Diving (PCSSD) accreditation. Has the only dive training pool in Donsol and the surrounding towns. Has Donsol's only resident dive instructor and has Grade A Air. Has the lowest rate for the solo diver. Accepts credit cards (Visa, MC, Amex, JCB) without surcharge.

spots.name: D'Spa
spots.desc: The only full service spa in Donsol and the surrounding towns and is attached to Giddy's Place. You have a lot of options including scrubs, body, foot and stone massages.

spots.name: ATMs
spots.desc: There are two ATMs in Donsol which take Master Card and Visa Card.

spots.name: Butanding Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Popular for its icy cold beer, mixed drinks, good food and seafood, good music and well-stocked bar and separate video karaoke area. One of the few places to eat past early dinner time. Free WiFi. Try the local dish "Crispy Pata" or deep fried pork leg which is a Philippine specialty. Accepts credit cards.

spots.name: Sadtong Panawn Restaurant
spots.desc: 500 m after the Visitor Center going east, houses few antique collections, including an old piano, pre-World War II bicycle and chair, 300-year-old vases, antique televisions and so on. The restaurant serves fresh seafoods like squid sisig and grilled squid in sweet sauce. and before leaving Donsol, try their signature flaming chicken inasal. The restaurant has free WiFi and has shows and events…

spots.name: BARacuda
spots.desc: The owner, Juliet, goes fishing in the day to offer you fresh fish at night. You can choose your own fish from the day's catch and they will cook it for you. They also serve cocktails. The bar is alongside the beach on a terrace, overlooking the sea. Really friendly place, Juliet will come and chat with you if you are alone. She also tends to bring rum at the end of dinner, for free. The prices…

spots.name: AGM Beachfront Resort Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves freshly caught fish, crabs, shrimps and other seafood, and also meat and fresh vegetables sourced from nearby farms. Chinese, Filipino, and Continental foods are available for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

spots.name: Amor Farm Beach Resort
spots.desc: The restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner with both Western and Filipino food. At dinner time ask what fish arrived that day as fishermen arrive daily in their boats to sell their catch directly to the restaurant. They will cook it any way you like. They also have a bar and a great atmosphere.

spots.name: Gibalon Historical Shrine
spots.desc: Marked as the historic site of the first Christian mass in Luzon.

spots.name: Aparri Marker
spots.desc: A Hollywood-like signage facing the mouth of the mighty Cagayan River.

spots.name: Archdiocesan Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary
spots.desc: Aparri's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt following American bombing in World War II

spots.name: Cagayan Ecclesiastical Museum
spots.desc: A museum featuring colonial-era Roman Catholic artefacts inside the Lyceum of Aparri campus.

spots.name: Ammaleran Beach
spots.desc: A longer stretch of beach heading east towards the town of Buguey.

spots.name: Bluewater Falls and Cave
spots.desc: The main tourist attraction in Baggao, it is a sprawling natural complex composed of dense forests, pristine springs, a 13-tier waterfall and rapids along the foothills of the Sierra Madre. Its highlights are the Blue Lagoon, whose turquoise waters are accessible following a lengthy hike, and the Bluewater Cave, a water-filled chamber with an estimated length of .
spots.price: ₱30. Mandatory tour guides for ₱500 for a group of 4 people

spots.name: Lipit Canyon
spots.desc: A long gorge in the Bluewater complex lined with peculiar rock formations.

spots.name: Laglagto Rock Formation
spots.desc: A series of rock formations along a gorge of the Pared River. It also has a hanging bridge.

spots.name: Asinga-Via Hot Spring
spots.desc: A stream with sulfuric waters surrounded by rock formations.

spots.name: Abaggaoan Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival celebrating local history and culture.

spots.name: BF Ecofarm and Leisure Park
spots.desc: An ecotourism venue with farm and staycation accommodations.

spots.name: Aldaw ti Baggao
spots.desc: Meaning "Day of Baggao" in Ilocano, it is a festival commemorating the town's founding anniversary.

spots.name: Taggat Lagoon
spots.desc: Claveria's seas are often very rough except for this section of beach that is protected by natural rock formations. You may have to keep clear of the fishing boats that are parked around the lagoon, testifying to the area's active fishing community.

spots.name: Lakay-Lakay and Baket-Baket Rock Formations
spots.desc: A pair of rock formations at the edge of a cape that separates Taggat Lagoon from Cabicungan Bay, named after a local legend about a couple that was turned into stone by a curse and are now the said rock formations. Lakay means man in Ilocano, while Baket-baket refers to his wife.

spots.name: Cabicungan Public Beach
spots.desc: An extensive stretch of gray sand running the length of Cabicungan Bay from Claveria Port to the mouth of the Cabicungan River. Most of the town's resorts are concentrated around this area, while Claveria Boulevard, also known as Belado Avenue, the town's main promenade, runs parallel to the beach.

spots.name: Claveria Viewdeck
spots.desc: An observation point on a hilly stretch of the highway overlooking Cabicungan Bay and downtown Claveria. This should not be confused with an older viewdeck a few meters on the same road that has now been abandoned and overgrown.

spots.name: Sentinela Cove
spots.desc: A small cove containing the Ubing-Ubing Rock formation, said in local legend to be the child of the couple turned into the Lakay-Lakay and Baket-baket formations who was also turned into stone by the same curse that struck his parents.

spots.name: Pata Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse overlooking the mouth of the Pata River, which separates Claveria from the town of Sanchez-Mira to the east.

spots.name: Bantay Kalbo
spots.desc: The northern-most point of Claveria is a hill jutting out into the Babuyan Channel and ringed by rocky cliffs. It is named as such for its grassy appearance (bantay means watchman and kalbo means bald).

spots.name: Santa Maria Ecotourism Park
spots.desc: A small park along the Cabicungan River with mangroves and cottages.

spots.name: Culao Pekkan Falls
spots.desc: A small cascade on the hills separating Claveria from Sanchez-Mira.

spots.name: Gattaran Church
spots.desc: Gattaran's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era
spots.addr: National Highway, Barangay Centro Sur, Gattaran

spots.name: Nassiping Church ruins
spots.desc: Built during the Spanish era and dedicated to Saint Michael the Archangel, this was the Roman Catholic parish church of Nassiping when it was a separate municipality. After Nassiping was annexed by Gattaran, the church fell into ruin, but somehow managed to avoid being razed altogether, resulting in a mostly intact nave and tower. The structure has been partially roofed over and now serves as the…

spots.name: Sicalao Abut
spots.desc: A local natural protected area along the Zinundungan River featuring pristine rivers, waterfalls, caves and forests.

spots.name: Janggu Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival depicting bogeymen from local folklore, featuring processions of costumed residents dressed as mythical creatures reminiscent of the Krampus-like figures common during folk festivals in Europe.

spots.name: Black Water Lagoon
spots.desc: More of a brackish pond than an actual lagoon, it forms the nucleus of the People's Integrated Agri-Tourism Center, which serves as the town's municipal park.

spots.name: Cross in the Sky
spots.desc: A built on top of Black Hill. It is accessible following a climb and offers panoramic views of the town, including the Basilica.

spots.name: Piat Hill Viewpont
spots.desc: A Hollywood-inspired sign spelling the town's name, built on top of a hill with panoramic views over the town center.

spots.name: Mapannao Lake
spots.desc: An elongated lake that sustains migratory birds through its wetlands.

spots.name: Biuag and Malana Ecopark
spots.desc: A pair of mountains separated by the Matalag River and named after two opposing giants in local folklore. Derisively known as Ambush Point as it was a favorite site by NPA rebels to stage attacks on military convoys in the 1970s and 80s, it was redeveloped by the local government into an ecotourism venue containing picnic grounds, a bicycle zipline and a cable car.

spots.name: Blue Lagoon
spots.desc: A secluded and pristine freshwater natural pool in the Zinundungan Valley.

spots.name: Mount Annaguan
spots.desc: The highest peak in town, at . The summit holds views of the town as well as the neighboring provinces of Apayao and Kalinga.

spots.name: Padekat Festival
spots.desc: Named after the local term for rice cake, it is the town's annual festival marking the establishment of the municipality on April 26.

spots.name: Crocodile Island
spots.desc: An islet in the middle of the strait separating Palaui Island and Luzon. It is named as such because the silhouette formed by the rock formations resembles the head of a crocodile. It has white sand beaches chock-full of coral and shells.

spots.name: Anguib Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach with generally calm waters due to the presence of barrier reefs.
spots.price: Rates start at ₱200 and rise depending on the length of stay and additional rentals

spots.name: Mapurao Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach which despite its location in the mainland, is only accessible through a boat ride from Port San Vicente to the adjacent Jerolynda Resort.

spots.name: Holy Guardian Angels Parish Church
spots.desc: Tuao's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt following the 1949 earthquake. Beside the main building is a squat two-story building that remains of the Spanish-era belltower.

spots.name: Mamba Ancestral House
spots.desc: The colonial-era residence of the Mamba family, one of the leading political dynasties in Cagayan. The house was also used as the headquarters of the government of Free Cagayan during World War II, and afterwards became the administrative building of the Itawes National High School in the later years of the 20th century.

spots.name: Tuao Viewdeck
spots.desc: An observation post on the hilly boundary with Kalinga province that offers views of the surrounding Chico River valley.

spots.name: Biwag Shrine
spots.desc: A makeshift shrine featuring a tacky statue of Biwag, a folklorical giant. Offerings of gin and cigarettes are commonly left at the shrine, while a celebration is also held to commemorate Biwag on the feast day of Barangay Tallag, also known alternately as Biwag, every May 6.

spots.name: Malasi Lake Sanctuary
spots.desc: A sanctuary for the endangered Philippine Duck, it is a preserve centered around a pair of lakes.

spots.name: Horno
spots.desc: The ruins of a towering structure that used to be an oven (horno) for making bricks during construction of the parish church during the Spanish era, which was not completed due to the Philippine Revolution. The present church is of a later 20th century construct.

spots.name: Cabagan Triangle Park
spots.desc: A small park in the middle of a road junction. It features a clock tower using LED screens and a statue of a horse-drawn carriage (calesa), a monument to Cabagan being one of the few places in the country to retain this mode of transport.

spots.name: Tupa
spots.desc: A stretch of rapids at the point where the Pinacanauan River leaves the Sierra Madre that is a favorite swimming spot for locals.

spots.name: Cabagan Museum
spots.desc: A one-room exhibition space on local history and culture, set inside the upper floor of the former municipal hall.
spots.addr: Aggabao Hall, Cabagan-Santa Maria Road, Barangay Centro

spots.name: Cabagan Science Elementary School
spots.desc: The administrative building of the town's main primary school is an American-era bungalow (commonly known as the Gabaldon) dating from the early 1900s.

spots.name: Balai Rosalinda Resort
spots.desc: A recreational venue with swimming pool, accommodations, and karaoke in the town center.

spots.name: Round Rock Resort
spots.desc: A recreational venue with swimming pool and karaoke near Cansan junction. For those who are not squeamish, a cockfighting arena opened a few meters away in 2026.

spots.name: Josefina T. Albano Sports and Cultural Complex
spots.desc: Said to be the largest municipal arena in Cagayan Valley at the time of inauguration, this hosted travelling matches of the Philippine Basketball Association in the 2000s. It now hosts barangay level leagues and pageants, while during vacant times, residents just play basketball in the court.

spots.name: Kalesa, Kabayu, Kalaseru Festival
spots.desc: Cabagan celebrates its patronal fiesta in honor of Saint Paul the Apostle on January 25. Starting January 15, a variety of events are held to celebrate the town's culture, including its pancit and especially the kalesas, hence the names Kalesa (cart), Kabayu (horse) and Kalaseru (coachman).

spots.name: Baka Festival
spots.desc: San Pablo's patronal fiesta is held on January 15 and celebrates the town's agrarian tradition, particularly the raising of cows. Highlights include rodeo and motorbike competitions.

spots.name: Cabagan Public Market
spots.desc: Has a gift shop (OTOP Hub) run by the municipal government selling local delicacies and handicrafts. Market day on Sundays, when there are more merchandise to be bought than usual.

spots.name: GM's Food House
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Chinese-Filipino dishes. Also does bulk orders.

spots.name: Aling Kikay's Panciteria
