spots.desc: The oldest surviving panciteria in Cabagan, founded by a descendant of a Chinese immigrant who invented pancit Cabagan during the American period. Aling Kikay's children also run adjacent panciterias.

spots.name: Mariloi's
spots.desc: Panciteria serving pancit Cabagan. Due to its popularity, an extension with more seating and menu items, along with a gift shop selling foodstuffs was opened a few meters down the highway.

spots.name: Urban Cafe + Kitchen
spots.desc: A chicken wings and pork ribs restaurant offering meals paired with rice as well as pancit Cabagan. Group-sized platters are also available.

spots.name: Alfresco Pizzeria and Bistro
spots.desc: A rooftop Italian restobar serving pizza and pasta. Has live music on weekends.

spots.name: The Hood
spots.desc: A restaurant set up in the yard of a private residence that also serves fried rice meals.

spots.name: Sy Bakery
spots.desc: A bakery and food store run by the same Filipino-Chinese family since the 1950s, as evidenced by the interior displays and the old wood-fired oven used to make their breads. Among the highlights are the tasty bread (slang for loaf bread), pan de coco (buns filled with coconut jam) and egg (custard) pie.

spots.name: Pin-tag Restobar
spots.desc: A restaurant serving fried rice meals with meat, also fried.

spots.name: Apayao Brew
spots.desc: A coffeeshop that also serves a favorite hanging-out spot for residents.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Pillar Parish Church
spots.desc: A Baroque Roman Catholic church, established in 1740. The original church included a belfry that was destroyed during a devastating earthquake, while the rest of the building except the façade was destroyed by American bombing raids in World War II. The reconstructed interior has been painted with frescoes and murals.

spots.name: Meraki Garden
spots.desc: The park is spacious and has a lot of different things to offer. The plants looks beautiful and the park is well taken care for.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway, Napaccu Pequeño, Reina Mercedes

spots.name: Primark Town Center
spots.desc: An amalgamation of the town's main market and a department store chain.
spots.addr: 45 Maharlika Highway corner Cortes Street, San Fermin

spots.name: Otep's Tinuno
spots.desc: The resto offers a wide array of typical Filipino food from Pinakbet to Inihaw to Beef Bulalo.

spots.name: Taste of Cauayan
spots.desc: By far the best place to get steak around Cauayan City. Their steak is excellently flavored.
spots.addr: Road A, Coloma Subdivision, San Fermin

spots.name: Kabayan's Arrozcalduhan and Tapsilogan
spots.desc: Affordable and tasty Filipino food. Though, its self service. Worth to try.

spots.name: Poor Clare Monastery
spots.desc: A nunnery run by the Order of Saint Clare that opens to pilgrims seeking to fulfill vows to pray in seven to 14 churches as part of the Visita Iglesia ritual during Holy Week.

spots.name: Aguinaldo Shrine
spots.desc: A small memorial to Emilio Aguinaldo and Palanan's heyday as the last capital of an independent Philippines fighting against the American occupation. It was built on the site of Aguinaldo's residence, where he was also captured by the Americans on March 23, 1901, a day after his birthday.

spots.name: Saint Mary Magdalene Parish Church
spots.desc: Palanan's main Roman Catholic church. It retains three bells from the Spanish era.

spots.name: Dicotcotan Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of white-sand beach facing Palanan Bay. Its name derives from the soft sand light enough for human feet to sink through.

spots.name: Diago Beach
spots.desc: A less-visited white sand beach directly facing the Pacific Ocean, on the other side of the peninsula on where Dicotcotan Beach is located.

spots.name: Palanan Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse guarding the promontory separating Palanan Bay from the open waters of the Pacific Ocean. It also marks the easternmost point of northern Luzon.

spots.name: Blue Lagoon
spots.desc: A pristine blue-colored lagoon curiously situated further south from downtown Palanan, at a significant distance inland from the coast. There is no visible outlet, although there are fishes living inside of it apart from a spillway that channels some of its waters towards the Palanan River.

spots.name: Digoyo Point
spots.desc: In July 1972, the ship MV Karagatan, which was carrying weapons destined to the New People's Army from China, ran aground on the reefs surrounding the area and was intercepted by the security forces. This incident later became the reasons Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos cited in his subsequent decision to impose his Martial Law dictatorship two months later. The wreckage of the ship is a…

spots.name: Culasi Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of black-sand beach facing Palanan Bay that forms a sandbar at the mouth of the Palanan River.

spots.name: Camp Samal
spots.desc: Site of the 1977 National Jamboree of the Boy Scouts of the Philippines. This camp, whose name is formed by combining the surnames of a local couple, provides views of the Cagayan River, the town proper, and nearby Delfin Albano.

spots.name: Magoli EcoPark
spots.desc: A recreational area and swimming spot around a mini-dam at a point where the Pinacanauan de Tumauini river leavers the Sierra Madre.

spots.name: Chapel of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary of Paragu
spots.desc: A chapel in one of Tumauini's rural barangays housing the century-old venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Paragu.

spots.name: Sinabuluan Cave
spots.desc: A cavern on the foothills of the Sierra Madre. Only its seven nearest chambers are open to the public.

spots.name: Saint Jerome Parish Church
spots.desc: Bagabag's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era but largely destroyed by an earthquake in 1949 and replaced by a drab building. A surviving relic is the partially destroyed Spanish-era belltower, which has been blighted by the construction of a water tank on top.

spots.name: G&B Special Buko Pie
spots.desc: The first buko pie shop in Bagabag. Its pies are commonly resold in bus stops across Cagayan Valley.

spots.name: Mashallah
spots.desc: A restaurant founded by a former migrant worker in Bahrain serving Indian and Middle Eastern dishes.

spots.name: Nueva Vizcaya Provincial Capitol Complex
spots.desc: The current headquarters of Nueva Vizcaya’s provincial government was built during the administration of Governor Patricio G. Dumlao. The capitol building is a study of architectural ingenuity. It has a park with exotic plant species, concrete benches and sidewalks lighted with giant lamps and man-made lagoon ideal for rowing the colorful mini-boats operated by people with disabilities. The…

spots.name: People's Museum and Library
spots.desc: A museum on the history, culture and ethnography of Nueva Vizcaya, housed in a two story building that used to be the headquarters of the provincial government during the Spanish era. The permanent exhibition is at the second floor, with temporary exhibits at the lobby.
spots.addr: Del Pilar Street, Don Tomas Maddela

spots.name: Rizal Shrine
spots.desc: A hillside monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal, commissioned by a Jordanian turned Filipino citizen in gratitude for having been rescued by a Filipino migrant worker went he went missing in the Saudi desert. It contains the second-largest statue of Rizal, a bronze and composite fibreglass sculpture with a height of and weighing 12 tons. The monument can be seen from as far as Solano.

spots.name: Mount Palali
spots.desc: A high peak on the eastern boundary with the municipality of Quezon that looms over northern Nueva Vizcaya.

spots.name: Ammungan Festival
spots.desc: An annual celebration of Nueva Vizcaya's history, culture and resources, featuring parades, fairs and pageants.

spots.name: Mrs. Baker's Restaurant & Pastry Shop
spots.desc: A relatively splurge casual dining restaurant serving Filipino and western dishes. It also has a bakeshop.

spots.name: Bacolod Grill
spots.desc: A grilled chicken inasal restaurant that has been in operation as early as the 1990s.

spots.name: Apayao Brew
spots.desc: This coffee shop has great location, awesome staff, and of course some lovely coffee.

spots.name: St. Louis Beltran Parish Church
spots.desc: Solano's central Roman Catholic parish church is not very special architecturally, but it houses a replica of the Black Nazarene.

spots.name: Bangaan Rolling Hills
spots.desc: A hidden paradise, beautiful hill formations, view of the town and full of grass. Due to an increase number of visitors the pathway was widened, making the hills less elegant.

spots.name: Canili Lake
spots.desc: A man-made reservoir formed by the Canili Dam used for agriculture, fishing and hydropower purposes. It covers the boundary with the municipality of Maria Aurora in Aurora province and is part of the hydropower system that includes Pantabangan Dam in Nueva Ecija.

spots.name: eMpyrean Bliss Hotspring Farm Resort
spots.desc: A resort along the Digoliat River built around a natural hot spring.

spots.name: Bundok Bakery
spots.desc: Restaurant and bakery. Its main specialty is coconut (buko) pie.

spots.name: Governor's Rapids Nature Park
spots.desc: Maddela's main tourist draw, it is an undisturbed section of the Cagayan River that was named after a Japanese officer who drowned in the area during World War II. It is a popular swimming, rafting and caving venue.

spots.name: Maddela Eco-Tourism Park
spots.desc: Another natural park complex west of town. Its highlight is Maddela Falls, a seven-tier cascade, with a natural crystal-clear pool at its base.

spots.name: Maria Angela Falls
spots.desc: A cascade in a secluded hiking trail named after a local politician.

spots.name: Panagsasalog Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

spots.name: Parish & Archdiocesan Shrine of San Isidro Labrador
spots.desc: Cuenca's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Gothic style in 1879.

spots.name: G2B Lomi
spots.desc: Local restaurant specializing in lomi, a noodle dish popular with both locals and foreigners, especially hikers. Their bestseller is "overload lomi", which is the same lomi dish with lots of toppings, and good for 4.

spots.name: Lipa City Community Park
spots.desc: Sizable park with an outdoor swimming pool, plus facilities for tennis, basketball & other sports.

spots.name: Lipa Town Center
spots.desc: Shopping center in the heart of Lipa. It’s a great place to shop for clothes, accessories, and other items, as well as enjoy a number of activities and entertainment.

spots.name: Lipa City Public Market
spots.desc: The central marketplace in town, serving fresh produce, pasalubong and cheap goods for bargain hunters.

spots.name: Robinsons Place Lipa
spots.desc: Three-storey mall, with a supermarket, department store, and Toys R' Us.

spots.name: Lomi King
spots.desc: Specializes in the local lomi recipe. Also serves pancit, all-day Filipino breakfast, rice meals, and sandwiches.
spots.addr: Jose P. Laurel Highway, Mataas na Lupa

spots.name: Chito's Restaurant & Cafe by Sideway Grill
spots.desc: Ambiance is for those trying to get a glimpse of the past: old colonial style architecture, capiz windows, hard wood everywhere. Servers were friendly and always on the lookout for your needs. Menu is expansive. Price is very reasonable, for the serving size you get.

spots.name: Antonino’s Pizzeria
spots.desc: They use their own produce for their ingredients. Brilliant concept. Tables and chairs are located beside tomato, chili, basil, etc.
spots.addr: #7 Bienvenido Peña Drive, Barangay Mataas na Lupa

spots.name: Cafe de Lipa
spots.desc: Now a chain, they serve authentic barako coffee, with a modern twist. Coffee brewing lessons are available.

spots.name: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf - Lipa
spots.desc: Coffeehouse chain serving a variety of beverages including its signature ice-blended options.

spots.name: Calijon Falls
spots.desc: Waterfall complex, with two large falls and two small ones. One of the large falls drops into a clear water pool. The two smaller falls creates a shower while other forms small cascades.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish Church
spots.desc: Malvar's main Roman Catholic church, built in a modernist style.
spots.addr: President Jose P. Laurel Highway, Poblacion

spots.name: Mount Gulugod Baboy
spots.desc: A high peak that looms over the Calumpan peninsula. Its summit offers views extending as far as Tingloy and Mindoro islands.

spots.name: Museo San Jose de Malaquing Tubig
spots.desc: San Jose's local history museum, housed in the town's former town hall built during the Spanish era.

spots.name: Sarap Ala-eh!
spots.desc: Cheap Batangueño dishes, such as lomi and crispy pata, as well as cultural experience through Batangas Tagalog words.

spots.name: Corcolon Lomi House
spots.desc: Inland food destination visited for its cheap bowl of lomi noodles.

spots.name: Poctol mangrove forests
spots.desc: They are part of a larger area along Tayabas Bay filled with mangroves

spots.name: Mount Daguldul
spots.desc: The highest point in the municipality, at 678 m. It is reachable from a trail, and a trek takes about 2 hours.

spots.name: General Miguel Malvar Shrine
spots.desc: Houses a statue and a museum on Miguel Malvar, Filipino general of the Tagalog Republic during the Philippine-American War.

spots.name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Parish
spots.desc: There is little known about the church's early history, but it dates back to around the 17th century, when Santo Tomas town center was established. The old church was destroyed by American artillery bombardment during World War II in 1945, and was replaced by a modernist church building and belfry. There is a memorial to the 15 Holy Spirit Sisters, mostly Germans, who died.

spots.name: Jose P. Laurel Memorial Library
spots.desc: The personal property of the family of Jose P. Laurel, a native of Tanauan who became president of the Japanese-installed Second Philippine Republic during World War II. The lot was donated to the Philippine Government as a historical site and public library.

spots.name: Old Municipal Hall of Tanauan / Plaza Mabini
spots.desc: The original site of Tanauan old City hall. A great place to for exercise (Walking, Running, Biking, Dog walking and Skateboarding).

spots.name: Almeda Ancestral House
spots.desc: A colonial-era private residence along Tanauan's main thoroughfare.

spots.name: Balayan Baywalk
spots.desc: Once a littered waterfront, it has been cleaned in 2019, and provides views of Balayan Bay that are similar to those in Manila's Baywalk.

spots.name: Casa Cacao
spots.desc: A private Spanish era bahay na bato belong to one of Balayan’s old rich families, which includes actor and comedian Leo Martinez, who introduced many common Batangas tropes in popular culture. The house is named in honor of the family’s fortunes in the cacao industry. The house is .

spots.name: Balayan Presidencia
spots.desc: One of the few remaining municipal government buildings in the Philippines remaining from the Spanish era.

spots.name: Casa Grande
spots.desc: The oldest surviving house in Balayan, dating from the 1850s. The residence's namesake was a friend of national hero Jose Rizal and, along with his sister, vigorously lobbied for Philippine independence against the United States.

spots.name: Parada ng Lechon
spots.desc: Mostly a celebration for a plentiful harvest, it also doubles as the feast day of St. John the Baptist. The day starts with water battles on the streets, like those also done at Watah-watah in San Juan in Metro Manila. In the morning, prepare to get wet with pails of water and water cannons from fire engines, and have a Super Soaker ready. After the water battles, lechon (roast pig) dressed in…

spots.name: Casa Corazon Motorcycle Museum
spots.desc: A private collection with many bikes and some classic cars. Lots of BMW machines including one from World War II with a machine gun mounted on the sidecar. The complex also includes a restaurant, hotel and some park areas.

spots.name: Leisure Farms
spots.desc: The first hobby farming community and agro-tourism site in the Philippines.

spots.name: Xentro Mall Lemery
spots.desc: First major mall in town. Has a Robinsons supermarket, and hotel beside it (see #Sleep).

spots.name: SM Center Lemery
spots.desc: Quite a large mall. Has a SM Hypermarket, Watson's pharmacy and fast food chains.
spots.addr: Ilustre Avenue corner P. Gomez Street, District IV

spots.name: Lemery Public Market
spots.desc: Crowded and noisy central market, selling cheap produce and dry goods.

spots.name: Citimart
spots.desc: Opens early and closes late. Cheaper buys than the major chains SM Hypermarket and Robinsons.

spots.name: Jamocha Cafe & Bistro
spots.desc: Mostly Filipino food, decent quality and prices. Live music some nights.

spots.name: Saint Francis Xavier Parish Church
spots.desc: A Romanesque parish church dating back to 1852. Spanish era church. Looks amazing from the outside.

spots.name: La Iglesia de la Nuestra Señora de la Escalera
spots.desc: The ruins of a church that was burned down during the Philippine Revolution against in 1896. The ruins are partly overgrown by a Balete (banyan) tree.

spots.name: Caleruega Chapel of Transfiguration
spots.desc: A picturesque chapel within the Caleruega Retreat Center. It is dedicated to Saint Dominic of Guzman and offers commanding views of Mount Batulao. It is a favorite wedding venue for those who can afford it.

spots.name: Mang Kulas Lomi House
spots.desc: Do yourself a favor and visit this lovely restaurant in batangas. The service is unmatched. The staff and owners truly cares about your experience. The food is absolutely amazing – big serving, great for sharing and flavorful . Absolutely the best meal we had while in batangas. Highly recommend!
spots.addr: Wawa Port Road corner Evangelista Street

spots.name: Café Stefania
spots.desc: Pizza, pasta, Filipino dishes, Western-style baked goods, all the usual variations on espresso. Most food and drink are good quality, but don't order brewed coffee; they fail miserably at that. Lovely decor, a/c, free WiFi, small but good library. Prices high but not outrageous.

spots.name: Taal Municipal Plaza
spots.desc: An open area with the municipal hall on one side and other town services such as the police station and post office on another side. It becomes quite busy during festivals with music, other entertainment and food stalls.

spots.name: Old Taal Church Ruins
spots.desc: A Statue of St. Martin de Tours now stands on the site of the “Old Taal Town” along the lakeshore.

spots.name: Maliputo Landmark
spots.desc: It is at the edge of San Nicolas town. It offers a great viewing point for Taal Volcano and the eponymous lake.

spots.name: Villavicencio-Marella House
spots.desc: Heritage home beside Casa Villavicencio. It was built as a wedding gift to a son of Gliceria. Unlike the main house, this is open to walk-in visitors.

spots.name: NHCP Museo nina Leon at Galicano Apacible
spots.desc: Leon and Galicano Apacible Museum has 6 galleries depicting the lives of brothers Leon and Galicano. First was lawyer, judge and military commander against the Spanish. The other was political activist and diplomat. The visitors may hear theirs stories in a specially prepared film to be watched right upon the entry. Museum is located in nice 19th-century ancestral house. Upper floor showcases…

spots.name: Goco Ancestral House
spots.desc: It was built in 1876 in bahay-na-bato style. It is the ancestral house of former Ambassador Raul Goco, son of Juan Cabrera Goco, who was a Treasurer of the Filipino Revolutionary Movement. This house is only open by special arrangement with a minimum of four people needed for a visit, with a Filipino-themed lunch, afternoon snacks and a heritage tour included in the admission.

spots.name: Ylagan - Dela Rosa Ancestral House
spots.desc: This house, in Bahay na bato style, was restored by Dr. Martin Ylagan-de la Rosa and his wife in 1995-1997. Since it is a private house, visits must be by special arrangement only. Temporarily closed as of October 2023.

spots.name: Galleria Taal
spots.desc: Heritage home, turned to a museum with exhibits of old photographs of the Philippines, and vintage cameras

spots.name: Taal Public Market
spots.desc: There are many food stalls serving both local delicacies (see #Eat) and other Filipino food. The north and east sides of the market have many stores catering to the tourist trade with embroidered goods, wood carvings and assorted souvenir items.

spots.name: Krisdale Supermarket
spots.desc: Not a large or remarkable store; Taal residents generally go to SM or Robinson's malls in Lemery for serious shopping. Krisdale is useful for routine items and as a landmark for some tricycle or jeepney journeys.

spots.name: Bistro Taal
spots.desc: Large place with good a/c and free Wi-Fi. Does a lot of wedding receptions and other Filipino family events.

spots.name: Cuchara Y Tenedor
spots.desc: Set inside a 19th-century warehouse, the restaurant serves Spanish and Batangueño dishes including tawilis and paella.

spots.name: Don Juan Boodle House
spots.desc: Boodle is a large platter with rice in the middle and many other dishes around it; it serves four to six people. This place offers several different boodles at 1299-1799, including a seafood boodle and one with dishes originating from Taal like adobong dilaw and tawilis. Boodelitos at 549-599 serve two. Also various lesser dishes, starting around 100, coffee, drinks, and free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Korean restaurant
spots.desc: All seating is on a covered patio, no air conditioning but it has shade and often a breeze.

spots.name: Solace Blend and Brew Cafe
spots.desc: Plenty of space (two floors plus a patio), nice decor and, unlike most restaurants in the area, plenty of parking. Food is good to excellent, they offer a good range of beer and other drinks, and service is efficient. Coffee is OK, but nothing special. Prices are on the high side by Philippine standards, though not outrageous

spots.name: Arko de Taal
spots.desc: Nice decor, large patio area with smoking permitted on parts of it, mainly Filipino food. Free WiFi, live acoustic music on Friday & Saturday.
spots.price: Meals from 99 to 1749 for an elaborate multi-person platter

spots.name: Tambayan
spots.desc: Live music on weekends. Four small cheap places with only outdoor seating. Filipino food, burgers, pizza, beer.

spots.name: Garajh
spots.desc: Upmarket place with a mostly Filipino menu. Live music on weekends.

spots.name: Josephine's Backyard Steakhouse
spots.desc: Two floors, main restaurant below, coffee shop above. Decor is lovely, an old Filipino house, and there are lots of attentive staff. Food is generally fine, but the steaks are disappointing — good quality meat and well-spiced, but cut too thin so it is impossible to cook them rare or medium rare.

spots.name: Andres Bonifacio Monument
spots.desc: Andres Bonifacio went into hiding in Indang from the Magdalo faction of the Katipunan, but he was captured in 1897 at the barrio of Limbon following an encounter where his brother Ciriaco was killed and another brother, Procopio, was also captured. A monument and a historical marker is erected at the approximate location where Bonifacio was during his capture.

spots.name: Old Municipal Hall
spots.desc: One of the few surviving municipal buildings from the 19th century, it was where Andres Bonifacio and his brother, Procopio, were detained immediately after their capture from Barrio Limbon in 1897 before being transferred to Naic. It is now a local history museum.

spots.name: Laya at Diwa
spots.desc: Meaning "Freedom and Spirit", it is a granite monument depicting a grouping of upright nude figures at the entrance to Cavite State University and surrounded by a wide park that is the only area of the campus open to the public.

spots.name: Saint Anthony Falls
spots.desc: A two-tier waterfall that was partially dammed upstream to create rock basins for swimming.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of Fatima
spots.desc: Binakayan's Roman Catholic church, built in an octagonal layout and housing a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Paniguian Falls
spots.desc: A cascade just outside downtown accessible through a forest trail.

spots.name: Buhay Forest
spots.desc: An extensive forest reserve at the edge of the Maragondon mountain range.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de Guia Parish Church
spots.desc: Magallanes' main Roman Catholic church,built during the Spanish era and extensively renovated since then
spots.addr: De Guia corner San Jose Streets, Barangay 3

spots.name: Muscovado Festival
spots.desc: An annual celebration of the town's main product, Muscovado sugar produced from Magallanes' extensive sugarcane plantations.

spots.name: Salipit Coffee Farm
spots.desc: A coffee farm growing Liberica and Robusta varieties. There is also a restaurant where their produce is paired with typical Filipino delicacies.

spots.name: Kaloy's Cafe
spots.desc: Cafe with non-conventional fruit drink options such as bignay, a local berry.

spots.name: Earth's Cup Coffee and Cacao Farm
spots.desc: Offers fusion coffee and chocolate cocktails sourced from its very own produce.

spots.name: Casa Hacienda de Naic
spots.desc: One of the few surviving friar estate manors from the Spanish era. It was also used as a headquarters for the Philippine revolutionary government led by Andres Bonifacio in 1897.

spots.name: Torres Farm Hotel and Resort
spots.desc: A resort and hotel complex whose main draw is a collection of miniaturized landmarks from around the world.
spots.price: ₱260 for a picture-taking tour, ₱290 for tour with usage of swimming pools, valid for seven hours. Separate rates apply…

spots.name: Pawikan Festival
spots.desc: A celebration of Naic's natural resources and biodiversity. The highlight of the event is the release of captive sea turtle hatchlings (pawikan) into Manila Bay.

spots.name: Lolo Claro's
spots.desc: A branch of a Maragondon-based restaurant offering fried chicken. Group meals are also available.

spots.name: Verdance Cafe and Kitchen
spots.desc: A cafe and restaurant serving all day breakfasts and a mix of Filipino, western and Asian dishes.

spots.name: Noveleta Tribunal
spots.desc: The old town hall of Noveleta, it once housed the eponymous Noveleta Tribunal of the Magdiwang faction of the Katipunan.

spots.name: Noveleta Plaza
spots.desc: This small town square has statues of Emilio Aguinaldo and other Filipino revolutionaries.

spots.name: Holy Cross Parish Church (Roman Catholic)
spots.desc: This church, built in 1937, is on the site of a chapel that was destroyed during the Philippine revolution.

spots.name: Santa Cruz Parish Church (Aglipayan Church)
spots.desc: This church was established in 1905 by General Pascual Alvarez and is as one of the old existing Aglipayan churches in the country, although its current structure was built much later. It houses an image of the Virgin Mary locally called "Nanay Paz" (Mother Peace), based on the one in Antipolo, and is venerated by Aglipayans and Roman Catholics alike.

spots.name: Noveleta Public Market
spots.desc: Wet section bustling with seafood vendors every morning. Quite noisy and smelly.

spots.name: Lucsuhin Natural Bridge
spots.desc: It is a natural bridge formation between Barangay Lucsuhin and Kalubkob in Silang, Cavite. The formation crosses the Ylang-Ylang River and is the first, large natural bridge reported in the country. The bridge and cave is not a protected area.

spots.name: Perlas ng Silang
spots.desc: Meaning "Pearl of Silang", it is a flower farm featuring an assorted number of flowering plants, manicured gardens and lawns, and sculpted horticultural images.

spots.name: Riviera Golf Course and Country Club
spots.desc: 36 holes, has a Korean restaurant. The course's terrain is flat, but challenging due to winds, but the weather is generally clear and temperatures are cooler.

spots.name: Acienda Designer Outlet
spots.desc: Opened 2018, this open-air outlet mall houses a collection of 100 designer clothing shops in four European-themed sections. Its main catch is that most items are 70% off the tag price, all year round. There is also a small foodcourt and a branch of Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, a domestic coffeeshop chain.

spots.name: Ilog Maria Honeybee Farm
spots.desc: Large assortment of products sourced from the farm's honeybees such as soap, propolis and royal jelly, shampoo, and Honey Cider vinegar. Their throat spray is quite effective for smokers.

spots.name: Santis Delicatessen
spots.desc: A branch of a Metro Manila-based delicatessen store. They also sell ready-to-ear deli sandwiches and sweets.

spots.name: Balinsasayaw
spots.desc: They serve good Filipino food inside bahay kubo cottages, with fly and mosquito netting, fans, and power outlets. The restaurant has a second branch at the junction with Aguinaldo Highway and J. Rizal Street in Barangay Lucsuhin leading to Silang town proper, beside Premier Plaza.

spots.name: Aling Tonya's Seafood Palutuan
spots.desc: A seafood restaurant that has operated since 1974 and serves fresh seafood despite its inland location by keeping live specimen to be cooked upon order.

spots.name: 11th Airborne Division Marker
spots.desc: On February 3, 1945, the 11th Airborne Division of Lt. Gen. Robert L. Eichelberger’s 8th U.S. Army airdropped military supplies and personnel together with the Philippine Commonwealth troops on the Tagaytay Ridge amidst enemy groundfire. Their mission was to secure Tagaytay City and guarantee the easy flow of troops and supplies to Manila, an action later proved as significant to the liberation…

spots.name: 41st Division USAFFE Marker
spots.desc: Tagaytay played a significant role in Philippine history. During World War II, Filipino soldiers and military officers found refuge on its vast forests and ridges. It was used as landing site and sanctuary for the Filipino USAFFE soldiers and paratroopers on their way to liberate Manila on February 3 to March 3, 1945. The 41st USAFFE marker is a place where one can know more about Tagaytay’s rich…

spots.name: The Flower Farm
spots.desc: On a windy slope of a hill sprawls a flower farm that keeps Manila abloom whole year round. This five-hectare flower farm has many varieties of flowers, such as chrysanthemums with assorted colors, gerberas, carnations, roses, and anthuriums.

spots.name: Japanese Friendship Garden
spots.desc: This garden was constructed to inculcate the value of freedom, peace and international unity into the hearts and minds of the people. It is in front of Development Academy of the Philippines Conference Center, in Brgy. Sungay East.

spots.name: One Destination
spots.desc: This travel spot in the sky city is a strip of fancy restaurants and bars. Being the nightlife hub of Tagaytay, it offers varied cuisine and entertainment to tourists. Some of the noted establishments around are Dencio's Grill, Pancake House, Starbucks Coffee, Yellow Cab, RSM, Leslies, Max's Restaurant, Cliffhouse, Antonio's Grill, and Henlin.

spots.name: People's Park in the Sky
spots.desc: A blending of natural and man-made attractions, poised on the highest point of Tagaytay City and the province of Cavite. It stands on a of solid ground and overlooks four bodies of water – Taal Lake, Balayan Bay, Laguna de Bay and Manila Bay - including nearby mountains. It is located at Dapdap West and Dapdap East, approximately east from the Tagaytay City Circle. The Palace In The Sky the main…

spots.name: Pink Sister's Convent
spots.desc: Behind the bars and glass of the Adoration Convent of Divine Mercy are those who answered the call to live in silence. Located at the Holy Spirit Drive in Barangay Maitin in the city, the convent often called the Pink Sisters Chapel has endless visitors carrying their own list of prayers. Also included in their visit is the chance to see nuns praying with them 24 hours a day, seven days a week…

spots.name: St. Anne's Shrine
spots.desc: The shrine is a small garden where a grotto of the Virgin Mary stands, surrounded by well maintained shrubbery and flower garden. In front of the grotto is a small grass clearing, which is conducive to quiet reflection. From Manila, take BLTB buses that pass by Barangay Silang Crossing to the Tagaytay Marker. At Tagaytay Marker, alight to take a utility jeep leading to Barangay Sungay where the…

spots.name: Sky Ranch Tagaytay
spots.desc: amusement park opened in 2013, with an assortment of rides, restaurants and souvenir shops. It houses the Ferris wheel Sky Eye.

spots.name: Tagaytay Picnic Grove
spots.desc: Tagaytay's playground is the popular Picnic Grove, a large park that features huts and tables for picnicking, horseback riding, a restaurant, an eco-trail boardwalk, a zipline and cable cars on the gentle slopes of the Tagaytay Ridge. It is a prime location, providing the finest view of the volcano far below.

spots.name: Tierra de Maria
spots.desc: A Catholic sanctuary garden known for its 50-foot statue of the Virgin Mary found right beside Tagaytay Picnic Grove. Catholics consider this as the HOME (Haven Of Meditation and Enrichment) of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Puzzle Mansion
spots.desc: Museum which is reputed for holding the largest jigsaw puzzle collection in the world according to Guinness. The museum was started by puzzle collector, Georgina Gil-Lacuna.

spots.name: Ayala Malls Serin
spots.desc: One of the newer malls, part of real estate conglomerate Ayala's development Serin, beside the Our Lady of Lourdes Parish.

spots.name: Josephine Restaurant
spots.desc: Provides authentic Filipino cuisine, best if you are seated at the back, which has great view of Taal Volcano. They also provide catering for large events. The ambiance is good especially for lovers and families too. A very cool place specially starting during the "ber months", from September.

spots.name: Casa Hacienda de Tanza
spots.desc: One of a few surviving friar estate houses from the Spanish era.

spots.name: Lohitor Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival, coinciding with the anniversary of its foundation and named after a portmanteau of three items associated with Tanza made with paper mache: Lobo (balloon), Higante (giant), and Toro (bull).

spots.name: Calle Real Restaurant
spots.desc: A Filipino-Spanish restaurant set inside a colonial-era residence.

spots.name: Mount Pico de Loro
spots.desc: A dormant volcano. The mountain is one of the ancient volcanic features of the Bataan Arc. Pico de Loro was first named by Spanish seafarers as its pointed summit resembles the shape from afar. The summit is commonly used as a signal by seafarers to turn east to get to Manila Bay. The Mt Palay-Palay–Mataas-na-Gulod is a protected landscape.

spots.name: Santo Niño de Ternate Parish
spots.desc: Ternate's main Roman Catholic church. It was built in the 19th century and houses a venerated image of the Christ Child.

spots.name: Andres Bonifacio Shrine
spots.desc: The site where the two Bonifacio brothers, including Andres, were executed by the Emilio Aguinaldo administration after a show trial that convicted them of treason, amidst their contributions to the downfall of the Spanish colonization. The neglected shrine is reachable through a 2.5 km drive on unpaved roads, used mostly by trucks quarrying the nearby mountains. There is parking at the end of…

spots.name: Mount Kalanggaman
spots.desc: It takes about 2 hours to reach the summit of this 585 m mountain, the cone of an extinct caldera volcano.

spots.name: Mount Palay-palay
spots.desc: There are multiple trails up to this 313 m peak, the dried-up cone of a caldera. The shortest trails takes about 45 minutes to an hour to complete. At the summit is a campsite.

spots.name: Lolo Claro's
spots.desc: A local institution serving fried chicken since 2000. Group meals are also available.
spots.addr: Governor's Drive corner Maragondon-Bucal-NIA Road, Barangay Garita A., Maragondon

spots.name: Bumbungan Ecopark
spots.desc: The park was the result of a botched attempt to build a dam over the Bumbungan River, when an engineering error led to the water continuously overtopping the spillway and creating a mini-waterfall before municipal authorities decided to build a higher bridge and convert the original structure into a small park and allow visitors to dip their feet in the spillway, do some laundry or just lie down…
spots.hours: 8AM–5PM, closed during inclement weather or when the water is heavily contaminated with brown sediment, usually…

spots.name: Japanese Garden
spots.desc: A war memorial built by the Japanese to commemorate their dead during World War II. It has a viewpoint providing views of Caliraya Lake following a climb of 100 steps.

spots.name: The Cliff at Naculo Falls
spots.desc: A private resort providing access to a viewdeck overlooking Naculo Falls, a cascade upstream from the Cavint/Pagsanjan Falls.

spots.name: Kalayaan Twin Falls
spots.desc: A set of waterfalls with four other minor cascades that is a favorite swimming spot for locals during the summer months.

spots.name: Plaza Lagumbay
spots.desc: A small square and recreational space with civic monuments and a Hollywood-like Kalayaan sign.

spots.name: Kalayaan Welcome Marker
spots.desc: A cliffside spot at the boundary between Kalayaan and Lumban overlooking the Caliraya power plant that offers panoramic views over Laguna de Bay into Mount Sembrano in neighboring Rizal province.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Holy Rosary Parish
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Luisiana, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1873.
spots.addr: Fabricante corner Estrellado Streets, Zone I

spots.name: Lumban Welcome Marker
spots.desc: A Hollywood-like signage at a cliffside spot at the boundary between Kalayaan and Lumban overlooking the Caliraya power plant that offers panoramic views over Laguna de Bay into Mount Sembrano in neighboring Rizal province.

spots.name: Burdang Lumban Festival
spots.desc: A festival showcasing Lumban's main products, particularly its textiles and embroidery.

spots.name: Battle of Mabitac Monument
spots.desc: A colorful monument commemorating a rare victory by Filipino forces against the Americans during the Philippine-American War in 1900.

spots.name: Balete Tree
spots.desc: A towering old strangler fig tree along the national highway.

spots.name: Magdalena Town Plaza
spots.desc: An extensive public square with a small garden, a monument to national hero Jose Rizal, and a busts gallery of former mayors in front of the municipal hall. Flanked by the Spanish-era parish church and the American-era municipal hall, the grounds were laid out according to a design established during the colonial era, which explains why the area is a favorite filming shoot. There is a Walk of…

spots.name: Magdalena Municipal Cemetery
spots.desc: The town's cemetery, built in 1938, is also a common filming location due to its old design and the original arch at its entrance.

spots.name: Magdalena Mini Park & Children's Playground
spots.desc: A small park with a Hollywood-like sign of Magdalena, statues of superheroes and animals, including Monstro the Sperm Whale from Pinocchio.

spots.name: Balanac Dam
spots.desc: An irrigation dam along the Pagsanjan River that is a favorite swimming spot for locals during the summer months.

spots.name: Tulay Pigi
spots.desc: In the 19th century, a Spanish priest ordered his parishioners to build a bridge connecting Majayjay and Magdalena over the Pagsanjan River. He treated his workers badly and frequently whipped them in the buttocks, hence its name (Tulay Pigi literally means Buttocks Bridge, while Puente del Capricho literally means Bridge of Caprice). This ultimately backfired, and the bridge was left unfinished…

spots.name: Dalitiwan Stream
spots.desc: A cold stream running from Mount Banahaw. At the gorge surrounding Dalitiwan Bridge are two resorts allowing access to the stream and partially channeling the waters to create man-made cascades and rock pools.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de la Porteria Chapel
spots.desc: An 18th-century chapel containing a venerated image of the Virgin Mary.
spots.addr: Arellano corner F. Blumentritt Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Old Presidencia
spots.desc: Majayjay's colonial era municipal hall burned down sometime in the 20th century and was abandoned in favor of a new site near Majayjay Church. Nevertheless, the old building's shell remains as an imposing ruin, with the stairs and parts of its portico still intact.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de Porteria Grotto
spots.desc: Placed beside the Olla (Santa Cruz) river, this was where the Nuestra Señora de Porteria image was originally thought to have been placed before the chapel in the town center was built.

spots.name: APA Wildlife Rescue and Conservation Park
spots.desc: A privately-owned zoo with more than 900 animals in the woods outside town.
spots.price: Adults: ₱345, concessions: ₱295, group discounts also available

spots.name: Bukal Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall at the boundary of Majayjay and Liliw that is claimed by both municipalities.

spots.name: Sprite Falls
spots.desc: Another set of waterfalls upstream from the Dalitiwan Bridge.

spots.name: Ukit-Taka Festival
spots.desc: An annual festival honoring Paete’s signature heirloom industries: (wood)carving (ukit) and taka (paper-mache toys).

spots.name: Kape Kesada
spots.desc: Small coffeehouse which also features paintings and artworks by local artists. A patio overlooks the Paete River.

spots.name: Heritage Houses
spots.desc: Despite heavy bombing during World War II, Pagsanjan retains a sizeable number of houses from the colonial era, some of which have been converted into restaurants or commercial outlets. These are concentrated in the town center, particularly in J.P. Rizal, Mabini and P. Caballes Streets.

spots.name: Aling Taleng's Halo-Halo
spots.desc: In operation since 1933, it serves Filipino dishes and delicacies in group-sized portions. The highlight is the halo-halo, which includes sweetened heart of palm (ubod). It also sells takeaway Filipino snacks such as banana chips and biscuits.

spots.name: Calle Arco Restaurant
spots.desc: Set in a 1950s house full of antiques and souvenirs from the owners' travels abroad, it serves Laguna dishes based on recipes passed down by the owners' family.

spots.name: Mount Ping-as Pilgrimage Park
spots.desc: A hilltop Roman Catholic pilgrimage site featuring the Stations of the Cross and a Hollywood-like Pakil sign.

spots.name: Turumba Spring Resort
spots.desc: Pakil prides itself on its pristine spring waters coming from the Sierra Madre, such that even local floods sometimes produce a blue-green rather than mud-brown color. The resort, which is supplied by natural spring water, is also said to have therapeutic and even miraculous powers, with pilgrims to the Turumba Festival also coming to bathe or drink the waters to bolster their experiences.

spots.name: Estaca
spots.desc: A small wharf over the Pakil River with panoramic views of Laguna de Bay and Pakil town itself.

spots.name: Turumba Festival
spots.desc: Regarded as the longest religious festival in the Philippines, lasting from April to October, although in practice the festivities are only done on 11 occasions between those said months. It is held to honor Our Lady of Turumba, a painting of the Virgin Mary regarded as miraculous and involves participants dancing and singing as the image is taken from Pakil Church to the streets for a procession.

spots.name: Ambon-Ambon Falls
spots.desc: A cascade along the Pangil River that literally means "Drizzle-Drizzle" in Filipino.

spots.name: Buntot Palos Falls
spots.desc: A cascade along the Pangil River that literally means "Eel's Tail" in Filipino.

spots.name: Panguil River Eco-Park
spots.desc: An extensive ecotourism site covering the Pangil River watershed and much of the Pangil highlands including forests and waterfalls. It also provides overnight accommodation.

spots.name: Pila Town Plaza
spots.desc: Pila's main public and recreational space, with views of Pila Church, Municipal Hall and some of the most beautiful heritage houses in the town, a reference to the practice of rich people showcasing their wealth by building their residences on prime real estate, namely the main square.

spots.name: IFI Saint Anthony Parish
spots.desc: One of the oldest Aglipayan churches in the Philippines, built in 1932.

spots.name: Pila Elementary School
spots.desc: The administrative building of the town's main primary school is an American-era bungalow (commonly known as the Gabaldon) that is among the recognized national treasures in Pila.
spots.addr: M.H. del Pilar Street, Bulilan Norte

spots.name: Clinica Napil
spots.desc: A 1930s residence owned by the same family that runs the clinic.

spots.name: Pinagbayanan Crematorium
spots.desc: The remains of a precolonial burial site where many of Pila's antiquities were discovered. As the site stands on a private lot, access is erratic and on a case-by-case basis with the owners and caretakers.

spots.name: Pailah Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival, celebrating its agricultural and natural resources.

spots.name: La Cosina Antonio
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Filipino and Western dishes inside a converted heritage house

spots.name: Laguna Provincial Capitol
spots.desc: Houses the provincial government offices, some parks, and festival grounds. The neoclassical capitol building at the entrance is designed by American architect and urban planner William Edward Parsons.

spots.name: Villa Valenzuela
spots.desc: Lying on the banks of the Santa Cruz River beside Santa Cruz Bridge, the mansion was built in 1919 for one of the town's leading families and resembles a castle. It is a closed private residence that looks abandoned and haunted, but its low fences allow pictures of its spiral staircases, ornate facades and windows to be taken from the outside, particularly when approaching from the bridge. See if…
spots.addr: Zamora Street corner Quezon Avenue, Santo Angel

spots.name: Municipal Hall
spots.desc: One of a few surviving Art Deco civic edifices in the Philippines.

spots.name: Santa Cruz Plaza
spots.desc: A tree-lined square filled with various monuments, including a 1920s era memorial to Jose Rizal. During major holidays, the square and the adjacent FT. San Luis Plaza are filled with various food stalls.

spots.name: Emilio Jacinto Burial Place and Monument
spots.desc: A small monument marking where Filipino revolutionary hero and Santa Cruz native Emilio Jacinto was temporarily buried following his death from malaria in 1899 before being transferred to Metro Manila.

spots.name: Ina ng Awa Chapel
spots.desc: A makeshift Catholic shrine for the Virgin Mary established by a local family and considered miraculous by residents.
spots.addr: Pedro Guevara Avenue. Alternate entrance at A. Regidor Street

spots.name: National Shrine and Cathedral of the Our Lady of Maulawin
spots.desc: An Aglipayan church hosting a piece of Molave (Maulawin) lumber containing an image of the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Laguna Sports Complex
spots.desc: Part of the Laguna University complex, it hosts major sporting events held in Laguna.

spots.name: Metro Central Mall
spots.desc: Typical mall with fast food chain. Has a jeepney terminal in front for those heading to Lucban.

spots.name: Makiling Botanic Gardens
spots.desc: Little streams and rivulets cut through the demonstration garden.

spots.name: National Arts Center
spots.desc: A school for young artists managed by the Cultural Center of the Philippines. Perhaps what stands out most though are the truly exceptional views of Lake Laguna.

spots.name: Paciano Rizal Shrine
spots.desc: Jose Rizal's older brother, Paciano, became a general in the Philippine Revolution and the Philippine-American War. When peace came, Paciano moved to Los Baños and bought a plot of land from which he built a house in 1927 and did farming. The private residence is still owned by Rizal's heirs and is open only by prior arrangement, but contains a museum dedicated to Paciano's life complete with…

spots.name: General Yamashita Memorial Monument
spots.desc: In 1946, General Tomoyuki Yamashita, the "Tiger of Malaya", was executed by hanging at this site following his conviction for war crimes committed by Japanese forces during World War II, including the conversion of UPLB into a concentration camp. A small shed housing a simple tombstone with Japanese inscription now stands at the site. A few meters to the back is a similar shrine to General…

spots.name: Magnetic Hill
spots.desc: An elevated site where an optical illusion makes it appear that cars move on their own or in the opposite direction.

spots.name: Spice Jar Restaurant
spots.desc: Good Mexican food plus a few Filipino dishes, pizza, donuts, & expensive steaks. No guacamole or margueritas.

spots.name: Santo Sepulcro Shrine
spots.desc: A chapel housing a venerated statue of the dead Christ known locally as Lolo Uweng.

spots.name: Hallow Ridge Golf Course
spots.desc: Golf course south of Manila, popular hangout by foreigners and locals. Hilly course with a slightly mild climate, but playing is a challenge due to terrain and occasional rain. Has a Japanese and Korean restaurant.

spots.name: Robinsons Galleria South
spots.desc: Four-story lifestyle mall, with a food court, supermarket and multistory parking

spots.name: Izakaya Rai Rai Ken
spots.desc: Japanese cuisine, such as sushi, sashimi, and bento. They serve sake, as well as soju – due to many Korean tourists eating here.

spots.name: Pares-pares sa Kubuhan
spots.desc: Lutong bahay dishes served in nipa cottages at a reasonable price.
spots.addr: 7 Maharlika Street, United San Pedro Subdivision, San Antonio

spots.name: Ting Qua Qua
spots.desc: Branch of local chain offering cheap Filipino-Chinese dining.
spots.addr: Puregold San Pedro, Magsaysay Road, San Antonio

spots.name: Kapiterya
spots.desc: Another nice place to hang out and dine near San Pedro Exit.

spots.name: Balibago Complex
spots.desc: The traditional commercial heart of the city, which also hosts the bus terminals.

spots.name: Paseo Outlets
spots.desc: Lifestyle mall, part of the Greenfield City private township which spreads into neighboring Cabuyao. Shops and restaurants are spread out in 9 buildings, with their own parking lots.

spots.name: Robinsons Santa Rosa
spots.desc: Three-storey mall, with fewer shops and restaurants. Has a supermarket and cinema, but no department store. Used to be frequented by locals before the opening of its rival, SM City Santa Rosa.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora del Pilar Church
spots.desc: Alaminos' main Roman Catholic church, dating back to the Spanish colonial era near the municipal hall. Its patron is the Nuestra Señora del Pilar, after an image of it was retrieved from a town well.

spots.name: Museo ni Cipra
spots.desc: An art museum featuring abstract and geometric art inside the Acropolis South subdivision. It was established by the Museo ni Cipra Foundation as a means of platform to showcase the works of its founder Cipra Kamatoy whose works has been featured in the Ayala Museum in Makati, and other local artists supported by the foundation. Some artworks are available for purchase.

spots.name: Kayumanggi Foods
spots.desc: Alaminos-based preserved-fruits manufacturer. They maintain a store where tourists can purchase preserved fruit products in jars. Also within the site is Francisco’s Halo Halo, ran by the same company where they sell halo-halo, a popular shaved-iced Filipino dessert mixed with various toppings including beans and fruits.

spots.name: Heritage Houses
spots.desc: Liliw retains a sizeable number of houses from the colonial era, some of which have been converted into restaurants or commercial outlets. These are concentrated in the town center, particularly in San Juan, Gat Tayaw, Plaza Rizal, and P. Burgos Streets.

spots.name: Liliw Church of Christ
spots.desc: A white-painted, Gothic inspired church that is one of the oldest Protestant places of worship in the country, established in 1904.

spots.name: B.N. Badong Footwear Trading
spots.desc: One of the oldest footwear stores in Liliw, in operation since the 1960s. Also sells purses.

spots.name: Arabela
spots.desc: Italian dishes, not limited to pasta and pizza, and a selection of cakes and pastries at their bakery. Location rather quite has too low headroom (approximately 5′3″), as the dining area used to be the basement of a colonial-era residence.
spots.price: House style pasta: 270-300; pesto: 280-320; pizza: 290-405 (depending on size and thickness)

spots.name: American Ribs & Wings
spots.desc: A chicken wings and pork ribs chain offering meals paired with rice. Group-sized platters are also available.

spots.name: Caffè Lilio
spots.desc: A restaurant serving coffee, pastry, pasta and sandwiches inside a converted heritage house.

spots.name: White House Bistro 1938
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Filipino and Western dishes housed inside a heritage mansion built in the 1930s.

spots.name: Mang Larry's Artisanal Distillery
spots.desc: A lambanog distiller that sells finely crafted coconut liquor, with its premium vintage aged for five years.

spots.name: Nagcarlan Municipal Hall
spots.desc: Built in 1941, it is one of the few remaining civic buildings in the Philippines to survive World War II.

spots.name: Komikero Komiks Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to comic strips featuring the collection of comic artist Gerry Alanguilan, whose works include domestic and international publications such as Marvel and DC Comics.

spots.name: Doña Leonila Park
spots.desc: A tree-filled park filled with fountains and neoclassical and Filipino-themed statues, it is a favorite recreation hub among residents. It sits on a promontory overlooking Dagatan Boulevard and provides views of Sampaloc Lake.
spots.addr: Trece Martires Street co. Dagatan Boulevard

spots.name: Fule-Malvar Mansion
spots.desc: A prominent landmark, the mansion was built in 1915 in the beaux-arts and Art Nouveau style that was typical of the American period for the first city mayor of San Pablo, Potenciano Malvar, and his wife, Eusebia Fule, both of which came from prominent families. Visiting presidents and dignitaries were often hosted here. Since then the house has changed ownership multiple times and as of 2025 is…

spots.name: Doña Prudencia D. Fule Ancestral House
spots.desc: A Spanish-era bahay na bato last inhabited by a scion of the Fule family known for her devotion to the education sector. In the 1930s, she donated the house and the adjoining plot to build a high school that now bears her name. The house was at times used as a school building before falling into neglect and becoming inhabited by squatters claiming to be Doña Prudencia's heirs. Following a legal…
spots.hours: Museum for Industrial Arts and Economics: Open Mon-Fri during school hours. Otherwise ask caretakers for permission.
spots.addr: Prudencia D. Fule Memorial National High School, Maharlika Highway, Brgy. San Nicolas

spots.name: Old San Pablo City Hall
spots.desc: Built in a neo-classical style, this imposing structure is one of the few surviving civic buildings in the Philippines from the pre-World War II era. It contains a small museum on the history of San Pablo.

spots.name: Pio Conducto Ancestral House
spots.desc: A private residence built for one of San Pablo's well-to-do residents in 1924, it became known as the setting of the 1988 classic Filipino horror film Tiyanak featuring a demon-baby from Filipino folklore and has since become a stereotype for a haunted house, lightened somewhat by the grotto of the Virgin Mary in the yard. Only the semi-cylindrical exterior and ornate window grills can be seen on…

spots.name: Sulyap Gallery Cafe
spots.desc: Restaurant with overnight accommodation set in a compound with ancestral houses.

spots.name: Iskong Bantay Watchtower
spots.desc: The remains of a Spanish-era coastal watchtower built in the 18th century to defend Atimonan against raids by Moro pirates and other foreign invaders such as the Dutch. The site was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2020.

spots.name: Bangkong Kahoy Valley
spots.desc: A secluded, forested valley between Mounts Banahaw and San Cristobal that is home to campsites, natural springs and other attractions deemed holy by Banahaw pilgrims.

spots.name: Lake Gunao
spots.desc: A volcanic crater lake near the Tiaong-Dolores Road west of downtown Dolores. It was formed as part of the Laguna Volcanic Field and is an extension of the more famous Seven Lakes of neighboring San Pablo, but is less visited and has fewer tourist infrastructures.

spots.name: Kutang San Diego
spots.desc: A Spanish-era coastal watchtower built in the 18th century to defend Gumaca against raids by Moro pirates and other foreign invaders such as the Dutch. The site was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 2020.
spots.addr: Nava Boulevard corner Quezon Street, San Diego

spots.name: Gumaca Municipal Hall
spots.desc: Built during the American occupation in 1921, it is one of a few civic buildings in the country to survive World War II.

spots.name: San Diego de Alcala Park
spots.desc: A small recreational space built on top of a limestone hill overlooking Lamon Bay. Its highlight is a monument to Gumaca's patron saint, Didacus of Alcalá.

spots.name: La Casa de Doña Ana
spots.desc: A large Bahay na Bato (stone house) built in Neoclassical style by a local couple. Among the ancestral homes in town, only the Casa is designed with that style.

spots.name: Mortuary Chapel Ruins
spots.desc: These are what remains of the old mortuary church of Lucban Public Cemetery. built in the late 1700s on top of a hill overlooking the town, this church features two belfries and a magnificent ornately designed façade which is quite unique for this type of church. although the church is now in ruins the exterior is still well preserved, though weathered.

spots.name: Buddy's Restaurant
spots.desc: The flagship branch of a restaurant chain that began in Lucban in 1985 and has since spread across the Calabarzon region and Metro Manila. It serves Lucban and Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
spots.addr: 99 Rizal Avenue corner San Luis Street, Barangay 8

spots.name: Gat Uban Park
spots.desc: A small park featuring a monument to the town's legendary founder and a Hollywood-like sign of Mauban.

spots.name: Rizal Hill Park
spots.desc: A promontory in the middle of downtown Mauban that was used as a military lookout throughout the town's history and now provides panoramic views of the surrounding area.

spots.name: Mauban Public Bath
spots.desc: The well-preserved remains of a public bathhouse built in 1725.

spots.name: Heritage Houses
spots.desc: Downtown Mauban hosts an uncommonly large number of houses dating from the Spanish and American colonial eras. These are mostly concentrated in the town plaza and continue to be used as private residences or commercial establishments.

spots.name: Robinsons Easymart Mauban
spots.desc: A grocery housed inside the white-colored ancestral residence of Father Horacio dela Costa, an eminent Jesuit priest and historian.

spots.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria Parish Church
spots.desc: Pagbilao's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1730. Its belfry contains some colonial-era bells.

spots.name: Pagbilao Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of local government in Pagbilao, it was built in 1927 and is one of a few civic buildings in the Philippines that survived World War II.

spots.name: Gudani-Salvanera Ancestral House
spots.desc: A well-preserved colonial-era private residence built in the late 19th century and transferred in 1909 to its current location due to the expansion of the Manila Railroad.

spots.name: Palsabangon Mangrove Forest
spots.desc: An extensive protective area composed of estuarine mangrove woodland along Pagbilao Bay. It has various species of flora and fauna such as crabs, monitor lizards and birds.

spots.name: Pagbilao Grande Island
spots.desc: A large island at the eastern edge of Pagbilao Bay. To the east is Pagbilao Chica (little) island, actually an extension of the main island connected to it by a narrow isthmus. It is home to Pagbilao's unspoiled beaches and at the same time, a thermal power plant that has been an eyesore for the environmentally-concerned.

spots.name: Pagbilao Public Market
spots.desc: Built in 1916, it is one of a few such buildings to have survived World War II.

spots.name: Agawan Festival
spots.desc: Annual harvest festival held every May 15. Among the highlights is the Pinagong-eating contest, involving the rapid consumption of Quezon's own notoriously hard bread.

spots.name: V&V Pizza
spots.desc: Pizza (house special, ham and cheese, Hawaiian, and pepperoni), sisig and shawarma. The location is small, and orders are done in a kiosk.

spots.name: Buddy's Restaurant
spots.desc: A branch of a provincial restaurant chain based in Lucban serving Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway corner Pablo Street, Poblacion

spots.name: Sariaya Bread House
spots.desc: A bakery operating since 1982 that sells local delicacies such as pinagong, a hard but sweet bread, and broas, a meringue-like contraption sold in large metal cans.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway corner Rizal Street, Poblacion

spots.name: Casa Comunidad de Tayabas
spots.desc: Stone house built in 1831, used as a guesthouse for visits by Spanish dignitaries. This house also served as the place of the trial of Hermano Pule after his arrest on 1841.

spots.name: Tayabas Parke Rizal
spots.desc: Great place for relaxation and family bonding at the heart of Tayabas.

spots.name: Tayabas Cemetery Chapel
spots.desc: A Spanish-era chapel in the middle of the town's main cemetery.
spots.addr: Tayabas Roman Catholic Cemetery, Tayabas-Sariaya Road

spots.name: Buddy's Restaurant
spots.desc: A branch of a provincial restaurant chain based in Lucban serving Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.

spots.name: Mallari Distillery
spots.desc: A producer of premium lambanog (spirit made from coconut) owned by the same family since 1901. It is one of a few lambanog-makers selling vintage bottles of the drink, similar to French wine production systems, and one of a few allowed to export lambanog to overseas markets.

spots.name: Tiaong Church
spots.desc: Tiaong's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and extensively altered since then.

spots.name: Doña Concha Umali Ancestral House
spots.desc: A 1920s Art Deco mansion built for one of Tiaong's leading families but later abandoned except by a few caretakers and subsequently rumored to be haunted. While prior permission is needed from the owners to enter, the low fences allow for bystanders to admire the fountain in the front yard showing a man wrestling with a crocodile, and even peek into the glassware laid out at the dining table.
spots.addr: Claro M. Recto Street, Barangay II

spots.name: Moises Escueta Alaala Park
spots.desc: A small recreational space with civic monuments, including that of Ye Fei, a Filipino-Chinese mestizo who moved to China and rose to become a senior general and politician under the Communist regime.

spots.name: Ugu Bigyan's Pottery Garden
spots.desc: The residence of local pottery artist Ugu Bigyan, which was opened to the public in 2000 as an arts space and workshop.

spots.name: Angono Street Murals
spots.desc: The Angono Street Murals are a series of sculpted street murals that depict the paintings of national artists, predominantly the ones of muralist Carlos “Botong” Francisco and others. Look out for his house and studio along Doña Aurora Street.

spots.name: Blanco Family Museum
spots.desc: The Blanco Family Museum is a collection of art by prominent painter Jose Blanco, his wife, and their seven children.

spots.name: Nemiranda Arthouse
spots.desc: A museum that consists of paintings and sculptures of Nemesio "Nemi" Miranda.

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Saint Clement
spots.desc: Angono's main Roman Catholic church, a modernist edifice with a light, airy and cheery interior whose main draw is a 1923 miniature painting of the Baptism of Christ by local artist Juan Senson that was declared a national treasure and displayed in the adjacent ecclesiastical museum.
spots.hours: Museum open by appointment. Ask the parish center for details

spots.name: Angono Forest Park
spots.desc: Angono Forest Park is a quiet, forested park to stretch your legs, feed ducks, and see wildlife.

spots.name: Angono Lakeside Eco Park
spots.desc: Angono Lakeside Eco Park is a park frequented by bikers, joggers, and picnickers alike for its sunsets and view of the Metro Manila skyline.

spots.name: Eastridge Golf Club
spots.desc: Eastridge Golf Club is a large, 72 par, 18-hole golf course located in the rolling green hills of Angono and Binangonan.

spots.name: Balaw Balaw Restaurant and Art Gallery
spots.desc: A restaurant and art museum known for its exotic dishes, such as Adobo Kamaru and Ginataang Kuhol, and its vast collection of paintings and artifacts.
spots.addr: Doña Aurora St. cor. Manila East Rd, Doña Justa Village

spots.name: Cafe Giya
spots.desc: A charming al fresco cafe that offers a romantic pit stop to enjoy coffee and refreshments.
spots.addr: G/F Cafe Giya Building, Block 2, Village East Executive Homes, 3 Col. Guido Road

spots.name: Mount Kalbaryo
spots.desc: A hilltop Catholic shrine involving a flight of 288 steps to see a grotto of the Virgin Mary and a Cross.

spots.name: Punta del Diablo
spots.desc: A rocky promontory stretching into Laguna de Bay, named as such because it was said by folk legends to have been made by the Devil in a failed bid to woo a local girl.

spots.name: Nuestra Señora de los Angeles de Binangonan
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic church in the rural Morong Peninsula that houses a venerated 19th-century sculpture of the Virgin Mary which, along with the statue of Saint Ursula in Binangonan Parish, are the two most important religious icons of Binangonan.

spots.name: Aling Kika's Food Products
spots.desc: Selling a variety of kakanins (rice cakes) like bibingka, sapin-sapin and biko since the 1970s.

spots.name: Palo Alto Falls
spots.desc: This man-made falls in Palo Alto is an hour drive from the town center.
spots.addr: East Dr., Palo Alto Residential Estates

spots.name: Kinamatayan Falls
spots.desc: Legend says two lovers who had family issues committed suicide at the falls so no one will be able to separate them, hence the falls' name, which literally means "place of death". A few minutes of hiking will take you to the cold-as-ice falls of Kinamatayan.

spots.name: Kasarinlan Eco-park
spots.desc: A park situated where the Baras River empties into Laguna de Bay, with views of the lake itself and surrounding wetlands.

spots.name: Mangantila Café
spots.desc: A Filipino restaurant at a secluded location beside Laguna de Bay.
spots.hours: No reservations on weekends and holidays

spots.name: Morong Comandancia
spots.desc: The town's old municipal hall and police garrison during the Spanish and American occupations. The ground floor hosts the Morong Municipal Tourism Office, while the second floor houses the Museong Pambayan ng Morong (Morong Museum), which has exhibitions on local history and sells a few souvenirs. At the side of the building is an Art Deco gazebo built during the American period.
spots.price: 150 for Morong Museum, P250 with photography

spots.name: Cavalier Monument
spots.desc: An equestrian statue on the junction between Manila East Road and J.P. Rizal Street leading to the town propers of Baras, Tanay and Pililla.

spots.name: Duckling Society
spots.desc: A recreational spot on the estuary formed by the Morong River as it enters Laguna de Bay

spots.name: Candida
spots.desc: A traditional dance festival that began in the 1970s and held in conjunction with Easter celebrations.

spots.name: San Diego de Alcala Parish Church
spots.desc: Built between 1599 and 1632 as a chapel of ease. As of August 2026, the church is undergoing renovations and is expected to reopen in October 2026, with masses being held temporary in a nearby covered court.

spots.name: Bahay na Bato
spots.desc: A private residence built from stone bricks during the Spanish era

spots.name: Parola
spots.desc: Provides a view of the Laguna lake and Rizal's nearby towns.

spots.name: Tinipak River and Rock Formation
spots.desc: A series of white stone rapids and boulders along the Agos River.

spots.name: Mount Irid
spots.desc: A high peak near the triboundary with Rizal, Laguna and Quezon provinces that is also claimed by the municipality of Rodriguez, although hikers generally enter the area through Barangay Santa Ines in Tanay. The mountain is home to a few endemic wildlife including subspecies of orchids, rafflesias, pitcher plants and forest mice.

spots.name: Tanay Town Center
spots.desc: The only mall in Tanay, with the Savemore grocery chain as one of its tenants.

spots.name: Saint Rose of Lima Parish Church
spots.desc: Teresa's main Roman Catholic church, dedicated to Saint Rose of Lima and built in a camalig (traditional barn/warehouse) style.

spots.name: Turumba sa Mahal na Patron Santa Rosa
spots.desc: A celebration of the town's patron saint, Saint Rose of Lima

spots.name: Jhayko's Grill and Restaurant
spots.desc: Selling rice meals, sizzling sisig (minced pork jowl) and other snacks.

spots.name: Rodriguez Ancestral House
spots.desc: A colonial-era house that used to be the residence of the town's namesake, Senate president Eulogio Rodriguez.

spots.name: Mount Irid
spots.desc: A high peak near the triboundary with Rizal, Laguna and Quezon provinces that is also claimed by the municipality of Tanay. The mountain is home to a few endemic wildlife including subspecies of orchids, rafflesias, pitcher plants and forest mice.

spots.name: Mount Balagbag
spots.desc: A peak at the boundary with the city of San Jose del Monte in Bulacan province used as a stand-in location for films set in northern Luzon and one of the closest hiking destinations to Metro Manila.

spots.name: Death March markers
spots.desc: The Bataan Death March passed through the center of Abucay, as marked by the life-size white obelisks lining the original route along Bataan National Road.

spots.name: Wawa Lati Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse at the mouth of the Abucay River overlooking Manila Bay.

spots.name: Sibul Nature Spring Resort
spots.desc: A waterpark run by the municipal government that uses cold water from a natural spring supplied by the Mount Natib massif.

spots.name: Country Pool Villas
spots.desc: An events venue with swimming pool, pickleball court and other recreational facilities

spots.name: Zero Kilometer Death March Marker
spots.desc: A marker commemorating the starting point of the Bataan Death March for Allied soldiers who were garrisoned in Bagac, with markers continuing to trace their route along present-day Linao Highway until Pilar in eastern Bataan, where they merged with the main body of POWs coming in from Mariveles. These markers are distinguished with their white color and pyramidal appearance.
spots.addr: T. Camacho Street corner Bagac-Mariveles Road, Barangay Poblacion, Mariveles

spots.name: Japan-Philippines Friendship Tower
spots.desc: A memorial to Japanese-Filipino reconciliation after World War II featuring a Japanese peace bell.
spots.addr: Gov. JJ Linao Highway corner Bagac-Mariveles Road, Atilano L. Ricardo

spots.name: Bagac Church
spots.desc: Bagac's main Roman Catholic church, built partially from coral stone.

spots.name: Zero Kilometer Death March Marker
spots.desc: The Bataan Death March began in Mariveles and stretched for 102 km. A similar marker for those garrisoned in Bagac exists in the latter town, while markers tracing the route of the Death March are scattered along Governor J.J. Linao Highway and the Bataan National Road leading to Dinalupihan and the boundary with Pampanga. They are distinguished with their white color and pyramidal appearance.
spots.addr: Avenue of the Philippines, Barangay Poblacion

spots.name: Mariveles Five Fingers
spots.desc: A series of five upland coves aligned beside each other on the boundary between Manila Bay and the South China Sea, offering hiking, cliff jumping, swimming and diving opportunities. The coves mark the southernmost tip of the Bataan peninsula.

spots.name: Pawikan Conservation Center
spots.desc: Unlike eastern Bataan, west Bataan's coastline has not been industrialized, enabling sea turtles (pawikan) to lay eggs and hatch on Morong's shores with minimal disturbance. The center secures the eggs from laying until hatching and release, with visitors allowed to explore and participate in the activities. There is no on-site accommodation, but the complex is surrounded by resort-hotels.
spots.hours: Closed outside the sea turtle breeding season

spots.name: Morong Church
spots.desc: Morong's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period using coral stones to double as a fortress.
spots.addr: Juan Luna corner Burgos Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Morong Public Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of beach along the South China Sea in downtown Morong.

spots.name: Pawikan Festival
spots.desc: A municipal festival celebrating the presence of sea turtles and the thriving biodiversity in town. The highlight of the event is the release of captive sea turtle hatchlings (pawikan) into the South China Sea.

spots.name: Loleng's Hu Tieu-an
spots.desc: A Vietnamese restaurant run by a Filipino who previously worked at the processing camp for Vietnamese refugees.

spots.name: Tangilad Dam
spots.desc: An irrigation dam on the foothills of Mount Natib with views of the surrounding lowlands and Bataan National Park.

spots.name: Death March markers
spots.desc: The Bataan Death March passed through the center of Orani, as marked by the life-size white obelisks lining the original route along Bataan National Road.

spots.name: Sinagtala Farm Resort and Adventure Park
spots.desc: An extensive complex with hotel and camp-like accommodations plus agro/ecotourism-related activities and recreations.

spots.name: Our Lady of the Pillar Parish Church
spots.desc: Pilar's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish-era in 1834 using adobe bricks.

spots.name: Death March markers
spots.desc: Pilar was the confluence point of Allied POWs from Bagac in western Bataan and Mariveles during the Bataan Death March. Their routes are marked by the life-size white obelisks lining Bataan National Road and Governor J.J. Linao Highway.

spots.name: Dunsulan Falls
spots.desc: This is a waterfall located at the foot of Mount Samat, northeast of the National Shrine.

spots.name: IMA Flora's Pamangan
spots.desc: A fixture in Pilar since 1979. The family-owned restaurant's strategic location at the junction of two major highways, a buffet of Filipino and Kapampangan dishes for prices less than mall buffet chains and its two expansive mess halls have made it a popular stopover for tourists and regular motorists as seen in the tour buses parked outside. A la carte dining available. Can get crowded at lunch…
spots.addr: Gov. JJ Linao Highway corner Roman Superhighway, Ala-uli

spots.name: Lingling Garden Restaurant
spots.desc: Filipino and Chinese cuisine. Their specials are the crispy pata (pork knuckle), fried pork belly and kare-kare (peanut stew).

spots.name: Pilis Falls
spots.desc: A cascade along its eponymous creek located in the slopes of Mount Nagpali.

spots.name: Samal Museum and Library
spots.desc: A local history museum with library that also houses the municipal tourism office.

spots.name: Baliwag Clock Tower
spots.desc: The first and only free-standing clock tower in Bulacan, also a local symbol and landmark. It is constructed in 1999 and inaugurated in 2000, during the 137th birthday anniversary of hero, Mariano Ponce.
spots.addr: Dr. Gonzales Street, and Senator Ninoy Aquino Avenue

spots.name: NHCP Museo ni Mariano Ponce
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to national hero Mariano Ponce, one of a series of writers who advocated for autonomy and later independence from Spain in the late 19th century. The museum was built on the site of Ponce’s residence, which burned down in 1962.

spots.name: Holy Week processions
spots.desc: On Holy Week, particularly Holy Wednesday and Good Friday, Baliwag hosts the longest Lenten procession in the Philippines, featuring up to 120 statues showing the passion of the Christ and related images being transported on floats from the San Isidro Labrador parish church in neighboring Pulilan to San Agustin parish in Baliwag. Many of the images are family heirlooms that are only displayed in…

spots.name: Francisca Reyes Aquino Shrine
spots.desc: Shrine built in honor of Philippine National Artist Francisca Reyes Aquino, who was credited for her contributions to Philippine art and culture in the field of native dance. The place is managed by the National Historical Institute.

spots.name: The Garden
spots.desc: A leisure area within the Ciudad de Victoria which features a variety of plants. It also hosts the Animal Kingdom, a mini-zoo with various wild animals, and a merry-go-round.

spots.name: Karilagan Stevia Farm & Pavilion
spots.desc: A farm-resort and events venue with its own restaurant and cafe.

spots.name: Soc Rodrigo Residence
spots.desc: A colonial-era heritage house built in 1929 that was the ancestral home of Francisco "Soc" Rodrigo, a figure who took on multiple roles in Philippine social and political life such as playwright, journalist, author, politician and senator. While closed to the public, its iron-grilled fences allow for viewing of its surrounding gardens and the striped façade of its upper floors.

spots.name: Ycasiano-Enriquez Ancestral House
spots.desc: A Spanish era bahay na bato built for the family of one of Bulakan's gobernadorcillo (mayor) in the 18th century.

spots.name: General Gregorio del Pilar Birthplace
spots.desc: A small park and shrine built on the site of the house where General Gregorio del Pilar, a revolutionary commander who died aged 24 in a battle in Ilocos Sur against US forces during the Philippine-American War in 1899, was born. It has a statue of the boy-general and a flagpole. Wreathes are laid at the statue on November 14, his birthday and on December 2, the anniversary of his death.

spots.name: Dakip
spots.desc: A Holy Week ritual memorializing the Way of the Cross. It features men in Biblical-era costumes reenacting the Passion of the Christ while walking for around the barangay for between 4 to 5 hours. Expect to see participants flagellating themselves or being beaten with palm leaves by spectators in commemoration of Jesus Christ's sufferings as part of their devotion and Lenten penance, although the…

spots.name: Majoh Chowmaster
spots.desc: Restaurant serving chao fan (Chinese fried rice) based meals.

spots.name: Meyto Shrine
spots.desc: A small shrine with a gazebo commemorating the first Mass in Bulacan in 1572.

spots.name: Old Bagbag Bridge
