spots.desc: A Spanish-era bridge built over a channel connecting the Pampanga and Angat Rivers. It was the site of a bloody and decisive battle in 1899 that saw Americans defeat Filipino forces during the Philippine-American War and enter Pampanga, forcing the flight of the Republican government further into northern Luzon. The old bridge has been superseded by a newer one just beside it and has now lost a…

spots.name: Calumpit Municipal Hall
spots.desc: A rare Art Deco civic building sometimes used as a stand-in for period films and TV series.

spots.name: Jed's Island Resort
spots.desc: A sprawling resort complex featuring 11 swimming pools, statues of popular cartoon characters and overnight accommodation.
spots.price: ₱209 entrance fee, separate charges for rentals and accommodation

spots.name: Orante’s Floating Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant whose dining area consists of barges along the Angat River.

spots.name: 13 Falls
spots.desc: A segment of rapids with 13 cascades deep in the forests of DRT. Within the complex is the Candle Monument, a memorial to the guerrillas who set up a base in the area while fighting Japanese forces during World War II.

spots.name: Mount Brigino
spots.desc: A mountain with campsite offering views reaching up to the neighboring provinces of Pampanga, Nueva Ecija and even Metro Manila.

spots.name: Mount Manalmon
spots.desc: A peak that is popular among hikers in Biak-na-Bato National Park. It also contains Madlum Cave and forms one side of a gorge along the Madlum River that is also shared with Mount Gola, another popular hiking destination. The area is also claimed by the municipality of San Miguel.

spots.name: Tila Pilon Hills
spots.desc: A series of grass-covered hills that are nicknamed the "Chocolate Hills of Bulacan" after its resemblance to the original in Bohol.

spots.name: Balistada Hills
spots.desc: A sequence of highlands that offers views of surrounding peaks such as Mounts Pinagbanderahan (named because Japanese soldiers and guerrillas kept contesting who could plant their respective flags at its summit during World War II), Susong Dalaga (literally "Maiden's Breast" in Tagalog), and Mabio. Treks to Balistada are often combined with climbs to any of the three mountains.

spots.name: Talon ni Eva
spots.desc: Translated as "Eva's Waterfall" in Tagalog, although some locals will say Eva is actually the nickname of a man named Evaristo. It is a cascade at the foot of Mount Sumacbao accessible by hiking through a trail.

spots.name: Puning Cave
spots.desc: A cave with chambers of varying sizes. Its interior is also a pathway for the Puning River.

spots.name: Nuestra Senora del Santissimo Rosario Parish Church
spots.desc: A gothic-like Roman Catholic church hosting a venerated Marian image of Our Lady of the Rosary dating from the late 18th century.

spots.name: Bilaran ng Tibaguin
spots.desc: After a boat ride to one of Hagonoy's isolated coastal barangays, visitors can learn more about the community's relationship with the water and get the chance to buy seafood in this open-air space for drying fish (bilaran means a place to leave things out to dry).

spots.name: Habibi Resort and Sizzling House
spots.desc: A resort complex with swimming pools, karaoke rentals and a grill restaurant.

spots.name: SM City Marilao
spots.desc: Two-story high big box surrounded by some warehouses and paddies. This houses a passenger van terminal, many restaurants, a SM Store location, a SM Hypermarket, and cinemas. To the front of it is the future location for Marilao Station on the Manila-Clark railway.

spots.name: Kawayanan Festival
spots.desc: This annual festival is being hosted by the City Government of Meycauayan. The festivities include street dancing using bamboos as major props and ornamentals. It depicts the city's local culture and historical outlook.

spots.name: Aliw Shopping Complex
spots.desc: It's a small mall but packed with a lot of different shops like Jollibee, a noodle house, some food stalls, Pandayan Bookstore, Puregold, donut shops, and a lot of tiangge and gadget stores at the second floor. They even have the Pound for Pound gym inside and some beauty shops.
spots.addr: MacArthur Highway corner Requino Street, Calvario

spots.name: Saint Andrew the Apostle Parish Church
spots.desc: Norzagaray's main Roman Catholic church, which burned down multiple times since the Spanish era but has continuously been rebuilt in its original style.

spots.name: Pinagrealan Cave
spots.desc: A cave that served as a refuge for revolutionary leader Emilio Aguinaldo during the war of independence against the Spanish in 1897.

spots.name: Bitbit Bridge
spots.desc: A road bridge offering stunning views of the upper reaches of the Angat River valley.

spots.name: Bitbit Ecopark
spots.desc: A popular recreational and swimming spot in the Angat Watershed.

spots.name: Casay Festival
spots.desc: The annual festival celebrating the establishment of Norzagaray as a municipality.

spots.name: Bakas
spots.desc: A popular swimming spot along the Norzagaray River with rock formations smoothly polished by the currents.

spots.name: Simborio Chapel
spots.desc: A rare 19th-century octagonal chapel. Built on the former municipal cemetery beside the church, it now lies in the middle of a residential block after the cemetery was moved to outside downtown for hygienic reasons.

spots.name: Battle of Quingua Memorial
spots.desc: A memorial to the 1899 battle set inside a small, tree-lined park featuring a mural depicting the event.

spots.name: Parola Museum
spots.desc: A privately-run museum on local history and culture housed inside a structure that resembles a lighthouse (parola).

spots.name: Casanova-Aguirre Ancestral House
spots.desc: A well-preserved house built in 1927 and used as a setting for several films.

spots.name: Casa San Francisco
spots.desc: A house built in 1929 that was converted into an events venue.

spots.name: Aguirre Centennial House
spots.desc: A 1920's house inside the Butterfly Haven Resort, which has a butterfly garden.

spots.name: Casa Balbina
spots.desc: A private residence built in 1910 that has the largest veranda in Pulilan.

spots.name: Adriano Salvador Heritage House
spots.desc: Dubbed as the "Malacañang of Pulilan", in 1908 this historical house served as the joint municipal seat of government of the two adjoining towns of Quingua (Plaridel) and Pulilan.

spots.name: Pulong Kabyawan Agricultural Farm
spots.desc: An ecotourism site promoting rural culture, although the view is somewhat spoiled by the presence of industrial warehouses nearby. The complex has a reconstructed colonial-era mansion containing a museum about farm life and temporary exhibitions of folk art.

spots.name: Carabao Festival
spots.desc: This festival is celebrated annually. Pulileños celebrate the feast in honor of their saint by parading carabaos (water buffaloes) and making them kneel in front of the church as a sign of respect to Saint Isidore Labrador, patron saint of farmers. Also included in the parade are cows, horses, street folk dancers, marching bands and floats of commercial establishments of the town.

spots.name: Banal na Bundok
spots.desc: Meaning "Holy Mountain" in Filipino, it is a hillside monument/park filled with monuments to Jesus Christ and other key figures in the Bible. It is a popular pilgrimage site during the Lenten season, when visitors clamber to pray atop the various hilltop shrines.
spots.addr: Sibul-Biaknabato Road, Sitio Pangarayuman, Barangay Biak na Bato

spots.name: Tecson House
spots.desc: A residence built for the Tecson family, whose members included an officer in the Philippine Revolution.

spots.name: Sevilla House
spots.desc: A now decrepit residence built in 1921 for a former mayor. Unlike other houses at the time, the dwelling has three storeys.

spots.name: Sevilla's Sweets
spots.desc: A roadside store selling local dairy-based confectionaries such as yema and pastillas.

spots.name: Mount Labi
spots.desc: Believed to be the highest mountain in town, it is a peak whose summit requires a 2-day climb. Along its slopes are the Silangan and Deesap falls, the latter being the tallest waterfall in Nueva Ecija.

spots.name: Aurora Quezon Ambush site
spots.desc: Perhaps the main claim to fame (or infamy) of Bongabon in Philippine history is that it was the place where former first lady Aurora Quezon was assassinated along with her daughter, son-in-law, and several others when their convoy was ambushed along the highway by Huk rebels in 1949. The killing provoked national and international outrage and saw support for the Huks, then riding on popular…

spots.name: Ilog Jordan
spots.desc: A pristine waterway (ilog means "river" in Tagalog) originating from Mount Olivete that is used for irrigation and swimming purposes by surrounding resorts.

spots.name: Dilalam Lake
spots.desc: A man-made reservoir used primarily for irrigation purposes.

spots.name: Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church
spots.desc: Bongabon's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and retaining its red-brick facade.

spots.name: Museo de Bongabon
spots.desc: A museum on local history and culture, housed inside the former municipal hall.
spots.price: ₱25 adults, ₱20 elderly/disabled, ₱10 students, additional fees for filming and commercial photography

spots.name: Bongabon Bike Park
spots.desc: A complex featuring dirt biking trails on hilly terrain catering to mountain bikes.

spots.name: Sibuyas Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival dedicated to its main agricultural product (sibuyas means onion in Tagalog).

spots.name: Tagpuan sa Lumang Gapan
spots.desc: Meaning "Meeting-Spot in Old Gapan", it is a cluster of well-preserved colonial-era houses concentrated around two perpendicular cobble-stoned streets beside Gapan Church. During major holidays, the street is closed off to vehicles and becomes a pedestrian-friendly zone complete with stalls.
spots.addr: Delos Reyes corner Jacinto Streets, San Vicente

spots.name: Gapan City Plaza
spots.desc: Gapan's main public space, featuring civic monuments, trees and a Ferris wheel. A fine spot for recreational activities, finding some shade from the weather or just people-watching. On weekends, the area hosts a night market.

spots.name: Casa Batik
spots.desc: A garden and farm filled with (mostly) bougainvilleas and other flowering plants, some of which are also on sale. There is also a cafe onsite. Also a popular venue for weddings and photography sessions.
spots.price: ₱100, ₱80 concessions for senior citizens and disabled persons and ₱50 for students, free for children below

spots.name: Pantabangan Old Town
spots.desc: The old site of Pantabangan was razed by bulldozers and dynamite before it was submerged by of waters from Pantabangan Lake, but since the 1980s it has reappeared as an island on five separate occasions coinciding with extremely low water levels caused by drought and the El Niño, the most recent being in 2026. During such occasions, there is a higher volume of tourists from outside town seeking…
spots.hours: March-May, if the water levels are low enough

spots.name: George Point
spots.desc: A dinosaur-themed nature park with large animatronic dinosaur statues, swimming pools, children's playground and overnight accommodations.

spots.name: Lake Farm de La Marre Park
spots.desc: An agritourism-themed resort with spa and overnight accommodation.

spots.name: Saint Isidore the Farmer Parish Church
spots.desc: San Isidro's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and extensively renovated since then. It houses a venerated image of the Christ Child and a copy of the Marian image of Our Lady of Porta Vaga.

spots.name: Carron Dreampark
spots.desc: A carnival/theme park with arcade games and other typical children's entertainment amenities.
spots.addr: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Santo Cristo

spots.name: Tayabo Nature Park
spots.desc: Has a flight of hundred steps into a hilltop pagoda, which has views of Nueva Ecija and the Caraballo Mountains

spots.name: Bale Batu
spots.desc: Meaning "Stone House" in Kapampangan, it is a residence designed and built by local artist Jesus Padilla using cement and pulverized rocks from nearby Mount Arayat and modeled after Angkor Wat in Cambodia.

spots.name: Gintung Pakpak Ecopark
spots.desc: An ecotourism venue at the foot of Mount Arayat featuring forest groves and a man-made reservoir.

spots.name: Soupy Buns
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Taiwanese cuisine, including xiao long bao.

spots.name: Macabebe Ecopark
spots.desc: An extensive nature complex at the very edge of Macabebe marking spot where the Pampanga River empties into Manila Bay. It has wetland formations and a small beach, though the estuarine waters are not recommended for swimming.

spots.name: Heliograph Tower
spots.desc: An obelisk-like structure built by the Spanish to serve as a "sun telegraph" that transmitted Morse code messages using the sun's rays. It is one of a few remains of an extensive Spanish military communications and watchtower system in Central Luzon and was later used to store and manufacture sugar.

spots.name: Magalang Municipal Hall
spots.desc: One of a few civic buildings in the Philippines that survive from the American occupation, dating back to the 1920s.

spots.name: Banal A Bunduk Dalan Ning Krus
spots.desc: Meaning "Holy Mountain, Way of the Cross" in Kapampangan, it is a religious complex at the foot of Mount Arayat that attracts pilgrims during the Lenten season for its 14 Stations of the Cross laid out across a trail that culminates in a statue of a risen Jesus Christ.

spots.name: Plaza Magalang
spots.desc: One of the better-designed and maintained town squares in the Philippines, featuring a large gazebo, civic monuments to local heroes and other noteworthy achievements, and a statue of a carabao.

spots.name: Don Antonio Luciano House
spots.desc: A colonial-era residence inside a secluded compound that was also used as a filming location for some domestic period films.

spots.name: Aquino-Gueco House
spots.desc: A Spanish-era residence belonging to a minor branch of the Aquino political dynasty in neighboring Concepcion, Tarlac. The view is partially obscured by mango trees.

spots.name: Ordonez-Calma House
spots.desc: A colonial-era residence whose ground floor has been leased out to commercial establishments.
spots.addr: Angeles-Magalang Road corner Morales Street, Santa Cruz

spots.name: Camaru Festival
spots.desc: Magalang's annual festival, coinciding with the feast of its patron saint, Bartholomew and dedicated to the local delicacy, crickets (camaru in Kapampangan)

spots.name: Angeles City Flying Club
spots.desc: The main recreational aviation club in Central Luzon, offering short flying, paragliding and related activities. The club's facilities also include a cafe and swimming pool.
spots.addr: Woodland Airpark, Sitio Talimundok, Santa Maria

spots.name: Sunset Park
spots.desc: A riverside promenade parallel to the Minalin-Bacolor Dike Road.

spots.name: Aguman Sanduk Festival
spots.desc: Meaning "Fellowship of the Laddle" in Kapampangan, it is an annual harvest festival that has been celebrated since 1932 in which male residents dress up as women.

spots.name: Pakbung Hudas
spots.desc: Meaning "Explosion of Judas" in Kapampangan, it is an Easter ritual in which a giant effigy of Judas Iscariot is blown up in front of Minalin Church using firecrackers. The ritual is also practiced in the neighboring town of Santo Tomas.

spots.name: Edelyn's Homemade Nuts
spots.desc: A store producing and selling local peanuts and other munchies in jars.
spots.addr: 620 Purok 6, Santa Rita Subdivision, Santa Rita

spots.name: De Jesus Ancestral House
spots.desc: An 18th century residence that somehow managed to survive the Pinatubo eruption intact and unburied by lahar.

spots.name: White House
spots.desc: A two-story private, white-painted mansion built during the Spanish era.
spots.addr: Rizal corner San Jose Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Bale Kastila
spots.desc: A 19th-century Spanish-era residence with an extensive balcony that used to be the estate house of a sugarcane hacienda. It fell into neglect and was used as a shooting location for domestic horror films before being restored to its original Victorian and Art Nouveau design complete with tiles in 2024. There are plans to convert the house into a bed and breakfast and event venue.

spots.name: Nabuclod Mountains
spots.desc: Part of the Zambales Cordillera, it provides views of the Central Luzon plains up to Mount Arayat.

spots.name: Palakol Summer Place
spots.desc: A shallow point along the Gumain (Telesiko) River set in the backdrop of the high SCTEX Gumain viaduct that is a favorite swimming place for residents. Cottages can be rented from the owners, who are mostly from the local indigenous Aeta community.

spots.name: Lopez Mansion
spots.desc: Built in 1929 as the residence of a sugar magnate, Don Alejandro Lopez, it is the first concrete house in Pampanga. The house later fell into a long period of neglect caused in part by family squabbles and lahar flows caused by the Mount Pinatubo eruption, which is why some locals refer to the place as the “Haunted Mansion” when asked for directions. The house was repaired in 2016 and is now used…

spots.name: Guagua Municipal Hall
spots.desc: Built in 1937, it is one of the few remaining civic buildings in the Philippines to survive World War II.
spots.addr: Gil Puyat Avenue, Plaza Burgos, Poblacion

spots.name: Plaza Burgos
spots.desc: Guagua's main square, featuring civic monuments, a gazebo and trees. A fine spot for recreational activities, finding some shade from the weather or just people-watching. It is also the de facto main transport terminal for most jeepneys in Guagua.

spots.name: Araullo Ancestral House
spots.desc: A private residence built in 1928. Despite the perimeter walls, its two storeys are visible from outside.
spots.addr: Gil Puyat Avenue, Santo Niño, Poblacion

spots.name: Bale Pinaud
spots.desc: A nipa (pawid)-roofed residence built in the early 1900s for the David-Siongco family, whose members have produced senior clergy members, journalists and other intellectuals who have influenced cultural discourse in the Philippines.
spots.addr: Pedro S. David Street, San Juan Nepomuceno, Betis

spots.name: Christ the Redeemer Park
spots.desc: A small park with a life-sized statue of Jesus Christ overlooking Guagua's wetlands

spots.name: The Original Razon's
spots.desc: The flagship branch of a restaurant chain that began in Guagua in 1972 and later expanded to Metro Manila in 2003. Its main specialties are dinuguan (pork blood stew), pancit luglug noodles, and its minimalist halo-halo, made from finely-shaved ice, sweetened bananas, leche flan, milk and sweetened macapuno,
spots.addr: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, San Matias, Locion

spots.name: The Original Galan 1st Class Chicharon
spots.desc: The oldest chicharon (pork rind) maker in Pampanga, in operation since 1968. Sells the product by weight. Atsara (pickled vegetables) sold separately.
spots.addr: Guagua-Santa Rita Road, San Roque, Poblacion

spots.name: Funnside Ningnangan
spots.desc: A Pampanga-based restaurant and grill chain serving Filipino dishes.
spots.addr: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, San Matias, Locion

spots.name: Apag Marangle
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Kapampangan cuisine since 2008. Some of their more exotic delicacies include crickets (camaru), fried and stuffed frogs, and Tinolang Tugak (frog s in a thin soup with vegetables).
spots.addr: Jose Abad Santos Avenue corner Dalan Betis, San Juan Nepomuceno, Betis

spots.name: Diosdado Macapagal Museum and Library
spots.desc: A two-story building that was built behind the bahay kubo where Diosdado Macapagal, the 9th President of the Philippines, once lived. Inside the museum are historical photographs of Macapagal and other memorabilia, and a replica of the Office of the President's desk as it looked during his administration.

spots.name: NHCP Museo ni Jose B. Lingad
spots.desc: A museum about the life of Jose B. Lingad (pronounced “ling-gad”), a Kapampangan politician who held senior positions in the provincial government, the executive branch and the national legislature before being assassinated in 1980 when he was a political opponent of President Ferdinand Marcos and his martial law dictatorship. The complex, which converted Lingad's simple two-story ancestral house…

spots.name: Plaza Lubao
spots.desc: Lubao's main square, featuring a bust of President Macapagal, trees and a Hollywood-like sign of Lubao.

spots.name: Pradera Verde Golf Club
spots.desc: A golf course set in an eponymous tourism and luxury residential estate. The complex also has its own airfield, and hosts the annual Lubao International Balloon and Music Festival.
spots.addr: Jose Abad Santos Avenue, Barangay Prado Siongco

spots.name: Lubao Bamboo Hub & Eco-Park
spots.desc: An ecotourism park on the Lubao wetlands featuring an extensive bamboo grove. As of 2026, the complex is closed for renovations.

spots.name: Dara Falls
spots.desc: A set of four cascades. Its name was shortened because its last syllables are also the Filipino word for pubic hair.

spots.name: Miyamit Falls
spots.desc: A waterfall on the Mount Pinatubo massif. A permit from the municipal hall is needed before entering.

spots.name: Tutulari Avatar Gorge
spots.desc: A gorge named in part because it resembles the setting from the film Avatar (the one with blue aliens).

spots.name: Hacienda Dolores Chapel
spots.desc: A Spanish-era Roman Catholic barangay chapel, built in 1838 and repaired following damage caused by the 2019 earthquake.

spots.name: Sandbox
spots.desc: Part of the Alviera private development, it has a giant swing and an obstacle course. Being in a relatively dry area near Mount Pinatubo, it can become hot during the months of March to May, so prepare to get sunburned.

spots.name: Inararo Trail
spots.desc: One of many trails leading to Mount Pinatubo and its crater lake, with a duration of 8-10 hours and length of that is thankfully covered by 4x4 drives through gullies clogged with lahar. Although the trail's jump-off point is actually in Sapang Bato in Angeles City, the majority of the route passes through Porac and usually includes stops at other attractions along the Pinatubo massif such as…

spots.name: Villa Epifania
spots.desc: A 1930s Art Deco residence that is the first concrete structure in Santa Rita. It is a common location shoot for films, TV series and ghost-hunting expeditions.

spots.name: Gosioco Ancestral Manor
spots.desc: The well-preserved ancestral residence of one of Santa Rita's most prominent families, built in 1841. The owners offer pre-arranged heritage lunches/dinners and tours with a minimum of 10 people needed for a visit.

spots.name: Pineda Ancestral House
spots.desc: A residence built in 1917 that later became a school building.

spots.name: Salaria Coffee
spots.desc: A cafe inside the grounds of the Gosioco Manor run by the Gosioco family.

spots.name: Old St. Michael the Archangel Parish Church
spots.desc: The oldest religious structure in Tarlac, built around the 18th century. It was here where Gen. Pedro Pedroche and his men were executed by Gen. Francisco Makabulos and the revolutionary troops, executed on charges of rebellion at the orders of Gen. Antonio Luna during the Philippine-American War in 1899. But sadly, the church was gutted by fire in 1997, and it has yet to be restored.

spots.name: New St. Michael The Archangel Parish Church
spots.desc: A replacement structure for the burned-down parish church, built in an imitation Baroque style.

spots.name: Maria Clara (Leonor Rivera-Kipping) House
spots.desc: This house was owned by Leonor Rivera who could have been the wife of the national hero, Jose Rizal. They were in a relationship for 11 years. Leonor's mother did not like the rebellious Jose and intercepted the letters of the young lovers. Leonor, convinced by her mother that Jose no longer loved her, reluctantly married the Englishman Henry Kipping, but died shortly afterwards. Leonor is said…

spots.name: National River Park Corridor
spots.desc: A 1.4-kilometer park along the Cutcut River at New Clark City.

spots.name: New Clark City Aquatics Center
spots.desc: An open-air water-sports venue which hosted events of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games. Its structure is based of the baklad, a type of local fish trap.

spots.name: Death March Memorial Shrine
spots.desc: A monument with an inverted V structure commemorating the tragedy of the Death March as well as dedicated to the heroism of Allied soldiers of World War II. It is sometimes mistaken by unsuspecting visitors to be the larger Capas National Shrine.

spots.name: Tambo Lake
spots.desc: A secluded lake created after the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo. It became a fishing ground for the indigenous Aeta people.

spots.name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish
spots.desc: Capas' main Roman Catholic church, founded in 1776. The church's architecture is rather bland due to it being rebuilt after World War II, but the parish's feast day draws crowds.

spots.name: Bueno Hot Springs
spots.desc: Deep yourself in two natural hot springs which were modified to fill two concrete pools of 60-90 cm (2-3 ft) of water. Water temperatures range from 45-49.5°C (113-121°F) and has a neutral pH level of 5.5.

spots.name: New Asia Golf & Spa Resort
spots.desc: A 27-hole, par 108 golf course in Barangay O'Donnell along the river of the same name. The facility also offers Korean-inspired sauna and in-house spa services.

spots.name: 4x4 vehicle ride to Mt. Pinatubo
spots.desc: Book a 4×4 vehicle ride to the Mount Pinatubo volcano at the Tourism Office in Brgy. Santa Julian.

spots.name: Mount Telakawa
spots.desc: Mount Telakawa is a hiking destination for travelers opting for a more obscure alternative to Mount Pinatubo. The mountain has an elevation of 630 meters (2066 ft) above the sea level. Its name comes from a local term for "a pot place upside down" which is a reference to its shape.

spots.name: Jumping Wild Boar Ecopark Ranch
spots.desc: Horseback riding, All-terrain vehicle (ATV) ride, and community immersion at the Jumping Wild Boar Ecopark.

spots.name: Capas Public Market
spots.desc: Low cost meat and produce along with local goods can be bought here. Side has carinderia for the hungry shoppers. Parking can be tricky for cars and would recommend going there with a tricycle.

spots.name: Saint Monica Parish Church
spots.desc: Botolan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1736 with a triangular facade.

spots.name: Bancal Ecopark
spots.desc: An ecotourism park along the Bancal River featuring kayaking trips and tours of the mangroves at the nearby estuary.

spots.name: Capayawan Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of beach used more often by local residents and tourists seeking budget-friendly options.

spots.name: Ina Poonbato Shrine
spots.desc: A shrine dedicated to the venerated Marian image of Ina Poonbato (Mother Lord of the Rocks), a sculpture of the Virgin May discovered on a rock by Aeta villagers in the 1600s and relocated following the Pinatubo eruption in 1991. Its religious importance increased when the statue was found undamaged by lahar flows amid the ruins of its original location in the barangay of Poonbato.

spots.name: Camp Kainomayan
spots.desc: The base camp for expeditions leading to Pinatubo. It also features recreational amenities such as a swimming pool, a zip line and wall climbing spots, in addition to a tourist information center from where packages to Pinatubo and related attractions can be negotiated.

spots.name: Mount Mariglem
spots.desc: A peak involving a 2- to 3-hour climb through exposed terrain with the only vegetation being grass, not the best option during the summer heat from March to May. Most climbs involve a descent afterwards to the Maligha and Agbobotilya Rivers to cool off.
spots.hours: Registration required at Cabangan Tourism Office, and a maximum of 150 climbers are allowed daily. Reservations only…

spots.name: Cabangan Beach
spots.desc: Cabangan's beachfront stretches through eight barangays along the South China Sea and consists of grayish sand. However, the strong waves make the beach more ideal for surfing than long-range swimming.

spots.name: Dapya River
spots.desc: A stretch of clear waters included in hiking itineraries for Mount Mariglem.

spots.name: Agbobotilya River
spots.desc: A stretch of clear waters included in hiking itineraries for Mount Mariglem, featuring water-sculpted cliffs and natural pools.

spots.name: Cabangan Pier
spots.desc: A privately-built pier that was built to host barges extracting sand from Cabangan. It is also used by residents as a recreational and boating area at the estuary of the Bangan River.

spots.name: Cabangan Public Market
spots.desc: Market days on Tuesdays and Fridays, when there are more merchandise to be bought than usual.

spots.name: Bonita's Kitchen
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Filipino dishes. Their main draw is the bulalo (beef soup with bone marrow).

spots.name: 1st Streat Snack Bar
spots.desc: Serves varied dishes such as sandwiches, burgers and seafood. Offers takeaway platters for those trying to buy picnic meals to the beach.

spots.name: Mami Madz
spots.desc: A small place serving goto (rice porridge with tripe) and mami (chicken noodle soup) near Cabangan Beach.

spots.name: Casa Baraka
spots.desc: Restaurant serving Filipino comfort food. Also hosts live bands on some occasions.

spots.name: San Salvador Island
spots.desc: An island with extensive white sand beaches, a giant clam sanctuary and a thriving fishing community inside a marine reserve.

spots.name: Bacala Guesthouse
spots.desc: A fishermen's shelter built on stilts atop a sandbar near San Salvador Island.

spots.name: Panglit Island
spots.desc: An island containing mangroves and a offshore sea cucumber farm.

spots.name: Cinco Picos
spots.desc: A massif with five peaks in the Subic Peninsula that is regarded as a sacred spot by the Aeta people, with a height of .

spots.name: Pinaglabanan River
spots.desc: A stretch of pristine freshwater in the Subic Peninsula reachable by hiking from Sitio Cawag.

spots.name: Bacarra Belltower
spots.desc: Bacarra church's belltower was built during the Spanish era. Over the years it gradually tilted on its side due to earthquakes and its location on an alluvial plain with soft ground. In 1983, the church's dome collapsed in an earthquake, giving its current decapitated-like appearance. Despite this, the tower was declared a national cultural treasure in 1973.

spots.name: Vijia Watchtower
spots.desc: The ruins of a Spanish-era coastal fortification meant to look out for pirates and foreign invaders.

spots.name: Bacarra Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of local government in Bacarra. Despite multiple renovations it has retained its original neo-classic façade.

spots.name: Lazo Ancestral Home
spots.desc: A well-preserved Spanish-era residence built for one of Bacarra's elite families.
spots.addr: Rizal Boulevard corner Andres Lazo Avenue, Santa Rita

spots.name: Peralta Ancestral Home
spots.desc: A Spanish-era residence used as a shooting location for domestic period films.

spots.name: Sentinela Hill
spots.desc: During the Spanish era, a redbrick watchtower was placed on top of the hill as a lighthouse and watchtower against marauding Moro pirates and foreign navies, hence the hill's name. The watchtower has been carefully preserved.
spots.addr: C. Torres Street, Barangay San Lorenzo

spots.name: Saint Lawrence Parish Church
spots.desc: Bangui's main Roman Catholic church, built in 1877 and extensively renovated since then.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish
spots.desc: The city's main Roman Catholic church, built in the Romanesque style.

spots.name: General Artemio Ricarte National Shrine & Museum
spots.desc: A small shrine with a park and museum dedicated to General Artemio Ricarte, a Filipino revolutionary who is acknowledged as the father of the Philippine Army.

spots.name: Batac Public Market
spots.desc: The building burned down following a fire in July 2026. Vendors have been temporarily relocated to the nearby Bagsakan Center.

spots.name: Batac Riverside Empanadaan
spots.desc: A covered food hall along the Quiaoit River hosting multiple stalls selling the signature Batac empanada.

spots.name: Kaangrian Falls
spots.desc: A multi-tiered stair like formation with the water cascading on every step until it drops to a pool below.

spots.name: Military Park Cape Bojeador
spots.desc: A small park in front of a military garrison that showcases some heavy weaponry and vehicles of the Philippine military

spots.name: Saud White Beach
spots.desc: Heart-shaped cove popular with both national and international tourists, movie producers, and travel writers with its emerald water and breathtaking views.

spots.name: Bantay Abot Caves
spots.desc: Verdant seaside knoll that, on account of seismic and wave pressures, developed a tunnel that is frequented by swallows and the sea at times.

spots.name: Timmangtang Rock
spots.desc: Timmangtang Rock stands majestically a few meters away from Bantay Abot caves along the shoreline. You cannot separate Bantay Abot Cave from the Timmantang Rock for they are believed to be lovers, the former being the female and the latter the male. They are collectively termed as "Lover's Rock". This rock is bell-shaped, hence the name Timmantang and affords views of the calm blue sea.

spots.name: Nacatnagan Cliff
spots.desc: Cliff marked by virgin forest with rare ferns and wild orchids growing below. Some mountain climbing opportunities. From the top, you can glimpse panoramic views of Pasaleng Bay, Maira-ira Point, Sitio Gaoa, and even Babuyan Island on a clear day.

spots.name: Malingay Cove (Blue Lagoon)
spots.desc: Half-moon bay tucked away below Maira-ira Point with Nacatnagan Cliff to the east and Dos Hermanos in the north. Here thick forest meets crystal blue waters and fine white sand.

spots.name: Dos Hermanos Islands
spots.desc: Sea stacks with caves noted for seaweed "gamet" harvesting and tropical fisheries.

spots.name: Kabigan Falls
spots.desc: Enchanting 80 ft waterfall surrounded by thick forest and well-known for its concavity.

spots.name: Saguigui Falls
spots.desc: Small relatively unknown waterfall 3.5 kilometers away from the national highway.

spots.name: Bolo River
spots.desc: Some kayaking opportunities around Dampig, Tarrag, and Poblacion 1.

spots.name: Paoay Sand Dunes
spots.desc: A stretch of sand dunes on the arid coastal plain stretching to Laoag that has also been used as a shooting location for desert scenes in domestic movies.

spots.name: Paseo de Paoay
spots.desc: A Baroque-themed two-story commercial building containing souvenir stores and restaurants, with a colonnaded arcade for those seeking shelter from the scorching Ilocos sun.

spots.name: Kusina Valentin
spots.desc: Serves Ilocano and Filipino fare. Its main specialty is Pinakbet Pizza, which was invented by the restaurant and features pizza topped by the ingredients of the signature Ilocano vegetable stew, including fermented fish paste (bagoong). Also has a Sunday breakfast buffet.

spots.name: Sulvec Watchtower
spots.desc: The remains of a Spanish-era watchtower and fortifications meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

spots.name: Paraiso ni Juan
spots.desc: Meaning "Juan's Paradise", it is a grotto built on top of a protruding rock off Sulvec Beach, itself a popular swimming spot, marking the spot where the Spanish conquistadores who first arrived in Narvacan were shipwrecked. It is a picturesque venue for sunsets, but the site itself is only accessible during low tide.

spots.name: Mount Noah
spots.desc: A towering hill with views over Sulvec Cove, the Cordillera Mountains and downtown Narvacan.

spots.name: Tangadan Tunnel
spots.desc: A road tunnel cut through a stretch of the Cordillera Mountains to bypass the narrow treacherous stretch of the Abra River Gorge. The tunnel marks the approximate boundary between Ilocos Sur and Abra provinces and has rest stops on the Ilocos Sur side.

spots.name: Sangaan Rolling Hills
spots.desc: A series of symmetrically shaped rolling hills at the boundary with Abra province

spots.name: Narvacan Tobacco Farmer's Tourism Park & Commercial Complex
spots.desc: A sprawling mixed-use commercial and tourism complex featuring a farmers' market, civic monuments, a dancing fountain, and a replica of the shipwrecked vessel carrying the Spanish conquerors of Narvacan.

spots.name: Saint Stephen Protomartyr Parish Church
spots.desc: San Esteban's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era.

spots.name: Bateria Watchtower
spots.desc: A stout, Spanish-era watchtower meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

spots.name: Apatot Beach
spots.desc: An extensive stretch of cream-colored sand running to Biak na Bato (Mapisi Rock), a rock formation marking the boundary with the town of Santiago. There is a marker commemorating a clandestine US submarine shipment of weapons to anti-Japanese guerrillas in 1944 during Word War II.

spots.name: Santo Cristo Milagroso Chapel
spots.desc: A chapel built by the cove where the Santo Cristo Milagroso was said to have washed up in 1620 from Japan, where it had been hidden away by Christians being persecuted by the Tokugawa Shogunate. At the same time, a twin image of the Virgin Mary, known as the Virgen Milagrosa, washed up in the neighboring village of Paguetpet, part of Badoc, and is also venerated in that town’s basilica. The cove…

spots.name: Cabulalaan Hills
spots.desc: A series of rolling foothills of the Cordillera Mountains that have become a popular hiking destination.

spots.name: Kudlap Burial Cave
spots.desc: A cave that was used as a precolonial burial ground. It was declared a national cultural treasure by the Philippine government in 1977.

spots.name: Tili Di Nuang Falls
spots.desc: A series of cascades along the boundary with the municipality of San Gabriel.

spots.name: Picao Hanging Bridge
spots.desc: A pedestrian walkway over the Balili Bridge connecting the downtown barangay of Suyo with the upland barangays of northern Bagulin.

spots.name: Kudal Park
spots.desc: A recreational space and campground with panoramic views over the highlands.

spots.name: Bahay na Bato
spots.desc: Meaning "stone house", it is a beachside house and art gallery featuring local history artefacts and works by Korean sculptor Bong Kim, who also designed the house using rocks, wood and pebbles collected along the beaches of Luna.

spots.name: Darigayos Beach
spots.desc: The most famous beach in Luna, featuring white sands along a cove and ideal surfing conditions.

spots.name: USAFFE-NL Military Shrine and Park
spots.desc: A beachside memorial to the time when Darigayos Beach hosted Camp Spencer, the operational headquarters of American and Filipino forces during the Battle of Bessang Pass in 1945 during World War II.

spots.name: Tangadan Falls
spots.desc: The town's main tourist attraction, it is a cascade along the upper reaches of the Baroro River at the boundary with the municipality of Bagulin. The waterfalls are commonly included in package tours from San Juan and are a common itinerary for travelers in La Union.

spots.name: Mount Mugong
spots.desc: The highest mountain in La Union, with a height of . Its summit offers views extending as far as Benguet.

spots.name: Dupagan Falls
spots.desc: A cascade along a gorge that is also used as a hydropower source for a nearby plant.

spots.name: Lucap Wharf/Lighthouse
spots.desc: The highlight of the area serving as the embarkation point to the Hundred Islands but also a seafront venue with stores, restaurants, a miniature model of the islands, and a very peculiar lighthouse with stairs wrapping around the outside of the structure.

spots.name: Bolo Beach
spots.desc: Local beach at about where the Hundred Islands start, but may have to pay and also it is not as serene as some (e.g. seaweed, dirty toilets).

spots.name: Maxine By The Sea Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: This one is nice because you can look out at Lingayen Gulf and all the launches to the Hundred Islands while you eat. But a little spendy. Also has 9 rooms for 3100.

spots.name: Los Pedritos Alaminos
spots.desc: Tasty bread. There cinnamon roll is heavenly.There brazo however is a bit rough. Dine in food are good as well specially there bulalo and bangus sisig and crispy pata.
spots.addr: 2nd Floor Montemayor Commercial Complex, Marcos Avenue, Poblacion

spots.name: Holy Cross Parish Church
spots.desc: Alcala's main Roman Catholic church, first built in 1881. It was rebuilt in 1968 following an earthquake. It is as a popular pilgrimage site in Pangasinan for housing a relic of the Holy Cross.

spots.name: Sigay Fiestahan - Buffet of the North
spots.desc: Very spacious place, great place to eat, good for wedding receptions, birthday parties and reunions.

spots.name: Bolinao Falls
spots.desc: There are 3 falls in this area: Bolinao Falls 1, 2, and 3, all in a relative east-west line on the Bolinao River. Just follow the crowd or ask for directions if needed. Really nice curtain falls and emerald pools you can swim in. Also there are resorts here if you decide you'd like to stay a while.

spots.name: Cindys Cave
spots.desc: Subterranean pools so wear your aqua booties and hopefully the water is fairly clean.

spots.name: Balingasay River
spots.desc: Balingasay river is one of the rivers in the Philippines that is awarded as the cleanest river. The water is flowing from the sea so the water is salty specifically near the bridge where children are jumping into the river. A variety of fish are living here. Beside the river is a restaurant where you can buy food and pay for a river cruise. This river cruise takes you for a ride and explore the…

spots.name: Patar White Sand Beach
spots.desc: One of those knockout beaches that make a lot of lists for reason of its beauty and warm, calm, tropical surf.

spots.name: Saint Isidore the Farmer Parish Church
spots.desc: Burgos' main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1876.

spots.name: Cabongaoan Beach
spots.desc: Perhaps the most well-known beach in Burgos, Cabongaoan Beach is pleasantly sandy, with little to no rocks prickling visitors’ feet as they pad about. The beach is also known to have tidal pools both shallow and deep, and a viewpoint where visitors can enjoy the scenery of the coast. The so-called "Depth Pool" is a tidal pool on the rocky side of the beach gets filled with water when the waves…

spots.name: Nambalan Beach
spots.desc: Unlike most beaches where there are stretches and stretches of sand, Nambalan Beach also has grassy areas shaded by coconut trees where anyone could lay down blankets and enjoy the breeze and scenery before heading out to get a suntan. Visitors are also allowed to set up camp for free so that they could enjoy the stars come nighttime.

spots.name: Sangbay Falls
spots.desc: It can be challenging for some to get there because of the 30-minute walk from the main road but the rewards at the other end are well worth the effort.

spots.name: Señor Divino Tesoro Shrine
spots.desc: Many pilgrims from neighbouring cities/towns and provinces visit Calasiao to pray at the Señor Divino Tesoro shrine, whose feast day is held every May 2 and 3. The statue of a crucified Jesus Christ is believed to grow in size and grant miracles.
spots.addr: Mamaradlo co. Mabini Streets, Barangay Poblacion East

spots.name: Death Pool
spots.desc: Where water gets pulled into a depression in the coral/rock bedrock of the shore.

spots.name: Tambobong Beach
spots.desc: Creamy white sand and lots of boats. Has some secluded coves, too, but unfortunately also some litter problems sometimes.

spots.name: Sabangan Island
spots.desc: A quiet space surrounded by many trees as well as mangroves. You can lounge around the sand or play beach volleyball. On some areas, cooking is allowed so visitors can bring food without paying a corkage fee.

spots.name: Balaki Island
spots.desc: Ideal for snorkeling, camping and swimming. And since this is a private island, getting access requires coordination with the Infanta Tourism Office and budget set aside for the gasoline of the boat and meals for the boat crew but the stay is free. The marine life in the vicinity is rich and healthy proof is the presence of seagrass around the island. Also the waters aren't too deep and the…

spots.name: Balincaguin River
spots.desc: Balincaguin River is open to everyone at any time of any day and is ideal during hot summer days. There has been news of development of a Swim-Bike-Row tour but until then, guests are free to lounge and relax.

spots.name: Santo Rosario Cave System
spots.desc: If you're a fan of cave adventures, exploring the Santo Rosario Cave System is for you. Though visitors are required to crouch down and carefully navigate themselves past the cave’s small entrance. Bats are flying around and the path inside changes in every few steps so visitors need to be cautious. You may get scrapes and bruises but mini-waterfalls, the clear pool of water and the enchanting…

spots.name: Cacupangan Cave
spots.desc: The Cacupangan Cave System proudly features four kilometres of stalagmite and stalactites beautifully carved by nature for centuries. In order for visitors to enter the cave, they have to carefully trek through a rough road and avoid the slightly jagged rocks and the slippery mud trails along the way. Once you're inside the cave, the rocks smooth over and are stable but guests still need to be…

spots.name: Rizal Park
spots.desc: True to its name, the park contains a statue of the iconic Filipino freedom fighter.

spots.name: Baba's Eco Farm
spots.desc: Baba’s Eco Farm is a recommended place of experience for plant lovers, artists and art lovers, green advocates and even to the public with interest in a new quiet landscape to relax in and to take pictures of.

spots.name: Virgin's Well
spots.desc: A natural spring said to be endowed with miraculous powers by Our Lady of Manaoag.

spots.name: One Alo Resort
spots.desc: A resort complex whose main highlight is the Pyramid of Asia, a looming structure built in 1999 by the resort's previous owner, a religious mystic.

spots.name: San Carlos Plaza
spots.desc: City park, Safe for visiting hour since police were there as well to help and assist.

spots.name: Mount Zion Pilgrim Mountain
spots.desc: Go mountain biking along this challenging vertical route that features a Christian shrine and breathtaking views at the top.

spots.name: New Public Market
spots.desc: Place is accessible but heavily congested every Market Day (Saturday) where you can buy almost everything. It has drugstores, hardware, water refilling station, agricultural products, etc.

spots.name: EatN'Run Pares Station
spots.desc: The best place to eat your cravings of authentic Filipino cuisine.

spots.name: Meggy's
spots.desc: Filipino food eatery. Lechon Kawali/Lumpiang Shanghai/Crispy Sisig/Fried Rice/Sausage/Bone marrow/Beef tapa.

spots.name: Roberto’s Backyard
spots.desc: Filipino/American restaurant. Very ambiant and cozy place. The ambience is great and relaxing!

spots.name: San Fabian Church
spots.desc: San Fabian's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style.

spots.name: Farmville San Fabian
spots.desc: An ecopark and farm resort featuring a replica of the Hobbit Village from the Lord of the Rings.

spots.name: San Fabian Central Beach
spots.desc: A long stretch of white-gray sand that forms a promenade along downtown San Fabian.

spots.name: Agpay Ecopark
spots.desc: A municipal nature reserve and recreational area between the foothills of the Cordilleras and the San Roque Reservoir.

spots.name: Pinsal Falls
spots.desc: A cascade inside the Agpay Forest Reserve at the foothills of the Cordilleras.

spots.name: Lipit Falls
spots.desc: A cascade along the Cabalisian River, a tributary of the Ambayaoa.

spots.name: Red Arrow Monument
spots.desc: A small war memorial built in memory of the Battle of Salacsac Pass. It was moved to the downtown after its original location at the foot of the pass was razed for the upgrading of the trail into a full-blown highway.
spots.addr: Nueva Vizcaya-Pangasinan Road corner Washington Street, Poblacion East

spots.name: Bued Toll Bridge
spots.desc: A viaduct over the Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway (TPLEX).

spots.name: St. Patrick of Ireland Parish Church
spots.desc: Tayug's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style.

spots.name: Balungao Hilltop Adventure and Hot and Cold Spring Resort
spots.desc: Hot and cold pools in which to immerse yourself. Zip line. Hiking trails to nearby Mount Bulangao.

spots.name: MangMac's
spots.desc: Open air dining experience. Good food and ambiance. Quick and accommodating staff. Affordable prices. Available street parking.

spots.name: Highest Point View
spots.desc: Located at above sea level, this attraction used to be the highest point in the Philippine Highway System until it was surpassed by another spot in Tinoc, Ifugao in 2019. The location also provides a view of the mountains of Atok and surrounding municipalities including Mt. Pulag.

spots.name: Haight's Place
spots.desc: Located at above sea level, it provides a panoramic view of Atok's vegetable terraces which includes the Naguey Rice Terraces in the west. Frost occurs in the area from December to February. The place was named after an American soldier who fought during the Spanish-American war who brought the first vegetable seedlings for the area which has a temperate climate who also married a local and…

spots.name: Benguet-Kochi Sisterhood Park
spots.desc: A park commemorating the 40th sisterhood ties between the province of Benguet and Kochi prefecture of Japan located within Haight's Place. At least 34 cherry blossom trees were planted in the area in mid-2016. A future tourist destination especially among the locals after the trees' first bloom expected to occur in 2019.

spots.name: Ifugao Rice Terraces
spots.desc: These amazing irrigated rice paddies were carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago. The village is nestled among perhaps the finest examples of them in the region. Anywhere in or above the village provides phenomenal views. Also, you may walk along them if you like.

spots.name: Viewpoints
spots.desc: There are several viewpoints on the opposite side when coming from the Saddle. The first few are easy to reach, except for the strenuous hike up lots of concrete steps. For the brave, there is another viewpoint on the highest point; you should not be afraid of hights and sure-footed if you attempt to go there. The valley view is wonderful.

spots.name: Tappiyah Waterfalls
spots.desc: A beautiful 70-meter falls about a 30-minute walk from the village. It's a great place to go for a swim. To go there without a guide, when arriving from the Saddle head on the opposite side of the rice terraces amphitheater (through the rice terraces or down to the village and up to the promontory). From here go down again with the only path with stairs to the other side.

spots.name: Patpat Sitio (Sub-Village)
spots.desc: Patpat is a small sub-village of Batad. While this sitio itself does not have too many attractions, the two-hour hike going there passes through some amazing sights. You first cross a river with a hanging bridge, then hike up rice terraces which lead into a small forest with numerous little waterfalls and springs. Upon reaching the ridge of the mountain, relax in a waiting shed which gives you…

spots.name: Ifugao weaving
spots.desc: Beside the Foreigner's Inn at the main village there is a small hut with an elderly woman weaving traditional clothing with a backstrap loom. Her items cost 400-500 each.

spots.name: Handmade Ifugao knives
spots.desc: Also in the main village of Babluy is Juan Buy-a, the village blacksmith. He usually makes items for actual use (not lousy souvenirs), and you may chance upon him finishing a lovely blade with carved handle and scabbard. With some good haggling and a bottle of gin (which you should always carry around in Batad), you may get it at a great price!

spots.name: Sweet potato fries
spots.desc: Sweet potato is planted in the swidden farms around Batad. So, before going on any mountain hike, an energy-boosting snack of fried sweet potato fries is a must! You can also order a few pieces of boiled sweet potato to take with you. Available at any of the restaurants in Batad.

spots.name: Cristina's
spots.desc: Offers simple but filling meals many of which are featuring locally grown rice. They also have bright but basic rooms upstairs for 250 per person.

spots.name: Mount Atugu
spots.desc: A mountain ridge marking the boundary between the barangays of Bitu and Anao that is said to resemble the silhouette of a partially-laid down woman. Hikers climb to the summit to enjoy the views during sunrise.

spots.name: Umalbong Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A functioning rice terrace complex used by the surrounding village.

spots.name: Lion's Head
spots.desc: A small lion's head carved into the rock at a curve along the highway.

spots.name: Mount Napulauan
spots.desc: The second highest mountain in Ifugao after Mount Pulag, with a height of . Climbers risk the extraordinarily difficult climb to view the sunrise at its summit, as well as its mossy forests. The mountain was also used as a headquarters by Japanese general Tomoyuki Yamashita during the final days of World War II in 1945.

spots.name: Hungduan Eco-village
spots.desc: A collection of traditional houses showcasing indigenous Ifugao culture.

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines - Cordillera
spots.desc: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, featuring artefacts on Cordilleran natural history, art, ethnography and culture.

spots.name: Pangagawan Caves
spots.desc: A pair of caves (Bat and Labrynth) with an underground river and waterfall.

spots.name: Ambuwaya Lake
spots.desc: A pristine lake which is said to have inundated a village as part of a curse according to local legend.

spots.name: Bagnit Falls
spots.desc: A cascade whose waters irrigate the rice terraces downstream.

spots.name: Imbuliklik Rock
spots.desc: A giant roadside boulder large enough to accommodate a viewdeck on top. It overlooks a highway curve and provides panoramic views of the Nagacadan Rice Terraces.

spots.name: Saint Joseph's Church
spots.desc: Kiangan's main Roman Catholic church. Its present octagonal and spired structure dates back from 1956, when it was rebuilt by Belgian missionaries following its destruction in World War II.

spots.name: United Church of Christ in the Philippines Kiangan
spots.desc: A gabled Protestant church built by American missionaries in 1926.

spots.name: Yamashita Surrender Site
spots.desc: An old school building where General Yamashita formally surrendered in 1945. It houses a few artefacts from the event.

spots.name: Tenogtog Falls
spots.desc: A three-tiered cascade named after a local word for "slice", a reference to the area being in a hunting ground.

spots.name: A'pfaw Mahencha Falls
spots.desc: A three-tier cascade accessible through a trail with 536 steps from Khohang Garden.

spots.name: Khohang Garden and View Deck
spots.desc: A mountainside garden with pine trees and a viewdeck overlooking A'pfaw Mahencha Falls.

spots.name: Mount Nagchajan
spots.desc: The site of the Japanese stronghold during the Battle of Mayoyao Ridge, riddled with caves and foxholes used as shelters. There is a small war memorial at the peak, which also offers panoramic views over Mayoyao.

spots.name: Mayoyao Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of local government in Mayoyao, strategically overlooking a cliffside with views of the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Lumaguid Stone
spots.desc: A large boulder along the Balangbang River held together by three smaller rocks. According to legend, Mayoyao will remain prosperous as long as the boulder stays in its position.

spots.name: Mount Amuyao
spots.desc: The eighth-highest mountain in Luzon, it is a peak at the boundary with Mayoyao, Banaue and Mountain Province whose summit offers views reaching to the plains of Isabela. According to Ifugao legend, it is where the first Ifugao couple sought shelter following a great flood that submerged the province.

spots.name: Igkhumtad ad Majawjaw
spots.desc: The town's annual cultural festival, featuring performances of native songs and dances.
spots.hours: Last Tue, Wed, and Thu of April

spots.name: Maura's Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe whose specialties are Japanese freshwater eel (pikaw) and pigeon pea soup.

spots.name: Maligcong Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A series of rice terraces in a remote village. Views from the terraces can be seen following a hike on Mount Kupapey.

spots.name: Santa Rita Cathedral
spots.desc: The seat of the Roman Catholic church in Mountain Province, built in an octagonal layout with multiple towers.

spots.name: Bontoc Museum
spots.desc: Bontoc museum is a must-see if you are only stopping briefly into town. It has many great pictures and artifacts from the local tribes.

spots.name: Francis Pain
spots.desc: Francis is a great guide who knows 13 local dialects, he will take you up from Bontoc to the Kalinga tribes. Check out Buscalan where you can see Whang Od perform traditional tattoos, and other very remote villages.

spots.name: Cable Café
spots.desc: This is your really only option for drinking in town. It has some great live music there and has a friendly atmosphere.

spots.name: Sumaguing Caves
spots.desc: A large and extensive cave system with jagged rocks, boulders, stalactities and stalagmites.

spots.name: Lumiang Cave
spots.desc: A cave that is also used as a burial site featuring hanging coffins, usually combined with a tour of Sumaguing Cave.

spots.name: Mount Ampacao
spots.desc: A mountain with panoramic views of Sagada and the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: Saint Mary's Episcopal Church
spots.desc: The main church in Bontoc, built during the American period and a reminder that of the Protestant dominance in this part of the Cordilleras.

spots.name: Sagada Weaving
spots.desc: Store for local and handwoven products are one of the more popular souvenir shops in Sagada. It is one of Sagada's biggest employers and you can visit the weaving looms to view how intricate the weavers go about in producing the handwoven raw materials. Very affordable prices too.

spots.name: ATM
spots.desc: There are three ATMs: a PDB in the tourist center, at the Sagada Rural Bank (downstairs around the corner) and one at the 3rd floor of the Eduardo Gaudan Longid Center building at the main junction (probably no credit card).

spots.name: Yoghurt House
spots.desc: A popular and excellent restaurant. They serve meals from breakfast to dinner. Specialties include varied yoghurt dishes and fresh local produce.

spots.name: Bilig Cafe
spots.desc: Excellent rice meals, pancakes, fantastic coffee, and more. Check out the cool postcards on the ceiling.

spots.name: Salt & Pepper
spots.desc: The restaurant has good vegetarian options, Filipino specialties and picnic baskets to take out for a hike! The friendly staff also take orders for late dinner (beyond the curfew hour) and early (before 6AM) breakfast or packed meal. Wifi available. The restaurant also offers tour meal packages for a cheaper price. Contact the number above for inquiries.

spots.name: St. Joe's Cafe
spots.desc: Inconsistent food, but the sizzling plates are quite good, and the building feels like a ski lodge.

spots.name: Bana's Coffee
spots.desc: Serves native coffee and excellent breakfasts on a ledge overlooking the valley.

spots.name: Kimchi Restaurant and Bar
spots.desc: In the center of town, when most of the places close down, and the lights go out, this is the only place still open late into the night. Nice music. They close up when people stop drinking. The Korean food is also very good. The owner lived in Korea for 15 years.

spots.name: Treasure Rock Resto Bar and Inn
spots.desc: Overlooking a Hanging Coffin or 2 at the end of the main Sagada road before you cross the bridge in the direction of the big cave. Jerry the owner will light you a bonfire while you watch the sun disappear from the front of the bar, and if you're lucky his wife will cook some tasty fried chicken too. has no official closing time. Difficult to find, look for the hand-painted sign and climb upwards…

spots.name: Gasan People's Park
spots.desc: The largest park in Gasan, this is where the town's annual passion play is staged every Black Saturday, as well as the Gasang-Gasang Street Dancing Festival every Easter Sunday. The Gasan Public Library is located inside the park.

spots.name: Gasan Sea View Park
spots.desc: Also known as the Gasan Baywalk, fairs are often held here. A wooden suspension footbridge—the only one of its kind in Marinduque—connects the park to neighboring Barangay Dili.

spots.name: Kawilihan Park
spots.desc: Located on the highest point in Gasan, it has a commanding view of the town center, with giant ipil-ipil trees being the park's main attraction.

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish
spots.desc: Located on the second-highest point in Gasan, the church has a viewing platform with wonderful views of the town center below. A grand new church—believed to be the biggest in Marinduque—has replaced the old church (which was converted into an auditorium), with a large altarpiece at the end. While substantial work is complete, the church is not yet finished, and the church accepts donations for…

spots.name: Talao Cave
spots.desc: 6 km from the town center, this is a series of twelve caves in the middle of the forest which are only accessible on foot along three mountain trails emanating from the main road.

spots.name: Balthazar's Tavern
spots.desc: Opened in May 2012 and run by a U.S.-trained chef, it serves Western and Filipino dishes. As it is on the top floor of the town's tallest building, it has a commanding view of the town and the sea. The restaurant also has an all-you-can-eat buffet on Sundays for 175.
spots.addr: 4/F DJ Plaza, Bonifacio cor. San Jose Sts., Barangay Uno

spots.name: Barbarossa Pub and Restaurant
spots.desc: Run by a German, it is the town's most famous restaurant, on the old site of the Gasan Public Library. The restaurant is as known for its repertoire of dishes as it is for its well-stocked bar.
spots.addr: Gomez cor. San Jose Sts., Barangay Dos

spots.name: Ristorante d'l Jose
spots.desc: Gasan's only Italian restaurant, it also serves Filipino and Chinese dishes.

spots.name: Tita Laida Food House
spots.desc: Gasan's best halo-halo is served here, as well as other Filipino dishes. The restaurant also serves pizza, and is particularly known for its pancit.

spots.name: Coral Garden
spots.desc: One of the best snorkeling and freediving spots in Puerto Galera, known for its vibrant coral formations and diverse marine life. The shallow waters are home to colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and occasional rays. The area is part of a marine sanctuary, ensuring excellent underwater visibility and a well-preserved ecosystem. Best explored with a guided boat tour.
spots.price: Entrance fee may apply for snorkeling tours

spots.name: Muelle Bay
spots.desc: A beautiful hidden hideout with a natural harbor where most ferries and boats dock. The bay is lined with shops, bars, and restaurants, making it a great spot to enjoy the scenic waterfront views while having lunch or a romantic dinner. At sunset, keep an eye on the sky—giant flying foxes (fruit bats) emerge from the nearby mangrove forest and take flight in search of food, creating a mesmerizing…

spots.name: Muelle Pier
spots.desc: A scenic harbor area with a small promenade lined with cafés and restaurants, where visitors can see flying foxes (giant fruit bats) emerge from the nearby mangrove forest as they begin their evening search for food.

spots.name: Tukuran Falls
spots.desc: Also known as Hidden Paradise, these multi-tiered waterfalls cascade into natural pools surrounded by lush jungle. Visitors can swim in the cool, clear water or relax in the peaceful environment. The journey includes a trek through rice fields, river crossings, and tropical forest, making it an adventure in itself.

spots.name: Tamaraw Falls
spots.desc: A scenic multi-tiered waterfall cascading into natural pools. The lower pool, located under a bridge, offers a refreshing swim in cool mountain water. A few meters upstream, visitors can enjoy stronger waterfalls surrounded by lush greenery. Nearby, a small beach area can be found along the road.

spots.name: Underwater Cave
spots.desc: A underwater cave, known for its rock formations and marine life. Visitors can explore hidden chambers and natural rock pools.

spots.name: Badladz Adventure Divers
spots.desc: A small dive shop known for its friendly instructors and personalized service. They offer PADI courses from beginner to Assistant Instructor level, as well as snorkeling trips, kayak rentals, and beach BBQ experiences.

spots.name: Extreme Sports Puerto Galera
spots.desc: An adventure sports park offering a variety of high-adrenaline activities, including ATV rides, paintball, archery, airsoft, and target shooting. A great spot for thrill-seekers looking for an alternative to beach activities in Puerto Galera.

spots.name: Land Bank ATM
spots.desc: A reliable ATM in Puerto Galera town, operated by Land Bank. Accepts most local and international cards. Withdrawal limits and fees may apply.
spots.price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

spots.name: PNB Savings Bank ATMs
spots.desc: Two ATMs available at this location, operated by PNB Savings Bank. Accepts both local and international cards. Recommended for reliable cash withdrawals, though machines may run out of cash during peak season.
spots.price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

spots.name: Candava Supermarket
spots.desc: A local supermarket offering a variety of groceries, fresh produce, household goods, and snacks.

spots.name: HL Supermarket Golden Conway Holding Inc
spots.desc: A local supermarket offering a variety of groceries, fresh produce, beverages, and household essentials.

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: A convenient 24/7 store offering snacks, drinks, basic groceries, and essential items. A reliable option for quick bites, cold beverages, and travel necessities.

spots.name: Puerto Galera Public Market
spots.desc: A bustling local market offering fresh seafood, fruits, vegetables, meats, and a variety of local goods.

spots.name: Mercury Drug
spots.desc: A well-known pharmacy chain in the Philippines, offering a wide range of prescription and over-the-counter medicines, personal care products, and medical supplies.

spots.name: Mr.DIY
spots.desc: A popular hardware and home improvement store offering a wide selection of household items, tools, stationery, toys, and personal care products at affordable prices.

spots.name: Cebuana Lhuillier
spots.desc: Offers currency exchange services. Also provides money remittances, pawnshop services, bill payments, and insurance products. More currency exchange points in Sabang.

spots.name: Robby's Cafeteria Steakhouse
spots.desc: A casual steakhouse and cafeteria-style restaurant known for its grilled steaks, sizzling plates, and hearty Filipino dishes. The restaurant also serves pizza and features a small shop selling a wide selection of cheeses, cold cuts, and other imported goods.

spots.name: Ambulong Island
spots.desc: Ambulong Island is a 30-km² island with fine beaches, cliffs and abundant coral formations. It is characterized by white sand beaches, cliffs along pillars jutting out of the water, and underwater caves. Coral gardens and tropical fish are abundant in several coves. An islet called Grace Island is located at a limestone cove at the southern tip of Ambulong. A fisherman's village is located at the…

spots.name: Ilin Island
spots.desc: Ilin Island has a village of shell divers, being abundant in shells and coral reefs. There are ancient burial caves of early Chinese traders, ethnic fishing villages, and numerous dive sites from which to view many tropical fishes. Lush foliage encircle the clear blue waters of the South China Sea. There are scuba diving facilities, a 6.8 CTM compressor, seaport facilities, diveboats, and PADI…

spots.name: White Island
spots.desc: White Island has a long powdery beach where buried turtle eggs are occasionally found. It has an almost mile-long beach with smooth and powdery white sand. The tranquil and peaceful island is an ideal place for swimming, scuba diving and fishing. Turtle eggs are occasionally found buried in the sand, and visitors are cautioned to keep them undisturbed.

spots.name: Aroma Beach
spots.desc: A favorite sport for local residents near San Jose Airport. The beach is named after aroma trees in the area.

spots.name: Second Landing Marker
spots.desc: World War II Marker commemorating the second landing of Gen. Douglas MacArthur in the Philippines in December 15, 1944 which led to the Liberation of Manila and mainland Luzon from occupying Japanese forces. The granite marker is complemented by three murals.

spots.name: San Jose Municipal Plaza
spots.desc: The town center and the destination, locals and tourist alike. Also has a park. Town festivities and events are also held in this area especially in the grandstand area. A handful of souvenirs and merchandise can be bought here especially during the annual town fiesta in May or Christmas season.

spots.name: Old Mangarin
spots.desc: Ruins of a Spanish coastal colonial fort. It contains four cannons which was used as defence against pirates during the colonial era. The area is connected by a wooden hanging bridge.

spots.name: Mt. Iglit National Park
spots.desc: Mounts Iglit-Baco National Park is located in an area shared by the municipalities of Sablayan, Calintaan, Rizal and San Jose. The latter is also the main gateway there. It is a sanctuary for the 'tamaraw' (Bubalus mindorensis), an endemic species of buffalo found only in Mindoro. It provides a nice eco-tourism, trekking, or mountaineering alternative to beach/dive resorts. However, a part of the…

spots.name: Kusina ni Lea
spots.desc: Casual dining outlet with a name which roughly translates to "Lea's Kitchen".

spots.name: Papa Bull’s Park
spots.desc: Papa Bulls in the swampy mangrove area within the municipal complex of the Municipality of Simunul. This crocodile is now a major tourist attraction where several people come to view it.

spots.name: Bagid Beach Resort
spots.desc: During the American period, a group of soldiers arrived here only to be bewildered by its natural beauty. Inspired by the tropical landscape, they composed a song titled “Tawi-Tawi Beach”. It’s a popular site for picnic goers with its crystal-clear waters.

spots.name: Enchanted River Hianatuan
spots.desc: A deep spring river of rather mesmerizing shades of blue and home to numerous species of fish, popularized in a poem called Rio Encantado. Daily feeding by conservationists in the afternoon but swimming disallowed as of 2017.

spots.name: Sohoton Cove
spots.desc: Sohoton Lagoon and Caves is a more than 600 hectare Eco-reserve situated in the isolated south of Bocas Grande island. Accessible only on lower tides, this pristine sanctuary offers a grand experience. The trip is conducted by boat and is required most of the day.

spots.name: Hoyohoy Highland Stone Chapel Adventure Park
spots.desc: Nature park with a view deck providing views of the city and Panguil Bay. Also has a stone chapel and a zipline (claimed to be the longest in Asia)

spots.name: Isulan Central Plaza
spots.desc: Little two-storey department store and supermarket with a Mang Inasal and Landbank ATM outside.

spots.name: Durian Garden
spots.desc: A durian farm that also consists of a recreational center and restaurant. It also sells durian ice cream, pies and other sweets.

spots.name: Polomolok Town Plaza
spots.desc: A plaza beside the town hall that serves as a central gathering point for the community. Various activities, such as sports, can be done here.

spots.name: Megan Buko Halo
spots.desc: Specializes in buko halo, meaning halo-halo with coconut as its base.

spots.name: Baras Bird Sanctuary
spots.desc: you can see 7 species of migratory birds, without binoculars. There are 2 pathways to choose from. The easiest and shortest trail can be explored within 15 minutes while the full trail is approximately 30 minutes covering about 2.5 hectares.

spots.name: Tacurong Public Market
spots.desc: This is where you can buy local delicacies, supplies, fresh vegetables and fruits, meat and also purchase local handicrafts and pasalubong like Talakudong hats, Arnis sticks, malongs.

spots.name: Liwasan ng Dapitan
spots.desc: During his exile, Jose Rizal, with the assistance of the Spaniards, beautified this simple town square to make this like those typical of European cities

spots.name: José Rizal Memorial Protected Landscape
spots.desc: The preserved estate of Jose Rizal during his exile in the then quiet town.

spots.name: Punto del Desembarco de Rizal
spots.desc: Commemorating the arrival of José Rizal on his 1892 exile to Dapitan.

spots.name: Pinoy's Chicken Inato
spots.desc: Sells "Fried Chicken Take-Out Treat" at ₱199. Or try its Chicken Inasal.

spots.name: Village Cafe
spots.desc: Juices, coffee, snacks, Filipino and Western-style dishes. Free WiFi. Charming little cafe serving good food.

spots.name: Calauit Game Preserve and Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.desc: This reserve created by Presidential decree in 1976 houses various African species (giraffes included...) wandering in the wild.

spots.name: Fishing
spots.desc: Fishing is very good. You can find lots of fish at there, for example tuna. Local men always go fishing there. You can buy simple equipment to fish there, where it is very cheap.

spots.name: Ocam Ocam Beach
spots.desc: A beautiful beach with a little village and beach cottages to rent.

spots.name: Siete Pecadoes aka Seven Islands
spots.desc: Among the best and easiest to access sites to snorkel in Coron. It is 3.5 km east of Coron town, and 200 m from the closest beach. It is easily accessible by snorkelling straight from the beach as the reef starts right in front of it. Experience swimming in an aquarium, beautiful corals and a great variety of fishes. There is a caretaker who will collect 100 from tourists, but mostly enforced…

spots.name: Smiths Island
spots.desc: A small island with white sand beach. A caretaker family stays there during the day, and sells snacks and drinks. Thare are stunning views of white sands and blue seas. The fee to spend some time here is 100 per head. You can reach it while island-hopping on a bangka. It takes 20 minutes sailing from Kayangan lake to reach here.

spots.name: Cheron Island
spots.desc: Directly opposite Malcapuya Island. It has a plat of white sand, outgoing into the sea. Fee — 500 for 4 persons.

spots.name: Coron Divers
spots.desc: The only dive center owned by a Filipino. Arni is the big boss. Everything makes you feel in a Filipino family (even more if you stay at Chinette's Coron Reef Pension, 10 m away in front of Coron Divers) Youl find it right beside the Jollybee. It's the only dive outfit in town run by Filipinos and also the cheapest.(4500PHP perDay/ 3dives 2026)

spots.name: Discovery Divers
spots.desc: Tucked away on 'Discovery Island' a 10-minute boat ride from the pier. Talk to Vivian in Coron town at the Discovery Bar or get to the pier around 8AM to catch the boat out. Gunter is a great guy with a lot of experience in the area.

spots.name: Reggae Dive Center
spots.desc: Reggae is professionally run by a friendly and very competent German instructor. Rocksteady is almost a kilometer from the town center, very near the hospital Not a good choice if you want to dive the IRAKO.(6000PHP per Day /3Dives 2026)

spots.name: Neptune Dive Center
spots.desc: Neptune Dive Center is one of the newer dive shops in Coron, but is owned and operated by a team that has been living and diving there for years. Emphasis is on small groups and personal service. Neptune Dive Center is the only purpose built dive shop in Coron. Prices are mid-range compared to the other dive shops in the area.

spots.name: SeaDive
spots.desc: They have the only recompression chamber in all of Palawan onsite. The biggest dive shop in town, with divemasters who claim to have over 10,000 dives on the Coron wrecks. Priced higher than the other dive shops. Known for crowded boats and high divemaster to diver ratios.

spots.name: Chindonan Island Resort & Divecenter
spots.desc: In Coron Bay, it is known for its great location towards all shipwrecks. It takes 10-20 min to get to your favorite shipwreck. A dive team there is known for its great service.

spots.name: Coron Freediving
spots.desc: Longest-established freediving center in Palawan with the best in freediving standards from Apnea Total, PADI, and Molchanovs, catering to all levels from beginner to advanced.

spots.name: Kingfisher Park
spots.desc: Offering guided mangrove kayak tours (500), trekking Mt Lunes Santo and bamboo cooked lunch (500), and Starry Starry Night mangrove firefly/plankton cruises (200). visit the website for tour booking details.

spots.name: Mermaid-Club
spots.desc: You can learn mermaid swimming and diving with the Mermaid-Club. Find their office right within the freediving school on Real Street.

spots.name: La Sirenetta
spots.desc: Beautiful waterfront restaurant on stilts offering international food with entrees ranging from 200-400. Recognizable on the water as sculpted mermaids adorn the posts supporting the roof of the open air dining area. (Accessible through alleyway beside Coron Divers and Coron Reef Pension House and also by boat.)

spots.name: Bistro Coron
spots.desc: Owned by Bruno (who can be seen in the kitchen wearing nothing but a towel and a scowl in the mornings) it is home to French food at prices well above the local average. Entrees go from 155-270 for the most part, mains are more but crab and lobster meals are available for even more. Get the onion soup, the apple pie, the coq au vin, the basquaise, the salade niçoise, the cordon bleu. San Miguel…

spots.name: Trining Bacsa
spots.desc: Locally owned and operated restaurant located around the corner from Coron Market. Offers authentic Filipino cuisine.

spots.name: KokosNuss Resort
spots.desc: has a good kitchen. They have a Palawan style all you can eat BBQ deal. 6 or more people required at 475 each. They also have a Christmas feast on Dec 24 which is the BBQ and definitely worth going to if you are around (tell them in advance if you are going). San Miguel is 32. Breakfasts are good as well.

spots.name: SeaDive Resort
spots.desc: Continental variety of food. Situated Over the water, seafront view. Offers inexpensive seafood and a nightly special. Entrees from 150-400.

spots.name: WG Restaurant
