spots.desc: The owner William gives free tourist advice with your meal, and is extremely helpful and friendly. You'll get local prices if he is helping you. He also has accommodation.

spots.name: Calamian Planet Online
spots.desc: An Internet cafe where you may check your mail and print document, pictures & other.

spots.name: M/Bca Lady Amor - Port Barton Island Hopping Tour
spots.desc: Lady Amor is a local boat company offering island-hopping tours and boat transfers. The company operates a fleet of traditional wooden bancas accommodating different group sizes.

spots.name: Jaunt Palawan
spots.desc: Jarjhon Salgarino is a freelance tour guide and tour coordinator based in Palawan.

spots.name: Anda Falls
spots.desc: If you're tired of salt water stinging your eyes, there is a large and deep concrete cistern to swim in at the base of the falls.

spots.name: Anda water caves
spots.desc: There are many underground rivers with transparent water coming from the mountains to the sea.

spots.name: Food center
spots.desc: Has 8 stalls offering cheap Filipino food, pizza & pasta in a long, open-air, covered area. Dawn to dusk.

spots.name: On The Road Resto & Bar
spots.desc: On the Road is a place where local people and foreigners can learn about all cultures. BBQ, fresh beer, cocktail, many kind of music, Wi-Fi, Apple TV.

spots.name: Old Castle
spots.desc: Looks like a European castle, except that it is on a beach with palm trees. Good food, mostly European menu.

spots.name: Baclayon Church and Museum
spots.desc: Baclayon is known for its historic Catholic Church, an important part of Boholano and national heritage, being declared in 1995 as a National Historic Treasure. This massive ancient edifice still retains its centuries old architectural design and is considered the best preserved of its kind in the region. The relics of antiquity found in the church, and museum, which date back to the early 16th…

spots.name: Historic Marketplace
spots.desc: Another Spanish-era building in the town ís the spacious public market with giant stone columns supporting the roof. The products of local industries like the sarok, winnowing baskets, fans, shopping bags, mats and the like are sold at the market day every Wednesday. Fruits, vegetables, pigs, chickens, dried fish, and other products from people in the hinterlands are also sold to serve the needs…

spots.name: Ancestral Houses
spots.desc: Spared through community advocacy from a provincial road-widening project’s plan for their demolition, the Spanish colonial ancestral houses that line the main road of Balcayon have instead been preserved and stand as compellingly as ever. There are over 67 ancestral houses in the municipality, which are within easy walking distance from Baclayon Church. The houses show Spanish-Filipino wooden…

spots.name: Pamilacan Island
spots.desc: part of the Municipality of Baclayon, is a small island 14 km, or a 1-hour pump-boat ride, from the mainland. There are only around 235 families living on the island, whose main livelihoods now concentrate on dolphin and whale watching tours and subsistence fishing, but in the past have also included whale, dolphin and manta ray hunting. Officially Pamilacan means “resting place of the mantas’…

spots.name: Dolphin and Whale Watching Tours
spots.desc: The waters of Baclayon are renowned throughout the Philippines as being the premier site for Dolphin and Whale Watching Tours. The Whale species to be found are the Short-finned Pilot Whale, Melon-headed Whale and Pygmy Killer Whale, while the Dolphin species include the Rissoís, Spinner, Bottlenose and Spotted Dolphins. As of February 2011, many Whale Sharks have also been spotted off the cost…

spots.name: Buggy Rides
spots.desc: Now run through Peacock Garden Resort, an exhilarating buggy ride through the rural barangays (villages) of Baclayon is available. If merely speed and tight turns aren’t your things then the tour can also be ideal for naturists, with flora and fauna, and bird watching information stops included along the way. The tour is designed to be beneficial for the remote barangays, with a portion of the…

spots.name: Scuba diving
spots.desc: Baclayon offers an extremely rich and biodiverse marine system perfect for Scuba diving. An especially popular dive site off Pamilacan Island is ‘Dakit-Dakit’, where the once damaged coral reefs from dynamite-fishing are on the repair with many varieties of coral heads, soft corals and coral strings growing. The sloping reef dive also provides encounters with huge schools of large Jackfish…

spots.name: Mountain biking
spots.desc: Many of Baclayon’s off-road trails have been developed for mountain biking, and the municipality is fast becoming a hub for the sport in Bohol. The mountain biking trails include easy and moderate cross-country rides, using barangay roads and single track, carabao trails. Baclayon also has long off-road trails connect different municipalities, such as Loboc, Albur, Loay, Corella, Sikatuna and…

spots.name: Heritage Walk
spots.desc: Baclayon Ancestral Homes Association (BAHANDI) is a neighborhood organization set up to promote and preserve not only the Baclayon ancestral houses, but also the heritage of the community. BAHANDI offer a Heritage Walk, touring the historic church, elementary school, ancestral houses, and visit a demonstration of Broas making; a Baclayon delicacy. The tour also includes a beautiful table set-up…

spots.name: Market Day Wednesdays
spots.desc: Poblacion - Set in the historic, Spanish-era Baclayon marketplace, the Wednesday Market Days provide a great opportunity to see and taste Baclayon culture up close. Native handicrafts are available, along with delicious, locally produced delicacies and sweets such as Broas (ladyfingers), nut bars, pastels, tortas, rice cake and suman. An impressive variety of fruit, vegetable and dried fish are…

spots.name: Aproniana Souvenir Shop
spots.desc: Self proclaimed “Bohol’s ultimate souvenir destination”, Aproniana sells a wide range of souvenirs covering all of Bohol’s major tourist attractions at more affordable prices than sold near at the destinations themselves. The air-conditioned store covers 100 m² over 2 levels, but can still get somewhat overcrowded if multiple tourist buses are passing through at the same time.

spots.name: 6 to 7
spots.desc: A small restaurant along the main highway in Poblacion underneath an ancestral house.

spots.name: Boo Boo's Pride
spots.desc: A large floating restaurant beside the wharf, which has been converted into a Karaoke Bar. This is a favorite amongst the locals of Baclayon who can be found singing 7 nights a week until the small hours of the morning. Meals are also available on board.

spots.name: Hilltop 360 View Park
spots.desc: This is a private complex to enjoy the view over Chocolate Hills. The starting path to the complex is unpaved and dubious. Turn in when you see the signage. The road gets better afterwards. There are two viewpoints, plus you can do horse riding and pond fishing here.
spots.addr: Central Nautical Highway, between Sagbayan Peak Park and Carmen town

spots.name: Sagbayan Peak Park
spots.desc: includes amusement park and tarsier sanctuary (despite the name, it is a small cage where the tarsiers are harassed to be awake in the day, you shouldn't support this).

spots.name: Loboc River Cruise
spots.desc: A river cruise lasts about 90 minutes. In addition to a buffet lunch, the cruise will dock alongside stations on the river that feature ethnic dance and music performances. On-board, a prevalent scam features a photographer offering "free photographs." However, despite using simple point-and-shoot or outdated DSLR cameras, the act of taking the photo is the only free aspect; the emailed JPEG…
spots.price: 850 with buffet lunch. 100 for soft drinks. Tipping is expected for the dancers.

spots.name: Hinagdanan cave
spots.desc: There is a tiny lagoon inside a coral cave. Enjoy a dip in a fresh water. The cave is completely dark, the guides have a flashlight. The admission is around 20. To get here, you can take a bus or mini van towards Panglao island from Tagbilaran. If you tell them you are going to Hinagdanan cave, they will know what intersection to drop you off at.

spots.name: Bohol Bee Farm
spots.desc: They also run a few cafes and restaurants in Tagbilaran and Alona beach. Also provides accommodation from ₱2,000.

spots.name: Momo Beach
spots.desc: Small quiet beach on the north west of the island. Coral reef is situated only a couple of hundred meters off shore, it's a good location for snorkelling straight from the beach.

spots.name: Bear and Rabbit Food Haus and Bar
spots.desc: The only bar and nightclub in Daanbantayan. Serves excellent food and provides karaoke Sunday through Thursday and a disco on Friday and Saturday evenings. Indoor dining, fully air-conditioned.

spots.name: Stone Ark
spots.desc: Large rock on the Cotcot - Mulao river. A hiking destination

spots.name: Tayud Cockpit Arena
spots.desc: Cock fighting is quite popular in the Philippines and in neighboring Indonesia, and it is common for large sums to be wagered. Most visitors find it far too cruel to be an enjoyable thing to watch.

spots.name: MoodNight Bar
spots.desc: Restaurant and dance bar with live music, customers mostly young Filipinos.

spots.name: Pasilong Park
spots.desc: A beautiful fountain rests in the middle of the park where many locals take pictures especially at dusk.

spots.name: Sardine Run
spots.desc: The famous school of a million plus sardines that once called Pescador Island home have now moved even closer to shore. In fact the sardines congregate right at the reef drop-off on Panagsama beach. Shore diving is a breeze here and most dive operators have their shops abutting the shoreline. If you swim 20-30 m from shore, the reef drops off dramatically, as deep as 70 m in some places and it is…

spots.name: Orchid Gallery
spots.desc: It's not so much a gallery, but an orchid plant school that has a pool and nice shaded areas and some specimens of the local wildlife. You can buy orchids and other plants.
spots.price: There is a small entrance fee

spots.name: Lambug Beach
spots.desc: Take a tricycle about 20 km south towards Badian to find Lambug, a beach that to a greater extent than Basdako reminds you of a deserted island. Especially during the weeks, you can sometimes find yourself completely alone on the beach. Should you like to work on your swing, there is also an 18-hole golf course nearby.

spots.name: White Beach
spots.desc: About 7 km north of Panagsama you'll find White Beach or Basdako, meaning 'Big Sand', a nice white sandy beach lined with a beautiful coral reef about 30 m out. Pack your mask and snorkel. White Beach is a popular spot to visit, especially during the weekend, so if you're looking for more quiet beach life go during the week or make your way a bit further north up the beach. There are a couple of…

spots.name: M’Ocean Freediving
spots.desc: This school has freediving courses for PADI or AIDA certification. It is managed by the current Philippine women's record holder Wei Zosa.

spots.name: Gaisano Grand Mall
spots.desc: Has a supermarket and large department store, McDonald's, PNB Bank with a 24-hour Visa card Metro Bank ATM.

spots.name: Gaisano Town Center Mall
spots.desc: A large department store and supermarket with places to eat and a Landbank ATM.

spots.name: Food Stop
spots.desc: Can be a bit hard to find, but well worth the effort, just next to the road between Moalboal and Panagsama. It doesn't look like much from the outside, but they serve generous portions delicious Filipino and Asian dishes for 150 each.

spots.name: B-Side Cafe
spots.desc: A deli and restaurant designed to cater to the needs of the locals and foreign visitors. Offers international and local food and the deli has a wide array of imported groceries, cold cuts, sausages and wines. Cheaper than most places in Panagsama.

spots.name: Julies Bake Shop
spots.desc: Nice bread, coffee and drinks. Part of a national chain with two locations in Moaboal, one in the public market and the other north of town along the highway.

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: Full A/C. It sells beers, rice meals, hotdogs, coffee, ice cream, ice. Has cellphone load.

spots.name: Island Wok
spots.desc: Serves a fusion of Asian dishes such as Korean spicy noodles, Japanese bento meals, Chinese dumplings, cheese sticks and vegetarian to name a few choices. Local and imported beers are also part of the choices as well. The food here is not salty not oily that taste excellent. They also have free wifi which is amazingly fast. Love the service and the nice garden terrain.

spots.name: Venz Kitchen
spots.desc: A tourist favourite with friendly staff serving up a range of traditional dishes, local favourites and more. It's incredibly popular, so get there early or be prepared to queue.

spots.name: Maya's Mexican
spots.desc: In the main part of Panagsama Beach and does excellent Mexican food - a nice change. They do superb fresh shakes (mango) and have a great BBQ.

spots.name: Chili bar
spots.desc: One of the most popular bars in town. Generally good food, and their chili is excellent. Has the best pizza in Moalboal according to a sign outside (many are inclined to agree). Has pool tables. Sells souvenir T-shirts with their emblem, a grinning chili pepper clutching a beer; these are quite nice, if pricey by local standards at around P300.

spots.name: 7 Sins Bar
spots.desc: Across the street from Chili Bar, also with a pool table and lots of seating.

spots.name: Arista Restaurant
spots.desc: Sits right on the waterfront. They have a decently priced Filipino/German menu, and great service to go with the good food.

spots.name: The Three Bears
spots.desc: Offering nice burger at a decent taste and price compared to the other eateries in the area. Desserts are outstanding. The place is decorated in an amusing bear-themed style.

spots.name: Tumalog falls
spots.desc: A cascading waterfall. Ask someone in the village to take you there, cost for a ride about 120.

spots.name: Sumilon Island
spots.desc: Can be visited on organised boat trip which starts regularly at the whale shark-watching point.

spots.name: Whale shark watching
spots.desc: Prices include gear, instructor and a boat. Session time is limited to 30 minutes.
spots.price: 1500 to dive, 1000 for a snorkel and swim, and 500 to stay on the boat

spots.name: Lapyahan sa San Remigio and San Remigio Cultural Center
spots.desc: The main beach of the town featuring white sands and a vast stretch of sea grass. Public tables and gazebos are available for reservations (fee) or on a first-come, first-served basis. The adjacent San Remigio Cultural Center provides a venue for gatherings and free public Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Balay Ni Tatay Farm Resort
spots.desc: a farm resort located in North part of tacloban, Offer a native and organic food.

spots.name: Mahagnao Volcano National Park
spots.desc: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) classifies Mahagnao as Inactive volcano. Although the volcano has been inactive, it is classified as potentially active due to the active thermal features of the mountain.

spots.name: Palo Public Market
spots.desc: The municipality's central market, destroyed during the onslaught of Typhoon Haiyan, but was rebuilt.

spots.name: Cainting Cave and Falls
spots.desc: This site, which forms part of the lush Sogod Rainforest served as meeting point of 3 rivers which offers a scenic junction of a natural pool. The presence of leeches locally known as “limatok” thrive on its waters. The area can be reached after a 5-km walk from the road in barangay Pancho Villa to the barrio of San Francisco Mabuhay. Pancho Villa is a 20-minute habal-habal ride from Doctor…

spots.name: Magsuhot Park
spots.desc: The 500-hectare forested Magsuhot National Park is 3 km from barangay Mahayahay. It has four 20-meter high waterfalls falling into a common basin.

spots.name: Salas Park
spots.desc: Best to see during the night, where it overlooks Bacolod. The trip to the park is what locals call, little Baguio with all the zig-zag and steep roads. You would also be surrounded with old pines, mahogany and the cool air. Best for hikers too. A local guide is available to bring you to various springs and falls. Come to discover.

spots.name: Himogaan River
spots.desc: Residents call that place as the Himoga-an River Overflow that is located at Barangay Puey, Sagay City, Negros Occidental. The Himoga-an River is the longest river of Sagay City. It was wide and clean so you would not wonder why most people living near that area usually take a bath and wash their clothes there.

spots.name: Inangtan Hanging Bridge
spots.desc: "Inangtan" in local dialect means "to connect". The Inangtan Bridge connects the Barangay Maquiling proper from its rural half that is separated by Himoga-an River.

spots.name: Peopes Park
spots.desc: A nice park to walk around has a board walk over looking the sea.

spots.name: Gaisano Mall
spots.desc: Major chain with malls in many cities. Has a Gaisano supermarket

spots.name: Mojon Church
spots.desc: Just inside the southern boundary of Bais with Tanjay, this church is often overlooked because drivers' attentions are concentrated on the blind curve in the road. The inside, with its gracefully curving screens and woodwork and finely carved mahogany altar pieces, is prettier than the outside. Next door are some fine, large colonial houses sheltering beneath a canopy of mature trees with…

spots.name: Bank of the Philippine Islands
spots.desc: Two external ATMs accept Visa, UnionPay, JCB, Plusnet, Cirrus, Maestro and MasterCards 24/7, charging a fee of 200 for each withdrawal. Users of Australian debit cards might want to try the "Savings" option if "Current" does not work. Maximum withdrawal in any one transaction is 20000.

spots.name: Amorganda Supermarket
spots.desc: A small, usually crowded shop with weak air-conditioning and poorly treated staff that accepts Visa and MasterCard.

spots.name: Dive Guide Dauin
spots.desc: Dive Guide for diving Dumaguete, Dauin, Siquijor and Apo-Island​, PADI and SDI Instructor, Photo and Video Assistance

spots.name: Aquarius Restaurant Dauin
spots.desc: Thai and European cuisine. 1000 sqm. garden, parking spaces, al fresco dining.

spots.name: Crystal Caves
spots.desc: Nice gardens with plenty of shade trees have three pavilions where you can leave your bags and gear and use clean toilets. The cave is about 150m walk over rough karst and through sheltering trees. Since the cave atmosphere has pretty well 100% humidity you might want to pause for a few moments to cool off before you enter. There is an iron walkway at relatively high level of about 140m from the…
spots.price: 215 includes a hard hat and the services of a guide

spots.name: Kabugan Cave
spots.desc: Large colonies of three different species of bat and an opening that allows a shaft of sunlight to penetrate.

spots.name: Odloman
spots.desc: At a length of some 8,870m, this cave system is the second longest in the Philippines after St Paul's Underground River in Palawan's National Park. It's not a cave for casual visitors since it can only be accessed by swimming 20m across an underground torrent of by rappelling down from a squeeze in the roof. Seasoned spelunkers will be rewarded with large galleries, narrow corridors, and some…

spots.name: Andrew's Diner
spots.desc: Cafeteria style with outside tables set in a tranquil garden with artificial waterfall.

spots.name: Tillys Sail Tour
spots.desc: A sailing family residing in Tambobo Bay, offers sailing tours as well as boat repair for world cruisers.

spots.name: Malatapay Market
spots.desc: The farmer’s market is equally welcoming to townspeople, shoppers, tourists, and visitors. Specialties include: Handcrafted goods, woven bags and purses, woven floor/beach mats, tools, fruits & vegetables, fish (fresh & dried), Filipino "Good Will" clothing, bamboo furniture, housewares, prepared food, and restaurants with seafood, lechon baboy, cold beer and soft drinks. As you walk past the…

spots.name: Miagao Church
spots.desc: The Miag-ao Church is one of the Philippines' architectural and religious gems and one of the Philippines' four world heritage listed baroque churches. A couple of minutes further is the University of the Philippines campus.

spots.name: Old Passi Municipal Hall
spots.desc: A town hall built in 1930, and the few buildings that survived the razing of Passi by the Japanese.

spots.name: Plaza Paloma
spots.desc: This Spanish-era town square has a pineapple sculpture, its main attraction.

spots.name: St. William Parish Church and Convent
spots.desc: A Spanish-era church with a façade that resembles more of a fortress, with large buttresses on the front and back. It was first built in 1612, to replace smaller churches destroyed by an earthquake. The architecture reflects the church's secondary purpose as a Spanish military outpost.

spots.name: Immaculate Conception Church
spots.desc: The most beautiful church in the island of Samar. Built solely by manual labor, this edifice of adobe stone is indeed a cultural heritage. Inside, one can find uniquely carved icons as a Spanish Baroque altar. This 400+-year-old Catholic church, inspired by the Spanish colonizers that came to the Philippines after the Magellan expedition, also features chiseled doorways and has a classical…

spots.name: Guiuan Church Tower
spots.desc: A monumental to native labor, it is the tallest existing tower in the municipality. Two thirds of its height was said to have been destroyed by earthquakes many years ago. The imposing belfry is a comforting sight for an exhausted overland travellers that come from various points of the country via Borongan, the provincial capital of Eastern Samar.

spots.name: Pearl Island
spots.desc: This is a quaint coral islet developed by BFAR. It is devoted to experimental round and blister pearl culture and giant clams project and is ideal for scuba diving and underwater sports.

spots.name: PAGASA Radar Station
spots.desc: A sophisticated weather forecasting instrument. One of the PAGASA stations in the country. Located on top of a hill, and offers a panoramic view of the town, the Leyte Gulf and the vast Pacific Ocean.

spots.name: 3149 US Naval Base
spots.desc: On December 1, 1944, a fleet of LCT's Liberty Ships and barges poured into the Guiuan Bay to unload machines that was to transform Guiuan into one of the biggest naval bases in the Far East at the time.

spots.name: Pray at the Shrine of St. Anthony of Padua
spots.desc: This picturesque barrio is famous for its Shrine of St. Anthony of Padua whose miraculous attributes devotees and visitors from afar and wide.

spots.name: Surf
spots.desc: Declared as the surfing capital of the Visayas in 2001, by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. This is an ideal place for surfing during the months of September to December due to the presence of big waves by the northeast trade winds.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Plaza
spots.desc: An area of natural park and that has trails for walking, biking and other activities. Owned and maintained by the local government.

spots.name: Sunkai Cafe & Resort
spots.desc: This beachside hangout features beautiful cottage designs, a glass-walled swimming pool, and spectacular sunset views. It has quickly become a popular spot for weekend getaways, family reunions, and vibrant events like pool parties.

spots.name: Nijaga Park
spots.desc: The large central plaza named after the revolutionary Benedicto Nijaga. The park also has an artificial replica of Bangon-Bugtong Falls.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Plaza
spots.desc: A plaza with an image of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, and a fountain.

spots.name: Bagacay Beach
spots.desc: An uncrowded pearl white strip of coastline, with coconut trees, offering a scenic view of islands and towns.

spots.name: Binaliw Isle
spots.desc: A potential deep diving spot, about 40-50 m from the seafloor and measuring less than a hectare in area. The islet is surrounded with aquifers equally and uniformly spread at the peripheral limits of the islet with white sand and pebbles. Beneath the deep waters are corals of multifarious varieties, rare white pebbles spread over the floor, 20 types of shells, and ornamental types of aquamarine…

spots.name: Malajog Beach
spots.desc: Grayish sand, blue waters, swaying palm trees, towering rocks and three balconied cottages give this spot a South Sea island appeal. Magnificent view of sunset behind nearby islands. This beach is famous as it is frequently visited by foreign diplomats and VIPs, and several films are shot here.

spots.name: Malajog Ridge Nature Park
spots.desc: The mountain ridge forming this park is the source of the stones used to build the Calbayog Cathedral. The park's major attraction is the Calbayog Zipline (Calbayog City Zip), which goes down from the mountains facing Malajog Beach down into an island, and after that, you get on a boat back to the mainland on Malajog Beach.

spots.name: Mapaso Spring
spots.desc: "Mapaso" literally means hot in Waray. Fresh crustaceans (pokot) abound. They are naturally pinkish resembling scalded shrimps due to the high temperature.

spots.name: Mawacat Slide
spots.desc: It is a natural spoon-like formation which inclines by about 45 degrees and stretches 50 meters long. Water flows along this giant cistern and from the top you can slide through the mossy lane to the cool inviting pool below.

spots.name: Naga Beach
spots.desc: Cottages line its grayish sandy shore. Its cool fresh water and scenic view of Samar Island attracts picnickers and beachcombers.

spots.name: Danao Cave
spots.desc: Made up of seven chambers inhabited by various species of snakes and bats, as evidenced by deposits of guano. The cave serves as an initiating place for those who want to acquire a talisman.

spots.name: Guinogo-an Cave
spots.desc: Its large entrance leads to a natural tunnel with an uneven ceiling, some portions of which touching your head making for an eerie trip through the dark, cool interior.

spots.name: Tinagoan Cave
spots.desc: Tinago-an means hiding place in Waray. Its naturally dark tunnels offers excitement and thrill to adventurers.

spots.name: Bangon-Bugtong Falls
spots.desc: The most majestic of Calbayog's waterfalls. As you ascend the stream, you will see a circular pond about 30 m in diameter, wide enough for swimming and deep enough for dinging. The cascading water comes from streams flowing endlessly, resulting from pressure on its disgorge, which becomes larger as the day passes

spots.name: Lologayan Falls
spots.desc: It is separated from the mainland by the Silangan Channel. A series of towering altars of rugged stones where between its depressions flow ribbon-like cool water that appears to cleanse the hair of a legendary lady. A source of drinking water for local folks.

spots.name: Pan-as Falls
spots.desc: These falls are the primary source of water for Calbayog's residents. At places where the cataract is so high, the water falling into the pool below becomes a mere mist.

spots.name: Tabokno Falls
spots.desc: A beautiful and scenic waterfall, and a favorite picnic site for Calbayog residents

spots.name: Ton-ok Falls
spots.desc: A scenic waterfall hidden in lush tropical vegetation. Its waters are also used by a nearby hydroelectric dam.

spots.name: Lulugayan Falls and Rapids
spots.desc: Located on the Calbiga River (whose source is Lake Kalidongan); of hundreds of falls, the Lulugayan Falls are the most majestic. It is sometimes called Mini Niagara by visitors.

spots.desc: Oldest sign going to proper town of Taal.

spots.desc: Has fast food chains and a Walter Mart supermarket.

spots.name: World Peace Bell
spots.desc: The World Peace Bell, housed in a gazebo, is a donation by the World Peace Bell Association, a Japanese organization promoting awareness on the world peace movement. It was inaugurated in 1994. The World Peace Bell grounds also has other features such as the Peace Wall, a mural and flag poles with names countries at its base (although flags are no longer hoisted). The grounds is also the location…

spots.name: Peace Monument
spots.desc: A marker erected to mark Quezon City as a Rotary Peace Community as part of the "Community Peace Cities/Towns" concept conceived by the Rotary Club of Wagga Wagga, Australia.

spots.name: Quezon City Experience
spots.desc: Focuses on the history of Quezon City. The interactive museum is divided into multiple pod buildings which were designed to be green building compliant.

spots.name: Quezon Heritage House
spots.desc: A historic house museum which used to be the house of the family of President Manuel L. Quezon and was at 45 Gilmore Street in New Manila, Quezon City. The museum focuses on the personal life of Quezon in contrast to the Museo ni Manuel L. Quezon which focuses on Quezon's political career.

spots.name: Fern Garden
spots.desc: A garden dedicated to ferns, however as of 2016, only a few ferns are present at the garden. Nevertheless, the garden provides a secluded place for park visitors that prefers a quieter place.

spots.name: St. John the Baptist Church
spots.desc: Built between 1830 and 1883 using coral blocks and mortar, this landmark is the oldest standing stone church in Catanduanes and a key historical site in the province.

spots.name: Batalay Shrine
spots.desc: A historic pilgrimage site marking the spot where the first Christian cross was planted in Catanduanes. It honors Father Diego de Herrera, the first apostle of the province, who was shipwrecked and buried here in 1576.

spots.name: Mary's Woods
spots.desc: A peaceful outdoor sanctuary and pilgrimage site featuring a tree-lined walking path, outdoor Stations of the Cross, and a Marian grotto set amidst lush forest surroundings.

spots.name: Bato Bridge
spots.desc: A prominent local landmark spanning the wide Bato River, connecting the town center to outer barangays and providing scenic views of the riverbank, surrounding hills, and historic Bato Church.

spots.name: Bato River Park
spots.desc: A scenic riverside park and promenade offering relaxed views of the wide Bato River, local fishing boats, surrounding green hills, and nearby Bato Bridge.

spots.name: Bato Boulevard
spots.desc: A scenic coastal and riverside boardwalk along the Bato River, popular among locals and visitors for relaxing strolls, sunset views, and local street food stalls.

spots.name: Bato Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of local government for the municipality of Bato, situated right in the town near major historical and riverfront landmarks.

spots.name: Maribina Falls
spots.desc: The most popular and accessible multi-tiered waterfall in Catanduanes, featuring cool freshwater swimming pools, shaded picnic huts, and lush tropical surroundings.

spots.name: Balongbong Falls
spots.desc: A scenic and lesser-visited waterfall set amidst lush countryside, offering cool freshwater pools and natural river landscapes ideal for swimming and quiet nature breaks.

spots.name: Carorian Wonders & Poseidon Rock
spots.desc: A coastal island-hopping destination featuring towering white rock formations (Poseidon Rock), twin natural turquoise saltwater swimming pools, hidden lagoons, and dramatic ocean cliffside landscapes.
spots.hours: Open daily (best visited during morning calm seas)

spots.name: Bote Lighthouse
spots.desc: Local tour guide is mandatory. Perched on a high hill overlooking the Pacific Ocean, this historical lighthouse requires a short, continuous hike to reach, rewarding visitors with panoramic 360-degree views of Sakahon Beach, surrounding green hills, and the ocean coastline.

spots.name: Sakahon Beach
spots.desc: A peaceful, secluded cove featuring clear blue waters, fine white sand, and scenic coastal rock formations, popular for relaxing away from crowds and serving as the trail head for Bote Lighthouse.

spots.name: Mt. Lantad
spots.desc: A prominent high peak in Bato offering scenic mountain views, rich local flora, and trekking routes suitable for outdoor enthusiasts and hikers looking to explore the municipality's interior highlands.

spots.name: Batalay Mangrove Eco-Park
spots.desc: A scenic coastal mangrove sanctuary featuring elevated wooden boardwalks through dense mangrove forests, ideal for nature walks, birdwatching, and learning about local marine ecosystem conservation.

spots.name: Binondo Church
spots.desc: built in 1596, it is one of the oldest places of Christian Worship. The Church is home to the Our Lady of China and in-front of the church, Plaza San Lorenzo Ruiz lies; it is named after a Filipino-Chinese saint, St. Lorenzo Ruiz. Next to the side entrance is the Santo Cristo de Longos, an image of the Crucified Christ, known to be found by one deaf and mute Chinese in an old well in the barrio…

spots.name: Kuang Kong
spots.desc: Buddhist temple open to the public and is worth visiting as it shows the roots of the Chinese-Filipino, you can burn incense sticks and utter your prayers. There is also these red wooden half moons you can use to have your fortunes told. Couch your questions in such a way that they're answerable by "YES" or "NO". Swirl a pair of these wooden half disks over your incense sticks so they catch the…

spots.name: Seng Guan Temple
spots.desc: Another Chinese temple worth seeing, located along Narra Street, it is usually jam-packed with people burning incense and offering food and fruits to Buddha during celebrations of the lunar calendar.

spots.name: Arranque Market
spots.desc: Visit the wet market of Arranque Market, here fresh seafood and exotic food such as snakes, pigeons, rabbits, frogs etc. is found, it is often seen crowded like most wet markets are.

spots.name: Carvajal Street
spots.desc: Along Caravajal Street vendors selling fruits and Chinese delicacies can be seen from Black Chicken and Sea Cucumber, along it is also Chinese groceries, Noodle Houses and Snack houses.

spots.name: Wai Ying Fastfood
spots.desc: Taste their Mami, Dumplings and Hakaw and many other Chinese dishes.

spots.name: Royal Garden
spots.desc: Serves authentic Chinese cuisine like dim sum as well as exotic Chinese cuisine such as shark's fin. This restaurant is usually filled with Chinese people speaking Chinese, in a way you might feel that you are in China.

spots.name: President's Teahouse
spots.desc: This teahouse is a smaller version of President's Restaurant however it is affordable and the food is OK. They serve food from Dumplings and authentic Chinese Cuisine.

spots.name: National Museum of Anthropology
spots.desc: Stately, neoclassical museum housing a broad collection of Filipino cultural materials & artifacts.

spots.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
spots.desc: Massive museum with collections of Filipino fine art, archaeology, botany, natural history & more.

spots.name: National Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: Zoological, botanical & geological specimens displayed in an elegant venue with a soaring atrium.

spots.name: National Planetarium Manila
spots.desc: Museum of space history, Small venue with educational displays on planets & space plus shows in a dome-shaped theater.

spots.name: Mehan Garden
spots.desc: See Asia's first botanical garden, opened on the late 1850s, renamed after John C. Mehan, the park superintendent.

spots.name: Department of Tourism
spots.desc: Almost a twin of the former Finance Department headquarters nearby, this Neoclassical building is a prominent feature of the eastern end of Rizal Park. The colossal statue of Lapu-Lapu - a fairly recent addition to the park - stands between the two buildings, and the giant relief map of the Philippines is just a short walk away.

spots.name: Metropolitan Theater
spots.desc: An Art Deco building designed by Filipino architect; Juan M. de Guzman Arellano, first opened in the 1930s and then was severely damaged after the liberation of Manila by America and the Filipino forces in 1945, it was again reconstructed by the Americans however by the 1960s it fell into disuse but again reopened in the 1970s, and then again it fell into decay. As of January 2023, the theater is…

spots.name: Kilometre Zero
spots.desc: Historical landmark, Small marble marker, reference point for all Filipino distance measurements & popular for photo ops.

spots.name: Dads Saisaki Kamayan
spots.desc: Kamayan literally means to eat with your hands in Filipino. Their native buffet has a wide range of Filipino food to offer for just under 10 US$/person. Specialties include the lechon (suckling pig) and grilled seafood. Kamayan also has branches in Makati and Quezon City and is usually located alongside its sister restaurants Dad's (Western food buffet) and Saisaki (Japanese food buffet).

spots.name: Amber Food
spots.desc: Manila, the Philippines' capital, blends history, culture, and modern life. Amber Restaurant, known for its delicious Filipino dishes like pansit, has multiple branches in the city, offering a cozy dining experience.
spots.addr: 1st Floor, De Leon Center, 1151 M. H. Del Pilar St, Ermita, Manila, 1000 Metro Manila

spots.name: Plaza Miranda
spots.desc: Look around Plaza Miranda which is just outside Quiapo Church, Pedestrian square dating to 1961, with granite tiles & neo-Baroque features around a central obelisk.here peddlers ironically sell occult amulets that are incompatible with the Catholic Faith.

spots.name: Ocampo Pagoda
spots.desc: The Ocampo Pagoda is an example of "Where East meets West" architecture, the pagoda is mixed of European and Oriental architecture and looks like as if a temple in good old China has been invaded by the English and made into a castle. The history is that Don Jose Ocampo wanted and ordered to beautify his garden.

spots.name: Bahay Nakpil-Bautista
spots.desc: Built by Arcadio Arellano in 1914 when Philippine architecture was influenced by Art Nouveau in building houses and buildings, historically it was the home of Dr. Ariston Bautista and his wife Doña Petrona Nakpil along with her brother; Julio Nakpil with his wife, Gregoria De Jesus who was also the widow of Andres Bonifacio; a Filipino leader during the Spanish colonial era. During World War II…

spots.name: Boix House
spots.desc: Built during the 1890s of Neo-Renaissance ornamentation. Temporarily closed as of August 2023.

spots.name: Victory Lacson Underpass
spots.desc: An underground air-conditioned mall that was renovated in 2014 to be well lit and safe. There are over a hundred small shops, small eateries and kiosks. There are also multiple ATMs.

spots.name: SM Clearance Outlet
spots.desc: Veteran retailer with a large inventory of clothes, shoes & accessories at a discounted prices.

spots.name: Quinta Market & Fish Port
spots.desc: Indoor market opened in 1851, with scores of stalls selling fish, local produce & household goods.

spots.name: Pinoy Sikat Handicrafts
spots.desc: nice place to buy Philippine handicraft, You can get a lot of beautiful pinoy made items on a very cheap price here.

spots.name: Globe Lumpia House
spots.desc: Opened in 1956, this long-time Quiapo institution is known for its lumpia, with freshly-made vegetable lumpiang sariwa being the house specialty.

spots.name: Pastora Special Palabok
spots.desc: People from all over Manila flock to this humble stall inside the city's old central market to get their fix of pancit palabok, which on a number of occasions has been deemed Manila's best.
spots.addr: Carlos Palanca St. cor. Quezon Blvd

spots.name: Jolli Dada’s Eatery The Original Palabok Pancit & Halo Halo
spots.desc: A food trip in Quiapo wouldn’t be complete without a visit here. We went on a Saturday afternoon and had to wait in line for about 10-15 minutes. There are limited seats so you have to be patient.

spots.name: Amis Restaurant
spots.desc: One of the Hidden gems in Manila. Very affordable meals and drinks.

spots.name: Rosas Pancitan
spots.desc: Definitely, a must-try food place in Quiapo! Rosas Pancitan is best known for their sotanghon soup, although they also offer rice cakes and other treats.

spots.name: Palabok d'e Tisoy
spots.desc: Try their special palabok with squid, lechon kawali and boiled egg toppings.

spots.name: Plaza La Liga Filipina
spots.desc: A small park at the now-demolished house where the La Liga Filipina, a Filipino revolutionary organization led by Jose Rizal, Andres Bonifacio, and Apolinario Mabini, were established.
spots.addr: Ilaya Street cor. Raja Matanda Street

spots.name: San Jose de Trozo Parish Church - Santa Cruz, Manila City (Archdiocese of Manila)
spots.desc: It has improved a lot throughout the years. The Church’s patron saint is St. Joseph because the people of the area used to be lumberjacks. Historical the area was called Trozo, because of the lumbers found in the place. As of 2022, the parish priest is Fr Peterson Tieng, LRMS. He gives passionate homilies and formation talks. They are also the ones responsible for the sick call for the…

spots.name: Old Tutuban Train Station
spots.desc: The old Tutuban Train station building still survives to this day and this heritage structure now serves as a mall in the midst of Tondo, Manila. This is the main hub for the Manila-Dagupan train line which was inaugurated in 1892 during the Spanish colonial period. A historical marker is now placed at the exterior of the building indicating its importance in Philippine transportation history.

spots.name: Tutuban Center Mall
spots.desc: This mall has gained reputation for being a budget-friendly mall. Just across the mall is the Philippines' own Grand Central Station; the Philippine National Railway Main Station which also has the same name that of the mall.

spots.name: 168 Shopping Mall
spots.desc: Bustling indoor mall with vendors selling casual clothing & home goods, plus lots of food options.

spots.name: Divisoria Market
spots.desc: The country's premier, if not the biggest, combined wholesale and retail center, as well as the largest spillover ambulant and flea market, is here.

spots.name: Ugbo Street Food Shops and Takeaways
spots.desc: The long and narrow stretch in Velasquez, Tondo, Manila, now fondly called Ugbo Street Food, has grown famous for its numerous kiosks that serve inexpensive snacks and desserts until the wee hours of the night. If you’re looking for an affordable place to enjoy delicious snacks and hang out with friends, check out this thriving community in Manila.

spots.name: Hideout House of Unlimeated
spots.desc: Great place to chill with rooftop view. You gotta try their Kaldereta and Cholesterol Sampler! They're the bomb! Lechon paksiw is delicious, too. Nachos is flooded with cheese!

spots.name: Romantic Baboy - Masangkay Street Branch
spots.desc: Eat all you can meat for the price of Php 549 is actually good deal.

spots.name: Taipei No.2 Station
spots.desc: Dishes of Taiwanese cuisine can be ordered at this restaurant.

spots.name: TeaSpoon Cafe-Juan Luna Branch
spots.desc: Pastries, rice meals, hamburgers, veggie salads, frappes, etc. are available.

spots.name: The Coffee Bar MNL
spots.desc: The drink, food, and ambience, It's relaxing, the servers are chill, everything taste great.
spots.addr: 1849 Dagupan St, Corner Tayuman St, Tondo, Manila, 1012 Metro Manila

spots.name: Collectors Den Cafe
spots.desc: Good coffee and nice interior. If you're up for a fresh place and a big fan of toy collections as well then is a must to visit. Also a good place to chill with friends and families.

spots.name: Quezon Memorial Shrine
spots.desc: The main attraction of the Quezon Memorial Circle. The Art-Deco monument which is adorned by mourning angels on each of its three pillars is a national shrine dedicated to the late President Manuel L. Quezon. Embedded artworks are also decorates the base of the shrine. At night the monument is illuminated with lights that gradually shifts its colors.

spots.name: Dancing Fountains
spots.desc: The centerpiece of the Liwasang Aurora. It is illuminated at light with moving water features accompanied by music.

spots.name: Liwasang Aurora
spots.desc: A circular paved plaza decorated in a style of a compass rose. Along with the adjacent stage, the Liwasang Aurora serves as the venue for various events such as concerts held at the Quezon Memorial Circle.

spots.name: Philippine-Israel Friendship Park
spots.desc: A small secluded area beside the Quezon Heritage House which is dedicated to the bilateral ties of the Philippines and Israel. It features a small three-sided monument which commemorates; President Manuel Quezon's "Open Door Policy" to Jews escaping from Nazi Germany, the United Nations Resolution 181 of November 29, 1947 which led to the creation of the State of Israel where the Philippines…

spots.name: Museo ni Manuel Quezon
spots.desc: A museum at the triangular base of the Quezon Memorial Shrine, dedicated to the political career of President Quezon. The remains of President Quezon are inside a marble sarcophagus inside the museum. His wife Aurora Quezon is also interred at the site.

spots.name: President Corazon Aquino House
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to President Corazon Aquino. Under-construction is scheduled to be completed in early 2017.

spots.name: Hardin ng mga Bulaklak
spots.desc: The Hardin ng mga Bulaklak is a flower garden which is a project of the city government, the Succulent and Cactus Society of the Philippines, and the Philippine Horticultural Society. It features various indigenous flowers and is often a location of gardening and flower shows by various gardening societies of the country.

spots.name: Tropical Garden
spots.desc: Garden featuring tropical plants which was inaugurated in October 2012. It features a small pond as well and is another venue for gardening and flower shows.

spots.name: Joys of Urban Farming
spots.desc: The urban farm where vegetables are planted in the park is part of Vice Mayor Joy Belmonte urban farming project, "Joys of Urban Farming". A custodian is available within the farm's premises where visitors could learn about growing crops at their own backyard.

spots.name: Charito L. Planas Garden
spots.desc: A small fenced garden dedicated to Quezon City Parks Development Foundation head, Charito L. Planas who was responsible for the rehabilitation of the park in the early 2000s.

spots.name: Cactus Garden
spots.desc: In a secluded area behind the Hardin ng mga Bulaklak, the Cactus Garden features cactuses and succulents of various types and sizes some almost as tall as a human. It also has a greenhouse but is usually off-limits to visitors.

spots.name: Quezon City Memorial Circle Zipline
spots.desc: For the adventurous and definitely not for the faint-hearted. Zipline from a height equivalent to about four-stories. The path of the zipline crosses the Pedal N' Paddle Pond. One Zipline station is near the Children's Playground and the other near the Joy of Urban Farming.
spots.price: 100 (one way) 150 (two way); senior citizen rates 80 (one way), 130 (two way)

spots.name: Circle of Joy
spots.desc: A children's playground within the park. The playground features various slides and other attractions such seesaws. The grounds are either covered in concrete or artificial grass which reduces the likelihood of little kids from getting dirty while still having fun.

spots.name: Circle of Fun
spots.desc: An amusement park within the park. It features various attractions and rides such as the "Fun Drop" a drop tower ride and the "Sea Dragon", a pirate ship type of amusement ride.
spots.price: 30 entrance fee (except children below and senior citizens)

spots.name: QMC Bicycle Rental
spots.desc: Bicycles and bicycles with side cars can be rented from a station located near the Children's Playground. The use of the rented vehicles are only for a bicycle track which circles around the Children's Playground.

spots.name: Pedal N' Paddle
spots.desc: A amusement space featuring bicycle and pedal-powered-boat rentals.

spots.name: Pokemon Go
spots.desc: A suitable place for players due to many Poke-stops within the park's premises, although the use of mobile data is highly recommended since the public Wi-Fi is unreliable.

spots.name: Tropical Hut
spots.desc: A good place to order burgers. Other food such as chicken and sundaes are also available at this fast-food restaurant.

spots.name: New Kamameshi House
spots.desc: A Japanese restaurant which offers an array of sushi as well as yosenabe or Japanese hot pot.

spots.name: Looc Fish Sanctuary
spots.desc: The marine protected area located at the heart of Looc Bay features a floating raft hut where visitors can snorkel and rent a kayak to observe schools of fishes within the crystal-clear waters.

spots.name: Blue Hole of Tablas
spots.desc: an underwater hole 10 meters below the surface where you can scuba or freedive

spots.name: Binucot Beach
spots.desc: A pristine beach offering crystal-clear waters, perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and beach picnics.

spots.name: Tinagong Dagat
spots.desc: Literally translates to "Hidden Sea", This stunning salt-water lake is surrounded by beautiful limestone formations and is remote enough that you could have the whole lake to yourself.

spots.name: Cuyo Fort and St. Augustine Parish Church
spots.desc: During the early Spanish period Fort Cuyo was constructed to protect the Cuyonon from sporadic Moro attacks and finished in 1680. The original complex of stone and mortar was a square with four bastions. The present complex, which occupies 1 ha, is a solid rectangular edifice with walls 10 m high and 2 m thick. It has a tall belfry and watchtowers; its cannons, which face the sea, are now fired…

spots.name: Kiteboarding and windsurfing
spots.desc: The Philippines is considered by some people to be one of the best places for windsurfing and kiteboarding in Asia and Cuyo Island has become a good choice for many. It has two spots for these sports. One is in Cuyo Town at Capusan Beach. The other is at Quejano/Victoria Beach some 20 minutes away. Kiteboarding instruction at Capusan is provided exclusively by the Cuyo Watersports Association and…

spots.name: Capusan Beach and Quejano/Victoria Beach
spots.desc: Capusan Beach in Cuyo Town is the most popular spot for kiteboarding due to its long sand bar, ample space, combination of shallow and deep water and free public access. Quejano/Victoria Beach on the east side of the island also offers very good conditions. Those who consider themselves mediocre kiters find ideal conditions to practice the water start in chest deep crystal clear water in a…

spots.name: Aguado pilgrimage
spots.desc: Mt. Aguado features life-size stations of the Way of the Cross constructed from the foot to the peak of the mountain. Cuyonon devotees, visitors and tourists make the annual pilgrimage to Mt. Aguado as part of the penitential rites done in Cuyo during the Holy Week particularly on Holy Thursday.

spots.name: Snorkeling
spots.desc: There are numerous places within the entire Cuyo Archipelago where one can find an amazing variety of underwater sights. For the casual visitor it is generally advisable to snorkel in those areas free from hazards such as fishermen and other surface water sports activities. Black sea urchins are to be avoided!

spots.name: Evolution
spots.desc: Malapascua's only 5-star Instructor Training Facility rating from TDI. Evolution offers a full range of TDI tech classes. Day trips and local dives are run 365 days a year by a professional team. Evolution is a full service resort with 16 rooms and a well-known restaurant on site and is owned and operated by a seasoned Irish and English duo. In 2015 Evolution became a Green Fins top member having…

spots.name: French Kiss Divers
spots.desc: French Kiss Divers is a small diveshop who offers SSI courses from open water to Instructor and a panel of specialties such as Nitrox, Deep, Night, and Wreck, a very good knowledge of the dive sites. The dive group doesn't exceed 4 people. They often organize day trips in surrounding islands like Kalanggaman or Carnaza.

spots.name: Malapascua Exotic Dive & Beach Resort (IDC Centre)
spots.desc: Offers all in one - accommodation, restaurant, bar, diveshop, travel service. This eco-friendly resort has its own recycling plant and 24-hour generator. This PADI 5-star Instructor Development Resort is the only National Geographic Center in Malapascua. Courses range from beginner through to Instructor (100% pass rate) and technical diving courses. They cover more than 22 dive sites around…

spots.name: Sea Explorers
spots.desc: Located at the center of Bounty Beach beside Ocean Vida Resort with a bar on the island. In the Visayas since 1989, offering all PADI recreational courses from beginner up to Instructor courses.

spots.name: Thresher Shark Divers
spots.desc: PADI 5-Star Career Development Centre was established in 2004, offering guided dives and PADI courses from beginner to professional level with very experienced PADI Pros. Regular trips include morning thresher shark dives at Kimud Shoal, local reef and macro dives, Gato Island, night dives and wreck dives. Open Water divers may be able to join some shark dives with instructor supervision; deeper…
spots.hours: 8am-7or 8pm, dive schedule confirmed the day before
spots.addr: Bounty Beach, Logon, Daanbantayan, Cebu 6013 Philippines

spots.name: Malapascua Scuba Eco Adventures,
spots.desc: PADI Diving courses from beginner to professional. Especially for SPANISH Divers .Diving in small groups with experienced divemasters in a fun environment. More 10 years experience on Malapascua and Divemasters. Eco-friendly resort, Dives to see the thresher sharks Monad Shoal, Kimud Shoal, Kalanggagamn, Gato Island,

spots.name: Oscar's Restaurant
spots.desc: An eclectic mix of international dishes with a daily changing menu. Open air beachfront restaurant located above Thresher Shark Divers.

spots.name: The Craic House
spots.desc: The Craic House serves up delicious daily specials based on the best local produce and quality imported ingredients personally sourced by the owners. Everything that can be homemade is homemade from bread, wraps, falafel, cakes, pies, relishes, pates.

spots.name: Purple Snapper Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: They have great burgers. Also try their pizzas and fettuccine chicken alfredo.

spots.name: The Pub Upstairs
spots.desc: An open air bar located above Thresher Shark Divers, nestled amongst the palm trees with a sea view, The Pub Upstairs is a lively watering hole for an apres-dive beer or cocktail. An excellent selection of local and imported beers and spirits.

spots.name: Kape't Tagpuan sa Isla
spots.desc: Coffee Shop

spots.desc: Try their dumplings and fried dumplings.

spots.name: Lord Stow's Bakery - Ongpin
spots.desc: Egg tart and other Chinese, Filipino delicasies.

spots.name: Paterno Mansion

spots.name: Kim Chong Tin Hopia Factory
spots.desc: This is an old-fashioned pugon baked hopia since 1927.

spots.desc: Anglican church.

spots.desc: One of Manila's favorite Chinese restaurants.

spots.name: Causeway Seafood Restaurant-Masangkay Street Branch
spots.desc: Authentic Cantonese dishes.
