spots.name: Chachago Masangkay - Orchard Residences
spots.desc: Bubble tea store.

spots.name: Angelina
spots.desc: Original Italian food.

spots.name: Gateway Museum
spots.desc: Museum dedicated to Filipino arts and supporting new artists.

spots.name: Payatas Dumpsite
spots.desc: Clearly not for the normal traveller easily shocked by the stench and the poverty, this dumpsite, which receives a third of Metro Manila's waste, is one of the district's local landmarks. This was once an empty ravine until it was converted into a landfill to replace Tondo's Smokey Mountain. Though touring the facility requires advance permission, you can see the life of Payatas's poorer families…

spots.name: Pinoy Big Brother House
spots.desc: Home of the Philippine Big Brother franchise. The façade makes this more of a house, but it also hosts the studios where Pinoy Big Brother is aired. The surrounding area can become very crowded during eviction nights, where thousands of fans wait. The house is generally closed when Pinoy Big Brother is not being broadcasted.
spots.addr: 18 Eugenio Lopez Jr. Drive, South Triangle

spots.name: Dampol Bridge
spots.desc: A 19th-century red-brick bridge built over a creek and still used by motor vehicles. The roadway itself is modernized, but its original structure is still intact and can be seen after borrowing a key from caretakers at Saint Vincent Ferrer Church to unlock a gate leading the bottom of the bridge.
spots.addr: Aritao-Quirino Road, Dopaj, Dupax del Sur

spots.name: Sea of Clouds
spots.desc: A stretch of upland rural highway leading to Quirino province, so-called because the low-lying clouds appear to inundate the area in the mornings.
spots.addr: National Road, Binuangan, Dupax del Norte

spots.name: Bundok Pag-ibig
spots.desc: Meaning "Love Mountain" in Filipino, it is more of a grass hill that somewhat resembles the iconic Windows computer screen, particularly when the rainy season turns the surface green.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway, Gabut, Dupax del Sur

spots.name: Mount Susong Dalaga
spots.desc: Meaning "Maiden's Breast", it is the highest peak, with a height of , inside the Pantabangan-Carranglan Watershed Forest Reserve, a protected area with that straddles the boundary between Dupax del Sur and the towns of Carranglan and Pantabangan in Nueva Ecija.

spots.name: Dupax Watershed Forest Reserve
spots.desc: An ecotourism site in the forested foothills of the Caraballo mountains leading to panoramic vistas over the surrounding valley.

spots.name: Green Oasis of Dupac
spots.desc: A farm-to-table restaurant serving fusion Filipino and Mediterranean cuisine.
spots.addr: Aritao-Quirino Road, Mangayang, Dupax del Sur

spots.name: Mount Romelo
spots.desc: A peak surrounded by multiple waterfalls. Most hikes to the mountain combine a stop with the Buruwisan Falls.

spots.name: Aristocrat
spots.desc: Now a chain, it has been one of the most famous and longest-lasting restaurants in Manila. Serves Filipino food at decent prices. It has been closed down due to concerns about wastewater disposal.

spots.name: Cafe Adriatico
spots.desc: The flagship of LJC Restaurant Group. Open from 7AM to 6AM the following day (4AM on Sundays). A popular hang-out place for locals and tourists. Among the café’s specialties are Chicken Kiev, Spareribs Adobo, Salpicao Rice, Callos, Lengua Estofada, Classic Café Adriatico Burger, Pancit Palabok, and an authentic Spanish hot chocolate beverage called “Chocolate Eh’.

spots.name: Casa Armas
spots.desc: Specialties: paella, cuchinillo (must be ordered 6 hours in advance) and garlic crab Thanh Long style (admittedly not very Spanish but great nonetheless).

spots.name: Korean Village Restaurant
spots.desc: From kimchi to its beef stew, japchae, and bulgogi to Korean ice cream bars. Order à-la-carte or yakiniku style.

spots.name: Tanabe Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Superb Unagi (eel), must-try Usuyaki beef with enoki mushrooms, quality sushi & sashimi and value for money bento boxes.

spots.name: Market Café
spots.desc: US Angus Rib Eye grilled to perfection. Butterfly Prawns with Risotto. New York Cheesecake that kind of stuff.
spots.addr: 588 Pedro Gil St. corner M.H. del Pilar St

spots.name: Bedrock
spots.desc: Flintstones-themed bar/eatery. Wonderfully weird and often a bit camp. They have live music nights.

spots.name: Don Roman Santos Building
spots.desc: Historical landmark, as of September 2023 it is Temporarily closed.

spots.name: Blumentritt Street market
spots.desc: Just below the LRT. this street is full of small stalls selling all kinds of cheap products. Some products include: shoes, baking materials, beauty products and clothing. Although patrolled by police, it is still full of pickpockets.

spots.name: Chades Tapsilog
spots.desc: One of Manila's best tapsilogan eatery. Also has branch in Alvarez Street.

spots.name: Ambos Mundos Restaurant
spots.desc: Chinese food restaurant, one of Manila's popular Chinese restaurants.

spots.name: Jollibee
spots.desc: A fastfood establishment which serves hamburgers, hotdogs, fries, spaghetti, fried chicken, palabok, among others.

spots.name: McDonald's
spots.desc: It serves hamburgers, fries, fried chicken, spaghetti, pies, among others.

spots.name: Old Swiss Inn
spots.desc: Located right beside Paco Park, this restaurant serves Swiss and European cuisines such as soups, salads, grilled food, pastas and sandwiches, among others.
spots.price: Signature dishes start at 385 per single serve
spots.addr: G/F Garden Plaza Hotel & Suites, 1030 Belen St

spots.name: Yvan Navy
spots.desc: This fast food establishment is known for its very affordable quarter pounder burgers.

spots.name: Teus Mansion
spots.desc: Purchased and converted into a guesthouse in the 1970s, it showcases European silver ware including notable 18th and 19th century silversmiths Paul de Lamerie and Paul Storr. It has been given as a gift to the Marcoses during their Silver wedding anniversary.

spots.name: Mabini Bridge
spots.desc: Mabini Bridge, formerly and still referred as Nagtahan Bridge, is a road bridge crossing the Pasig River between Nagtahan Street in Santa Mesa and Quirino Avenue in Paco, Manila. It was constructed between January and February in 1945. It initially served as a pontoon bridge transporting U.S. Army jeeps and evacuate citizens caught in the crossfire during the Liberation of Manila. In lieu with…

spots.name: Arch of the Centuries
spots.desc: Venerable baroque arch erected in 1680 & moved piece by piece to its current location in 1954. a city icon in Manila.

spots.name: UST Museum
spots.desc: Eclectic university museum housing paintings, religious, geology, zoology & botany exhibits. Museum of Santo Tomas University is considered the oldest museum in the Philippines. It was formally established in 1869. Museum consists of 4 sections: natural history, fine art (paintings), ethnography and religious artifacts. The collection is impressive, especially natural history. This is really a…

spots.name: Plaza Noli Public Square / Plaza
spots.desc: A mini circle park, a place to sit, relax and to have a chitchat.

spots.name: Dangwa Flower Market
spots.desc: Manila's flower market, heavily flocked during Valentine's and All Saint's day and All Soul's Day, it is flocked by people.

spots.name: Trabajo Wet & Dry Market
spots.desc: Public market, lots of choices to buy for, the place is so busy, many foodstalls and if you're lucky you'll have the cheapest price for the friuts.
spots.addr: M. dela Fuente Street corner Loyola Street

spots.name: Kubo by Gillid’s
spots.desc: Kubo by Gillid's is a boodle-fight alfresco dining restaurant in Sampaloc.
spots.addr: #844B Sto Tomas Street corner Blumentritt Road

spots.name: EMILIA, House of Filipino Food
spots.desc: Filipino, Spanish winery & restaurant near the Malacanan Palace.

spots.name: Trinity Jean Pancit Cabagan
spots.desc: They have the best pancit cabagan, even better than the ones in Cabagan, Cagayan Province.

spots.name: Kanto Tayo
spots.desc: Dumplings, Pork Siomai, Beer Bucket, Chicken Wings with Fries. A very nice and unique drinking place in Manila! They have unli promos at a very reasonable price. The price of beer and other alcoholic beverages are really affordable. Has a lot of food choices. Quality of food is okay but can be better. All in all, a really fun and nice place. Perfect place to hang out with friends.

spots.name: James & Che's BBQ House - Adelina
spots.desc: A very delicious barbecue dish I had here. A lot of choice by a good variety of meat. The restaurant looks clean and very busy between 5 pm 6 pm and is a great place to crash and fill your stomach.

spots.name: Yoshimeatsu UST U-belt
spots.desc: Many choices of side dishes and meats. They have tempura, enoki, scallop with cheese, crispy fried chicken karage, kani salad, miso soup, cheese ball, and red tea.

spots.name: Max Mango Loyola Branch
spots.desc: An excellent mango graham shake. Try their avocado overload too.

spots.name: 00:00 Cafe
spots.desc: Quaint quiet place in the middle of a bustling street with a homey and bright atmosphere which is a great place to work or study.

spots.name: Topiary Garden
spots.desc: A small secluded garden at the top of the Gateway Mall. Benches and tables are available. See the garden's animal-shaped foliage.

spots.name: Socorro Water Towers
spots.desc: Historic concrete water towers built in the 1930s. as of August 2023 Cubao Water Towers is Temporarily closed.
spots.addr: 15th Ave, Cor. Col. Bonny Serrano Ave

spots.name: "Christmas is Home"
spots.desc: Live Christmas display in Araneta Center, featuring Filipino and Western Christmas traditions and Araneta Center. It was revived in November 28, 2018, after it was held from 1966 to 2002.

spots.name: SM Araneta City
spots.desc: One of the oldest malls owned by retail giant SM, but it looks more like its older sister in Makati's Ayala Center, SM Makati. This instead houses a department store and supermarket inside; all other shops and restaurants are outside.

spots.name: McDonald's - New Frontier Theater
spots.desc: The second Mcdonald's branch in the Philippines, it is located in one of the oldest structures in the area.

spots.name: Quezon Hall
spots.desc: The centerpiece and gateway of the University of the Philippines campus

spots.name: Academic Oval
spots.desc: Composed of Roxas and Osmeña avenues, this one-way road forming an oval around the University of the Philippines Diliman has space for walking, jogging, and biking, and popular for everyone.

spots.name: Blissful Belly
spots.desc: Continental restaurant and café. Very vegan/vegetarian friendly. Cakes, bread and juices are also available.

spots.name: Banapple
spots.desc: This once hole-in-the-wall, almost home-run restaurant cum bakeshop serves some of the best cakes and pies in town and serves mostly the intellectual crowd from the nearby universities of UP and Ateneo (who drive over just for lunch/dessert). Be sure to secure seats as a lot of students flock the place (especially during lunch, early afternoon and dinner) to sample their latest cakes (according…

spots.name: Iglesia Ni Cristo Templo Central
spots.desc: Central Temple of the Iglesia Ni Cristo (Church of Christ). The Central Complex includes the Central Temple, which is an 8,000-seat church with one of the largest pipe organs in the Philippines; the Iglesia Ni Cristo Museum, which showcases the history of the Church in exhibits and artifacts from all over the world, marking its global expansion; the Tabernacle, a large multi-purpose meeting and…

spots.name: La Mesa Eco Park
spots.desc: A beautiful 5-hectare eco park on the outskirts of Quezon city. A haven for people who'd like to get away from the heat and dust of the city. Quite hard to find though, and there is little public transport going there.

spots.name: Litex Market
spots.desc: The wet and dry market frequented by residents of the surrounding slum areas. It is also a metonym for the surrounding area.

spots.name: Dampa sa Libis
spots.desc: A fresh seafood market with several restaurants all under one roof, with a dining hall that seats up to 800 people at any one time. Buy some fresh seafood at the market, then have one of the restaurants cook it to your liking for an extra charge.

spots.name: Agezuki Japanese Cuisine
spots.desc: Known for their wide variety of sushi and sashimi, in addition to traditional Japanese fare, they serve quality dishes that won't break the bank.
spots.addr: A. Francisco Bldg., 83 Katipunan Ave., White Plains

spots.name: Apero
spots.desc: A neighborhood cafe with a selection of freshly-baked bread and pastries, coupled with an eclectic menu of French-inspired eats served in large portions.
spots.addr: The Club House, Corinthian Hills, Temple Drive, Ugong Norte

spots.desc: An unassuming jazz bar with a large selection of cocktails and imported whiskey. Guests can also listen to owner Jay Amante's large collection of vinyl records, with over 10,000 records available.
spots.addr: 2nd Floor, White Plains West, 42 Katipunan Ave., White Plains

spots.name: SM City North EDSA Sky Garden
spots.desc: Elevated park with a simulated river and waterfall, part of SM City North EDSA (see #Buy)

spots.name: ABS-CBN Studios
spots.desc: The oldest television studios inside the complex, with 10 studios housing ABS-CBN's popular shows like It's Showtime, Magandang Buhay, TV Patrol, and ASAP.

spots.name: Centris Station
spots.desc: Indoor mall of the Eton Centris complex, with select restaurants, shops and a SM Hypermarket.

spots.name: Wil Tower Mall
spots.desc: Small upscale mall with a Coffee Project café and All Day convenience store, part of the 46-storey Wil Tower condominium complex.

spots.name: Greens
spots.desc: Continental restaurant with many vegetarian and vegan friendly options including cake.

spots.name: Music Match
spots.desc: Karaoke bar with disco and a selection of food. Smoking allowed in some rooms

spots.name: Ace Water Spa
spots.desc: Indoor swimming pool, Ace Water Spa is a brand of water themed spa. There are many instruments you can use to give you a spa treatment like hot bath, pressurized water that could "massage" you, and sauna rooms.

spots.name: Robinsons Magnolia
spots.desc: Large shopping mall with cinema (Robinsons Movieworld) and food court.
spots.addr: Aurora Blvd, Doña Hemady St, New Manila

spots.name: Z Square Mall
spots.desc: Urban open-air shopping mall housing a supermarket & gym along with restaurants & food stalls.
spots.addr: Banawe Street corner Del Monte Avenue

spots.name: Daily Veggie n’ Café
spots.desc: Friendly Chinese restaurant for the travelling vegan or vegetarian.

spots.name: La Laguna Viewpoint
spots.desc: Along the sidewalk that leads between Big La Laguna and Small La Laguna you'll find a narrow path. Follow the path for 20 meters up the stairs and onto the top of a rocky out cropping which has an oddly placed cement pad at the top, as if for a house. From the top of the outcrop, you'll be provided with some lovely views of the surrounding beaches and the surrounding islands.

spots.name: La Laguna beach
spots.desc: Located a short walk around the hillock off the upper edge of Sabang beach, this is a short beach (about 300 metres in length) and yet miraculously further divided into Big La Laguna and Small La Laguna beach. The beach is clean, with white sand (unlike the brown sand of Sabang), filled mostly with day tourists, has a few quiet resorts and at least five dive shops as of 2012. It is especially…

spots.name: Lighthouse Walk
spots.desc: Follow the road up past the market to the village of Sinandigan and on to the lighthouse where there is a spectacular view of the Verde Island Passage and Luzon to the north, and on a clear day the summit of Mt Halcon to the south. To the east you can see the City of Calapan in the distance and further on the horizon, the island of Marinduque.

spots.name: Sabang Webcam
spots.desc: If you want to see Sabang Beach live, there is a website that has three webcam locations for Sabang beaches, one each for Big La Laguna, Small La Laguna and Sabang. The webcam image frequency is once every 30 seconds so you can see the real-time vista, the weather and the people and boats coming and going.

spots.name: Puerto Galera Reefs
spots.desc: A snorkeling and diving destination with coral gardens and diverse marine life, including sea turtles and reef fish.

spots.name: ABWonderdive
spots.desc: A PADI 5 Star Dive Beach Resort owned and operated by Danish couple Alice and Bjørn Askholm in Small Lalaguna. Offering all level of PADI courses – from entry level up to Dive Master, as well as a wide variety of specialties taught in English, Scandinavian, German, French and Tagalog. Accommodation is in their own nicely appointed rooms or in one of the many resorts nearby.

spots.name: Action Divers
spots.desc: A smallish dive shop has been in Small Lalaguba but is very proud of its high level of customer satisfaction and safety. They generally run 3 dives a day at 9AM, midday and 3PM. Local guides know all the good spots and understands the tides in the Verde Channel. If you contact them they can put together diving and hotel packages to suit your needs.

spots.name: Asia Divers
spots.desc: A reputable dive shop. The divemasters, hailing from Britain, Germany, and Canada, are friendly and dive in smaller groups (usually four divers and one divemaster). They typically run four dives each day, including one night dive, and put together some nice hotel/dive packages with their sister resort, The El Galleon, located adjacent to their dive shop.

spots.name: Atlantis Dive Resort
spots.desc: A Five Star PADI Career Development Centers; two of only few dive centers with such a rating in Asia, you will find the highest standard of dive education, first class facilities and world class dive guides.

spots.name: Big Apple Dive Resort
spots.desc: The resort is in the middle of Sabang beach. The bar and restaurant are open 24 hr, serving a wide range of food and beverages. With two full size billiard tables in the bar overlooking the bay of Sabang, and a wide range of accommodation to suit all budgets from cottage style fan rooms to luxury air conditioned apartments with standby generators guaranteeing 24-hr power. There is 'Super Sports'…

spots.name: Mermaid Resort and Dive Center
spots.desc: A world-class resort offering accommodation, nature tours, and diving services. It has over 30 spacious guest rooms and suites. The resort offers international and local cuisine as well as a fully equipped beach-front shop with new and top-of-the-line compressor room.

spots.name: Frontier Scuba
spots.desc: Owned and run by Rick Kirkham an instructor trainer. Frontier Scuba is a TDI / SDI 5-Star Instructor Training Facility, one of only a handful in Asia. Packages are arranged including direct private transfers from Manila Airport and excellent resort accommodations. Their partner resort has more than 40 rooms all with hot showers, cable TV, and air-conditioned, and are very reasonably priced. One…

spots.name: Octopus Divers
spots.desc: Very friendly owner Mac and dive masters teach all PADI courses from beginner to professional level, diving all year around, dive safaris all over the Philippines, specially Apo Island and Coron, new equipment, relaxed, good value, can organise accommodation, located in at-cans resort just behind Papa Fred Steakhouse. Also help you with island hopping, trekking tours, go-kart or mud-kart…

spots.name: Sea Rider Dive Center
spots.desc: 63 29215885994. The cheapest dive and courses rate in the island with excellent macro & pelagic spotter. Berde island trip and night diving are always part of their daily activities. They arrange accommodation and transportation from Manila Intl airport & Clark Field Pampanga Intl airport to Sabang vice versa. Free intro dive for Non Nitrox Divers. Free boat pick up for public commuters from…

spots.name: South Seas Divers
spots.desc: Friendly and fluent instructors in Jappanese, Korean, Tagolo, Spanish, and French. PADI courses offered at reasonable rates.

spots.name: Puerto Galera Hash House Harriers
spots.desc: The local branch of the Hash House Harriers, an international group with clubs on every continent. All you need is a little taste for adventure combined with an enjoyment of the outdoors, when every Saturday afternoon a mixed group of Filipinos and Foreigners follow trails around some of the finest hashing areas in the country, when you will have the opportunity to see some of its most…

spots.name: Snorkel at Coral garden
spots.desc: This can be arranged with any boat operator at Sabang beach. It costs 1500 to hire a bangka for the day - usually they take you to a few secluded small beaches on the islands close by, and to snorkel at these places. Coral garden has the best snorkelling in this area - most of the corals are still alive, and the variety of colourful fish is amazing. A warning - the waters sometimes get cool so…

spots.name: Maxbank
spots.desc: The only ATM in Sabang accepting local and international cards with a 3% commission. In Puerto Galera, the Rural Bank and Allied Bank have ATMs which accept cards on the Megalink and Expressnet networks and at the Allied Bank Visa cards (debit or credit). The nearest banks with international Cirrus/Maestro links are in Calapan or Batangas (including ATMs at Batangas Pier).

spots.name: JE and G Express Payment Center ATM
spots.desc: A convenient ATM option in Puerto Galera, accepting both local and international cards. Located near the payment center, making it a useful stop for cash withdrawals and other transactions.
spots.price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

spots.name: The Viewpoint Coffee Bar & Gastro Bar
spots.desc: Cafe/bar with Tapas style food. Great view to the west (sunset!).

spots.name: Not Just Coffee
spots.desc: A stylish café offering specialty coffee, fresh pastries, and a cozy atmosphere, with an ocean view.

spots.name: Hemingway's Bistrot, Certified Angus Beef Restaurant
spots.desc: Located at the West end of Sabang beach. Hemingway's Bistrot featuring traditional German, Filipino and international cuisine prepared by Master Butcher Pfannen Fred and Chef Jake.

spots.name: SeaShore Resort
spots.desc: Tasty Filipino style breakfast right on the beach front, comes with the brewed coffee for 100 only. Fast internet and one of the best pork BBQ stick in the area.

spots.name: Toko's Restaurant
spots.desc: Atlantis also have a resort in Dauin near Dumaguete, and that also has a Toko's.

spots.name: Sunsplash Resort
spots.desc: Sunsplash Resort offers breakfast and lunchtime menus with local and international dishes. In the evening at 5PM Sunsplash offers an all-you-can-eat BBQ buffet for 250, with a selection of BBQ meats, salads, local and international dishes to choose from.

spots.name: Capn Greggs
spots.desc: With an all wooden decor, and some interesting and punny posters on their walls, this second floor sea facing restaurant serves filling meals. Their vegetable curry with rice is especially delectable. It is also among the few restaurants in Sabang that has newspapers for patrons to read.

spots.name: Cheap Charlies Bar
spots.desc: If you're looking for a bar that offers you a genuine local experience with a western touch then Cheap Charlies is the place to go. It is known for its cheap drinks, free karaoke and simple but delicious food. If karaoke is not your thing they turn off the karaoke later in the night and turn up the music. Opens at 4PM and closes around 5AM (or later.) It is located just down the hill from Max…

spots.name: Minolo Port
spots.desc: A small but busy port where travelers can hire boats for island-hopping trips or snorkeling excursions.

spots.name: Aninuan Falls
spots.desc: A secluded waterfall in the Aninuan area, offering a tranquil retreat surrounded by lush greenery. The trek to the falls takes visitors through a scenic jungle path with river crossings. The natural pool at the base of the waterfall provides a refreshing spot for swimming and relaxation.

spots.name: Talipanan Falls
spots.desc: A small but scenic waterfall hidden in the lush jungle near Talipanan Beach. The trail to the falls passes through Mangyan Village, where visitors can learn about indigenous culture. The falls have a refreshing natural pool, perfect for cooling off after the hike.

spots.name: Mangyan Village
spots.desc: Mangyan are the indigenous people of Mindoro, known for their distinct culture and traditions. Many Mangyan communities strive to preserve their way of life, avoiding outside influences. Visitors can learn about their customs, traditional crafts, and way of life. A reliable guide is recommended for visiting. Please be respectful and follow local customs.

spots.name: Ponderosa Golf Club
spots.desc: A picturesque 9-hole golf course perched in the hills, offering panoramic views of Puerto Galera and the surrounding coastline. Hiking to Ponderosa Golf Club from White Beach takes about an hour, with an uphill trail. The club also features a restaurant and viewing deck.

spots.name: Stairway Foundation
spots.desc: An international NGO focused on helping street children and raising awareness about child protection issues. The foundation uses creative arts, education, and advocacy programs to support vulnerable youth. Visitors can tour the center, learn about their initiatives, and support their work.

spots.name: Aninuan Beach
spots.desc: A quieter and less crowded alternative to White Beach, with accommodations and dining options.

spots.name: White Beach Reef
spots.desc: A shallow coral reef near White Beach, great for snorkeling, beginner diving and underwater photography.

spots.name: Talipanan Beach
spots.desc: A peaceful beach, Talipanan Beach is a spot for swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying fresh seafood at beachfront restaurants. The beach is also home to Luca’s Italian Restaurant, a well-known spot for pizzas and homemade pasta.

spots.name: FreeDive School
spots.desc: Freediving courses ranging from beginner to instructor levels, including specialized training in breath-hold techniques, deep freediving, and safety protocols. Also offers accommodation.

spots.name: Euronet Worldwide ATM
spots.desc: One of the few ATMs on White Beach that accepts international cards. Cash withdrawal fees apply, and the machine may run out of cash during peak tourist season.
spots.price: Transaction fees apply for international cards

spots.name: Parkway Shopping Mart
spots.desc: A store offering a variety of essential goods, snacks, beverages, toiletries, and some imported items. A good place to stock up on supplies while staying in White Beach.

spots.name: 7-Eleven
spots.desc: A convenience store offering a selection of snacks, drinks, basic groceries, and travel essentials.

spots.name: Local Market Street
spots.desc: A lively street lined with small shops, fruit stalls, local eateries, and souvenir stores. A place to grab fresh tropical fruits, try local street food, or find handmade crafts and beach essentials.

spots.name: Polycare Pharmacy
spots.desc: A small but well-stocked pharmacy offering over-the-counter medications, first-aid supplies, and basic personal care products.

spots.name: Palawan Express
spots.desc: Offers currency exchange services. Also provides money transfer, bill payments, and financial services.

spots.name: Resto Veranda
spots.desc: A beachfront restaurant offering a mix of Filipino and international cuisine. Known for its seafood dishes, grilled specialties, and refreshing tropical drinks.

spots.name: Café Marco
spots.desc: A cozy beach café serving a selection of coffee, pastries, and light meals.

spots.name: Arcobaleno Pizza
spots.desc: A casual Italian eatery specializing in wood-fired pizzas, pasta, and Mediterranean dishes.

spots.name: Foodtrip Sa Galera Fastfoods
spots.desc: A local eatery serving Filipino fast food and street food favorites.

spots.name: Yego's Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant offering a variety of Filipino and international dishes, including grilled seafood, rice meals, and refreshing tropical drinks.

spots.name: Il Capo Smoke Haus
spots.desc: A barbecue and smokehouse-style restaurant offering grilled meats, smoked specialties, and Filipino-American fusion dishes.

spots.name: Izakaya Abe Chang
spots.desc: A Japanese izakaya-style restaurant serving authentic sushi, sashimi, grilled skewers, and ramen.

spots.name: Mai Pho Chaolong House
spots.desc: A casual Vietnamese eatery specializing in pho, chaolong (Vietnamese beef stew), and bánh mì.

spots.name: Tamarind Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant by the sea side has a wooden roof. Food options are similar to typical bar & grill restaurants.

spots.name: Wally's Bar
spots.desc: A beachfront bar known for its cold beers and tropical cocktails and sunset views.

spots.name: Tamarind Bar
spots.desc: A beachfront bar with a great selection of cocktails, beers, and bar snacks. Often features live music and fire dancing performances in the evening.

spots.name: Pirata
spots.desc: A sports bar and restaurant, offering cold drinks, international cuisine, and live sports screenings. A roadside venue attracting both locals and travelers.

spots.name: Pata Negra Alona Beach Dive Center Resort
spots.desc: Padi dive center resort, providing dive courses and daily trips to Balicasag, Pamilacan, Cabilao and Bohol. Scuba guides with more than 3,000 dives. New Aqualung scuba equipment. Resort and accommodation included.

spots.name: Piratas Alona Dive Center
spots.desc: Their PADI MSDT instructors teach students from beginners to professionals, plus specialty courses. They also do daily fun dives, dive trips to Balicasag, Pamilacan and Cabilao islands. They have brand new Cressi equipment.

spots.name: Reef Seekers Alona Beach Dive Center
spots.desc: Padi Dive center, providing dive courses and daily trips to Balicasag and Pamilacan scuba diving. Aqualung partner center.

spots.name: Dolphin watching
spots.desc: Boats leave from Alona Beach at dawn and will take you to see dolphins having their morning exercise. It is important to book your boat a day ahead of time because the dolphins appear quite early.

spots.name: Jadski
spots.desc: A money changer, internet café and souvenir shop. Credit cards should not be used there, as credit card number thefts have been reported by tourists who used credit cards at the business.

spots.name: Pyramid Bar and Restaurant
spots.desc: It is an al fresco restaurant along Alona Beach. Aside from fresh seafood catch, the restaurant serves other varieties like sandwiches, pasta, noodles, chili chicken, beef teriyaki and pork cordon bleu. The bar serves fresh fruit juices, carbonated drinks, beer, wine and cocktails. At night, torches complete the tropical dining atmosphere.

spots.name: Olango Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.desc: A wetland area with many water fowl, very popular with bird watchers; close to a hundred species are found here, about half of them migratory and half permanent residents. It is listed by the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, especially as Waterfowl Habitat. See Ramsar sites.Facilities are minimal; the sanctuary office sells coconut juice and provides a bathroom, but…

spots.name: Olango Reef
spots.desc: A government-protected fish sanctuary with good snorkelling, located south of Olango around the smaller islands of Nalusuan and Hilutungan. It is one of the largest reef areas in the Visayas, about 4.5 km².

spots.name: Spanish Flagpole
spots.desc: A red-brick flagpole built in 1873.
