spots.name: Trudi's
spots.desc: Trudi's on the beach is relatively cheap and quite good.

spots.name: Sky Ranch Pampanga
spots.desc: Part of SM City Pampanga, it houses Pampanga Eye, a 65 m high Ferris wheel providing a 360-degree view of Pampanga, including San Fernando itself, Mount Arayat and Mount Pinatubo

spots.name: Torongan Cliff
spots.desc: A cliff facing the Pacific coast where the first settlers to Itbayat are believed to have landed in 4000 BC. There is an indigenous Ivatan stone tomb called Axurud dating back to the precolonial era. It also has Torongan Cave, whose mouth was blocked by a typhoon and rendered inaccessible to visitors.

spots.name: Mount Karoboboan
spots.desc: The highest point in Itbayat Island, with a height of . A viewdeck provides panoramic views over the island and the surrounding islets, while residents swear they can see city lights from Kaohsiung in Taiwan at night.

spots.name: Rapang Cliff
spots.desc: A cliff facing the Pacific coast on a jagged series of finger-like promontories known as Karapangan, with a background of grass and rock. Nearby is the Stone Bell, a flat stone that creates a distinct sound resembling a ringing bell when hit and was used by the residents as an alarm clock, warning signal in case of invasion, and to call in their livestock.

spots.name: Tachimus Port
spots.desc: A promontory on the Pacific coast home to a much-photographed Arius tree that continues to grow despite its truck being continuously bent by Itbayat's ferocious winds.

spots.name: Paganaman Port
spots.desc: A sheltered cove facing the South China Sea. As the waves are calmer in this side of the island, it is used as a mooring area for the town's fishing fleet and is one of the few seaside areas where residents can swim, although the waves may still be to rough for outsiders. There are tidal pools and a subterranean cave known as the Blue Hole for the color of its waters.

spots.name: Mount Riposed
spots.desc: A peak that dominates the southern half of Itbayat Island. The summit offers views reaching up to the uninhabited island of Dinem on the Pacific coast.

spots.name: Mauyen Cliff
spots.desc: A series of drops at the southern coast of Itbayat that loom over Mauyen Port.

spots.name: Yawran
spots.desc: A village composed of houses built in the indigenous Ivatan style called jinjin. Unlike the more famous stone houses in Batan Island and Sabtang, the ones in Itbayat are made of wood and thatched roofs.

spots.name: House of Dakay
spots.desc: The oldest house in Batanes, built in 1887 in the traditional Ivatan way of using stones and thatched roofs.

spots.name: Ivana Lighthouse
spots.desc: Built beside Radiwan Port, it guards over the strait separating Batan Island from Sabtang.

spots.name: Maydangeb Beach
spots.desc: A secluded stretch of white sand near the boundary with Mahatao.

spots.name: Toblerone Hills
spots.desc: A series of moss- and grass-colored limestone hills named after its resemblance to the logo of the Swiss chocolate brand.

spots.name: Honesty Store and Coffee Shop
spots.desc: Probably Ivana's most famous landmark, it is a store with a self-service cafe next door deliberately left without attendants, leaving its components to the mercy of the customer's moral scruples. Payment its deposited in a box, while you may have to knock next door if you need change. The fact that it has a generally stellar record of not being robbed is a testament to Batanes' low crime rate and…

spots.name: Embers Cafe and Restaurant
spots.desc: It features a cozy, casual, and trendy setting with an Instagrammable vibe. It is well-regarded as a quiet spot that accommodates solo diners, groups, and remote work.

spots.name: Benitta & Flora's Bistro Cafe
spots.desc: Known for its cozy, charming ambiance and budget friendly menu, it serves as a popular hangout for college students, families and travelers alike.

spots.name: Museo de Isarog
spots.desc: This museum highlights the rich history, indigenous culture, and traditions of the Bicol region.
spots.addr: Partido State University, San Juan Evangelista St

spots.name: Kuya Bry's Grill & Restobar
spots.desc: Casual, cozy, and trendy atmosphere, features a mix of indoor and alfresco dining spaces complete with modern furniture, brick walls, and string lights that make it a great hangout spot for barkadas and families.
spots.addr: Zone 1, Maganda Street, San Antonio Poblacion

spots.name: Panumbagan Sandbar
spots.desc: A wide white sandbar featuring floating bamboo pods and cottages designed by local artist Milo Naval where you can view fish and snorkel.

spots.name: Abulug-Ballesteros Bayview Boulevard
spots.desc: An extensive seaside promenade along the Babuyan Channel running east towards the municipality of Ballesteros.

spots.name: Lucban Bridge
spots.desc: The longest bridge in northwestern Cagayan, offering commanding views over the Abulug River.

spots.name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Parish Church
spots.desc: Abulug's main Roman Catholic parish church. Nearby is the Dela Torre residence, home to a venerated image of the dead Christ (Santo Entierro).

spots.name: Gandia Farm
spots.desc: An eco and agritourism venue and recreational space along the Abulug River.

spots.name: Kannaway Cave
spots.desc: A coastal grotto with a natural pool, accessible only during low tide.

spots.name: Bangaan Viewpoint
spots.desc: An elevated lookout with views over the Babuyan Channel into neighboring islands. Nearby is a memorial to the Philippine Navy vessel BRP Datu Kalantiaw which ran aground on the island during a typhoon in 1981 with the loss of 79 sailors.

spots.name: Nagudungan Hills
spots.desc: A hilly promontory jutting southwards and ringed by high and rocky cliffs. There is a lighthouse on the site.

spots.name: Lussok Cave
spots.desc: Another coastal grotto with a natural pool and rock formations.

spots.name: Dipari
spots.desc: An uninhabited islet off the northern coast of Calayan Island visited by game-fishers.

spots.name: Naguilian Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of white-sand beach around a sheltered cove at the western side of the island.

spots.name: Pamoctan Island
spots.desc: An islet facing Naguilian Beach with its own white-sand beach.

spots.name: Banua Beach
spots.desc: A white-sand stretch on the southwestern side of the island.

spots.name: Musa Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of white-sand beach on the western side of Fuga Island.

spots.name: Rumang-ay War Memorial
spots.desc: A small obelisk along the beach commemorating the spot where Japanese forces conducted the first amphibious landings on Luzon during their invasion of the country on December 10, 1941 at the start of the Pacific theater of World War II.

spots.name: Matara Reefs and White Sand Beach
spots.desc: A partially-secluded stretch of beach on the boundary with Santa Ana, whose white sands contrast with the grey beaches in the rest of Gonzaga.

spots.name: Tallag Beach and Rock Formations
spots.desc: A row of large rocks eroded by the wind and waves, resulting in peculiar formations, caves and tidal pools.

spots.name: Liban's Farm and Nature Park
spots.desc: An ecotourism venue with camping and fishing grounds, a natural spring pool, and overnight accommodation.

spots.name: G Farm
spots.desc: A family-run farm that offers fruit and vegetable picking to guests.

spots.name: Calvary Hills
spots.desc: An park overlooking the Cagayan River with a replica of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his companions. The site can get crowded during Holy Week.

spots.name: Poor Clare Monastery
spots.desc: A monastery and pilgrimage site run by the Order of Saint Clare.

spots.name: Portabaga Falls
spots.desc: The main tourist attraction in town, it is a three-level cascade with a total height of and surrounded by a resort complex.

spots.name: Mingay Beach
spots.desc: The main beach destination in Santa Praxedes, it is a stretch of white sand leading to two separate coves at the terminus of the main road leading from downtown Santa Praxedes to the coast.

spots.name: Dibulo Falls
spots.desc: The tallest waterfall in Isabela, it is a high cascade deep within the Sierra Madre.

spots.name: Bonsai Forest
spots.desc: A preserve featuring rare flora such as naturally-forming bonsai plants, pitcher plants and orchids. Access to the area is restricted and will require a guide. Permits are obtainable at the municipal government offices

spots.name: Dinapigue Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Its top is accessible following steep ascent of 254 steps.

spots.name: Capisaan Caves
spots.desc: The fifth longest cave in the country at 4.2 km. It has layers of cave network including Lion and Alayan Caves with rare calcite formations and a subterranean river which doubles as a passageway to the best part of the cave. Brgy. Capisaan is about four hours by jeep from Solano on feeder and clay type soil road carved out of mountain sides. Tours can be arranged with the Sang-at-Salug…

spots.name: Mount Ugu
spots.desc: At the boundary with Benguet, the high peak offers trails that pass through native communities of the Kalanguya tribes and is becoming a favorite mountaineering destination among outdoor enthusiasts.

spots.name: Nueva Vizcaya Mural
spots.desc: An extensive mural along the highway leading to Bayombong outlining Nueva Vizcaya's history and culture.

spots.name: Nueva Vizcaya Agricultural Terminal
spots.desc: A major wholesale retail market for vegetable producers in southern Nueva Vizcaya to sell their products to traders who usually resell the crops in Metro Manila and elsewhere.

spots.name: Primark Center Bambang
spots.desc: Retail department store with a Savemore grocery and a McDonald's.

spots.name: Big Eats Barbeque
spots.desc: A cafeteria-style barbecue and grill also selling frozen steaks for takeout.

spots.name: Boo Le Vous Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe serving native-grown coffee infused with fruit flavors derived from locally-grown produce.

spots.name: Edralin Falls
spots.desc: A 7-tier cascade. Due to overcrowding, a 100-person visitors' limit is imposed during peak seasons.

spots.name: Dimmalikan Peak
spots.desc: A high mountain named after the three conjoined boulders at its summit.

spots.name: Capisaan Nature Walk
spots.desc: An eco-trail near Capisaan Cave in which the area's diverse avian population can be spotted.

spots.name: Salacsac Pass
spots.desc: The site of a World-War II battle fought in conjunction with the Battle of Dalton Pass. Unlike Dalton, the site sits on a higher altitude of around and was redeveloped following the concreting of the Pangasinan-Nueva Vizcaya Road in the early 2020s. There are stalls selling coffee and agricultural goods, a war memorial, and even a Sherman Tank on one of the resorts that have sprung up along the…

spots.name: Imugan Falls
spots.desc: A two-level cascade with a shallow catch basin. Trek over streams/rivers emanating from the falls. Enjoy trekking, exploration, swimming, fishing and cultural immersion. Also within the area is the Imugan Mountain Fresh Factory which utilizes wild berries and other fruits to produce spreads and jams while visitors can watch the production process and shop for preserved fruit spreads.

spots.name: Our Mother of Perpetual Help Parish Church
spots.desc: The main Roman Catholic church in Santa Fe, situated on the side of a mountain.

spots.name: Forest Park
spots.desc: An ecotourism site featuring groves of trees native to the Caraballo and Cordillera mountain ranges.

spots.name: Mrs G.
spots.desc: A cafe-style restaurant with bakeshop, grocery and decent restrooms.

spots.name: Aglipay Caves
spots.desc: The main tourist attraction in Aglipay, it is a complex of forests and hills whose highlight is a 37-chamber cave system where Gregorio Aglipay was said to have gone into hiding during the Philippine wars of independence. The area also has camping facilities.

spots.name: Claredita Falls
spots.desc: A 5-tier cascade on a vertical rock face surrounded by blue-colored lagoons.

spots.name: Napipiwongan Falls
spots.desc: A 7-tier cascade named after the local term for the swallows that reside in the area.

spots.name: Panagsalukag Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

spots.name: Susong Dalaga
spots.desc: Translated as "Maiden's Breasts" because of their appearance, they are a pair of forested limestone hills with a height of separated by a creek. It also has a cave that is accessible following a hike along a 275-step trail.

spots.name: Quirino Watersports Complex
spots.desc: A multilevel recreational complex featuring facilities for watersports, overnight accommodation and large-scale events.

spots.name: Ginnamuluan Festival
spots.desc: The town's patronal festival, also celebrating its heritage and culture.

spots.name: Mount Nagbukel
spots.desc: Meaning "round" in Ilocano, it is looming, forested limestone hill along the Ganano River, a tributary of the Cagayan River that forms a ecopark complex run by the municipal government.

spots.name: Mount Batumbaket
spots.desc: A forested mountain range with wild orchids and a jagged rock outcrop which gives the peak its name, derived from an Ilocano word for old woman.

spots.name: Susong Dalaga
spots.desc: Translated as "Maiden's Breast" because of its appearance, it is a forested limestone hill that forms a ecopark complex.

spots.name: Liwayway Caves
spots.desc: A series of 15 caves scattered across a row of forested hills. The site was also used for religious purposes by the Union Esperitista, a homegrown syncretic Christian group.

spots.name: Bagnes Nature Park and Campsite
spots.desc: An ecopark built on a village were some Kankanaey tribespeople were resettled. It offers cultural activities featuring the Cordilleras as well as hikes to multiple waterfalls in the area.

spots.name: Pammadayaw Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

spots.name: Landingan Viewpoint
spots.desc: A stretch of the highway overlooking the Cagayan River valley that offers views of the town and a flower garden surrounding it.

spots.name: Siitan Nature Park
spots.desc: A nature preserve along the Cagayan River featuring rafting, swimming and boating facilities.

spots.name: Bimmapor Rock Formation
spots.desc: A much-photographed and looming limestone formation along the Cagayan River named because of its resemblance to the stern of a ship (bapor in Filipino).

spots.name: Diamond Cave
spots.desc: A cave with looming rock formations and underground streams.

spots.name: Penenkakasisit Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual celebration of its foundation date, featuring local dances and costumed parades by its indigenous residents.

spots.name: Saguday Municipal Hall
spots.desc: One of the oldest buildings in town, dating back to the 1960s.

spots.name: Pagay Pagay Festival
spots.desc: The town's annual festival celebrating local customs and culture.

spots.name: Saint John Nepomucene Parish Church
spots.desc: Alfonso's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era.

spots.name: The Gingerbread House
spots.desc: A family and children-oriented theme park built exactly to look like a gingerbread house and other sugary contraptions. It also offers hands-on activities such as baking, candy-making and other arts and crafts. There is also an onsite cafe.
spots.price: P200, P160 for elderly and disabled, free for children and below

spots.name: Royale Tagaytay Golf Course
spots.desc: An extensive golf course that also has tennis courts, a spa, swimming pool and gym, as well as spaces for weddings.

spots.name: Alfonso Adventure Park
spots.desc: An extensive recreational venue that offers swimming, camping, ATVs, survival and other outdoor-based activities.

spots.name: Asador Alfonso
spots.desc: A 1-star Michelin restaurant inside a farm estate featuring Spanish cuisine. Among the highlights are the cochinillo (roast suckling pig), lamb and cheesecake. The restaurant building itself is an attraction for its sleek modernist architecture. There is a smart casual dress code. Reservations are necessary.

spots.name: Marcia Adams
spots.desc: Garden-themed restaurant serving Mediterranean cuisine. Reservations necessary.
spots.hours: 11AM-9PM M, W and Thu, 10AM-9PM Tu, 11:30AM-5PM F, 10AM-10PM Su, closed Sa

spots.name: Girasol
spots.desc: Garden-themed restaurant and bed and breakfast serving Filipino, Spanish and Mediterranean cuisine. Reservations necessary.
spots.price: Menu starts at P280, rooms start at P5200

spots.name: Verdiview
spots.desc: Filipino and international cuisine served in a lush, forested setting.

spots.name: Saint Joseph Parish Church
spots.desc: Bailen's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era. This should not be confused with the Aglipayan (Iglesia Filipina Independiente) across the street, which is also dedicated to Saint Joseph and was built much later.

spots.name: Paliguang Aso
spots.desc: A pristine swimming spot around a dammed stream. The name means "dog bath" in Tagalog. Nearby is Mag-asawang Bato ("Husband and Wife Rock"), a pair of giant boulders.

spots.name: Bangis ng Bailen Game Farm and Nature Resort
spots.desc: A sprawling eco-tourism resort and recreational venue which also breeds roosters for cockfighting (bangis means fierceness in Tagalog).

spots.name: Republica's Lechon House
spots.desc: A restaurant whose main specialty is lechon (roasted whole pig on a spit).
spots.addr: East-West Road corner Aguinaldo-Batas Dao Road, Kabulusan

spots.name: La Vianda Cafe and Restaurant
spots.desc: Restaurant at a family-owned farm with alfresco dining spaces and tents for those who take their privacy seriously/

spots.name: Sarayba House
spots.desc: A 19th-century residence previously owned by the grandparents of Mariano Trias. Following decades of neglect, the house was restored and is scheduled to reopen as a museum in 2026, although visitors are allowed to take pictures of the exterior.

spots.name: GBR Museum
spots.desc: A museum showcasing the art and Filipiniana collection of businessman Geronimo B. de los Reyes Jr.

spots.name: General Trias City Park
spots.desc: An extensive recreational space on the outskirts of downtown GenTri.

spots.name: Kaway'an Ecopark
spots.desc: An ecotourism and recreational venue with a large bamboo pavilion.
spots.addr: Crisanto M. De Los Reyes Avenue, Panungyanan

spots.name: Eagle Ridge Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: A sprawling mixed-use luxury development featuring the largest golf course in the Philippines, measuring .

spots.name: Rosario Church
spots.desc: Rosario's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era and containing the venerated painting of Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary, Queen of the Caracol.

spots.name: Casa Hacienda de Tejeros
spots.desc: A partial reconstruction of the friar estate manor where the first provisional Philippine government was established during the Philippine Revolution against Spain on March 22, 1897, although most history textbooks erroneously place the site in General Trias, whose boundary with Rosario lies along the southern perimeter wall of the compound.

spots.name: Caracol Festival
spots.desc: The town's patronal festival is held twice a year to commemorate the feasts of Saint Isidore the Laborer and Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary. Both occasions feature a procession of the Marian Caracol image, accompanied by street dancing to the tunes of the pandanggo folk dance at a slow pace resembling that of a snail (caracol).

spots.name: Tinapa Festival
spots.desc: An annual celebration of Rosario's signature product, smoked, cured fish (tinapa).

spots.name: Rosario Public Market/Primark Town Center
spots.desc: An amalgamation of the town's main market and a department store chain.

spots.name: San Pedro Bautista Parish Church
spots.desc: Candelaria's main Roman Catholic church, built with twin spires and housing a venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Candlemas.

spots.name: Candelaria Municipal Hall
spots.desc: An imposing civic building dating from the pre-World War II era

spots.name: Uma Verde Econature Farm
spots.desc: An ecotourism venue featuring a working farm and accommodations.

spots.name: Buddy's Restaurant
spots.desc: A branch of a provincial restaurant chain based in Lucban serving Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
spots.addr: Cabunag corner De Galo Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Jade and Jillian's House of Pies
spots.desc: A pie shop selling pies made from mango that frequently get sold out.
spots.addr: Maharlika Highway corner Cabunag Street, Poblacion

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of the Holy Rosary
spots.desc: Cardona's main Roman Catholic church, housing the venerated Marian image of Our Lady of Sapao.

spots.name: Cardona Rock Garden
spots.desc: A natural rock formation featuring assorted boulders and jagged rocks.

spots.name: Suah Rock Formation
spots.desc: A cliff at the edge of a promontory overlooking Dingalan Bay. The landscapes evoke those in Batanes.

spots.name: White Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of white sand that serves as the jump-off point for the trail leading to Suah Rock Formation and surrounding sites. It is primarily accessible by boat from Dingalan Port.

spots.name: Matawe Rock Formations
spots.desc: A series of jagged limestone outcrops and tidal pools continuously pounded by the open waves of the Pacific Ocean, best viewed during low tide.

spots.name: Dingalan Grotto
spots.desc: A roadside monument to the Virgin Mary overlooking Dingalan Bay accessible following an ascent of 1,200 steps.

spots.name: Umiray Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge near the mouth of the Umiray River which separates Aurora from Quezon province and offers panoramic views of the eponymous valley.

spots.name: Lamao Caves
spots.desc: A natural grotto continuously battered by the waves of the Pacific Ocean.

spots.name: Dingalan Lighthouse
spots.desc: A solar-powered lighthouse on a cliff with an elevation of overlooking Dingalan Bay.

spots.name: Dingalan Adventure Park
spots.desc: An extensive ecotourism park and recreational area covering many of the town's natural attractions.

spots.name: House of Tapsi
spots.desc: Restaurant with all-day servings of jerky (tapa) and fried rice (sinangag), a common breakfast combination.

spots.name: La Purisima Concepcion House
spots.desc: An American-era private residence with a central parapet and lavish external decorations on its façade.
spots.addr: J.C. de Jesus corner M. de Leon Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Santa Maria Plaza
spots.desc: A public park with a children's playground, civic monuments and a Hollywood-like sign of Santa Maria.
spots.addr: J.C. de Jesus corner C. de Guzman Streets, Poblacion

spots.name: Diocesan Shrine of the Mother of the Eucharist and Grace
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic Shrine built following reports of appearances of the Virgin Mary before residents in 1991.

spots.name: Jennie's Chicharon
spots.desc: A popular homegrown pork skin/rind (chicharon) brand with multiple branches and resellers across town.

spots.name: Steaks and Arrows
spots.desc: Steakhouse and other western dishes. Also has an archery range on account of the owners' favorite sport.
spots.addr: Norzagaray-Santa Maria Road, Dulong Bayan, Poblacion

spots.name: Santa Maria Dairy-Catmon MPC
spots.desc: Locally-made dairy products including flavored milk and yogurt.

spots.name: Mount 387
spots.desc: The main hiking attraction in town and in Nueva Ecija, named because it is exactly in height. The grassy summit and surrounding ridges have also generated another nickname, the "Chocolate Hills of Nueva Ecija", due to its similarities with the original in Bohol.

spots.name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church
spots.desc: Carranglan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1701 and restored following heavy damage during the 1990 Luzon earthquake.
spots.addr: Provincial Road corner San Nicolas Street, Poblacion

spots.name: Santo Niño De Puncan Shrine
spots.desc: A village chapel hosting the venerated and oldest known image of the Christ Child in Nueva Ecija, dating back to 1668. It has been restored to its original Spanish-era façade in the 2020s following restoration efforts to undo damage caused by the Battle of Balete Pass and the 1990 Luzon earthquake.

spots.name: Eva Bhil Eatery
spots.desc: A no-frills roadside cafeteria serving thick and juicy meat and fish dishes. Their specialty is the fish soup made from milkfish (bangus), which has a steak-like, albeit bony, texture.

spots.name: Apalit Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of Apalit's municipal government was built in imitation of the back of the White House, complete with an ellipse filled with trees, a park and a Hollywood-like sign of the town.

spots.name: Casa Sulipeña
spots.desc: A 19th-century bahay na bato that belonged to one of Apalit's elite families and hosted visiting Spanish and dignitaries from other countries including future US president William Howard Taft.

spots.name: Apung Iru Festival
spots.desc: Apalit’s annual patronal festival, dedicated to its patron saint, Saint Peter the Apostle (known in Kapampangan as Apung Iru). The highlight of the event is a fluvial procession along the Pampanga River.

spots.name: Funnside Ningnangan
spots.desc: A Pampanga-based restaurant and grill chain serving Filipino dishes.

spots.name: Holy Family Child Formation Center
spots.desc: A school with a massive Spanish-era colonial era residence inside. If you are barred from entering, the house is visible from the road given the school's low fences.

spots.name: The Great GIGATT Resort and Leisure Park
spots.desc: A resort with overnight accommodation, swimming pools, gardens and an aviary.

spots.name: Santa Monica Parish Church
spots.desc: Mexico's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish period but rebuilt in a modern style after an earthquake in 1880 that destroyed the structure save for its belfry.
spots.price: P20 parking fee for cars (first four hours), free Su

spots.name: Lazatin-Henson-Katigbak Mansion
spots.desc: A Spanish-era residence belonging to one of Pampanga's elite families.

spots.name: Rivera-Panlilio Ancestral House
spots.desc: A Spanish-era residence belonging to one of Pampanga's elite families.

spots.name: San Jose Matulid Chapel
spots.desc: Said to be the oldest Roman Catholic chapel in Pampanga, built in 1581.

spots.name: Bale Mi
spots.desc: The colonial-era residence of the Sandico family, built in 1827 and converted into an events venue.

spots.name: Kusinang Matua ng Atching Lillian
spots.desc: A heritage restaurant serving Kapampangan cuisine set inside a colonial-era residence. Meals involve a buffet and cooking demonstration by proprietor Lilian Borromeo, one of the leading masters of Kapampangan cuisine. Walk-ins are allowed for those seeking Atching Lilian’s San Nicolas Cookies, which are sold in individual boxes with 12 pieces.
spots.hours: Reservation required. Minimum of 10 people needed

spots.name: Dandy's San Nicolas Cookies
spots.desc: A bakery selling various local pastries including the Panecillo de San Nicolas (San Nicolas cookie), a buttery shortbread made with arrowroot flour, egg yolk and coconut milk and then shaped into molds featuring depictions of Saint Nicholas of Tolentine. The cookies are said by locals to have miraculous powers.

spots.name: Luis Taruc Monument
spots.desc: Placed on a road junction next to the municipal park, it is memorial depicting a sculpture of a peasant family. It is dedicated to the town's most famous resident, Luis Taruc, a peasant leader who founded the Hukbalahap, the country's largest guerrilla organization fighting against the Japanese in World War II, and then the Philippine government when it reneged on its promises to grant land…

spots.name: Hukbalahap Monument
spots.desc: A monument built in 2023 at the entrance of a private cemetery to honor the Hukbalahap (an abbreviation of Hukbong Bayan Laban sa Hapon; translated as People's Anti-Japanese Army) movement founded by Luis Taruc, who was born in what was then the rural village of Santa Monica in 1913. It features concrete statues depicting Taruc and two of his comrades in the Huk movement. Its construction, along…

spots.name: Old San Luis Bridge Park
spots.desc: A recreational space built over the remaining span of the old bridge over the Pampanga River connecting downtown San Luis with its rural barangays.

spots.name: Santa Lucia Parish Church
spots.desc: Sasmuan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era and extensively modified over the succeeding years while retaining its façade and pineapple-looking cupola.

spots.name: Sasmuan Coastal Wetland
spots.desc: A protected area of the Pampanga River delta on the southern edge of Sasmuan facing Manila Bay. It is a critical habitat for various flora and fauna, particularly birds, spanning across four barangays of Sasmuan and was internationally recognized as a Ramsar Site in 2021.

spots.name: Sasmuan Delicacies
spots.desc: A store selling popular delicacies and sweets from town such as polvoron and turrones de casoy, a nougat made from cashew nut. Although they do not have a physical store in Sasmuan itself, they have branches in major cities in Pampanga such as San Fernando and Angeles.

spots.name: Bamban World War II Museum
spots.desc: Bamban saw heavy fighting during World War II for control of the approaches to Clark Field. This small museum run by a former tour guide and head of the Bamban Historical Society within his bird-filled residence keeps artifacts from that period such as photographs, letters, weapons, costumes and other equipment. The museum also arranges tours of battlefields in town. Taking photographs of images…

spots.name: Santo Niño Parish Church
spots.desc: Bamban's main Roman Catholic church, known in town for its distinctive spires.

spots.name: Baofu Compound
spots.desc: This sprawling compound that was built at the back of the municipal hall as a self-sustaining business hub, complete with mid to high-rise buildings and condominiums commonly seen in Metro Manila and Angeles, has become the inadvertent poster image of Bamban after police raids in 2024 discovered the existence of criminal activities such as online extortion, fraud and unregulated gambling inside…

spots.name: Japanese Cave
spots.desc: A network of caves and tunnels on a hill that was used as a hideout by Japanese forces during World War II. Nearby is the town's official war memorial.

spots.name: Grotto Of Our Lady Of Lourdes
spots.desc: A hilltop Catholic shrine inspired by the original in Lourdes, France. It is accessible after an ascent of 100 steps.

spots.name: Bamban Municipal Library
spots.desc: A library housed inside the colonial-era former municipal hall.

spots.name: Concepcion Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The colonnaded seat of local government in Concepcion. In front is a monument to Ninoy Aquino, who started his political career in 1955 aged 23 as the town's youngest elected mayor.

spots.name: Aquino Ancestral House
spots.desc: The ancestral residence of the Aquino family, built during the 1930s and still owned by Ninoy’s brother, who sometimes visits. While access to the interior is restricted, visitors are welcome to take pictures of the exterior and admire the well-maintained lawn after informing the caretakers of their presence.
spots.addr: A. Luna corner Timbol Streets, San Jose

spots.name: Voice Of America - Tinang Relay Transmitter
spots.desc: During the Cold War, the US government took over a piece of land outside Concepcion to build transmitters for the Voice of America radio station broadcasting anti-communist propaganda across Asia. Since the American withdrawal in 1992, the site has been used by the Philippine government for its media outlets. While the complex is a restricted area, its red lights blink continuously at night and…

spots.name: Looc Lake
spots.desc: A freshwater lake surrounded by grassy fields set amidst the backdrop of the towering peaks of the Redondo Peninsula. The lake also has commonly-farmed fish species such as tilapia.

spots.name: Carmelite Monastery
spots.desc: A secluded Roman Catholic monastery built on top of a hill. The complex becomes a pilgrimage site during Holy Week.

spots.name: San Nicolas de Tolentino Parish Church
spots.desc: Castillejos's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1865.

spots.name: Bagsit River
spots.desc: A pristine stream lined with boulders whose blue-green waters originate from Mount Tapulao.

spots.name: Zennor Hydroponics Farm
spots.desc: A vegetable farm that is one of the pioneers of hydroponic (soil-free) growing methods in the country. The facility offers tours and also sells its produce directly to visitors.

spots.name: Anawangin Cove
spots.desc: The most famous and visited cove in town featuring white sand beaches and an agujo grove. The place can get crowded with campers from Metro Manila on weekends.

spots.name: Nagsasa Cove
spots.desc: A less crowded alternative to Anawangin with scant phone signal. There is also a shallow creek entering the cove near its southern edge.

spots.name: Casa San Miguel
spots.desc: A house inside a mango orchard built in 1921 and now hosting a museum on local history, culture and art.

spots.name: Mount Pundaquit
spots.desc: A highlight in the hiking trail from Pundaquit to Anawangin Cove overlooking Agnain and Diego's Coves.

spots.name: Silanguin Cove
spots.desc: The farthest of San Antonio's coves. Unlike the other coves, its beaches are of the gray sand variety. At the mouth of the cove is an eponymous island.

spots.name: Camara Island
spots.desc: A smaller island with rock formations and a small white sand beach.

spots.name: Mount Capalngan
spots.desc: A mountain with commanding views extending to the neighboring town of San Marcelino. Also has an eponymous waterfall.

spots.name: Bigfoot Restaurant & Rest House
spots.desc: Restaurant serving Filipino dishes. Their main draw is the halo-halo.

spots.name: Anat Falls
spots.desc: A shorter cascade than Anuplig, it is mostly visited by residents for its nearer distance from town and calmer waters.

spots.name: Lover's Peak
spots.desc: A stretch of highland overlooking downtown Adams named for its being a favorite dating spot for couples.

spots.name: Cardom Farm
spots.desc: A fruit farm that also offers unlimited coffee from beans that are also grown inside the complex.

spots.name: La Virgen Milagrosa Chapel
spots.desc: A chapel built by the cove where the Virgen Milagrosa was said to have washed up in 1620 from Japan, where it had been hidden away by Christians being persecuted by the Tokugawa Shogunate. The cove was subsequently named in the Virgin's honor. At the same time, a twin image of the crucified Christ, known as the Santo Cristo Milagroso, washed up in the neighboring village of Dadalaquiten, part of…
spots.addr: Ian Pan Road, Sitio Paguetpet, La Milagrosa

spots.name: Ilocos Norte Welcome Arch
spots.desc: A massive archway marking the boundary between Ilocos Norte and Ilocos Sur provinces. Behind the Badoc side of the arch is a small visitor center with rest area.

spots.name: Saint Mark the Evangelist Parish Church
spots.desc: Cabugao's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style.

spots.name: Pug-os Beach
spots.desc: A white-sand cove that is also used as a production center for sea salt.

spots.name: Rebba Falls
spots.desc: A set of rapids at the point where the Cabugao River exits the Cordillera Mountains into the coastal plain.

spots.name: Cariño House
spots.desc: An 18th century colonial residence where the Silang Revolt, the largest anti-Spanish uprising in the Ilocos Region before the Philippine Revolution of 1896, was planned. It now houses the city's local history museum.
spots.addr: Dario corner Gaerlan Streets, San Antonio

spots.name: Dario Ancestral House
spots.desc: A Spanish-era colonial residence that now houses an art museum.
spots.addr: Dario corner San Juan Streets, San Juan

spots.name: Candon City Ecopark
spots.desc: A sprawling nature reserve in the highlands of Candon, featuring flower gardens, bamboo groves, farm animals and houses of the indigenous Bag-o tribe.

spots.name: Samonte Memorial Park
spots.desc: Leafy public square with civic monuments and a memorial to the Cry of Candon, which marked the outbreak of the Philippine Revolution in the Ilocos Region in 1898.

spots.name: Mount Tuwato
spots.desc: A peak along the Bessang Ridge shared with the municipality of Sigay.

spots.name: Kimat Patil-ao
spots.desc: An hiking trail named after a local term for lightning, which is frequent in the area.

spots.name: Holy Child of Prague Parish Church
spots.desc: Cervantes's main Roman Catholic church, rebuilt as an octagonal building in the 1970s.

spots.name: Aluling Bridge
spots.desc: An important bridge connecting Ilocos Sur and Mountain Province, it provides scenic views over the Abra River.

spots.name: MPD Village
spots.desc: A multi-purpose resort and recreational area with a retreat house, spring-fed swimming pools and accommodations founded by Master del Pe, a resident and spiritual leader who runs a spiritual and philosophical organization called the Institute of Higher Consciousness.

spots.name: Magsingal Municipal Hall
spots.desc: The seat of local government in Magsingal, built to resemble a Spanish-era government building.

spots.name: Magsingal Belfry
spots.desc: Magsingal Church's belfry predates the actual church building by about 100 years. It also functioned as a watchtower guarding against pirates and foreign invaders. The belfry and the adjoining convent are part of the National Museum-Ilocos Region and was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2001.

spots.name: Puro Pinget Island
spots.desc: Not really an island but rather a round peninsula connected to mainland Magsingal by the narrow Puro Sandbar. It contains white sand beaches and a large concentration of beach resorts.

spots.name: Nagbukel Viewdeck
spots.desc: An elevated lookout point with views over the surrounding valley and Northern Luzon Heroes Hill National Park.

spots.name: Mabungtot Falls
spots.desc: The lower cascade of a waterfall system that includes Matedtedted Falls

spots.name: Matedtedted Falls
spots.desc: The upper cascade of a waterfall system that includes Mabungtot Falls

spots.name: Saint John the Baptist Parish Church
spots.desc: San Juan's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style.

spots.name: Solot-Solot Public Beach And Baywalk
spots.desc: A extensive stretch of beach and promenade at the main bay of San Juan.

spots.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria Parish Church
spots.desc: Santa's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era in 1854.

spots.name: New Quirino Bridge
spots.desc: A two-lane bridge over the Abra River Gorge marking the boundary between Santa and Bantay to the north. At both ends of the bridge are viewing platforms with panoramic vistas of the area, including the old arch bridge east of the river, which has now lost much of its span following typhoons and flooding.

spots.name: Calungboyan Bridge
spots.desc: An arched steel bridge connecting mainland Santa with Isla Azul, an island on the delta of the Abra River.

spots.name: Pinsal Falls
spots.desc: A stunning cascade with turquoise waters on the boundary with Abra province.

spots.name: Suso Beach
spots.desc: The main beach in Santa Maria, featuring cream-colored sands and free access.

spots.name: Ambucao Beach
spots.desc: An extensive stretch of cream-colored sand running to Biak na Bato aka Mapisi Rock, a rock formation marking the boundary with the town of San Esteban.

spots.name: Santiago Cove
spots.desc: The town's main draw, a horseshoe-shaped bay surrounded by Sabangan Beach, stretch of white-sand beach dubbed the “Boracay of the North”.

spots.name: St. James the Greater Parish Church
spots.desc: Santiago's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style by the Spanish during the late 18th century on a hilltop. It also functioned as a fortress against pirates and foreign invaders at the time.

spots.name: Sabangan Watchtower
spots.desc: A stout, Spanish-era watchtower overlooking Santiago Cove meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

spots.name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
spots.desc: Santo Domingo's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a baroque style in 1740. Diego Silang, who later led the biggest anti-Spanish revolt in the Ilocos Region in 1762, served as a bell ringer at the parish.

spots.name: Unknown Citizen Park
spots.desc: A small monument dedicated to the anonymous citizens of the municipality.

spots.name: Rizal Park
spots.desc: The main recreational and green space in town, featuring a monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal, that was erected in 1972, and Monumento ti Pagulidanan, an obelisk-like contraption built to celebrate unity and notable residents.

spots.name: Sived Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of gray sand in the northwestern side of town ideal for surfing.

spots.name: Puerto Beach
spots.desc: A stretch of sand along the southwestern side of town. It has the ruins of a jetty built by the Japanese during World War II.

spots.name: Aw-asen Falls
spots.desc: The main tourist draw in Sigay, it is the tallest waterfall in Ilocos Region, with a height of gushing through a vertical rock face. Access to the site is restricted to pre-organized tour groups for safety reasons.

spots.name: Mount Longon
spots.desc: Another mountain in the Bessang Ridge, often climbed as part of the Tuwato-Monserrat circuit.

spots.name: Namempengan Falls
spots.desc: An overlooked but similarly picturesque terraced waterfall system gushing along a shredded-looking and gently sloped rock face on the other side of town.

spots.name: Sigay Viewdeck
spots.desc: A panoramic viewdeck on the boundary with Suyo with vistas over Sigay's valleys.

spots.name: Pacaoan Sea of Clouds
spots.desc: A highland roadside viewdeck along the Pacaoan Ridge named for the waves of clouds that form around it on foggy days.

spots.name: Sugpon Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge connecting Sugpon with Sudipen with panoramic views over the Amburayan River valley.

spots.name: Mount Tapao
spots.desc: A mountain that served as a Japanese garrison during the Battle of Bessang Pass for the commanding views at its peak and is now a forested bird sanctuary.

spots.name: Bantay Kalbaryo
spots.desc: A highland pilgrimage site for followers of Paltiing, an obscure religion based in the Ilocos Region. It also has a demonstration farm operated by the municipal government.

spots.name: Saint Augustine Parish Church
spots.desc: Tagudin's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in the Baroque style in the 19th century. Its belltower, built separately from the church building, also functioned as a watchtower guarding against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The church's grounds also hold one of two sundials that were built in Tagudin during the Spanish era in 1841 and are the oldest…

spots.name: Tagudin Town Plaza
spots.desc: A recreational and civic space surrounded by the town church and the old municipal hall. It contains memorials to the Battle of Bessang Pass, when the plaza was turned into an Allied field hospital, and one of two sundials that were built in Tagudin during the Spanish era. The other is in the yard of Tagudin Church.

spots.name: Farola Lighthouse
spots.desc: A lighthouse overlooking the South China Sea built to commemorate the arrival by boat in the area of Belgian missionaries who replaced the Spanish friars in their task of evangelizing Tagudin and the animist highland areas in 1910. The surrounding beach is a mixture of black sand and pebbles.

spots.name: Bimmanga Bangka
spots.desc: A small ecotourism venue featuring a creek surrounded by mangroves and other estuarine vegetation.

spots.name: Ilocos Sur Welcome Arch
spots.desc: A massive archway marking the boundary between Ilocos Sur and La Union provinces. At the left side of the arch, if coming from the south, is a small visitor center with rest area.

spots.name: Amburayan Bridge
spots.desc: A two-lane bridge overlooking the extensive riverbed of the Amburayan River that marks the actual boundary between Ilocos Sur and La Union provinces. On one side is a panoramic view of the river descending from the Cordillera mountains into the coastal plain while on the other side is an equally panoramic view of the river as it reaches the South China Sea. Underneath the bridge are some shacks…

spots.name: Eagle of the North Park
spots.desc: A park featuring a massive sculpture of an eagle, believed to symbolize the Marcos regime's influence in the Ilocos Region.

spots.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic hillside shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary and the site of the alleged Marian apparitions to Judiel Nuerva, in what became known as the "Miracle of Agoo".

spots.name: Splash Town Waterpark & Resort
spots.desc: A resort with swimming pools and other waterpark-related activities and overnight accommodation.

spots.name: Samara Beach
spots.desc: The main coastal promenade in Aringay, with grayish sand stretching from the boundary with Caba to the north down to the Aringay River estuary.

spots.name: Santa Lucia Parish Church
spots.desc: Aringay's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in 1736 and extensively repaired following World War II damage. The plaza in front of the church was a battleground during the Philippine Revolution against the Spanish in 1898.

spots.name: Centennial Tunnel
spots.desc: An long unfinished tunnel built by the Philippine National Railways as part of a planned extension the railway line from Manila towards San Fernando, which was abandoned at the outbreak of World War II and was instead used as a bomb shelter by the Japanese.

spots.name: Bubon Posi
spots.desc: The highest point in Aringay, it is a peak of a mountain ridge bisected by the Aringay River. Its conical summit looms over the town and is a designated forest reserve and hiking spot.

spots.name: Dulao Lagoon
spots.desc: An estuarine lagoon lined with mangrove forests on the boundary with Agoo.

spots.name: Gallano Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A terraced rice farm on the slopes of the Cordillera Mountain Range overlooking the boundary with Tuba in Benguet province.

spots.name: Aringay Central Elementary School
spots.desc: The administrative building of the town's main primary school is an American-era bungalow (commonly known as the Gabaldon) dating from between 1907 to 1912.

spots.name: Zim-sim-og Twin Falls
spots.desc: A twin cascade facing each other on opposite sides of the Maragayap River with a height of and a basin pool with a depth of . It is named after a Kankanaey term to describe the sound of rock crashing against each other.

spots.name: Sapilang Falls
spots.desc: A cascade located within the sprawling forested compound of the Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University - North La Union Campus.
spots.price: entry permission required from university officials

spots.name: Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church
spots.desc: A post-modern Roman Catholic church design by national artist for architecture Leandro Locsin in 1956.

spots.name: Galongen-Quirino Surfing Area
spots.desc: A popular surfing spot along a sandbar at the mouth of the Maragayap River.

spots.name: Alpas La Union
spots.desc: A beachside cafe known for hosting live performances of some of the Philippines' leading musicians.

spots.name: Immuki Island
spots.desc: Not really an island but a series of three lagoons, mangroves, tidal pools and flats with clear waters and teeming with marine life. The entire site is walkable during low tide.

spots.name: Our Lady of Lourdes Grotto
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic hillside shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

spots.name: Paratong Beach
spots.desc: Bangar's main seaside promenade, featuring grayish sands and extending from the Amburayan River delta down to the boundary with Luna.

spots.name: Saints Peter and Paul Parish Church
spots.desc: Bauang's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a Baroque style in 1590 and consistently repaired to its original state following multiple earthquakes and wars.

spots.name: Bauang Bakawan Eco-Tourism Park
spots.desc: An extensive ecotourism reserve featuring mangroves (bakawan) along the coasts of Barangays Parian Oeste, Pudoc, and Payocpoc Sur

spots.name: Mount Kabugbugan
spots.desc: The highest point in Bauang with a height of . Its peak offers commanding views of Lingayen Gulf.

spots.name: Arguilla House
spots.desc: A colonial-era house belonging to Manuel Arguilla, one of the leading English-language Ilocano writers during the American period who was beheaded by the Japanese in 1944 for joining the guerrilla resistance during World War II.

spots.name: Bauang Watchtower Ruins
spots.desc: The remains of a Spanish-era watchtower meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.

spots.name: Gapuz Grape Farm
spots.desc: Established in 1980, it is one of 61 grape farms in the area after it was found that Bauang's semi-arid soil and climate was ideal for growing the fruit. Offers grape-picking to be paid by weight.

spots.name: Bolikewkew Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A rice terrace complex on the slopes of the Cordilleras overlooking the rapids of the Bolikewkew River. Its name derives from the Ibaloi word for "spiral".

spots.name: Libtong Lake
spots.desc: A lake with no known water source. While not fit for swimming due to its mud-colored waters, visitors can instead rent bamboo rafts for picnics.

spots.name: Budahaw Falls
spots.desc: A 2-tier cascade with a deep basin along the boundary with Sablan in Benguet that is accessible following a 2-hour hike from downtown Burgos. Its name derives from the Ibaloi word for "shooting star", after a legend in which many of these meteors are said to land upon the falls.

spots.name: Kananaskis Mountain Resort
spots.desc: A mountainside resort with swimming pools, flower gardens and accommodations.

spots.name: Burgos Eco Park & Resort
spots.desc: Another mountainside resort with swimming pool and events venue.

spots.name: Adawan Resort & Restaurant
spots.desc: A mountainside resort with swimming pool and restaurant overlooking a tributary of the Balili River.

spots.name: Balay Anito Falls
spots.desc: Meaning "House of the Spirits", it is a cascade that drops down to a deep pool.

spots.name: Puy-ocan Falls
spots.desc: A secluded cascade whose crashing waters produce a mist-like effect.

spots.name: Simminublan Falls
spots.desc: A cascade whose name derives from the cooking pot-like shape of its basin.

spots.name: Sasaba Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A terraced farming complex on the slopes of the Cordillera Mountains.

spots.name: Meditation Cross
spots.desc: A large concrete cross overlooking downtown Santol that is commonly visited during Holy Week.

spots.name: Dupag Rock Formations
spots.desc: A limestone formation in the Marag Valley with boulders reaching up to in height. It has variously been described as resembling a jagged maze and labyrinth, a mangled honeycomb, a human brain, or Swiss cheese.

spots.name: Manacota Underground River
spots.desc: A long underground waterway in the Marag Valley with crystal-blue waters reaching a depth of up to and looming cave formations.

spots.name: Lussok Cave
spots.desc: A cave with looming rock formations and an underground lagoon. Its name derives from a local term for the natural light that manages to penetrate its chambers and bounce off the stalactites and stalagmites.

spots.name: Apayao Eco-Tourism and Sports Complex
spots.desc: A recreational space and sports complex with accommodations run by the provincial government.

spots.name: Mataguisi Church Ruins
spots.desc: The stone shell of the mission church established by the Spanish. Its interior has been partly converted into a chapel.

spots.name: Holy Rosary Parish Church
spots.desc: Pudtol's main Roman Catholic church. While the church building itself is a bland modern structure, beside it are the partially manicured ruins of a mission church built by the Spanish.

spots.name: Maton Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge along Kabugao-Junction Luna Road overlooking the Maton River, a tributary of the Apayao River, and some picturesque rock formations.

spots.name: Hutungan Hidden Paradise
spots.desc: A series of rapids lined by rock formations and a gorge along the Maton River upstream from the Maton Bridge.

spots.name: Agguimangan Agro EcoTourism Farm & Home Stay
spots.desc: A farm with homestay and indigenous crafts showroom overlooking the Apayao River

spots.name: Saint Charles Borromeo Parish Church
spots.desc: Itogon's main Roman Catholic church, somewhat resembling a small chalet.

spots.name: Mount Ulap
spots.desc: A peak with grassy slopes on the boundary with Tuba. On a clear day, hikers can expect a sea of clouds below the summit.

spots.name: Mount Bidawan
spots.desc: A high peak. Along its trail is a shrine to the Virgin Mary called Ave Maria.

spots.name: Balatoc Miner Statue
spots.desc: A small monument to the town's mining industry at one of the first exploited areas of Itogon, featuring a statue of a miner in his work attire carrying his tools.

spots.name: National Museum of the Philippines - Kabayan
spots.desc: The regional branch of the National Museum of the Philippines system, featuring artefacts on Cordilleran natural history, art, ethnography and culture. It was built to find a suitable location for the study and preservation of the mummies of Kabayan from looting, and has one mummy on display.

spots.name: Timbac Caves
spots.desc: A series of caves used as burial sites for the mummies of Kabayan. Having been extensively damaged by looters, access to the site is partially restricted to protect the remaining mummies interred in situ.

spots.name: Lake Tabeyo
spots.desc: Part of a grouping of four lakes in the area collectively known as the Four Lakes of Kabayan, it is the most accessible lake and has a campsite and ranger station.

spots.name: Lake Incolos
spots.desc: Part of the Four Lakes of Kabayan, although it is actually more of a peat bog than a lake. Even if it looks dry, avoid walking over it lest you sink into the quagmire.

spots.name: Lake Latep-Ngapos
spots.desc: Part of the Four Lakes system, located in a secluded forest trail.

spots.name: Lake Ambulalakaw
spots.desc: The cleanest among the Four Lakes, with swimming prohibited to maintain water quality.

spots.name: Junior Pulag
spots.desc: A section of the Tabeyo Trail leading to the Four Lakes and Mount Tabayoc named after its resemblance to the grass and moss-covered summit of Mount Pulag.

spots.name: Sitio Pungayan
spots.desc: Situated at the top of Mount Kabuyao, it is a small farming village that shot to fame overnight in 2015 after it became the setting for one of the Philippines' most loved soap operas, a teen romance flick titled Forevermore with Fil-Am actress Liza Soberano in the lead role. While the subsequent overtourism has led to restrictions on entry to the site. The views of its sloped vegetable and…

spots.name: Aran Cave
spots.desc: A cave whose mouth is in Barangay Camp 4, but whose main chambers are in the neighboring Barangay of Twin Peaks. It is an extensive system named after a man-eating resident ogre.

spots.name: Bridal Veil Falls
spots.desc: A vertical cascade said to literally resemble a bridal veil.

spots.name: Ubong-ubong Cave
spots.desc: An extensive cave system on the border with Sison in Pangasinan.

spots.name: Pinewoods Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: A 72-hole golf course at the boundary with Baguio, with all the typical luxury amenities.

spots.name: Sanagi Oyster Mushroom Farm
spots.desc: A family-run organic mushroom farm producing oyster mushrooms. Apart from fresh produce it also sells other derivatives such as mushroom chips and breadsticks.

spots.name: Tan-aw sa Alang
spots.desc: Coffeeshop with panoramic views of the mountain valleys at the back.

spots.name: Awichon Cultural Village
spots.desc: A living ethnographic museum built on a cliff overlooking a tributary of the Chico River. The complex was founded by Alonzo Saclag, a musician and dancer who was recognized as a national living treasure by the Philippine government for his efforts to preserve indigenous Kalinga culture.
